# Polaris — Architecture Reference

Deep reference material extracted from CLAUDE.md. This file is **not** auto-loaded into Claude Code sessions — read it on demand when a task touches one of the areas below.

For the always-loaded project memory (conventions, business rules, env vars, deployment, RBAC overview, getting started, common tasks, out of scope, cross-cutting rules), see [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). For relationship/dependency lookups across services, see [TOUCHES.md](TOUCHES.md). For canonical implementation references when building a new instance of an existing pattern, see [UI-CANON.md](UI-CANON.md) (UI) and TOUCHES.md → Canonical backend patterns (backend).

## Architecture

```
polaris/
├── CLAUDE.md
├── BUSINESS-RULES.md               # Business rules 12-35 in full: the decision AND the incident that forced it. CLAUDE.md keeps each rule's invariant + a pointer.
├── TOUCHES.md                       # Lookup index: per-service writers/readers/invariants + 6 cross-cutting concerns. Reviewed alongside CLAUDE.md on every commit per "Before any commit, review CLAUDE.md, TOUCHES.md, and design/POLARIS-UI-GUIDE.md for updates" — keeps regression-prone relationships visible without rereading every consumer.
├── UI-CANON.md                      # The Polaris UI canon: the canonical-implementation index for UI patterns — when there are several ways to build the same thing (chart, modal, slide-over, sortable table, …), which file in THIS repo is the reference. Was Part II of design/POLARIS-UI-GUIDE.md until 2026-08-26; split out so a kit re-sync of design/ cannot delete it. Reviewed alongside CLAUDE.md and TOUCHES.md on every commit.
├── design/                          # Drop-in snapshot of the portable UI kit — POLARIS-UI-GUIDE.md (the contract: tokens, themes, shell, tables, modals, the phone SPA, the alert email), plus css/ js/ email/ specimens. A sync may also drop in an `APPLY-*.md` work order naming the divergences to port that round (APPLY-TO-POLARIS.md for the 2026-08 kit port, APPLY-WIDGETS.md for the widget pass); those are consumed and deleted once applied, so don't cite one from elsewhere. Re-synced WHOLESALE from the kit and never edited to chase public/, which is the living source. Nothing Polaris-only belongs here — that is UI-CANON.md.
├── README.md
├── .env.example
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
├── prisma.config.ts                 # Prisma 7 config (datasource URL, seed command)
├── prisma/
│   ├── schema.prisma                # Database schema
│   └── seed.ts
├── docs/
│   ├── INSTALL.md                   # Fresh-install guide (RHEL/Rocky/AlmaLinux 9, Ubuntu/Debian, Windows Server). Includes disk-sizing requirements per volume (DB ≥50 GB, app/state ≥5 GB, /var/log ≥5 GB on STIG layouts) and recovery steps for the "/var is full and Postgres is crash-looping" case. Don't follow this for upgrades — those use the in-app updater under Server Settings → Maintenance → Updates.
│   └── fmg-discovery.md             # FortiManager discovery decision tree (operator-facing): transport mode (proxy vs direct), roster filtering, per-class stamping for FortiGates / FortiSwitches / FortiAPs, push toggles, projection apply. Companion to the phase-by-phase narrative in CLAUDE.md's "FMG Discovery Workflow" section.
├── scripts/
│   ├── test-fmg.mjs                 # FortiManager integration test harness
│   ├── audit-multi-mac-assets.ts    # One-off: unstitch assets cross-stapled by old IP-fallback bug
│   ├── check-fmg-tokens.ts          # One-off: print stored FMG/FortiGate token length/prefix to diagnose token corruption
│   ├── fetch-std-mibs.mjs           # Repopulate src/services/stdMibs/<MODULE>.txt by fetching the eleven canonical standard MIB modules that back the twelve browse-tree keys (SNMPv2-MIB / IF-MIB / HOST-RESOURCES-MIB / ENTITY-MIB / ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB / LLDP-MIB / POWER-ETHERNET-MIB / BRIDGE-MIB / Q-BRIDGE-MIB / RSTP-MIB / IP-MIB — IF-MIB serves both `std:interfaces` and `std:if-ext`). Per-module `mirror` field selects the source: pysnmp.com for all but four, the netdisco-mibs `rfc/` tree for the four switch physical-layer modules (pysnmp was returning HTTP 522 when they were added; each was verified against its published RFC and by canonical-OID resolution). Writes SHA-256 + the actual source URL into SOURCES.md alongside the files, LF-normalizing each module first so the recorded hash matches the bundled artifact on any checkout (`.gitattributes` has `* text=auto`, and pysnmp serves IP-MIB CRLF). SOURCES.md is fully GENERATED — its hand-written sections (cross-module anchors, the known cosmetic gap, licensing) live in this script, because editing them in the output file alone means the next refresh deletes them. Run when refreshing the bundle; existing files are overwritten in place.
│   ├── copy-build-assets.mjs        # BUILD STEP (not ad-hoc): second half of `npm run build` (tsc && node scripts/copy-build-assets.mjs). Mirrors non-.ts runtime assets that tsc won't emit — today the stdMibs/*.txt files — into dist/services/stdMibs/. Without it, every std SNMP-walk (LLDP-MIB etc.) on a built install fails with "Standard MIB ... is not installed on the server", because stdMibLibrary.ts reads the files relative to its compiled location (dist/). Fails the build if it copies 0 files. Every build site invokes `npm run build` so the copy is guaranteed; see cross-cutting/deployment in TOUCHES.md.
│   └── smoke-std-mibs.ts            # Spot-check that each bundled std MIB parses + resolves to its canonical OIDs (sysDescr=1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1, lldpRemTable=1.0.8802.1.1.2.1.4.1, etc.). Backstop for the resolver + parser; vitest unit tests in tests/unit/stdMibLibrary.test.ts cover the same ground formally.
├── public/                          # Vanilla JS frontend (served statically)
│   ├── index.html                   # Dashboard — operator-customizable widget canvas (SolarWinds-style column layout). Read-only by default; a "Customize Page" button (top-right) enters EDIT MODE ("Add Widgets" + "Done Editing"). The dashboard is an ordered list of COLUMNS (each a 12-grid width 3/4/6/12) holding a vertical stack of widgets (height step 1–3 → 280/576/872px). In edit mode: "Add Widgets" opens the full picker (translucent overlay with the dashboard dimmed behind it, a Group-By category list, search, name sort, and a ★ favorite toggle per widget — favorites in localStorage via favorites.js); drag a widget (from the picker or an existing one) → a green "+" insertion placeholder marks the slot and a trailing "+ New block" target accepts drops into a fresh column; the dragged widget lifts with a shadow. Per-column width selector (¼/⅓/½/Full) + remove-column ×; per-widget a ⠿ drag handle (moves the widget to any column), a 1×/2×/3× height cycle, gear config (besides per-widget options, every NOC widget carries a **Regions** scope — All regions / My regions / Selected regions…, narrowing to the caller's effective `regionTags` or to a per-widget checkbox pick of the created region names (list fed by `/dashboard/filter-options` via the memoized `PolarisWidgets.getRegionOptions()`); newly-added widgets default to **My regions** (an unrestricted caller with no effective regions still sees everything), and the unauthenticated /dash wallboard hides **My regions** — no viewer identity to resolve it against — leaving All / Selected regions — and every NOC widget except the Status Map carries an **Asset types** toggle grid over the built-in types (the eight historical + `hypervisor` + `kubernetes_cluster`), default all on; both rendered by the shared `PolarisWidgets.renderNocFilterConfig`, threaded to the server as `?assetTypes=&regionTags=` so the payload is memoized per filter; every severity-bearing widget (Down Assets, Down Interfaces, Storage Forecast, the six top-N widgets, Active Alerts) additionally carries a **Minimum severity** select — All rows (default) / Notice / Informational / Warning / Serious and up / Critical only, the same ladder the ⤓ CSV export tiers use — that narrows the widget to rows whose device carries an active alert at or above that severity, filtered client-side before the row limit / header count / export (any tier past "All rows" therefore hides un-alerted rows, which the popover hint states); when the asset-type filter selects a strict subset, the chosen types appear in the widget's header title in parens, e.g. "Highest Avg CPU (Server, Switch)"), and remove ×. Header titles are composed by `PolarisWidgets.widgetTitle(module, widget)` in widgets/index.js (dashboard.js's `widgetTitleFor` is a thin alias) from the module label plus the two gear filters that change what a widget SHOWS: the asset-type parens above, and the **minimum-severity tier** appended as "… — Warning and up". A widget may declare a `severityLabel` used in place of its label while a tier is set — the six superlative-titled ones do ("Highest Avg CPU" → "Avg CPU"), because a top-N widget narrowed to alerting rows is no longer showing the fleet's highest values (those feeds sort severity-first), so the superlative would name something it isn't doing. Titles are single-line + ellipsized with the full text on the element's `title`, since the article's height is a fixed pixel value and a wrapped header steals a row from the chart below it. The page top bar is frozen (sticky `.page-header-sticky`) so Add Widgets / Done Editing / search stay reachable while the widgets scroll. The dashboard supports **multiple named dashboards as tabs** (layout schema v3: `{version:3, dashboards:[{id,name,columns}], activeId}`, max 24; v1/v2 layouts migrate client-side into a single "Dashboard 1" tab on load) — a "Create New Dashboard" button (right of "Customize Page") adds a tab, click a tab to switch, click the active tab's name to rename it inline, and remove via its × in edit mode. Layouts persist server-side per user (PUT /me/dashboard, debounced 800ms; "Done Editing" forces a save). Widget catalog: Recently Reserved, Assets by Type, Block Utilization (each fetches only its own /dashboard/summary section — `?sections=` — via the 15s-memoized `PolarisWidgets.getSummary({sections,...})`); the SolarWinds-style NOC set — Status Summary, Down Assets, Highest Avg CPU, Highest Avg Memory, Slowest Response, Packet Loss, Highest Disk Usage, Highest Temperature, Stale Polls, Recent Reboots, Active Alerts, Sites with Issues, Status Map (each fetches only its own /dashboard/noc-summary feed — `?feeds=` — via the 15s-memoized `PolarisWidgets.getNocSummary(opts, feeds)`, so a widget renders as soon as ITS query returns instead of gating on the slowest feed; Status Map uses /map/sites); plus role-gated Stale Reservations / Capacity Health / Discovery Activity / Conflict Queue. Each widget module under `public/js/widgets/` self-registers with `PolarisWidgets.register()` and exposes a `renderPreview` (mock-data mini for the library), `renderInstance` (full canvas render), and optional `renderConfig` (gear popover contents).
│   ├── login.html
│   ├── setup.html                   # First-run wizard
│   ├── ipam.html                    # IPAM tabbed surface — folds the legacy /blocks.html + /subnets.html pages into one sidebar entry. Tabs: IP Blocks | Networks. Hash-routed (`#tab=blocks|networks`, `#tab=networks&block=<id>`, `#tab=networks&subnet=<id>[&focusReservation=<id>]`). Each tab's markup lives in a `<template>` element; the orchestrator (`public/js/ipam.js`) clones one template into `#ipam-mount` at a time because the two tab markups share several DOM IDs (filter-pagesize, pagination, pagination-top). `public/js/blocks.js` and `public/js/subnets.js` are loaded once but expose `window.PolarisBlocks.init()` / `window.PolarisSubnets.init()` and suppress their own DOMContentLoaded auto-run when `window.__polarisIpamTabs=true` is set (ipam.html sets it before they load). Legacy /blocks.html and /subnets.html URLs are redirected client-side via tiny HTML stubs served by Express (`legacyIpamRedirect` in src/app.ts) so existing fragments (`#ip=<sid>@<ip>`, `#view=…`) are preserved across the hop. **Gated on `ipBlocks:read` OR `subnets:read`** — the nav entry (`anyPerm` in app.js's NAV_ITEMS) and the server-side page redirect (`pageRequiredPermission`'s `anyOf` in src/app.ts) both, since the page spans two function keys and one is enough to be usable; the orchestrator additionally hides a tab the role can't read and refuses to default onto it (a hash naming it falls back to the readable one), so a role granted only one of the two never lands on a 403. It fails OPEN while the permission matrix is still cold — hiding both tabs on a first-ever login would be worse than a retryable 403.
│   ├── blocks.html                  # Legacy — bookmarked URLs hit a server-side stub that redirects to /ipam.html#tab=blocks while preserving the original fragment. The file itself is still here so any tooling that fetches it for content keeps working; the runtime path is the stub.
│   ├── subnets.html                 # Legacy — same redirect treatment as blocks.html; targets /ipam.html#tab=networks.
│   ├── assets.html
│   ├── integrations.html
│   ├── events.html
│   ├── users.html
│   ├── server-settings.html
│   ├── (logo.png)                   # RETIRED 2026-08 — replaced by the themed marks below. Every favicon is now a two-link `prefers-color-scheme` pair (browser chrome follows the OS, not Polaris's data-theme), the PWA icon source is `img/brand/polaris-symbol-dark.png` (light ink, because every opaque icon variant paints ICON_BG and iOS composites onto black), and `BRANDING_DEFAULTS.logoUrl` points at that same file. `/logo.png` is still recognised by `isDefaultLogoUrl` because installs seeded before the cutover store it in their branding row — see brandingService.DEFAULT_LOGO_URLS.
│   ├── img/brand/                   # Polaris brand art, one file per (orientation, theme): `polaris-horiz-{dark,light}.png` (login card) + `polaris-vert-{dark,light}.png` (sidebar) + `polaris-symbol-{dark,light}.png` (the star alone — the accent overlay brandLogoService composites onto an operator's logo). "dark"/"light" name the BACKGROUND the file is for, not its ink: the dark-theme wordmark is light blue, the light-theme one near-black, so painting the wrong variant makes the logo vanish. The symbol pair splits the same way for a different reason — the dark variant's wedges are WHITE and the light variant's are NAVY, so on the wrong background half the mark disappears and the star reads as four disconnected arms. Chosen by public/js/brand-logo.js off `data-theme`. Downscaled from the source art (900×180 horiz / 600×512 vert / 512² symbol) — the originals are ~6000px and 120–400 KB each, which is a real cost on the pre-auth login page. **Also NORMALIZED across the pair, which the source exports were not:** the vertical light file's star was ~39% larger relative to its wordmark than the dark file's, with a 2px star/wordmark gap against the dark's 20px, so simply scaling each to a common width still rendered two visibly different logos. Both variants are now laid out to one geometry — star scaled to 371px high at y≈3, wordmark to 116px high at y=396, each centered — so swapping them on a theme flip moves nothing. Re-exported art must be re-normalized the same way (measure the alpha bounding box of each band, don't trust the export's packing); when doing it by compositing bands out of one source image, clip each band's layer to its OWN target rect — a clip with slack lets the other band show through at the wrong scale, which renders a small ghost wordmark above the real one.
│   ├── map.html                     # Device Map page (Leaflet basemap + Cytoscape topology modal)
│   ├── mobile.html                  # Phone-targeted SPA (Material 3). Single document, hash-routed, reuses /api/v1 + session auth from the desktop app. Phone-class user-agents hitting `/` or `/index.html` are auto-redirected here by the UA middleware in `src/app.ts`; the `?desktop=1` query param is the escape hatch the More tab's "Desktop view" link uses to bypass the redirect.
│   ├── alert-ack.html               # Acknowledge page for ONE alert (`?id=<notificationId>`) — where an alert email's / web push's Acknowledge button lands. A single centred card on the login page's shell (no sidebar, no nav), listed in app.ts's `protectedPages` so an unauthenticated reader signs in first and comes back via the `polaris_next` cookie. There is no token in the URL and no credential of any kind: identity is the reader's own session. Business rule 25.
│   ├── api.html                     # Developer API documentation, served at GET /api (and /api/) by src/app.ts. UNAUTHENTICATED — the only gate is the apiDocsConfig source-IP scope (loopback/rfc1918/custom; the app.ts middleware also intercepts /api.html so express.static can't serve the file around the gate). All endpoint content lives INLINE in this file on purpose: the HTML is the gated artifact, while js/api-docs.js stays generic. Standalone shell per the alert-ack canon (theme-init.js first, robots noindex, theme tokens, no sidebar) widened to a sticky-TOC + content layout. Covers the curated external surface only (auth/bearer model, errors, quarantine SIEM flow, assets, dashboard feeds, search, IPAM, events) — never the internal UI endpoints.
│   ├── dash.html                    # Dash wallboard — the UNAUTHENTICATED read-only duplicate of index.html's dashboard, served at /dash by the dash process (src/dash/dashServer.ts). Same widget canvas/picker markup + full widget script list (keep in lockstep with index.html — both files carry a comment); loads js/dash-mode.js FIRST (page flags: POLARIS_DASH_LOCAL, __polarisApiBase=/dash/api/v1, __polarisOn401 no-op) and js/dash-boot.js INSTEAD of app.js (slim boot: theme, synthetic /auth/me identity globals, permAtLeast, showToast/timeAgo copies, branding incl. title + favicon swap to branding.logoUrl, mirroring app.js applyBranding). No sidebar, no asset slide-over chain (table-sf/integrations/assets/jspdf/html-to-image dropped — widget click-throughs no-op via the POLARIS_DASH_LOCAL guard in widgets/index.js openAssetDetail). Layout persists per-browser in localStorage `polaris-dash-layout` (dashboard.js branches on POLARIS_DASH_LOCAL instead of /me/dashboard). Widgets the readonly role can't read (Discovery Activity / Conflict Queue / Capacity Health) hide via getAllowed().
│   ├── css/
│   │   ├── styles.css               # The whole desktop app. TWO token bases, neither a theme of its own: `:root` (dark, refined by `nightfall`) and the daylight base `:is([data-theme="morning"],[data-theme="noon"])`, which undoes the component CSS's light-on-dark assumptions ONCE for both — write any new daylight override with `:is(...)`, never a comma split, or `[data-theme="x"] .badge-y` loses its descendant on the second selector. Three theme blocks follow (`morning` / `noon` / `nightfall`); `--color-primary` is an alias of `--color-accent` in every block, since spinners / the sidebar update badge / the search-select focus ring reference it by that name. Never a raw hex in a rule that paints ON a surface — a literal is wrong in at least two of the three themes; hexes on a COLORED fill (badge tints, the primary button, avatars, map markers) are the exception.
│   │   ├── map.css                  # Device Map styles (marker icons, topology modal grid)
│   │   ├── mobile.css               # Material 3 component library for mobile.html. Defines both dark (`:root`) and daylight (`:is([data-theme="morning"],[data-theme="noon"])`) MD3 token blocks — ONE light palette for both daylight themes, since the desktop's morning/noon split is a warmth difference this token set has no room for and the More tab's control stays a two-way Dark/Light. Matching on the FAMILY is what keeps the shared `polaris-theme` localStorage key coherent across the two apps: `PolarisTheme.get()` answers a family, `PolarisTheme.set()` writes a real theme id (`morning` / `nightfall`) the desktop also understands — every component rule reads `var(--md-...)` so a theme flip swaps surfaces, primaries, and outlines without per-component branching. Status colors (monitor health pills, topology node hues defined in topology-render.js) deliberately stay literal — they need the same hue on both backgrounds for at-a-glance recognition. The GPS pin stroke flips per theme via `--user-pin-stroke` (near-white on dark, near-black on light) so the stick figure stays legible against either basemap. Also carries: `.user-pin` styles + walking keyframes for the Map tab's GPS pin (CSS keyframes alternate left/right limb rotations + a body-bob; honors `prefers-reduced-motion`); `.topo-screen` / `.topo-bar` / `.topo-search` / `.topo-graph` / `.topo-section` styles for the mobile topology surface; `.app[data-tab="__fullbleed"]` rule that hides the topbar slot + bottom navbar so the topology graph owns the whole viewport; landscape-orientation lockout (`@media (orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 480px)`) that replaces the UI with a "Rotate to portrait" overlay — universal fallback for iOS Safari which silently rejects `screen.orientation.lock()` outside an installed PWA. Also carries the `.app.kb-open` rules the auth screens' keyboard fit toggles — the `justify-content: flex-start` flip there is load-bearing, since overflow above a centered flex item is unreachable.
│   │   └── vendor/leaflet/          # Leaflet + markercluster + leaflet-draw 1.0.4 CSS + marker PNGs + draw spritesheet (bundled; CSP blocks external CDN)
│   └── js/
│       ├── api.js                   # HTTP client with auth/error handling. 401 redirect goes to /login.html unless `window.__polarisOn401` is set (mobile app sets this to route back to its in-app login).
│       ├── app.js                   # Navigation, layout, theme switching. `NAV_ITEMS` is the sidebar; each entry carries `perm: [key, level]` (or `anyPerm: [[key, level], …]` = visible if ANY holds, for a multi-key page like IPAM) and `renderNav` filters on it. Every entry whose page can 403 needs one — an ungated entry advertises a page whose first list fetch is the only thing telling the operator they can't be there. Keep each in lockstep with `pageRequiredPermission` in src/app.ts (nav gate = don't advertise it; page gate = don't let a typed URL land on it). Dashboard is deliberately ungated (its routes carry no gate; it's the post-login landing page)
│       ├── api-docs.js              # Behavior for api.html, GENERIC ONLY (served ungated by express.static like every /js asset, so it may not enumerate endpoints or carry doc text — the content stays in the gated HTML): fills `.js-base-url` from window.location.origin + "/api/v1" (the origin the reader browsed IS their base; the page deliberately loads no api.js), copy buttons on the curl blocks, IntersectionObserver TOC scrollspy.
│       ├── alert-ack.js             # Drives alert-ack.html: `GET /alerts/:id` — render the card — note + `POST /alerts/acknowledge` (with `source` = `ack_page`, or `web_push_action` when the URL carries `src=push`). It NEVER decides who may acknowledge (the route does; the page reports the refusal) and treats a **400 as form validation** (the note policy), re-rendering the form with the reason. Sets `window.__polarisOn401` so a session that expires while the page is open re-stamps `polaris_next` before bouncing to login, instead of losing the alert. States: form / acknowledged (yours or someone else's, with the note shown back) / already cleared / role-can't / not-here (404 AND 403 read the same to the reader) / retry.
│       ├── alert-ack-view.js        # `window.PolarisAlertAckView` — the PRESENTATION of one alert about to be acknowledged: `headerHtml` (test flag + the alert's sentence + the facts table), `factsHtml`, `noteFieldHtml(id, required)`, `errorHtml`, `accentValue(severity)` (severity → a `--color-sev-*` var reference, never a literal), `appLink`, `esc`, `fmtTime`. Lifted verbatim out of alert-ack.js when the in-app modal needed the same card — two surfaces render it now (the standalone page and alert-ack-modal.js) and they must not drift. Presentation only: it fetches nothing, decides nothing about who may acknowledge, POSTs nothing. Its classes (`.ack-facts`, `.ack-message`, `.ack-note-input`, …) moved to styles.css for the same reason; alert-ack.html keeps only its own shell rules.
│       ├── alert-ack-modal.js       # `window.PolarisAlertAckModal.open(alertId, {onAcknowledged, onOpenDevice})` — the in-app acknowledge dialog, the /alert-ack.html card in a modal. Opened from the Down Assets widget's row menu. Mirrors the page state for state (form / acknowledged / already cleared / role-can't / not-here / retry) off the same shared markup, and keeps the page's three properties: it never decides who may acknowledge (a 403 is a STATE, not a toast), the note policy is the server's (a 400 re-renders the form with the reason), and it re-reads after the write so the acknowledger's name is the honest one. It also re-reads BEFORE the form — the row that opened it is up to 30s stale plus the feed's 10s cache. Sends no `source`: that closed set names the emailed page and the push action only.
│       ├── brand-logo.js            # `window.PolarisBrandLogo` — which mark a surface paints, in one place, because the desktop login, the mobile login and the sidebar all have to agree. `resolve(branding, "login"|"sidebar")` → `{src, custom, showName, showSubtitle}`: the shipped art picked per `data-theme` (horizontal for the login card, vertical for the sidebar), an operator's logo when `customLogo` and that surface's `logoOnLogin`/`logoOnSidebar` flag is on (pointing at the server-composited `logo-accent.png` when `logoAccent`), and `showName` FALSE for the Polaris art — the wordmark is in the picture, so a caption would repeat it. `applyTo(img, …, {bust})` also tags the element `.brand-mark` so CSS can size fixed-aspect art differently from an arbitrary upload; `bust` is how the Customization tab forces a re-fetch of an accent URL whose bytes changed but whose path didn't. `onThemeChange` observes the `data-theme` attribute rather than hooking each surface's toggle, and the module registers the `prefers-color-scheme` listener that keeps a user who has never picked a theme tracking their OS. Loaded before app.js on every page, plus login.html and mobile.html.
│       ├── dashboard.js              # Dashboard orchestrator (column layout v2). Owns `state.layout = {version:2, columns:[{id,width,widgets:[{id,type,height,config}]}]}` + `state.editing`, loads from `GET /me/dashboard`, migrates a legacy v1 (`{widgets:[{col,row,...}]}`) layout to columns on load (`migrateV1ToV2`: bucket by col-start, order by row), and renders each column as a CSS-grid item (`grid-column: span width`) holding a flex stack. Edit mode (`enterEditMode`/`exitEditMode`) toggles `.is-editing` + re-renders so drag handles / controls / the "+ New block" target appear. Drag (picker card OR existing widget) computes a `{columnIndex, insertionIndex}` or `{newColumn}` target via `dropTargetFromCursor` (column + card-midpoint geometry), moves a single green "+" `.dashboard-drop-placeholder` into the target stack, and lifts the source with `.lifted`.
```
