│       ├── assets-tabs.js          # Per-user VIEW TABS for the assets table (the strip above the bulk bar). Each tab holds its own filter+sort state; the set persists per user via GET/PUT /me/table-tabs?scope=assets. Published as `window.PolarisAssetTabs` and loaded BEFORE assets.js, whose DOMContentLoaded awaits `init({hashSeeded})` so the active tab is applied before the FIRST fetch (one page load, not one per state source) — a deep-link hash filter wins for that load and is folded into the active tab (pre-tabs behavior). `syncFromTable()` is called from assets.js's `assetsApplyFilterState` on every filter/sort change and mirrors it into the active tab (debounced ~800ms PUT, flushed on beforeunload); `_applying` guards re-entrancy so applying a tab can't dirty the tab just left. First visit seeds ONE "All assets" tab from the live (localStorage-restored) state and deliberately writes nothing until the operator uses tabs. Click switches, double-click/F2 renames inline (Enter commits, Escape reverts), ✕ closes (never the last one; confirms only when the tab holds unsaved hand-built filters), + adds. `openInNewTab(preset)` / `noteFilterLoaded(preset)` are the two entry points assets-filters.js calls; a tab remembers the preset it came from as a reference only — editing it never writes back to a preset that may be someone else's. **Base ("default") filter:** `setDefaultFilter(preset)` pins one preset as the active tab's base — the view that tab resets to, so the operator can narrow further inside a saved filter and get back in one click — and APPLIES it (a click that visibly changed nothing on a tab already carrying hand filters would leave the operator unsure it took); `clearDefaultFilter()` unpins without touching the view on screen; `resetToDefault()` re-applies it; `activeDefault()` is what assets.js reads to label the page-controls button "Reset Filter" instead of "Clear Filters" (assets-tabs.js calls `window._renderAssetsPageControls()` after a base change that leaves the query alone, since that row is otherwise only repainted after a fetch); `refreshDefaultsFromPresets(list)` re-syncs each tab's snapshot from a fresh preset list (an edited preset reaches the tabs based on it; a preset that has GONE leaves the snapshot alone, so the tab keeps a base it can still reset to). The base marker is `.table-tab-base` (★) and does not replace the filters dot — "has filters" and "has somewhere to go back to" are two facts. **Per-tab favorites:** `init` registers a `favorites.js` PROVIDER for the `"assets"` entity (`registerFavoritesProvider`), so every existing star call site — `starCellHTML` in the row renderer, `isFavorite`, and the `getFavorites` read that builds `?favoriteIds=` — resolves to the ACTIVE tab's `favoriteIds` with no change on the assets.js side; switching tabs re-fetches, so the stars repaint themselves. The provider caps at 500 (`MAX_TAB_FAVORITES`) and toasts rather than letting the server drop the tail, names the tab in the star's tooltip (`titleFor` — the only surface that explains the scoping at the moment of the click), and counts favorites in the tab tooltip. A tab whose `favoriteIds` is null predates the feature and is seeded ONCE from this browser's legacy per-user localStorage set (every such tab, since that set is exactly what each tab used to show) and the adoption is written, so another browser can never re-seed a curated tab; a first visit still writes nothing. Closing a tab confirms when it holds favorites, since they live only there. DOM-tested in tests/unit/assetsTabsDom.test.ts (which eval's the real favorites.js, the provider seam being the point).
│       ├── assets.js
│       ├── assets-filters.js        # Saved filter presets (Assets header → "Filters ▾"). Renders the dropdown from GET /saved-filters?scope=assets on every open — "Save current filters…" + "Clear active filters", then My filters / Shared filters sections (each row loads on click, carries a Public badge + the publisher's name for others' presets, and a ✕ shown only to the owner or an `assets:fullwrite` caller). Load = `_assetsSF.applyState(preset.state)` + `assetsApplyFilterState()` (assets.js). The save modal collects a name (datalist of your own presets; a case-insensitive clash confirms an overwrite, which the server performs as an update) + a Private/Public radio (Public disabled without `assets:write`, with the reason inline) and shows a plain-English preview of exactly what's being stored. Presets hold the QUERY only — column widths/visibility stay per-browser in localStorage. Each row also carries a **★** (`data-sfl-default`) that pins/unpins that preset as the ACTIVE VIEW TAB's base filter (see assets-tabs.js) — the base lives on the tab, not on the preset, so this file only offers the verb; while a base is set the menu head grows "Reset to base filter «name»" + "Remove base filter from this tab" and renames Clear to "Clear all filters" (clearing is not unpinning). Every list fetch hands the fresh presets to `refreshDefaultsFromPresets`. All the tab-strip affordances are feature-tested on `window.PolarisAssetTabs` rather than assumed, so a browser holding a cached older assets-tabs.js keeps a working menu. Loaded by assets.html after assets.js. DOM-tested in tests/unit/assetsFiltersDom.test.ts.
│       ├── assets-maintenance.js    # Maintenance modal (Assets toolbar → Maintenance, gated maintenanceManagement): three tabs — Create Schedule (name + criteria builder with hostname/IP-CIDR/model/manufacturer/os/assetType/integration/behind-FortiGate rules — Integration renders a select of configured integrations, Behind FortiGate a text input with a firewall-hostname datalist, debounced live device-list preview via POST /maintenance-schedules/preview, one-time vs recurring editor with weekday/day-of-month/month+day/time-range/active-bounds controls) and Schedules (list with human-readable maintScheduleSummary, enabled toggle, edit-in-place via the Create tab, delete) and Calendar (month grid fed by GET /maintenance-schedules/occurrences — server-expanded, server-local wall-clock strings that are NEVER parsed as instants here; day bucketing is string arithmetic in _maintOccurrenceDays, half-open so an all-day window claims one cell and a 22:00→02:00 window claims two. Clicking a day cell prefills a one-time window on that date and jumps to the Create tab (today → now, any other day → 20:00, both +2h); clicking a chip loads that schedule into the editor. Ad-hoc chips are styled apart from planned ones and disabled schedules render struck through. Lazily rendered on first tab activation, repainted by _maintCalRefresh after every write). Editor lookups (asset types / integrations / firewall datalist) load in the background (_maintLoadEditorLookups — never awaited before listener binding, so Save is live the moment the modal paints). Exposes window.maintCreateAdhoc(assetId, hostname, endLocalIso, opts?{suppressChildren}) (sends schedule.startNow so the server stamps the start) for the status-pill / edit-modal ad-hoc one-shot flows (each of which carries a "Mark dependent devices as down" checkbox, default checked, mirrored in the builder + a Dependents list column) (+ maintScheduleSummary / maintLocalIso / maintValidateAdhocEnd helpers — the last is the shared guard both ad-hoc entry points run their datetime-local value through: an untouched time half reads as "", which used to be dropped silently, and "in the past" is judged against the SERVER's clock, below). **Server-clock helpers (`maintServerNow` / `maintLoadServerClock` / `maintServerClockLabel`, all exported on `window`):** every picker in this file is filled in in SERVER-local wall clock, because that is how the value is read back (the shapes carry no offset). `_maintLoadServerClock` reads `GET /maintenance-schedules/server-time` ONCE per page and caches the browser↔server difference as a single minute-rounded skew — timezone offset and plain clock drift folded together, which is all any caller needs, rounded because the pickers are minute-granular and the round trip adds sub-second noise. `maintServerNow()` returns a Date whose BROWSER-local digits equal the server's wall clock, so `_maintLocalIso(maintServerNow())` is exactly what a `datetime-local` must carry; it falls back to the browser clock while the skew is unknown (unread or read failed), which is the pre-fix behaviour and right whenever the two clocks agree. `_maintApplyServerClock` paints the live server time into the When hint (`#maint-tz-hint`) and re-prefills the one-shot fields when the async read lands — gated on `_maintOneshotTouched`, set by any keystroke in either field and by the calendar day-click and edit-load paths, so a late read can never overwrite a time the operator picked. The status-pill popover paints synchronously, so `assets.js` warms the same cache at `DOMContentLoaded`. Loaded after assets.js on EVERY page that carries the asset edit modal (assets/index/map/appmap/automations) — the modal's Maintenance tab needs maintCreateAdhoc, and gating that control on the file's presence made it read as "you don't have permission" wherever the file was missing. The toolbar button that opens the Maintenance modal itself is still wired on assets.html only. `openMaintenanceModal(opts?)` takes `opts.assetIds` — the Assets-page bulk-bar entry (select rows → Maintenance, `assets-bulk-maint-btn`, gated `data-maintenance-mgmt` like the toolbar button): the ids are pinned into `_maintEditingAssetIds`, the SAME explicit-assetIds channel an edited schedule's stored pins ride, so the preview, the explicit-includes line and the save body need no selection-specific path. Order is load-bearing — the prefill runs AFTER `_maintWireEditor()` (which resets the editor's fields) and paints the explicit line itself, since `_maintEditorHTML()` renders before the pins are in the DOM. A name is prefilled so the form is savable, but nothing is created until Save (unlike `maintCreateAdhoc`); `assets.js`'s `bulkMaintenanceSelectedAssets` refuses a selection past `MAINT_ASSET_IDS_MAX` (500, mirroring the route's `assetIds` cap) with the count.
│       ├── assets-ipcontext.js     # IP cross-reference panel under the **Add Asset** form's IP Address field (`window.PolarisIpContext` — `panelHTML(id)` renders the container, `mount({inputId, panelId, readForm, applyValues})` wires it). A manually added asset has no discovery behind it, so the containing network, the lease/reservation on the address and the gate it sits behind are facts the form would otherwise never surface; one debounced (400 ms) `GET /assets/ip-context` per address answers all of them. Requests are sequence-numbered so a slow answer to an older value never paints over a newer one, and a value that isn't address-shaped yet short-circuits before the network. `buildFindings` turns the payload into the rendered lines — the already-in-inventory hit FIRST and warn-coloured when the address is that asset's PRIMARY IP (that is a duplicate about to be created), the reservation warn-coloured and phrased from `sourceType` + `dhcpBinding` together ("In use by a managed FortiAP … the gate leases it dynamically"), the firewall line naming WHY that gate is believed (its ARP table resolved the address / it serves DHCP for the network / a device was sighted behind it), and a sighting suppressed when it names the gate the firewall line already did. A section the caller's role could not read renders "Not shown", never "none found". `applicableSuggestions` filters the server's advisory prefill to fields the operator has left BLANK — it assists a form it does not own — and treats latitude/longitude as one indivisible pair, because `getAssetFormData` refuses a half-filled one. Pure halves exposed for tests/unit/ipContextDom.test.ts
│       ├── assets-masspin.js       # **Mass Pinning** section of the Assets Settings modal (`window.PolarisMassPin` — `sectionHTML()` renders the `<h4>` + shell, `init()` mounts it): bulk pin/unpin of interfaces (incl. FortiGate IPsec tunnels) and storage mounts across a condition-filtered device set. Mounts the SHARED `PolarisConditionBuilder` over `GET /assets/pin-filter-schema` (the automations vocabulary, assets:read-gated), 400ms-debounced matched count via `pin-inventory` `mode:"count"`, facet radios, an explicit **Load matching devices** button (heavy inventory never rides keystrokes), then the aggregated checklist: one row per ifName/mountPath with a TRI-STATE checkbox, a `[ifType]`/`[IPsec]` tag, a "pinned on X / N devices" line, and an expand chevron whose per-device sublist renders **lazily on first expand** (1000 assets × dozens of names would otherwise be tens of thousands of hidden DOM nodes). Two delegated listeners cover every checkbox and chevron. Staged edits live in ONE `Map` of **diffs vs the server state** — staging a value back to what the server holds DELETES the key, so `summarize()` counts real changes and a round-trip of clicks leaves nothing staged. Tri-state click semantics are explicit because an indeterminate checkbox reports `checked === false`: not-all-pinned → pin on ALL devices of the row, fully-checked → unpin on ALL (the house "one more click takes all of them" answer). Facet switch / re-Load with staged edits prompts to discard (the row set changes underneath them). Apply confirms, POSTs `mass-pins` once, toasts the SERVER's counts (plus a warning toast naming the skip count), then re-Loads against the scope of the last load — not whatever the builder holds now — so the checklist shows post-apply server truth for the set just edited. The pure helpers (`stageKey`/`rowState`/`cycleRow`/`toggleDevice`/`buildApplyPayload`/`summarize`) are exposed for `tests/unit/massPinDom.test.ts`. Reads `#mp-all-assets`.checked as a PROPERTY (the happy-dom `:checked` trap).
│       ├── assets-discovery.js     # The network **Discovery** wizard, behind the Assets page's "+ Add Asset(s)" menu (`window.PolarisAssetDiscovery` — `open(existing?, {import?})`, `openList()`, plus the pure `groupKeyForHit` / `listRowItems` / `emptyDraft` for the happy-dom suite). Seven steps: Name → Targets → Methods → Run → Results → Monitoring → Summary, in the `appmap-rules-wizard.js` idiom (one closure-scoped draft, HTML/Wire/Collect/Validate per step behind COLLECT/VALIDATE tables, a footer synced per step, free navigation to visited steps, shared `.stepper` CSS with the stepper a DIRECT first child of `.modal-body`); ids are `nd-` prefixed. Three things differ from the other two wizards. (1) **Steps 4–5 are a RUN, not authoring** — step 4 SAVES the Discovery then POSTs a run and polls it (self-rescheduling `setTimeout`, a try cap, per-tick errors swallowed — the `runScriptTest` shape), and re-entering it REATTACHES to the newest run rather than losing a scan the operator closed the modal on (the agent-build.js progress-strip precedent). Progress is a text ratio plus a thin determinate bar, affordable here because the denominator is known up front unlike integration discovery. (2) **Step 6 reuses the integrations page's auto-monitor builders** (`_autoMonitorInterfacesHTML` / `_readAutoMonitorInterfaces` / `_autoMonitorStorageHTML` / `_readAutoMonitorStorage` — module-level functions in integrations.js and therefore globals; assets.html already loads it). Deliberate: the selection vocabulary is resolved server-side by ONE pair of pure resolvers, and a second render of it here is how the two surfaces would come to disagree about what a stored selection means. What this file supplies instead of that page's wire function is the DATA — the integrations version fills its checklists from `/integrations/:id/interface-aggregate` (assets that already exist and have been polled), while at scan time neither is true, so names and types come from the inventory the SCAN collected. The row contract is a documented selector pair (`input[data-name-checkbox="1"][data-prefix=…]`, `input[data-stor-name-checkbox="1"][data-prefix=…]`), and selections are grouped by POLLING METHOD because what can be pinned depends on what answered. (Moving those builders into a shared module is the better end state; it is a ~500-line move inside an 8k-line shared file and is deliberately not bundled with a feature commit.) (3) **Every control is gated by the key its own route checks** — a read-level caller gets a read-only walkthrough with no Save and no Run, and a caller who may scan but not create sees Export/Save but no "Add N assets", with a line saying to hand the run to someone who can (the results are saved with it). Tests: tests/unit/assetsDiscoveryDom.test.ts
│       ├── discovery-portability.js # One Discovery as a `.discovery.json` file (`window.PolarisDiscoveryPortability`). Export strips, import reads in the BROWSER (`await file.text()`, no upload route) and hands the wizard a draft that saves through the ordinary `POST /network-scans`, so the server's schema plus `validateScanInput` stay the authority. **`dependencies` first**, because that is what a human opening the file reads: **credential IDS never leave the install** — the only install-specific ids a Discovery carries, and a pointer into a secret store in a file operators email and commit — so they are recorded by NAME and re-picked on step 3. The row's identity and any run state (`runId`/`hits`/`selected`) are stripped too; carrying results into another install would offer devices that are not on its network. Two traps it exists to hold: an import **re-strips on the way IN**, so "never carries a foreign id" is a property of the code rather than a promise about the file (without it the wizard's first save would PUT against an unrelated row); and a method whose credentials were stripped is kept with an **EMPTY list, never dropped** — `validateScanInput` then refuses it, which is the error the importer should see, where silently demoting an SNMP scan to ICMP-only would look like it ran fine and found nothing. `autoMonitor` travels as-is (it names device facts, not install ids). Headline test: **every export is a valid import**. Tests: tests/unit/discoveryPortability.test.ts
│       ├── integrations.js          # Discovery progress, abort
│       ├── events.js                # Audit log viewer, syslog/SFTP settings
│       ├── users.js
│       ├── monitor-states.js      # The monitor state machine replayed over a probe-sample stream (`window.PolarisMonitorStates.replay/fromPayload`): one display state per sample — `up` / `warning` / `down` / `recovering` — plus the missed-poll count as it stood after that probe. The browser's SINGLE decider of which probe is amber and which is red, which answer is still blue and which is green, read by the asset System tab's Last-30-min strip (`_intermittencyStates` is now a one-line delegate), the desktop response-time chart (`_renderMonitorChart`) and the phone's (`loadMonitor` in mobile/asset-detail.js). Each of those three used to decide it privately, which is how a strip and the chart under it can describe one probe differently. `fromPayload` normalizes a monitor-history payload's `downDetection` block into the three answers that exist — covered / passive / UNKNOWN — since collapsing unknown into either invents a threshold or forbids a verdict. Mirrored server-side by `replayProbeStates` in services/probeOutageService.ts for the alert-email charts; the two are held together by a parity test rather than an import, nothing crossing that boundary. Loaded on assets/automations/integrations/index/map/appmap.html and mobile.html. Tests: tests/unit/assetIntermittencyBar.test.ts
│       ├── monitor-down-after.js  # The "how long until this device is called Down" arithmetic (`window.PolarisMonitorDownAfter.calc/human`, with the legacy `_polarisMonDownAfterCalc` alias): `interval × (count − 1) + ceil(timeout/1000)`, plus the note that spells the figure out. Its own module because the missed-poll COUNT now belongs to the down-detection automation (business rule 36) while the interval and timeout still come from the monitor-settings hierarchy — so the automations wizard, the asset detail surfaces and the settings cards all need one implementation, and the wizard's DOM tests eval only automations-wizard.js and could never have reached it inside integrations.js (7,500+ lines). Loaded before integrations.js on integrations.html / assets.html / automations.html. Tests: tests/unit/monitorDownAfterCalc.test.ts
│       ├── region-pills.js         # Region-tag pills (`window.PolarisRegionPills`): `load()` caches the `GET /map/regions` catalogue as name→hex, `colorFor(name)` / `rgbTriplet(hex)` / `pill(name, title?)` / `html(names, titleFor?)` render the translucent-fill + full-strength-border badge. Extracted from users.js so the Users page pickers and the Device Map’s "My regions" strip read ONE catalogue and paint one color per region — the same one-module-decides posture as brand-logo.js. The catalogue GET is gated `mapRegions:read`, so a load that 403s (a `deviceMap:read`-only viewer) is not an error state: every pill falls back to the neutral hue, which is already what a hand-typed tag outside the catalogue renders as. users.js keeps its own `_regionList` / `_regionByName` view of the same payload for the picker’s name list + orphan-tag test. Tests: tests/unit/regionPills.test.ts.
│       ├── totp-self.js           # Self-service two-factor (TOTP) UI (`window.PolarisTotpSelf`): `open(opts)` routes off `GET /auth/totp/status` — enroll when off, disable when on, refuse with the reason for any non-`local` authProvider (the enroll route rejects those, so a QR code that can never be confirmed is worse than saying why); `openEnroll` (QR + manual-secret fallback + 6-digit confirm → one-time backup-code modal), `openDisable` (current code or backup code), `showBackupCodes`. Extracted from users.js so the page-header account menu can reach the SAME flow on every page — /users.html is admin-gated, so a local user without `users` could never configure their own second factor even though every route it calls is self-service. `opts.onChange` lets the caller re-read state (the Users table reloads, the account menu re-labels its row).
│       ├── ip-panel.js              # The per-network IP slide-in: the address table, its per-row verbs, and the reserve / edit / auto-allocate modals. **Auto-Allocate is one modal with two modes** (`_openAutoAllocateModal`): "Single IP" is the original flow (the server picks the next free address at create time), "Multiple IPs" asks how many and whether the run must be CONTIGUOUS, previews the addresses through `POST /reservations/next-available/preview`, and renders a `.ipalloc-row` grid so each address gets its own hostname + MAC. The preview is debounced (300ms) and sequence-guarded so a later keystroke wins; hostnames and operator-typed MACs survive a count change because rows are keyed by POSITION. Submitting walks the rows one create at a time (`_submitMultipleAllocate`) with progress on the button, then opens a results modal with a per-row status and a CSV export — see the endpoint note for why it is not one batched request. `f-automac` auto-generates placeholder MACs, defaulting ON only where the network is push-eligible (elsewhere a placeholder MAC is a marker nobody asked for — business rule 26); a MAC the operator types is stamped `data-auto="0"` and is never overwritten or cleared by the toggle. **`vip` and `interface_ip` rows render read-only** with the purple `.ip-dot-device-config` dot and only "View Asset" — the address is owned by the device's config, and the server refuses the edit/release verbs too.
│       ├── map.js                   # Device Map: Leaflet markers, autocomplete search, Cytoscape topology modal. Nodes positioned by the shared `computeTopologyColumns` solver via a `preset` layout (dagre fallback when no FortiGate root); saved drag positions still restore in a layoutstop hook, and the connection-path overlay lays the path out left-to-right along the columns. **Single-click selects** a node, **double-click opens** its asset details. Edge hover shows a concise tooltip (both device names + interface ports + connection kind + per-side speed/status/errors, the last sourced from per-edge interface details the topology endpoint attaches). Each per-side interface line is **prefixed with its device name** (srcIf → source node, tgtIf → target node) so it's unambiguous which end a port lives on, and the endpoint resolves a single-member aggregate to its physical member before attaching detail (a serial-named FortiLink uplink trunk renders as e.g. `port52`). Topology modal toolbar carries a **Legend** button between Refresh and Reset Layout that toggles a draggable overlay built from `topologyLegendSpec()` (one row per node/edge/health pip); position + visibility persist per-user in `localStorage` under `polaris.topology.legend`. Defaults to bottom-right of the topology graph area; drag offsets stored as `{x, y}` relative to the graph container so resizing the browser between sessions never strands the panel off-screen. **Two screenshot affordances:** the header camera (`#topology-screenshot`) copies the **whole modal** — `cy.png()` map composited with the right-hand info panel rendered as text onto one canvas (`screenshotTopologyModal` / `_composeTopologyModalCanvas`); a floating camera at the top-right of the map area (`#topology-map-screenshot`, re-added on each `renderTopologyGraph` since the graph innerHTML is wiped on open) copies the **map only** via `cy.png()` (`screenshotTopology`). **Device-type visibility chips** (`#topology-type-toggles`, also re-added per render) float left of that camera: one show/hide chip per toggleable role present on the site (Switches / APs / Remote — the FortiGate root is not toggleable since it anchors the solver); hiding a type filters its nodes + touching edges out of the element set BEFORE `computeTopologyColumns` runs so the layout recomputes compactly, counts come from the unfiltered set so a hidden type's chip stays visible, and hidden roles persist per-user in `localStorage` under `polaris.topology.hiddenRoles`. A **Snap** chip in the same row (per-user `polaris.topology.snapToGrid`, default off) snaps drag releases to the solver's 130×95px grid and re-snaps all positions on enable. Drag layouts persist server-side per (site, view) in `TopologyLayout` for `deviceMap` writers (debounced PUT through `saveNodePositions` → `_queueServerLayoutSave`; the topology GET's `savedLayouts` embed wins over localStorage on load). **"My regions" strip** (`renderMyRegions` / `regionScopeSource`, toolbar `#map-my-regions`, ordered immediately left of "Edit regions"): the SIGNED-IN operator’s own effective region scope, read-only. It answers "which regions am I assigned to?" — which no other page told the operator themselves, the Users page showing it only to whoever can administer users — and each pill’s tooltip names WHERE the scope comes from (their account, their role, else an IdP group; app.js keeps the first two sets, so a tag in the effective union but in neither is group-derived). Deliberately NOT a map filter: the map already renders exactly the sites the viewer may read, so narrowing to "my" regions would hide sites they are responsible for. An empty effective scope means UNRESTRICTED, rendered as the words "all regions" rather than a bare label. Colors come from `PolarisRegionPills`.
│       ├── topology-render.js        # Shared Cytoscape element + stylesheet builders consumed by both desktop map.js and mobile topology-tab.js. Exposes `buildTopologyElements(data)`, `topologyStylesheet(theme, opts)`, `topologyLegendSpec()`, `computeTopologyColumns(elements)`, and `computeGroupedLayout(elements)` (quotient two-level layout for location-coded sites: per-group rank-compressed interiors + height-budgeted shelf packing of group boxes; returns the same {depth,lane} contract or null on untagged sites) so node colors per monitor health, edge styles for controller / interface-inferred / LLDP / mesh edges, ghost LLDP nodes, cross-site remote assets, and operator-uploaded icons stay consistent across surfaces. FG→switch controller edges are labeled with the real port pair (`srcIf.name ↔ tgtIf.name`, post trunk→member swap) when the edge is `verifiedUplink` AND the server attached interface details on both ends; otherwise they fall back to the logical `fortilink` label (dashed gray when unverified). **`computeTopologyColumns` is the deterministic layout solver** (replaces dagre auto-ranking): a node-weighted Dijkstra from the FortiGate (firewall 1 / switch 2 / AP 3 / endpoint 4) places **column anchors** on **even** columns by weighted depth (distinct depths compacted to contiguous columns), **leaves** on the **odd** column right of their parent, FortiLink-fallback switches (no interface/LLDP-verified path to the FortiGate) in **negative** columns (-2, their endpoints -3). An anchor is infra (FortiGate / switch / AP) that isn't a *terminal* AP — `isLeafAp` classifies a FortiAP hanging off a switch port with no wireless mesh/bridge children of its own as a **leaf** (placed in the parent switch's leaf column, NOT its own anchor column), so a FortiGate's switch chain stays in tight consecutive columns with each switch's APs hung directly off it instead of every AP's weighted depth fanning the switches across the canvas; mesh-root and bridged-switch-parent APs stay anchors. Rows come in **two passes**: (a) a **nearest-free-slot packing** pass over **anchors only** (a node's first anchor child in a different column continues the parent's row so chains stay flat; every other anchor scans downward from just below its parent's row for the first lane where its whole footprint fits — its own cell, the spine chain that will inherit its lane into later columns, and each chain member's planned leaf block one column right, that block starting one row below a member whose chain continues since the continuing spine edge occupies the member's own row — so rows pack tight near the spine and drift down only where subtrees congest, instead of every subtree pre-claiming a globally disjoint row band that pushed a left-column switch's later children below everything placed before them) and (b) a leaf pass that slides each parent's leaves as one **contiguous window** (grouped by parent, blocks ordered by parent row) starting at the parent's row, slid down as a whole to dodge occupied lanes or a drawn edge passing through the column (per-leaf dodging would fragment a block around another chain's spine running through it) — so each switch's AP stack lines up just below it, grouped together, never staircased rightward or split apart/interleaved by another switch's APs even when the `/topology` payload lists APs in interleaved order; orphans stack below everything. Mesh leaves (AP-as-station-on-AP, `isMesh`) and LLDP wireless-bridge switches (`bridgeEdges` → `isBridge`) stay anchors and route through their AP. Wired AP↔switch links (a managed AP's switch uplink or a bridged switch behind an AP) carry `isApLink` and render solid blue (#3b82f6) with a directional arrow — distinct from the dashed violet wireless mesh backhaul and the gray controller edges. `markPhysicalLoops` (exported; runs at the end of `buildTopologyElements`) stamps `inLoop: 1` on every wired edge lying on a cycle — Tarjan bridge-finding over the simple graph of interface/LLDP/AP-link/verified-uplink edges **plus MCLAG ICLs** (an ICL is a real cabled link, so when it closes a cycle — the usual MCLAG shape where both peers uplink to a common parent — it's part of a physical loop and gets haloed; an isolated ICL that's the only path between its peers is a bridge/cut-edge and stays unflagged; wireless and unverified controller edges are excluded; parallel cables between one pair collapse to one adjacency so a trunk pair isn't flagged) — and the stylesheet halos those edges yellow (`line-outline-color` #eab308) around their own line color, with a matching legend row. `fortinetNodeColor` renders dependency-suppressed ("Dep. Down") nodes gray. `topologyLegendSpec()` is the single source of truth for the desktop Legend overlay — node + monitor-health + edge (incl. Mesh/bridge) swatches with descriptions, mirroring the constants the stylesheet uses. Desktop opts in to the endpoint-overlay styles (synthetic round-rectangle endpoint node + .dimmed off-path styles) used by its connection-path overlay; mobile opts out.
│       ├── temp-unit.js            # Display-unit conversion for hardware-sensor readings (`window.PolarisTempUnit`). Samples are always stored/rolled-up/ALERTED-ON in Celsius; this converts at RENDER time only when the install set `branding.temperatureUnit="f"`, gated on each reading's own stored unit so fan RPM / voltage rails pass through. Read synchronously off the branding payload app.js caches in localStorage (so the sync string-building renderers can call it inline) and re-primed by applyBranding / PolarisAuthFlow.fetchBranding / dash-boot. Unit-tested in tests/unit/tempUnit.test.ts.
│       ├── chart-severity.js        # Pure severity-shading math for asset-detail charts (`window.PolarisChartSeverity`): `severityAt(tiers, v)` (most-severe MET tier, mirroring business rule 19), `gradientStops(tiers, minV, maxV)` → SVG linearGradient stops down the plot area (color changes only at a threshold; adjacent same-color slices merge; a fade zone capped at a third of each slice so 1°-apart tiers can't invert their stops; thresholds outside the domain CLAMP instead of widening the axis, so a range entirely above critical comes out entirely critical and an out-of-range tier contributes nothing), `visibleTiers` + `tierLabel` for the dashed reference lines. Loaded before assets.js on every page that can open the asset slide-over; consumed by `_severityChartLayer` in assets.js. Unit-tested in tests/unit/chartSeverity.test.ts. Also owns `downColorOf(severity)` + `DOWN_DEFAULT_COLOR` — the browser half of the down-state palette (business rule 36), flat hex rather than the theme tokens `colorOf` uses because the same values have to hold on all three themes AND on the alert email's white card. Mirror of `downSeverityHex` in src/utils/severityStyle.ts; read by the Last-30-min strip and the desktop response-time chart in assets.js and by the phone's in mobile/asset-detail.js, which is why mobile.html loads this file too.
│       ├── condition-builder.js    # The nested AND/OR device-condition tree (`window.PolarisConditionBuilder`), extracted from the automation wizard so the address book's contact device filter can render the SAME builder instead of a second flat one. `create({meta, valueOptions, onChange})` returns the render/wire/collect/validate set for a scope-shaped tree; `wireDnD(panel, rootSelector, onChange, maxDepth)` is the grip drag engine on its own, which the wizard's OTHER tree (the composite trigger builder, its own leaf rows, maxDepth 3) calls directly. Holds no catalog: every caller injects `meta` (the server's `scopeCondition` vocabulary — fields/ops/labels/maxDepth) and its own `valueOptions(field)` suggestions, which is what lets one module serve two different value sources. DOM order IS the tree, so a drag needs no model bookkeeping and `collect()` just walks it; `validate()` is shared so the same empty-group / empty-value / non-CIDR subnet is refused on both surfaces. Loaded BEFORE automations-wizard.js on all five pages that carry the wizard (appmap / assets / automations / index / map) — the wizard reads it while assembling the modal body, so a missing or late script is the silent "wizard won't open" failure. **A new server-side condition FIELD appears in all three builders with no client change — its value PICKER does not.** The field row is rendered from `meta.fields`, but `valueOptions(field)` switches on the field's `optionsFrom` in each caller (`scValueOptions` in automations-wizard.js, `valueOptionsFor` in automations-address-book.js, `valueOptions` in assets-masspin.js), and each ends in `default: return []` — so a new `optionsFrom` key with no case silently degrades that surface to free text instead of erroring. Add the case in all three (`interfaceNames` was the last one).
│       ├── automations-portability.js # Export / import ONE automation as a portable JSON file, plus the "view code" editor (`window.PolarisAutomationPortability`). Two deliberately different serializations: `stripForExport(body, catalogs)` removes every install-specific reference (delivery-channel / user / role / script ids, api_call actions and their unmasked headers, escalation chains, emailComposition, `scope.assetIds`/`integrationIds`, `assetId` condition leaves, `dimensionFilter.stateProbeId`/`widgetId`) and records each one as a NAMED **dependency** instead, so the file is portable and carries no secrets; `forCodeView(body)` keeps everything (ids included) because an edit there must round-trip losslessly. `buildExportFile` puts `dependencies` BEFORE `rule` — the nested schemas are `.strict()`, so a hint cannot ride next to the thing it describes, and a top-level block is also where a human opening the file looks. Three invariants the module exists to hold, each pinned by a test: the top-level `actions` list is emitted EXPLICITLY as `[{type:"event"}]` and never omitted (the server re-injects the audit Event only for `undefined`, which the wizard draft never produces — omitting saves a rule that writes a Notification row but logs nothing); an empty `scope` is never emitted (`{}` means MATCH NOTHING to `scopeWhere` while `step2Html` renders it as "All assets" checked, so a scope that strips to nothing becomes an empty CONDITION TREE, which `validateStep2` refuses); and a blanked `stateProbeId`/`widgetId` is reported back (both are optional and the engine applies them only when present, so blanking WIDENS the trigger to every probe on the device — the wizard's `tgValidateLeaf` now refuses to save one). `parseImportFile(text, filename, triggerTypes)` is the import gate — size cap, `JSON.parse`, `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` rejection, depth cap, envelope-version check, unknown-trigger-type refusal — and RE-STRIPS on the way in, so "an import never carries a foreign id" is a property of the code rather than a promise about the file. `checkDependencies` answers present / missing / can't-tell against the catalogs the wizard already holds (`present: null` for a kind with no catalogue, never a false "missing"). The code editor's footer carries both serializations: **Copy** hands over exactly what is on screen (ids, api_call headers) while **Export** runs the textarea's CURRENT contents through `buildExportFile`, so an unsaved edit can leave as a portable file and an export taken from the editor can never carry delivery wiring into a ticket. Both callers pass an `onExport` callback (the button is absent without one) and share it with their own Export entry point, so there is one export path and one dependency-count toast per surface; an unparseable edit refuses to export rather than writing a file off the last good body. `diffForConfirm` backs the code editor's confirm: PUT is a full replace, so deleting a key REMOVES that setting, and `enabled`/`severity`/`reset` fall back to schema defaults rather than their current values. Loaded after automations-wizard.js on all five pages that carry the wizard.
│       ├── automations-address-book.js # The address book (`window.PolarisAddressBook`): named email addresses alerts can route to, each optionally owning a set of devices. TWO surfaces, ONE renderer — the **Automations → Address Book tab** (`renderTab`) and the **recipient picker** the automation wizard's To/Cc/Bcc fields open (`openPicker({field})`) both paint through `abTable(cols, entries, hint)` over the shared `AB_CELLS` name/email/description/source cells, and differ only in COLUMNS: the tab adds Devices / Added by / Edit+Delete, the picker a selection checkbox and one Edit. Both show the same two panes — **People** (searched: contacts ∪ Polaris accounts ∪ the opted-in directory via `GET /contacts/search?directory=1`, 250 ms debounce) and **Tags** (browsed; map regions from `options.regions` plus the tag registry from `options.tagCatalog`, both riding the `GET /contacts/filter-schema` payload, so no second endpoint and no extra permission — built by the shared `tagRoutingEntries(schema)`, every row named `<name> Users` because what is being picked is the PEOPLE, and the two kept apart by `source` because a region matches `User.regionTags` only while a tag matches the flattened scope) — the picker adding the fire-time dynamic entries (Asset's Responsible Contacts, Asset's Region Users, Asset's L\<n\> Region Users) and the Add-to-To/Cc/Bcc footer, which mean nothing outside a Notify action. That dynamic catalogue is exported as `PolarisAddressBook.dynamicEntries(maxLevel)` because the wizard's recipient TYPEAHEAD offers the same entries — typing them was impossible until 2026-08, so they read as picker-only. **Loaded on every page the wizard is** (assets / index / map / appmap / automations), not just automations.html: the wizard's own Address book button calls into this module, and on the four pages it was missing that button threw. The tab's contacts come from `GET /contacts` rather than out of the search payload: a search entry carries neither `createdBy` nor the device filter (the two extra columns + the per-row ownership check behind Edit/Delete), and `searchAddressBook` caps at 50 deduped hits ordered users-first, so past 50 accounts the contacts would fall off the end of the very page that manages them; a hit whose address a contact already holds is dropped, so one mailbox is one row. Its shell is built once and only the panes reload (rebuilding would blur the search box mid-keystroke; the term survives Refresh + a save), and a table of nothing but user accounts still says "no contacts yet". The contact editor (`openEditor`) renders the device filter with the SHARED `PolarisConditionBuilder` over the wider `DEVICE_FILTER` vocabulary. Both dialogs build their OWN standalone overlay via app.js's `buildOverlay` (picker 1300, editor 1320) — never `openModal`, which reuses one shared `#modal-overlay` and would destroy the wizard's form DOM underneath.
│       ├── table-sf.js              # Shared list-table plumbing. `TableSF` = per-column sort + inline filter (text / multi-select / date-range / is-empty operators) driven by `data-sf-*` header attributes. `setupColumnLayout(tableEl, opts)` = divider-style drag-to-resize widths + the hover-gear column chooser, which also **drag-reorders** columns (`.sf-col-grip` per chooser row; required columns are anchors that hold their authored index). Reordering physically moves the `<th>` / `<col>` / body cells — CSS can't permute table columns — so `displayIds()` is the single source for every position-derived behaviour (nth-child hide rules, auto-fill column, resize neighbor) and a lazily-installed `MutationObserver`. `fitColumnsToContainer` keeps the visible columns summing to the container width by spreading any leftover across the resizable columns in proportion to their base widths (utility + `data-col-no-resize` columns keep their declared width and never stretch); a resize drag commits that stretch first so it tracks the pointer 1:1. `MIN_COL_W` = **5px** is the floor under every width it writes (drag clamp, fit pass, `setPrefs`) — a column can be parked at a sliver but never at 0px, and a column under `NARROW_COL_W` (36px) additionally gets `padding: 1px` + `overflow: hidden` from the generated per-table stylesheet, since a cell's border box can't render narrower than its own `1rem` padding on the table's `<tbody>` re-applies the order after each page render, no per-page change needed. `applyTableLayout(tableEl, typeKey)` wraps it for re-rendered tables (persists `{widths, hidden, shown, order}` under `polaris-table-layout-<typeKey>-<username>`); list pages thread the same blob through their own `polaris-prefs-<page>-<username>` prefs. Also hosts the shared `debounce` + `window.PolarisPrefs` load/save helpers.
│       ├── mobile/                  # Mobile SPA bundle (loaded by mobile.html). router.js (hash routing), auth.js (login + TOTP screens — also owns the on-screen-keyboard fit: while `window.visualViewport` reports a rect meaningfully shorter than the layout viewport, `.app` is pinned to it via `--vv-height`/`--vv-offset-top` and the login shell top-aligns so the password field and Sign in button clear the keyboard. iOS never shrinks the layout viewport, and the shell offers no way out on its own — body is `overflow:hidden` and `.login-shell` is exactly `min-height:100%`, so `.app-body` has nothing to scroll. Android, which does shrink it, is left to its native behavior. Same approach as the desktop `login.js`; see UI-CANON.md → On-screen keyboard fit), map-tab.js (Device Map tab — lazy-loads Leaflet/markercluster, plots health-coded firewall pins, opens a bottom sheet on tap; backs both #map and #site/<id>; site sheet's "View topology" button hands off to the in-app topology-tab via `topology/<siteId>` route — desktop link removed; basemap is theme-aware via `applyBasemapTheme()` — OpenStreetMap tiles in both themes, dark = the `.polaris-basemap-dark` tile-pane filter (defined in mobile.css, since mobile.html doesn't load styles.css) — and a MutationObserver on `<html>`'s `data-theme` swaps tiles in place when the user toggles theme from More tab; renders a stick-figure-with-hardhat user-location pin via `navigator.geolocation.watchPosition` with browser-reported speed + haversine fallback gated on GPS accuracy, walking-animation CSS plays only when actually moving, auto-starts when `permissions.query({name:"geolocation"})` is `"granted"` else after first recenter tap, GPS watch torn down on hashchange away from #map / #site; the pin's `--user-pin-stroke` flips per theme so the stick figure stays legible against either basemap), topology-tab.js (mobile topology surface — lazy-loads cytoscape/dagre/cytoscape-dagre on first open, calls into shared topology-render.js, top-to-bottom column layout (`computeTopologyColumns` depth→vertical; dagre fallback when no FortiGate root), no drag-to-reposition / no localStorage persistence / no screenshot / no fullscreen toggle, initial viewport zooms to the FortiGate or to a focus node when `?q=<term>` is in the URL, in-bar search wires `/topology/search` for endpoint→switch pivots, node tap opens a bottom sheet with monitor pill + endpoints list + "View asset" button; reached via `topology/<siteId>` detail route, fullbleed mode hides topbar slot + search slot + bottom navbar via `app.dataset.tab="__fullbleed"`; MutationObserver on `<html>`'s `data-theme` re-renders the graph when theme flips while topology is open, since the Cytoscape stylesheet captures theme at render time), assets-tab.js (Assets tab — paged card feed with type filter chips, tap-through to asset detail; a card whose device has live alerts also carries the strobing **Alerts flag** beside the hostname, built from the `activeAlert` summary already on the list payload — `alertFlagHTML` renders it through `PolarisMobileAlerts.flagHTML`, `paintAlertFlag` settles it from what the sheet loaded after an acknowledge or a clear, and the card is a `role="button"` DIV rather than a BUTTON because the flag inside it is a real button and a nested one swallows the tap that opens the device — the host's own keydown handler supplies Enter/Space), alerts.js (`window.PolarisMobileAlerts` — the phone's alert vocabulary and the per-asset **Alerts sheet**: `sevColor`/`sevRank` (the mobile mirror of `_alertSevRank`/`assetAlertStrobeColor` in assets.js and of `ALERT_SEVERITY_RANK` in src/utils/alertSeverity.ts, reading the `--md-sev-*` tokens in mobile.css), `summarize` (a loaded list reduced to the list endpoint's own {severity,count,unacknowledged} shape), `flagHTML`, and `openForAsset(assetId, {hostname, onSummary})` — a generic bottom sheet over `GET /assets/:id/alerts` offering Acknowledge at `alerts:write` (per row, plus one batched control for the whole device — a switch losing its uplink raises one alert per pinned interface) and Clear at `alerts:fullwrite`, each behind its own sheet-based prompt because `window.prompt`/`confirm` are suppressed in some installed PWAs. It also owns the acknowledge-note prompt the More tab's fleet-wide alerts list delegates to), reservations-tab.js (Reservations tab — list of active reservations from `api.reservations.list({status:"active", limit:200})`. Collapsed row: IP headline + `MAC · hostname` subtitle (MAC first, then hostname; falls back to subnet label when both empty). Tap the row to expand inline (one row at a time) showing hostname/owner/network/source/notes/expires plus role-gated action buttons: **Reserve** on `sourceType="dhcp_lease"` rows for any create-capable role — calls `window.PolarisReserveSheet.open()` (exposed by subnet-detail.js) with the lease prefilled and `existingLeaseId` so the lease is released atomically before the manual reservation is created (which then pushes to the FortiGate when the integration's `pushReservations` toggle is on); the button is blue by default (`btn-filled`, tooltip `Reserve in Polaris`) and flips green (`btn-success`, tooltip `Reserve on Gate`) when the row's `pushEligible` flag is set so the operator sees at a glance that confirming will also write to the FortiGate; **Edit** opens an inline PUT sheet (hostname/owner/MAC/notes/expires), labels MAC as required on push-eligible subnets to match the backend's reject-on-clear rule; **Release/Revoke** is a confirm + `api.reservations.release()` — labelled "Revoke" with tooltip `Revoke Lease` on `dhcp_lease` rows (FortiOS forgets the current lease; client can re-acquire) and "Release" with tooltip `Release Reservation` on every other source. Edit/Release mirror backend role gates — admin/networkadmin always pass; user/assetsadmin only when `r.createdBy === user.username`. **Open network** text button preserves the original tap-to-subnet navigation. The Edit / Free / Reserve-from-lease flows are also exposed as `window.PolarisReservationActions.{edit, free, reserveFromLease, canCreate, canModify}` so the Networks page (subnet-detail.js IP list) can drive the same tap-to-expand pattern with shared modal markup. Replaced the prior Alerts tab in the bottom nav), tabs.js (per-tab registry + Search results renderer + shared snackbar helper). The Search input itself lives in the shell-owned `#search-slot` (rendered once by app.js `renderShell` and persistent across navigation so the typed query survives tab/route changes); tabs.js exposes `window.PolarisSearch.{runSearch, debounce, setOriginRoute}` that the shell's input handler calls. Typing on any page replace-navigates to `/search` so results land in the body. The Search tab's own `renderTopbar` returns `''` (no duplicate bar); its `render()` re-runs the current persistent-input value so coming back to the tab shows the same results. **Page-aware ordering**: `setOriginRoute` is called by app.js `routeChanged` on every non-search route, so the result renderer hoists the matching section to the top (Reservations tab → reservations first; subnet detail → subnets first; assets tab / asset detail → assets first; map / site / topology → sites first; block detail / More→Blocks → blocks first; More→Subnets → subnets first). Mirrors the desktop search dropdown's page-aware section ordering., details.js (detail-route renderers — asset / subnet / block / site / topology; site delegates to map-tab, topology delegates to topology-tab), asset-detail.js (Asset detail **slide-up bottom sheet**, opened by `PolarisAssetDetail.open(id)` — a pure overlay with no route/hash change; the `asset/<id>` route survives only as a deep-link shim that paints the assets list as a backdrop then calls `open()`. Three states managed in-module: **expanded** (~90vh scrollable) ↔ **peek** (minimized to just the header band when the scrim — the dimmed area over the persistent searchbar — is tapped; the DOM is preserved, not torn down, so charts/scroll/per-asset `mountState` survive and re-expand is instant) ↔ **dismissed** (swipe-down via `attachSwipeToDismiss`, or the header close button); peek translate is measured from the live height into `--asset-peek-y` so snap-back composes with the swipe helper. All entry points call `open(id)` directly — assets-tab card tap, map site sheet, more-tab, subnet detail, both topology pivots, the search-hit consumer in tabs.js, and the LLDP-neighbor pivot (which replaces the sheet content in place) — each with a `PolarisRouter.go("asset/"+id)` fallback if the module isn't loaded; a `_openId` guard in `open()` and every loader bails a superseded asset's late fetch. Sections top-to-bottom: a **sheet header** (status dot + asset name + Screenshot + Refresh + Close — Screenshot rasterizes the full sheet body via the vendored html-to-image at natural mobile width with a WebKit double-capture workaround + an iOS canvas-area pixel-ratio cap, draws a hostname title strip, then delivers share-sheet → clipboard → download; `screenshotSheet` in asset-detail.js); a Hero with the status pill + identity bits (the name is NOT repeated here — it lives in the header); **Response Time** (collapsed by default — header subtitle shows the loaded avg / max / packet-loss summary at a glance, expand for the full response-time chart with 1h/12h/24h/7d/30d range buttons); **CPU + Memory** (collapsed by default — header subtitle shows the loaded `cpu avg N% · max N% · mem avg N% · max N%` summary with color spans matching the chart series, expand for the full chart; "Not collected for this monitor type" rendered in the subtitle when the asset's monitor type doesn't deliver telemetry); both charts render missed polls the way the desktop charts do — the line dives to the baseline in red with a gradient transition instead of bridging the hole, driven by explicit `ok:false` points for response time (mirroring desktop's `ptHasResponse`/`ptIsFailure`, so partial-loss rollup buckets still plot their average) and by inferred cadence gaps for CPU/memory, which carries no per-sample success flag (`charts.js` → UI-CANON.md "Failure-aware line rendering"); General (IP / MAC / type / model / OS / location / last seen); **Temperatures** — per-sensor list driven by `api.assets.systemInfo` for the current reading and a single unfiltered `api.assets.temperatureHistory(id, {range:"1h"})` call whose samples are grouped by `sensorName` client-side for per-sensor min/avg/max so each row shows `1h · min N° · avg N° · max N°`; **Interfaces** — filtered to `operStatus==="up"` (down hidden), sorted by `alias || ifName`, each row shows the operator-set alias as the primary label with the real ifName as the secondary line (or the interface's IP when alias and ifName collapse to the same value) and the resolved link speed via a local `formatBps()` helper; tap a row opens a `.scrim` + `.sheet` bottom sheet reusing the map-tab.js pattern with status (`oper X · admin Y`), speed, type/VLAN, IP, MAC, cumulative inErrors / outErrors plus an LLDP **Neighbor** card list filtered from the cached `lldpNeighbors[]` payload to `localIfName === iface.ifName` (peer-inferred entries are surfaced server-side so they appear here too — rendered with an italic "inferred" tag) — each neighbor card carries a **View asset** button when `matchedAsset.id` resolves, replacing the sheet content in place with the matched asset via `open(id)`. The two system-info-derived sections share one `api.assets.systemInfo` round-trip cached in module-level `_systemInfoCache` keyed by asset id so the sheet renders without a re-fetch; the Refresh action re-issues system-info alongside the chart pulls so a manual probe-now refreshes the new sections too. Three discovery-provenance sections follow: **Discovery sources** (`api.assets.getSources` → `GET /assets/:id/sources`, per-source list with the `SOURCE_LABELS` humanized sourceKind + integration name + lastSeen + externalId, mirrors desktop `_assetSourceLabels`; expanded by default), **Firewall sightings** (`api.assets.getSightings` → `GET /assets/:id/sightings`, fortigateDevice + ip + subnet/VLAN + source + lastSeen — endpoint needs `assetsQuarantine read`, so lower-privilege roles get a muted error note), and **IP history** (`api.assets.getIpHistory` → `GET /assets/:id/ip-history`); all three endpoints return bare arrays (the loaders read `Array.isArray(resp)`, not `resp.history`) and each header subtitle shows a count. The Hero also carries a **Quarantine** / **Release Quarantine** button (`quarantineButtonHtml` / `wireQuarantineButton`), gated on `assetsQuarantine:write` (read from `PolarisMobile.user().permissions`) and mirroring the desktop quarantine tab's eligibility — **Quarantine** (`btn-error`) for non-infra assets carrying a MAC, **Release Quarantine** (`btn-tonal`) for already-quarantined assets, nothing otherwise; it prompts for an optional reason (quarantine) or confirms (release) via `window.prompt`/`window.confirm`, then `refreshAfterQuarantine` re-fetches the asset to update the hero pill / header dot / button in place. The Hero also carries a **View SD-WAN** button (`btn-tonal`) for FortiManager/FortiGate-discovered firewalls — `loadSdwanGate` fetches `sdwan-members` / `sdwan-rules` / `perf-sla-links` (mirroring the desktop SD-WAN tab's prefetch-then-conditional gate) and reveals the button only when the device actually reported data, caching the payload in `_sdwanCache`. Tapping it opens a second stacked `.sheet`/`.scrim` bottom sheet (`openSdwanSheet`, same pattern as the interface sheet) with **Members** (status dot + member/zone + IP/link/speed + per-health-check latency chips), **Rules** (rule name/id + destination/criteria + member pills with the selected member highlighted + enabled state), and a **Performance SLA** section — a health-check `<select>` + 1h/12h/24h/7d/30d range segmented control driving three `PolarisCharts.lineChart` panels (latency / jitter / packet-loss) that overlay every member of the selected health-check (one color per member via a shared `sdwanColor` palette matching desktop), with a member legend, cross-member average stats line, and the SLA thresholds. Out of scope on mobile: per-interface throughput + errors charts, interface comment editor, IPsec tunnels, SNMP walk, per-source observed blob view.), more-tab.js (More tab — sub-page registry for Blocks / Subnets / Events plus the root menu with `Appearance → Theme` toggle row that flips dark↔light via `window.PolarisTheme.set` — sun/moon icon swap matches desktop's idiom, supporting label updates inline without re-rendering the tab), app.js (orchestrator: bootstraps auth, mounts the tab shell, dispatches tab and detail routes; detail specs may carry a `parentTab` to keep the corresponding navbar item highlighted; an early IIFE reads `localStorage["polaris-theme"]` (default `"dark"`, same key as desktop so a preference set on either surface flows to the other) and stamps `data-theme` on `<html>` *before* the orchestrator runs so the first paint never flashes the wrong theme; exposes `window.PolarisTheme.get()` / `.set()` for map-tab and more-tab to read/write without duplicating the localStorage key; bootstraps a best-effort `screen.orientation.lock("portrait")` — Android Chrome / installed PWAs honor it, iOS Safari rejects silently and the CSS landscape lockout in mobile.css picks up the slack).
│       └── vendor/                  # Bundled: jspdf, leaflet/, cytoscape, dagre, cytoscape-dagre, html-to-image (DOM→PNG rasterizer behind the asset-details whole-tab Screenshot button)
├── src/
│   ├── index.ts                     # Entry point
│   ├── config.ts                    # App config / env vars
│   ├── db.ts                        # Prisma client singleton
│   ├── utils/imageSize.ts           # pngSize / jpegSize / imageSize — pixel dimensions parsed from the file header (PNG IHDR; the JPEG marker chain walked to the first real SOF, skipping DHT/JPG/DAC inside the same marker range). Needed by brandLogoService to place the accent overlay: preserveAspectRatio can fit an image into a box but can't say what box the image already is. WebP deliberately returns null (resvg can't embed it, so there's no accent path anyway). Never throws.
│   ├── utils/imageMagic.ts          # detectImageMagic(buf) → ".png" | ".jpg" | ".webp" | null from magic bytes. Extracted from the branding-logo upload route; also used by appIconService to re-sniff on read (never trust the extension, and resvg can't decode an embedded WebP).
│   ├── utils/publicUrl.ts           # Parse POLARIS_PUBLIC_URL → public-facing port (nginx fronts TLS)
│   ├── utils/ipAllocation.ts       # Pure free-address selection behind the IP panel's Auto-Allocate modal (single AND multiple mode): `selectAvailableIps(hosts, taken, count, contiguous)` → `{ ips, largestRun, availableCount }` over an ordered, gapless host list — which is what lets adjacency in the ARRAY stand in for adjacency in the address space, and is the only assumption it makes. No Prisma, no I/O and no IP arithmetic (that stays in `utils/cidr.ts`); it only compares and slices strings, so the contiguity rules are unit-testable on their own. Two decisions live here: contiguous returns the EARLIEST fitting run rather than the largest (a later, roomier gap is not what "next available" means), and an unsatisfiable request returns an EMPTY list plus the two stats rather than a partial one — "allocate 12" half-done is not an outcome anyone asked for, so `reservationService.findNextAvailableIps` turns the stats into the 409 an operator reads ("the largest available run is 6").
│   ├── utils/fortiswitchCmdb.ts     # Pure parsers over the switch-controller managed-switch CMDB `ports` array (shared by monitoringService + the FMG/FortiGate discovery collectors, dependency-free to avoid an import cycle): `buildFortiswitchTrunkMembers` (trunk→physical-member map; LACP `members` + FortiLink auto-ISL `isl-local-trunk-name`) and `findFortiswitchUplinkPorts` (a switch's physical uplink port to its controller FortiGate via `fortilink-port` / `fgt-peer-device-name`)
│   ├── utils/portVlans.ts         # Pure Q-BRIDGE-MIB (RFC 4363) per-port VLAN decoding: `decodePortList` (PortList OCTET STRING → dot1dBasePort numbers; octet 0's MOST-significant bit is port 1) and `derivePortVlans` (dot1qPvid + the per-VLAN egress/untagged bitmaps → per-port {nativeVlan, taggedVlans}). The decision worth isolating: `dot1qVlanStaticUntaggedPorts` is often a verbatim COPY of the egress column (observed on FortiSwitch, 2026-08), and the RFC subtraction against a copy leaves EVERY port with an empty tagged set — a working trunk silently reported as carrying nothing. The untagged column is therefore believed only when it is a STRICT SUBSET of egress; otherwise the port's own PVID does that job. A port's native VLAN is never listed among its tagged VLANs either way
│   ├── utils/locationCodes.ts       # Pure parser for physical-location codes embedded in FortiSwitch/FortiAP admin descriptions (`b:` building / `f:` floor / `r:` room / `jb:` junction box). Case-insensitive keys matched at start-of-string or after whitespace; resolved server-side (Asset.description's codes when present, exclusively; else the device description's — notes are never a source) so the topology endpoint ships final strings and the browser never needs the grammar
│   ├── utils/linearTrend.ts         # Least-squares trend helpers for the storage-forecast surfaces: `leastSquaresSlopePerDay` (OLS slope in units/day — the JS reference implementation of the SQL regr_slope fit) + `daysUntilFull` (remaining/slope projection; null for flat/shrinking mounts or unknown capacity, 0 when already over)
│   ├── dash/
│   │   └── dashServer.ts            # The Dash wallboard listener — a small standalone Express app serving the UNAUTHENTICATED read-only /dash surface in its own process (POLARIS_ROLE=dash; also boots in-process under role "all" on POLARIS_DASH_PORT, default 3001). Middleware chain (order load-bearing): dashConfig-Setting kill-switch (10s TTL) → source-IP gate (`ipScope`: rfc1918+loopback / all / custom-CIDR-allow-list via isSourceAllowed; an UNAUTHORIZED source is DROPPED — socket destroyed, no response — so a scanner can't confirm the wallboard exists) → shared helmet CSP → GET/HEAD-only 405 → rate limit (general 600/5min; /weather/* rides the dedicated dashWeatherLimiter 4000/5min since one radar refresh is hundreds of tile GETs) → readonly-role snapshot stamped on req.roleSnapshot → /dash page + /dash/api/v1 (exact-path allowlist over the REAL dashboard/reservations/map routers + synthetic /auth/me + public branding, plus a /weather/ prefix rule for the parameterized weather-proxy paths) → /uploads static (custom branding logo, so dash-boot.js can swap the page favicon when hit directly) → public static. buildDashApp(opts) is the supertest seam.

│   │       ├── utilization.ts       # Reporting endpoints
│   │       ├── dashboard.ts         # `/dashboard/summary` + `/dashboard/noc-summary`. Both accept a subset param so each widget fetches only what it renders (`?sections=blocks|recent|assetTypes|monitorAlerts` on summary, `?feeds=<feed,...>` on noc-summary; absent = full legacy shape), and both serve every section/feed through a short server-side TTL cache (`utils/ttlCache.ts`, 10s = `NOC_FEED_CACHE_TTL_MS`) so concurrent widgets/tabs/kiosks share one computation. `summary` sections: blockUtilization from utilizationService.getGlobalUtilization, recentReservations from utilizationService.getRecentManualReservations (sourceType=manual only by default; cache key carries the recentLimit/sourceTypes params), assetTypeCounts via prisma.asset.groupBy (excluding decommissioned/disabled), and monitorAlerts via prisma.asset.findMany filtered to monitored + status in (warning, down), ordered by monitorStatusChangedAt desc nulls-last, capped at 50. `noc-summary` delegates to `nocDashboardService.getNocSummaryPayload` (feed registry + per-feed cache + `resolveFilteredAssetIds`); the route only parses params (`?assetTypes=server,switch,…` = the ENABLED built-in types, `?regionTags=East,West` = region names from the widget's Regions scope ("My regions" or a Selected-regions pick), `?fortigates=SITE-FG1,…` = FortiGate device names from the widget's FortiGates scope (assets behind any named gate; `__none__` = the "(No FortiGate)" gate-less entry), `?limit=` row cap, `?feeds=`) and resolves permissions. Both endpoints are permission-filtered, never 403'd (the dashboard is the redirect target for users bounced off gated pages): ipBlocks≥read → blockUtilization, reservations≥read → recentReservations, assets≥read → assetTypeCounts + monitorAlerts + all noc-summary asset sections, events≥read → noc-summary recentReboots, alerts≥read → activeAlerts (Notification-sourced since 2026-08; every role was seeded that key at read by migration 20260628000000, so no kiosk token lost the feed); denied sections return empty arrays (and never enter the cache), token callers get all-empty.

Canonical mount /automations; deprecated alias /notification-rules. Validates via ruleInputSchema; logic in notificationRuleService + notificationEngine.previewRule.
│   │       ├── maintenanceSchedules.ts # Maintenance-schedule CRUD (Assets → Maintenance modal) + POST /preview (target-filter dry-run → capped device list + total, monitored-only) + GET /occurrences?from&to (calendar tab: every schedule's occurrences expanded over a day range). Gated maintenanceManagement (read for list + occurrences, fullwrite for CRUD/preview). Thin: Zod outer shape here; recurrence + criteria validation and the inline reconcile live in maintenanceScheduleService.
│   │       ├── contacts.ts        # Address-book CRUD (Automations → Address Book) + GET /search (the unified recipient typeahead: Polaris users ∪ contacts) + POST /preview (device-filter dry-run). Reads gated `contacts:read`; writes use `requireOwnership("contacts")` + `assertOwnership` so a write-level caller edits/deletes only rows they created. `/search` + `/preview` declared BEFORE `/:id` so the literal paths aren't captured as ids. │   │       ├── networkScans.ts    # Saved network **Discovery** CRUD + runs, mounted /api/v1/network-scans behind a `networkScan:read` FLOOR on the whole router (the `/map` precedent — three of its read routes were auth-only until 2026-08, and a Discovery's targets and results are the same kind of recon material). `POST /runs/:runId/adopt` is the one route with a CHAINED gate — `networkScan:write` AND `assets:write` — which is the whole permission design: running creates nothing, so a role may be allowed to find out what is on a range without being allowed to add it. `/preview-targets` is read-level on purpose (pure IP math plus one indexed read; gating it at write would block the wizard's target preview for a role allowed to look at Discoveries), and it plus `/runs/...` are declared BEFORE `/:id` so the literal paths aren't captured as ids. Schemas are SHAPE only — the semantic rules live in `networkScanService.validateScanInput`. `POST /:id/run` answers 202: the sweep takes minutes and the wizard watches the run row. Tests: tests/integration/networkScans.test.ts
│   │       ├── notificationChannels.ts # NotificationChannel CRUD (Delivery tab) + per-channel Test send + VAPID generate (web_push). Gated automationManagement. Canonical mount /delivery-channels; deprecated alias /notification-channels. Backed by notificationChannelService + the channel senders.

Gated alerts:read (any viewer may opt in). Subscription owned by the session user; the web_push delivery channel routes to a user's endpoints. Since business rule 39 these are driven by `polarisPush.syncToPreference` reconciling a browser against `User.notificationPreference` at boot, not by an operator-facing on/off switch — there no longer is one.

UNAUTHENTICATED by design: a <link rel="manifest"> without crossorigin is fetched with credentials omitted, so a gated manifest 401s for everyone. │   │       ├── assetTypes.ts          # CRUD for the operator-extensible AssetTypeDef registry, plus the device-type MATCHING surface. Mounted at `/asset-types` BEFORE `/assets` so Express picks the registry endpoint instead of treating "types" as an asset id. Reads gated by `assets=read`; writes by `assets=write` (admin + assetsadmin). Built-ins seeded by migration are `isProtected=true` and reject rename/delete — but NOT a rules edit (`isProtected` guards identity, not matching), so `PUT /:id` refuses a name/label/description change on one while accepting `matchRules` / `matchContexts` / `matchPriority`. Rename is transactional — every Asset row holding the old name is rewritten in the same `$transaction` as the registry update. Three matching routes, all declared BEFORE `/:id`: `GET /match-schema` (the field / operator / context vocabulary + `AUTHORITATIVE_TYPE_SOURCES`, so the card renders the server's list rather than a copy — the `/assets/pin-filter-schema` precedent), `POST /match-preview` (read-level dry run over assets currently typed `other`; an optional `draft` body previews an UNSAVED edit by substituting it into the live registry, since a draft judged alone over-reports every device a higher-priority type would have claimed first), and `POST /match-apply` (`assets=write`, the retroactive step, audited as `asset_type.rules_applied`). Body schemas here are SHAPE only — regex compilation, clause count and value length live in `validateMatchRules`, because the seed and preview paths reach the service without passing the route.
│   │       ├── mibs.ts              # MIB Database CRUD + Browse + MIB-aware Walk. Mounted at `/server-settings/mibs` BEFORE the rest of /server-settings so its per-route guards (admin OR assets-admin on reads, admin-only on writes) take precedence over the blanket `requireAdmin` on the rest of /server-settings. Carries the `/structure` (parsed object tree) and `/walk` (decoded MIB-aware SNMP walk) endpoints alongside the existing list/get/upload/delete/profile-status/facets routes that moved here from serverSettings.ts.
