│   ├── services/
│   │   ├── brandLogoService.ts      # The operator's logo with the Polaris symbol composited onto its bottom-right corner (`branding.logoAccent`), rendered server-side via @resvg/resvg-js so login / sidebar / mobile can't each drift on the geometry. `accentGeometry` is the pure placement math (`ACCENT_FRACTION` = 0.5 of the logo's LONGEST side, clamped to half its shortest so a wide banner can't be swallowed; the canvas caps at MAX_RENDER_PX). Renders PER THEME (`renderAccentedLogo(theme)`, `?theme=dark|light` on the route, narrowed by `normalizeBrandTheme` since the value picks a filesystem path on an unauthenticated route) because the symbol art is theme-paired; the theme is part of the cache key and therefore of the ETag, so the two variants can't revalidate into each other. In-memory cache (≤4 entries) keyed on the logo + symbol mtimes + theme (the upload route writes a FIXED filename). Never throws — accent off / default logo / missing file / WebP / resvg failure all return null and the caller serves the plain logo. Served at the PUBLIC `GET /server-settings/branding/logo-accent.png` (declared in api/router.ts, above requireAuth, because the login page renders it pre-session).
│   │   ├── brandingService.ts       # The `branding` Setting row (appName / subtitle / logoUrl / logoAccent / logoOnLogin / logoOnSidebar / temperatureUnit — the DISPLAY-ONLY °C/°F preference for hardware sensors, normalized by `normalizeTemperatureUnit`; samples stay Celsius, see TOUCHES.md) + BRANDING_DEFAULTS. Extracted from routes/serverSettings.ts (which re-exports getBranding for its own routes + the public /branding alias) so appIconService and routes/pwa.ts can read branding without importing a route module. **`appName` may be EMPTY** — an operator whose uploaded logo carries their own wordmark blanks it, and the value is no longer snapped back to "Polaris" on read or write; surfaces that must print a name (page titles, the PWA manifest `name`, the acknowledge page) go through `displayAppName`. `logoAccent` / `logoOnLogin` / `logoOnSidebar` are read through `normalizeBrandingFlag` (only `undefined`/`null` take the default, so a stored `false` survives) and are inert without a custom logo; `hasCustomLogo` is the one definition of "custom", surfaced to the frontends as the derived `customLogo` field so they never compare paths.
│   │   ├── appIconService.ts        # PWA home-screen icons rasterized from the branding logo via @resvg/resvg-js (SVG canvas embedding the source as a data: URI). ICON_SPECS is the route's allowlist (192/512 any + maskable, 180 apple). On-demand + in-memory cache keyed on logo mtime (the upload route writes a FIXED filename, so mtime is the only invalidation signal). Never throws: unresolvable/traversal/missing/WebP/resvg-failure all degrade to the shipped public/img/brand/polaris-symbol-dark.png.
│   │   ├── certInfo.ts              # Leaf-cert fingerprint/SANs/expiry — dual-mode (reads disk in proxy mode, in-memory PEM in Node-HTTPS mode); layered cache with last-known-good fallback for cert-rotation atomic-rename windows
│   │   ├── ipService.ts             # Core IP math & validation
│   │   ├── blockService.ts          # Block business logic
│   │   ├── subnetService.ts         # Subnet allocation logic
│   │   ├── subnetArchiveService.ts  # Retiring a subnet without letting it squat on its CIDR (business rule 41). `snapshotSubnet` COPIES a subnet + its reservations into ArchivedSubnet/ArchivedReservation and leaves the live rows alone (the chassis-replacement path — nothing destroyed on the strength of an automatic detection); `archiveSubnet` snapshots then DELETES the live row, which is what frees `@@unique([blockId, cidr])` so a replacement gate's identical address space can be recorded. Deliberately NOT subject to business rule 4's active-reservation protection — that guards against destruction, and this preserves. Archived reservations are locked BY CONSTRUCTION (not in `reservations`, so none of the ~50 write sites can reach them).
│   │   ├── subnetChassisConflictService.ts # The `chassis-replaced` Conflict flavour — the first `entityType="subnet"` variant (business rule 41). Raise/refresh keyed on the (old, new) serial PAIR so a rejected row suppresses only that transition; `buildChassisDiff` computes the per-address old-vs-new diff ON READ (discovery syncs subnets in Phase 1 and reservations in Phases 3–5, so a payload built at detection time would compare the old chassis against itself); `diffReservationLines` is the pure verdict rule (only-old / only-new / differs / same, with `vip`/`interface_ip` lines shown but never migratable). Accept stamps the new serial onto the subnet; the dispatcher in conflictResolutionService owns the conflict's own status.
│   │   ├── reservationService.ts    # Reservation business logic
│   │   ├── reservationPushService.ts # Push manual DHCP reservations to FortiGate via an FMG integration (proxy or direct realtime, with read-back verify); used by reservationService on create + release. Also exports `buildTransportForIntegration` / `findScopeIdForCidr` / `listReservedAddresses` / `callFortiOs` so subnetRefreshService can reuse the same FMG-proxy/direct-FortiGate transport for read-only single-scope reconciliation. **Exports `classifyPushError(err) → "permanent" | "transient"`** — single source of truth for whether a push failure is operator-action-required (4xx, 502 with "verify mismatch" / "not visible on read-back" / "Authentication failed") or retry-eligible (everything else; defaults to retry-eligible). Consumed by `reservationService.createReservation` (transient → keep row + queue; permanent → rollback) and `retryPendingReservations` (transient → leave pending; permanent → flip to `failed_permanent`).
│   │   ├── infraReservationPushService.ts # OPT-IN post-sync discovery pass: turns a managed FortiSwitch/FortiAP's dynamic lease into a real MAC→IP `reserved-address` entry on its own gate. Double-gated (`config.pushReservations` + `config.autoReserveFortinetInfra`, both default off, both Fortinet integration types). Pins an address the device ALREADY holds, so pool occupancy is unchanged. The only scheduled DHCP write in Polaris, hence: bounded per cycle (RUN_CEILING 25), concurrency 2, MAC taken only from the gate's lease table, read-back-verified by `pushReservation`, and never re-attempted once the row carries push state — a permanent refusal stamps `pushStatus="failed_permanent"` + `pushError` so it drops out of the candidate set and shows the device's message in the IP panel. Eligibility is the pure `isInfraPushCandidate`. Stamps the push pointers the lifecycle release's pinned-unpush branch needs, so decommissioning the device removes the entry.
│   │   ├── placeholderMacAdoptionService.ts # Discovery Phase 7.7: replaces a reservation's PLACEHOLDER MAC with the real device's MAC once the gate reports one at that reserved IP, and re-pushes the corrected binding. Double-gated (`config.pushReservations` + `config.adoptDiscoveredMac`, both default off, both Fortinet integration types). Evidence is the ARP table + device inventory ONLY, keyed `(fortigateDevice, ip)` like Phase 7.6 (`buildMacEvidenceIndex` — ARP beats inventory, online beats offline, two disagreeing ARP rows drop the address). Eligibility is the pure `isAdoptionCandidate`: only a MAC matching the configured placeholder prefix is ever overwritten, the observed MAC must not itself be a placeholder, and a MAC already held by another active reservation in the same subnet is skipped (FortiOS would refuse it permanently). Device write goes through `updatePushedReservation` BEFORE the Polaris write so the two views can't diverge; a `pending` row skips device contact. Bounded per RUN, not per call (`AdoptionBudget`, 50) because FMG mode syncs once per gate. See business rule 26.
│   │   ├── reservationMacService.ts # The install-wide placeholder-MAC prefix Setting (`reservationMacPlaceholder`, default `02:0F:5E`). createSettingStore + pure normalizer + AppError-throwing save, the assetSourcePriorityService shape. Read self-heals a bad stored row to the default (an unparseable prefix would make `isPlaceholderMac` answer false for everything and silently disable adoption); save rejects, because an operator typing a vendor OUI needs to hear why.
│   │   ├── fortinetManagementAccessService.ts # Reads management-access (`allowaccess`) config for Fortinet devices during FMG/FortiGate discovery and summarizes it into `Asset.managementAccess`. `collectManagementAccess(integration, groups, opts)` builds one transport per controller FortiGate (via `buildTransportForIntegration` + `callFortiOs`, so FMG-proxy / FMG-direct / standalone all work) and reads: firewall `/api/v2/cmdb/system/interface` (the `config.mgmtInterface` interface's allowaccess), FortiAP `/api/v2/cmdb/wireless-controller/{wtp-profile,wtp}` (serial→profile→allowaccess), and FortiSwitch `/api/v2/cmdb/switch-controller/managed-switch` **plus `/api/v2/cmdb/switch-controller.security-policy/local-access`** (`LOCAL_ACCESS_CMDB_PATH`) — a managed switch has no per-device profile the way an AP does, so its access list is the controller's local-access POLICY: `parseLocalAccessPolicies` maps name→`{mgmt, internal}`, `pickLocalAccessPolicy` resolves the `default` policy every managed switch answers to — the policy is FLEET-WIDE, FortiOS having no per-switch attachment for one (confirmed against prod 2026-09-03), so the shape-matched assignment lookup ahead of it (any key on the managed-switch row mentioning `local-access`) is defensive only and every switch falls through it, and `localAccessHalfFor` picks the half by `config.switchManagementInterface` (`mgmt*` → `mgmt-allowaccess`, everything else → `internal-allowaccess`). One policy read per controller serves every switch it manages. A per-switch interface allowaccess still wins where firmware exposes one; `protocols: null` (unknown, never `[]`) when neither is readable. Returns `Map<serial, ManagementAccessSummary>`. Pure parsers (`parseAllowaccess` / `findInterfaceRow` / `buildFirewallSummary` / `parseWtpProfiles` / `parseWtpToProfile` / `buildApSummary` / `buildSwitchSummary` / `parseLocalAccessPolicies` / `pickLocalAccessPolicy` / `localAccessHalfFor`) are exported + unit-tested. `shapeManagementAccessForClient` is the one reducer to the four fields a browser needs (mgmtIp / protocols / https / ssh), shared by the Assets-list shaping in `api/routes/assets.ts` and by `assetUpstreamService`; never throw on malformed payloads. Per-device failures are swallowed (logged) so one unreachable FortiGate never aborts the pass. Read-only — never writes the device. Hooked into `syncDhcpSubnets` Phase 13.6 (gated `full|finalize`).
│   │   ├── fortigateLocationService.ts # Discovery-time `fetchFortigateSysLocation()`: REST `GET /api/v2/cmdb/system.snmp/sysinfo` against a FortiGate via the existing FMG-proxy / standalone transport (reuses `callFortiOs` + `buildTransportForIntegration` from reservationPushService). Returns the trimmed sysLocation string or null. Chosen over an SNMP get to avoid a separate credential resolver / net-snmp session and to work in FMG proxy mode where Polaris can't reach the FortiGate's management IP directly. Never throws — REST failures come back as null so the discovery sync continues with no location update.
│   │   ├── geocoderService.ts         # Address-string → lat/lng geocoder backed by OpenStreetMap Nominatim. `geocode(query)` normalizes the input (trim + collapse-whitespace + lowercase), consults `GeocodeCache` (90-day TTL; positive AND negative results cached), and on cache-miss hits Nominatim through a process-global 1 req/sec rate limiter (module-level chained Promise enforces the gap). User-Agent identifies Polaris per Nominatim's usage policy. Transport failures (timeout / non-2xx / parse error) do NOT poison the cache; only successful responses (including empty result arrays — the negative-cache signal) write rows. Never throws. Used by the FortiGate coord-resolution chain in `syncDhcpSubnets` Phase 3.
│   │   ├── fortigateCoordPushService.ts # `pushCoordsToFortigate()` — write-back orchestrator for geocoded coords. FMG mode writes to BOTH per-device metavars `Latitude` / `Longitude` (native FMG `update` on `/dvmdb/adom/<adom>/device/<n>` with `{"meta fields": {...}}`) AND CMDB `gui-device-latitude` / `gui-device-longitude` (native FMG `update` on `/pm/config/device/<n>/global/system/global`). Standalone FortiGate writes only CMDB via direct REST PUT on `/api/v2/cmdb/system/global`. Best-effort: per-target failures are logged and reflected in the returned `{ok, targets[], error?}` shape but never throw. FMG-mode CMDB writes land in FMG's CMDB but require an operator Install Device Configuration in FMG to reach the live FortiGate — Polaris explicitly does not trigger installs.
│   │   ├── subnetRefreshService.ts   # Per-subnet "refresh from device" action (Refresh button in the IP panel slide-in). Queries the originating FortiGate for ONE DHCP scope (CMDB reservations + live leases) via the same transport reservationPushService uses, reconciles against Polaris's `dhcp_reservation` + `dhcp_lease` rows on this subnet (manual / VIP rows untouched), and bumps `Subnet.lastDiscoveredAt`. Narrower than `discoverDhcpSubnets` — doesn't recompute asset sightings / decommissions / map regions / etc.; those reconcile on the next full integration cycle. Writes one `subnet.refresh` Event.
│   │   ├── reservationStaleService.ts # Stale-reservation detection: settings (staleAfterDays), alert lister (active|ignored), snooze/ignore mutators, and the job entry point that emits reservation.stale Events. The freshest-signal core (`effectiveLastSignalMs`) folds THREE real presence signals — `lastSeenLeased` (DHCP lease), `lastSeenArp` (FortiGate ARP table binding the reserved IP to the reserved MAC — stamped by sync Phase 7.6), and Asset.lastSeen (correlated by MAC then IP) — so statically-addressed / ICMP-silent devices that never lease aren't flagged. Excludes reservations on deprecated subnets (decommissioned-firewall networks) from the active list/count
│   │   ├── apRadioService.ts        # FortiAP radio + broadcast-SSID inventory — the two levels ABOVE a wireless station. `persistApRadioInventory(assetId, radios, source)` writes AssetApRadio + AssetApVap from either of the two sources (the controller's managed_ap `radio[]` array, written by discovery; the AP's own fapRadioTable over SNMP), MERGING per column so neither erases what the other established, and deleting the radios (and their VAPs) a scrape stopped reporting. `getApRadioInventory(assetId)` returns the radios with their SSIDs nested, ordered the way the tree renders — read by `GET /assets/:id/system-info`.
│   │   ├── arpPrimeService.ts        # ARP-priming presence sweep: fire-and-forget UDP datagrams (port 33434, 1-byte payload) at a list of reserved IPs so the FortiGate is forced to ARP-resolve each target right before discovery reads its ARP table — any live IP stack answers ARP even when it firewalls ICMP. `planSweepBatches` (pure: dedupe / IPv4-validate / cap 4096 / chunk 256) + `primeArpCache` (single udp4 socket, paced batches, per-datagram errors swallowed, never throws) + `ARP_SETTLE_MS` (2s sweep→read gap; FortiOS GCs unreferenced neighbor-cache entries in ~60-90s so callers must read promptly). Opt-in per integration via `config.arpPresenceSweep` (default off — the sweep is IDS-visible); called per-gate from fortimanagerService Step 3d.54 (proxy mode) and fortigateService Step 3e.54 (standalone + FMG-direct)
│   │   ├── networkScanRunner.ts   # Executes ONE network **Discovery** (business rule 34): expand the operator's targets (`expandScanTargets`), SUBTRACT every address inventory already carries (before any packet — "new addresses only" means there is no reason to touch a device Polaris already knows, and the `skippedKnownCount` is what keeps "nothing new" distinguishable from "nothing there"), then two stages: an **ICMP liveness** sweep (`pingHost` at concurrency 64 / 1.5 s — the cheap filter that decides whether a /16 of empty space costs 25 minutes or four hours) and **identification** (concurrency 12, each attempt an authentication plus, for SNMP, six walks — the stage that shows up on an IDS). The operator's method order is a PRIORITY order: the first method answering with a credential owns the identity, later ones record that they answered without overwriting it, and credentials within a method stop at the first success. `ScanHit.errors` keeps the OTHER methods' failure reasons, because "answered ICMP, refused every community" is the most common shape and names the credential to fix. **Nothing here calls `withSnmpGate`** — both `probeCredentialAgainstHost("snmp")` and `snmpWalkRaw` acquire the per-(host, port) gate internally, so the scan already FIFOs behind the monitor loop and wrapping again would deadlock. `runScan` never throws (the run row IS the wizard's view of it), progress + the cancel check ride one throttle so a /16 isn't 65k UPDATEs plus 65k SELECTs, the cancel clock is per-RUN so two Discoveries can't suppress each other's tick, and `hits` is capped at 2000 with a loud warn. **Creates no assets** — adoption is a separate operator action on a route chaining `assets:write`, which is what lets a `networkScan`-only role run a sweep. Tests: tests/unit/networkScanRunner.test.ts
│   │   ├── arpTableService.ts       # Persists each FortiGate's layer-3 neighbour cache into AssetArpEntry — the current-state table behind the firewall asset's ARP Table tab. `persistFortigateArpTables` does NOT collect: the rows already arrive on every FMG / standalone-FortiGate discovery cycle (`DiscoveryResult.arpTable`) and were previously consumed in memory by three passes and thrown away. Delete-replace per gate, scoped to `arpQueriedDevices` (the gates whose live read ANSWERED) so a proxied read to an offline gate, a missing monitor scope or an aborted run preserves the stored rows instead of blanking the tab — the AssetLldpNeighbor contract. Resolves the gate name → serial → assetId through the run's own DiscoveredDevice list and the `fortigate-firewall` AssetSource row, never the hostname (utils/fortinetParentKey.ts). Two fleet-wide reads for the whole batch (AssetSource rows + existing firstSeen values) then one transaction per gate, so the write cost tracks the FIREWALL count, not the asset count; a single gate's failed write is caught and logged so the rest of the fleet keeps its table. Pure shaping (normalize / dedupe-freshest / order / cap 4000 with a loud warn) lives in utils/arpTable.ts. Called from discoveryEngine Phase 7.5b
│   │   ├── ipContextService.ts    # Cross-references ONE IP address against everything Polaris already knows about it, for the manual Add Asset form (public/js/assets-ipcontext.js). `lookupIpContext(ip, {includeSubnets, includeReservations})` answers: the most-specific containing Subnet + its block/integration, the active Reservation on the address (lease or reservation — `dhcpBinding` and `sourceType` are reported separately, business rule 23), the `AssetArpEntry` rows that resolve it, the `AssetFortigateSighting` rows that have seen it, the `AssetMacTableEntry` switch port its MAC was learned on, and any Asset already carrying it as a primary or associated address. Read-only — no device I/O, no writes, nothing created. Containment reuses `buildIpContexts` (subnetService) rather than re-implementing the `cidr >>= ip` / `masklen DESC` SQL. **Which firewall** is decided by `resolveFirewall` over three sources ranked by how directly each observed the address: an ARP row (whose gate IS an asset already, no name resolution needed) → `Subnet.fortigateDevice` → the freshest sighting; the pure `pickNamedGate` states the subnet-over-sighting half of that ranking in one testable place. The two NAME-only sources carry FortiManager device names, so they resolve through `buildInfraParentIndex`/`resolveInfraParentAsset` (utils/fortinetParentKey.ts) — a hostname match here is exactly the conflation that module exists to prevent — and a name that resolves to no asset still NAMES the gate rather than being dropped. `buildSuggestions` (pure) derives the advisory prefill the form offers: MAC (ARP over reservation, the placeholder-MAC-adoption precedent), hostname from the reservation, and location/coordinates from the GATE asset (a gate's coordinates are the site's). Suggestions are never applied server-side. The subnet is resolved even when the caller lacks `subnets:read` — it is how the reservation is found and one of the three gate sources, and the gate NAME it contributes is the same value `Asset.learnedLocation` already shows to any `assets:read` caller — but the emitted blocks are gated, and `visibility` reports which halves were consulted so a hidden section can render as "not shown" rather than a confident "nothing found"
│   │   ├── dnsResolvedReservationService.ts # Auto-creates Reservation rows with `sourceType="dns_resolved"` for every Asset with an `ipAddress` that falls inside a non-deprecated Subnet and has no authoritative (manual / dhcp_reservation / dhcp_lease / interface_ip / vip / fortiswitch / fortinap / fortimanager / fortigate) reservation already there. Carries the asset's hostname (`hostname || dnsName`) and `macAddress` when known; `createdBy="system:dns-resolved"`. Exports `reconcileDnsResolvedForAsset(assetId)` (the per-asset path called from the Prisma extension hook in `src/db.ts` post-write + from the periodic job per-row), `reconcileDnsResolvedForAllAssets()` (the periodic sweep — batches of 25 via Promise.all), `releaseDnsResolvedForAsset(assetId)` (asset-delete hook), and `releaseDnsResolvedAt(subnetId, ipAddress)` (the discovery hand-off used by `syncDhcpSubnets` and `reservationService.createReservation` right before creating an authoritative row at the same target). Eligible asset statuses: active / maintenance / storage / quarantined. IPv4 only. Defers silently to authoritative entries — never raises Conflict rows, never pushes to FortiGates.
│   │   ├── utilizationService.ts    # Utilization reporting. `getGlobalUtilization` backs the legacy `/utilization` route and is also reused by the new Dashboard summary. `getRecentManualReservations` is the new helper that powers the Dashboard's "Recently Reserved" card — same `findMany` shape as `recentReservations` but filtered to `sourceType="manual"` so DHCP discoveries / leases / VIP echoes don't crowd it out, with `{id,cidr,name,vlan}` hydrated on the subnet relation so the card renders without a second fetch.
│   │   ├── nocDashboardService.ts   # Fleet-wide aggregates behind `/dashboard/noc-summary` (SolarWinds-style NOC widgets). getStatusSummary (groupBy monitorStatus + infra-subset uptime% + active-alert count), getDownNodes, getHighestCpu/getHighestMemory (avg of each asset's most-recent N telemetry samples — N = the caller's `sampleCount` from the widgets' "Average over" gear control, default `DEFAULT_TOPN_SAMPLE_COUNT` = 10, ceiling `MAX_TOPN_SAMPLE_COUNT` = 100, 1 = rank on the latest sample only — via a windowed `row_number()` over asset_telemetry_samples; the window scales at 6 min/sample (1h at the default) so it always holds N samples while staying chunk-excluded — hydrated in one findMany; replaced the prior DISTINCT-ON latest-value ranking), getSlowestResponse (averages each asset's most-recent 10 response times via a windowed `row_number()` over asset_monitor_samples — 6h window keeps the hypertable scan chunk-excluded — then hydrates names; replaced the prior instantaneous Asset.lastResponseTimeMs ranking), getPacketLoss (failed-probe ratio groupBy over asset_monitor_samples — no schema change), getHighestDiskUsage (per-volume used % — DISTINCT-ON latest per (assetId, mountPath) over asset_storage_samples, 48h window for the slow storage cadence, hydrated in one findMany with the mount as `detail`), getStalePolls (indexed candidate findMany + cached resolveMonitorSettings per candidate), getRecentReboots (an Event read), getRecentAlerts (the UNCLEARED Notification rows — an ALERT read, not an Event one: it listed every warning/error Event until 2026-08, which surfaced automation-less discovery/sync failures as permanent alerts nothing could clear and showed `Event.level`, whose critical/serious collapse displayed a `serious` automation as "error". Returns `{alerts, total}` — `total` being the uncleared count BEFORE the cap, free because the ordering already fetches the whole set, so the widget can say "50 of 214" instead of ending silently at a cap that eats the least severe rows first. Carries `assetId` (the widget's click-through) and `dimension` (which port / sensor / mount the alert is about — one per-interface automation raises one alert per pinned port, so without it those rows differ in nothing). An asset filter KEEPS the assetId-null rows: an alert about Polaris itself (a host_metric rule, a system-scoped event) belongs on every wallboard, since no asset filter can say anything about it), getSitesWithIssues (raw COALESCE groupBy + one bounded node findMany), and resolveFilteredAssetIds (turns the optional per-widget `{assetTypes, regionNames, fortigateNames}` filter into a constraining assetId set — `assetType notIn <hidden built-ins>` + `tags hasSome region:<name>` + behind-any-named-gate (`learnedLocation` equals-insensitive OR sighting rows; `FORTIGATE_NONE_SENTINEL` = gate-less assets) — or null when nothing narrows; every feed takes an `assetIds` arg). `getStorageForecast` (days-until-full per growing filesystem via `storageForecastService`, severity-first then soonest-full). **Severity-first ordering:** every asset-sourced feed decorates rows with the owning asset's highest ACTIVE automation alert (`activeAlertSeverityByAsset` over uncleared Notification rows, `ALERT_SEVERITY_RANK` incl. legacy info/error) and STABLE-sorts alerted rows first — each feed's own order (value desc / youngest outage / most overdue / soonest-full) holds within a severity band; `getRecentAlerts` is itself alert-sourced — it sorts the uncleared set by `ALERT_SEVERITY_RANK` desc, then triggeredAt desc, then the dimension NUMERICALLY (port2 before port10, the asset Alerts tab's tiebreak) in memory, since severity is a string rather than a rank column, and slices to the row cap AFTER sorting so a limit can't drop a critical; `getSitesWithIssues` takes the max rank across a site's affected nodes. `getNocSummaryPayload({feeds, canAssets, canEvents, canAlerts, assetTypes, regionNames, capLimit, sampleCount})` is the route's entry point: a `NOC_FEEDS` registry maps each of the 15 feed names (`NOC_FEED_NAMES`) to its permission gate (`assets` / `events` / `alerts` — the last only activeAlerts), empty value, runner, and response-key flattening (`status` fans out to statusCounts/uptimePercent/activeAlertCount; `downNodes` unwraps `.nodes` alongside `downNodesTotal`, and `activeAlerts` does the same with `activeAlertsTotal`); unknown feed names drop silently; every (feed, filter, cap[, samples]) computation — and the filter→assetIds resolution — goes through a shared 10s `createTtlCache` (only the `usesDepDown` feed — downNodes — keys on `?includeDependencyDown`, and only the `usesSamples` feeds — topCpu/topMemory — key on the samples count) (`NOC_FEED_CACHE_TTL_MS`, `clearNocFeedCache()` test hook) so N widgets/browsers recompute nothing. Read-only; every query scale-checked flat to 2000 assets.
│   │   ├── probeLossQuery.ts        # The ONE windowed failed-probe-ratio query over asset_monitor_samples, shared by the engine's probeLossPct trigger and the NOC Packet Loss widget. **EVERY MISS IN THE WINDOW COUNTS (2026-09-01)** — plainly failed/total, no anchor, no trimming. The two anchors it carried (GREATEST(first success, Asset.recoveryStartedAt)) stopped a device reading ~92% the moment it came back from a 55-minute outage, but ALSO collapsed the window of a device flapping to `down` each cycle to its last few probes, so a badly lossy link reported ~0% loss forever (prod 2026-09-01). Suppression moved to the ENGINE instead — the answering gate plus the automation's own `ignoreAtOrAbove` ceiling, both of which CLEAR rather than freeze (business rule 29). **It counts PACKETS, not rows, wherever it can**: an ICMP sweep row carries packetsSent/packetsReceived and describes a whole burst, so an asset with any burst rows is measured from those sums and its response-time poll rows are excluded (that poll may be SNMP/SSH/REST/WinRM, and a lost SNMP response is not "packet loss"); an asset with none falls back to the row ratio. {total, failed} kept its shape — the units beneath it moved. Engine mode keeps 0%-loss rows for hysteresis recovery; widget mode (onlyLossy) adds a HAVING asked of PACKETS, so a device whose every burst dropped packets while still getting something back is not filtered out as spotless. `includeFullyDown` RETIRED: with every countable row in the ratio a fully-dark asset reads 100% on its own. Counts every probeKind (one of only two such readers, with alertChartService's loss chart). **ONE exclusion, and its unit is the failure RUN (2026-09-03, business rule 29h)**: `runId` + `runOutage` window functions drop the failures of any maximal run of consecutive failures holding a row stamped `assetDown` — ONSET included, since the marker is only stampable from the probe that DECLARES the outage and leaving the onset in a shrunken denominator still read 10.5% a full window after recovery. Neither engine gate could see the case that forced it (a switch dark for 12 minutes comes back, starts ANSWERING, and its 30-minute window still reads 40%, under any sensible ceiling). Unlike the anchor it replaces, nothing is excluded by TIME and nothing here knows `missedPolls` (that count is the covering automation's and changes when a rule is edited — a run is bounded by successes instead): a run that stayed below the threshold is loss and counts in full, so an alternating device is measured exactly as it was. `coalesce(bool_or(...), false)` is load-bearing — NULL would make WHERE drop every failure in an unstamped run — and it is what keeps the change non-retroactive. `alertChartService.outageRunFailures` is the JS mirror, applied to both the loss chart's line and its caption
│   │   ├── storageForecastService.ts # Per-filesystem "days until full" forecasting — the shared computation behind the Storage Forecast dashboard widget (nocDashboardService `storageForecast` feed) and the `storageDaysUntilFull` automation metric (notificationEngine resolver). ONE regr_slope aggregate over a UNION of day-bucketed storage DETAIL samples (7d retention — covers every storage-scraped asset incl. the slow 24h cadence) and the DAILY rollups (365d, but cadence='fast' pinned assets only — see sampleRollupService), deduped per (asset, mount, day); 30-day lookback (`FORECAST_LOOKBACK_DAYS`), ≥7 distinct daily points (`FORECAST_MIN_POINTS`), growing mounts only, forecasts beyond 365 days dropped (`FORECAST_MAX_DAYS`). JS side only does the remaining/slope division via utils/linearTrend. Read-only; flat at 2000 assets.
│   │   ├── fortimanagerService.ts   # FMG JSON-RPC client & discovery orchestration. All FMG-bound calls (rpc, fmgProxyRest, resolveDeviceMgmtIp, ...) accept an optional `integrationId` and route through `getFmgWorker(integrationId)` so cross-feature traffic (discovery + reservation push + quarantine push + manual proxy + connection test) stays serial against FMG's "one-request-at-a-time" constraint.
│   │   ├── fortigateService.ts      # Standalone FortiGate REST API client & discovery. **Per-device REST queries fan out across 6 independent chains via Promise.all** so per-FortiGate wall-clock is `max(longest chain)` instead of `sum(all 12 steps)`. Chains (after Steps 1 + 2): A) DHCP CMDB → Promise.all(DHCP monitor + interface IPs); B) device inventory; C) managed switches → managed APs → AP-port mapping (serial intra-chain — 3e.5 needs both 3d and 3e); D) ARP table; E) geo coordinates; F) firewall VIPs. Peak intra-device REST concurrency is ~6 simultaneous calls; small-branch FortiGates (60F/61F class) handle this fine, and each step keeps its own try/catch so a slow individual query doesn't tank the whole device. Used by the standalone FortiGate integration directly AND by `fortimanagerService` in direct mode (`useProxy=false`) which delegates per-device work to `fortigateService.discoverDhcpSubnets`.
│   │   ├── fmgActivityService.ts    # DB-backed heartbeat of every `FmgWorker`'s lane state. The role that owns FMG traffic (discovery in split-role prod, the single process in "all" mode) snapshots all `getAllFmgWorkers()` to the `fmgActivitySnapshot` Setting row every 2 s; the web role reads it back via `getFmgActivityForIntegration(integrationId)` to power the "Active FMG Calls" row on the integrations page. Snapshots stamp `updatedAt + role`; `STALENESS_MS=10_000` is the freshness threshold the API + UI use to flag a dead heartbeat (e.g. polaris-discovery down). One write per 2 s per FMG-running process; reads are key-equality on `Setting.key`.
│   │   ├── fmgWorker.ts             # Per-integration FortiManager worker with two lanes. Module-level `Map<integrationId, FmgWorker>`, lazily created on first submit. The FMG concurrency constraint is specifically about `/sys/proxy/json` (the passthrough that forwards calls through to managed FortiGates) — FMG drops parallel proxy connections past 1-2 for the same API user. Native endpoints (`/pm/config/...`, `/dvmdb/...`, auth) hit FMG's own DB and don't share that constraint. Lanes: **proxy lane** is strict single-consumer FIFO (concurrency=1) and carries every `/sys/proxy/json` call; **native lane** is unbounded and just tracks inflight count for observability. Dispatch happens inside `rpc()` (fortimanagerService) by inspecting the JSON-RPC payload's first param URL; callers use `submitProxy` / `submitNative` explicitly. Cross-feature serialization still holds for proxy calls (discovery per-device monitor scrapes, proxy-mode reservation push, proxy-mode quarantine push, manual `/sys/proxy/json` proxy endpoint all share one slot); native calls (mgmt-IP resolves, CMDB scrapes, the device roster) parallelize freely. Exports `polaris_fmg_worker_queue_depth{integrationId}` + `polaris_fmg_worker_inflight{integrationId}` (proxy lane) and `polaris_fmg_worker_native_inflight{integrationId}` (native lane) so operators can see which lane is the bottleneck.
│   │   ├── integrationHealthService.ts # Backs `GET /integrations/health-summary`, the sidebar's 30 s poll. Two unrelated signals ride one response because the sidebar already fetches it on every page for every session: `failed` (enabled integrations whose last connection test failed) and `proxyAdvice` (enabled FortiManager integrations still on the proxy transport managing more than `FMG_PROXY_GATE_ADVISORY_THRESHOLD` = 10 gates). The advisory is about THROUGHPUT, not capability — `/sys/proxy/json` is serialized at concurrency 1 by FMG, so a poll cycle grows linearly with gate count while direct mode parallelises up to 20. Gate counts come from ONE `asset.groupBy`, never a count per integration: this runs every 30 s per signed-in session. `selectProxyAdvice` / `integrationIsFmgProxyMode` are pure and unit-tested; the threshold is duplicated in the Direct Polling hint in `public/js/integrations.js` and the two must change together.
│   │   ├── windowsServerService.ts  # Windows Server WinRM DHCP discovery
│   │   ├── entraIdService.ts        # Microsoft Entra ID + Intune device discovery via Graph
│   │   ├── activeDirectoryService.ts # On-premise Active Directory computer discovery via LDAP/LDAPS
│   │   ├── azureArcService.ts       # Azure Arc (Arc-enabled servers) discovery client. OAuth2 client-credentials against **Azure Resource Manager** — reuses src/utils/entraClientCredentials.ts at scope https://management.azure.com/.default, so no Azure SDK and no Microsoft Graph permission. Two interchangeable read paths normalizing through the same normalizeArcMachine: Azure Resource Graph (default — ONE POST across every readable subscription, with server-side projection) and a per-subscription paged Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines list used when ARG is off or unavailable (transparent fallback, logged once). ARM specifics the Graph client doesn't have: nextLink paging (not @odata.nextLink), ARG's skipToken body paging, and mandatory 429 backoff honouring Retry-After / x-ms-user-quota-resets-after. Pure exported helpers are unit-tested: normalizeVmUuid (rejects the all-zero GUID), swapVmUuidEndianness (the SMBIOS little-endian disagreement between Windows / dmidecode / VMware — both variants are indexed at match time or every Arc-on-VMware machine duplicates), parseArmResourceId, inferArcAssetType, filterArcMachines, matchesTagFilter, arcHostnameCandidates, buildArcObservedBlob, throttleDelayMs, describeAadTokenError. Also backs testConnection (token → per-subscription read → bounded machine list, so a missing Reader role can't report a false success) and the Query API modal's proxyQuery (host-pinned to management.azure.com, api-version required, POST allowed only to the Resource Graph endpoint).
│   │   ├── vcenterService.ts        # VMware vCenter discovery + telemetry client. vSphere Automation REST (session auth, per-host VM listing pins VM→host placement + sidesteps the 4000-item list cap, VMware Tools guest identity/networking per VM at bounded concurrency) + SOAP property-collector calls against /sdk (WinRM-Identify hand-rolled-envelope precedent, no XML dep) for everything REST won't answer. Three batched fetches, each one call for the WHOLE vCenter: **VM quickStats** (`fetchVcenterQuickStats` — CPU MHz + RAM usage + power state + uptime + `guest.disk` filesystems + `guest.net` vNICs; feeds the discovery usage snapshot AND monitoringService's per-tick warm cache), **ESXi host stats** (`fetchVcenterHostSnapshot` — quickStats + hardware summary + connection/power state + `config.network.pnic`/`vnic`/`vswitch`/`proxySwitch`/`portgroup`, paired with the datastore fetch in ONE SOAP session so a host's storage figures and its virtual networking come from the same round trip; the two halves report failure SEPARATELY via `hostError`/`datastoreError` because a vCenter role can be allowed one and refused the other, and collapsing them would cost discovery its datastore backing detail over a host-property gap). This is also discovery's Phase 2 fetch, which is what makes the host's vSwitches free there and keeps one parser for them, and **datastore facts** (summary capacity/free/uncommitted → provisioned, host mount list, VMFS extent NAA ids → array vendor via the exported `vendorFromNaa` prefix map, NFS remote host). `parseHostPnics` reads the live `<linkSpeed>` from the entry PREFIX only — `validLinkSpecification` and `spec` carry `<speedMb>` elements of their own, so a whole-entry match would report a supported speed on a dark port; `splitAtSpec` generalizes that head-vs-spec split for the vSwitch and port-group parsers, whose scalars (`numPorts`, `mtu`) also appear twice. vSwitch uplinks are read as DEVICE names from `spec.bridge.nicDevice` / `spec.backing.pnicSpec[].pnicDevice`, never from the opaque `pnic[]` key arrays, so the join onto the interface rows needs no key-mapping table; the NIC-teaming policy is read from inside `<nicTeaming>` because `spec.policy` is also an element named `policy`. Guest and host arrays parse to `null`, never `[]`, when the property is absent. Every SOAP surface degrades to nulls independently; datastores fall back to the REST list when /sdk is unreachable. Pure exported helpers (pickVmExternalId — instanceUuid with integration-scoped moref fallback; buildVcenterDependencyEdges — vMotion-safe cluster multi-parent; filterVms; SOAP parsers) are unit-tested. Also backs testConnection + the Query API modal's proxyQuery (REST surface only).
│   │   ├── searchService.ts         # Global typeahead search (classifies IP/CIDR/MAC/text; parallel entity queries). MAC lookups are range-aware: a full typed MAC also matches an AssetMacAddress range row containing it (lexicographic containment over canonical colon-uppercase bounds), and a partial hex term is additionally tried as a MAC prefix interval against ranges (`macPrefixBounds`)
│   │   ├── allocationTemplateService.ts # Saved multi-subnet allocation templates (Setting-backed)
│   │   ├── autoMonitorInterfacesService.ts # "Auto-Monitor Interfaces" feature: pure resolver over a multi-block union (byNames / byPatterns / byTypes / byLldp) + DB-bound aggregate/preview/apply for the FMG/FortiGate Monitoring tab. By LLDP pins any interface whose neighbor — direct `AssetLldpNeighbor.matchedAssetId` OR peer-inferred edge from `Asset.fortinetTopology` — resolves to a monitored asset of one of the selected types. The peer-inferred half (`loadInferredLldpByAsset` — class-aware raw SQL over `fortinetTopology->>'controllerFortigate'` / `parentSwitch` / etc.) covers managed FortiAPs whose FortiSwitch silently consumes LLDP without re-publishing via SNMP LLDP-MIB; same data source as the inferred Neighbor column on the System tab (see `peerInferredLldpService`). For the `fortiap` class, a post-load step (`normalizeFortiapInferredLldp`) rewrites synthesized `localIfName` from FortiAP-CLI naming (`lan1`) to SNMP-canonical (`eth0`) when the AP's interface table actually exposes the eth* form — without this, the resolver would pin a name that doesn't match any ifIndex on the fast-cadence scrape. UI label reads **By LLDP (includes inferred interfaces)** so operators see at a glance that the match set isn't LLDP-protocol-only. `compilePattern` dispatches wildcards vs raw regex per block. `coerceLegacySelection` rewrites the older single-mode discriminated-union shape (`{mode, ...}`) on read so the Zod parser + apply route + frontend renderer all keep working until the one-shot migration sweeps stored configs. Strictly additive to Asset.monitoredInterfaces. `loadLatestInterfaces` is EXPORTED for `massPinService` (the Mass Pinning section's fleet-wide picker), which is what keeps the 72h staleness bound + the IPsec-tunnel merge identical between the integration picker and the assets-page one.
│   │   ├── autoMonitorStorageService.ts # "Auto-Monitor Storage" feature (AD/Entra workstation+server classes only): storage-mount analog of autoMonitorInterfacesService. Pure resolver over a multi-block union (byNames / byPatterns / `all`) against each asset's latest `AssetStorageSample.mountPath` rows (72h-bounded DISTINCT ON) + DB-bound aggregate/preview/apply. Reuses `compilePattern` from the interfaces service. Strictly additive to Asset.monitoredStorage. Net-new — no legacy shape coercion. Mounts come from the Polaris Agent, so the picker populates only after agents report. `loadLatestStorage` is EXPORTED (like its interfaces sibling) for `massPinService` — the Mass Pinning section needs the same mount inventory for an arbitrary asset-id set, and duplicating the query would let the 72h staleness bound drift between the two pickers.
│   │   ├── massPinService.ts # Backend for the Assets-page **Mass Pinning** section (Settings modal): manual bulk pin/unpin of fast-cadence targets across a condition-filtered device set. `buildPinInventory` (pure) groups per-asset inventory by name and stamps each device's current pinned state from the provenance-correct array (tunnel rows read `monitoredIpsecTunnels`, real interfaces `monitoredInterfaces`, storage `monitoredStorage`), **index-encoding** devices as `{a: <index into assets[]>, pinned}` so hostnames appear once rather than per row; `getPinInventoryForAssets` wraps it over the EXPORTED `loadLatestInterfaces` / `loadLatestStorage` (so the 72h staleness contract is shared with the integration pickers, not re-derived) and drops dead-parent tunnels. `computeFinalPinArrays` (pure) merges one asset's deltas: pins dedupe against the existing array, an unpin of EITHER interface-family field removes the name from BOTH interface arrays (provenance can drift between the inventory fetch and the apply, and "stop fast-polling this name" is the intent either way), a contradictory pin+unpin nets to the pin, and any final array over `MASS_PIN_ARRAY_CAP` (64, mirroring UpdateAssetSchema) sets `capField` so the caller skips the WHOLE asset rather than writing partial fields. `applyMassPins` read-modify-writes in chunked `Promise.allSettled` batches of 50 (the applyAutoMonitorForClass pattern — per-asset arrays differ so updateMany can't apply) and writes ONE `asset.pins.bulk_updated` Event (asset.updated's trackFields don't cover pin arrays). **DELTAS, not final arrays** is the load-bearing choice: a whole-array replace would clobber a concurrent hand-pin of an unrelated name on the same asset, so last-writer-wins applies only to the same (asset, name). Unlike the auto-monitor apply passes this surface SUBTRACTS — safe here because every change is explicit operator intent on a specific pair, not an unattended per-discovery sweep. Deliberate non-actions on unpin: no monitorOverride recompute (it reads only `monitored`), no recordOperatorPinChanges (process/service pins only), no alert cleanup (interface/tunnel triggers gate on the pin set so readings stop and `clearVanishedStates` closes firing rows; storage triggers have no pin gate).
│   │   ├── agentAutoDeployService.ts # Discovery-time auto-deploy of the Polaris Agent to newly-discovered, agent-less AD/Entra workstations/servers. `inferAgentPlatform` (OS string → windows/darwin/linux) + `pickTransportAndCredential` (windows→WinRM-or-SSH, else SSH) are pure; `runAutoDeployForClass` is the DB-bound eligibility (no existing ManagedAgent, reachable host) + bounded-concurrency kickoff that reuses agentInstallService.startInstall. Opt-in (default off), idempotent (one ManagedAgent per asset), paced (≤maxConcurrent new installs per class per cycle, RUN_CEILING backstop). Emits agent.autodeploy.{kickoff,skipped,batch} Events.
│   │   ├── presenceVerificationService.ts # Post-discovery network-presence verification for AD/Entra-discovered assets (default on; `config.verifyPresence` toggle on the Monitoring tab). Directory timestamps no longer write Asset.lastSeen, so this pass establishes presence per asset, cheapest signal first: already-fresh lastSeen (e.g. FortiGate discovery sighted it) → agent heartbeat (ManagedAgent.lastSeenAt) → answering monitor probe (monitorStatus up/recovering + fresh lastMonitorAt) → single ICMP echo against dnsName||hostname (stored ipAddress is often stale). Ping failure writes NOTHING — absence of pong is not evidence of absence. `classifyPresenceSignal` is the pure cascade; the runner is bounded (concurrency 16, 2s/ping, 3-min pass deadline, skip counts reported — no silent caps) and batches lastSeen writes via $transaction. Emits an `integration.presence_verification` summary Event per pass.
│   │   ├── macAddressService.ts     # AssetMacAddress side-table WRITERS (moved from utils/macAddresses 2026-08 — utils stay pure): reconcileMacAddresses (discovery's in-memory-list sync; bulk INSERT…ON CONFLICT, deadlock-retried, never touches interface-fold rows) + reconcileInterfaceMacs (interface-scrape fold → [mac, macEnd] range rows, source-scoped full-replace with the occupied-key slide). │   │   ├── assetMergeService.ts     # mergeAssets() — operator-driven asset merge (inverse of per-source Split). Re-binds the absorbed asset's AssetSource rows + MAC/IP/sighting history onto the survivor (delete-on-conflict), re-binds ManagedAgent iff survivor has none, carries dependency edges (transferDependencyEdges — dependents always re-point; parent links blank-fill, dependencyWinner resolves the both-sides conflict), applies per-field winners (MERGEABLE_FIELDS) + tag union + max(lastSeen) + OR-ed `monitored` (carrying MONITOR_CONFIG_FIELDS / MONITOR_PIN_FIELDS when that flips the survivor on, business rule 10 permitting), deletes the ghost (its sample history cascades). Backs POST /assets/:id/merge. Two of its pieces are exported and SHARED with `acceptAssetConflict`'s sibling-conflict ghost absorb (`services/conflictResolutionService.ts`) so a conflict merge preserves the same things an operator merge does: `absorbAssetRelations(tx, from, to, opts?)` (re-bind sources + the four side tables + a ManagedAgent the survivor lacks + dependency edges, returns the moved counts) and `resolveMonitoringCarry(update, canonical, ghost)` (the `monitored` OR-carry + config/pin adoption + monitor-state reset, business rule 10 enforced on the staged status). `transferAssetSideTables` is additionally shared with `assetGhostMergeService`.
│   │   ├── conflictResolutionService.ts # Discovery conflict resolution engine, extracted verbatim from the conflicts route file (2026-08 audit). Owns the list/count reads plus loadPendingConflict (same 404/409 AppErrors the handlers threw) and the accept/merge/reject resolution for both entityType variants: reservation accept (VIP merge-mode vs field-apply), asset accept (per-field merge with fieldWinners, NetBIOS hostname upgrade, sibling-conflict ghost absorption inside one $transaction via the shared `absorbAssetRelations` + `resolveMonitoringCarry`), the ip-override accept/reject narrow path, reject-creates-asset, and the `upsertConflictAssetSource` identity stamp. `conflictSourceFor` dispatches ad / entra / vcenter-vm / vcenter-host handling. Route keeps only visibility/permission gating and passes plain inputs (conflict row, actor username) — never req.
│   │   ├── duplicateIpConflictService.ts # Duplicate-address conflicts (business rule 40) — the third `entityType="asset"` Conflict flavour (`proposedAssetFields.collisionReason="duplicate-ip"`), raised by the `detectDuplicateIpAssets` sweep when two or more network-present Assets (status NOT in UNMONITORABLE_STATUSES) record the same `ipAddress`. Owns the whole lifecycle: `loadDuplicateIpClaims()` (ONE grouped SQL read whose CTE narrows to duplicated addresses before returning rows, LEFT JOINed to `AssetIpHistory` for the per-address timestamp), the pure decisions `claimIsOperatorOwned` / `claimIsCurrent` / `distinctDeviceCount` / `groupHasEligibleType` / `groupCurrentClaims` / `memberSetKey` / `pickPrimaryMemberId` / `toStoredMember` (a stale record is not a duplicate: a discovered claim must have been re-asserted within `CLAIM_FRESH_DAYS`=7, an operator-owned one never expires, rows sharing one non-null MAC are ONE device, and a group needs at least one claimant from `CONFLICT_ELIGIBLE_ASSET_TYPES` — switch / access_point / firewall / server — with the other claimants still carried so an endpoint that took an AP's address is named on the card; the scan's `dups` CTE prefilters on the same list via `bool_or`, a superset since SQL can't see the freshness verdict), `reconcileDuplicateIpConflicts()` (raise one pending Conflict per ADDRESS carrying every claimant in `proposedAssetFields.members[]` + a `conflict.detected` Event / refresh while pending / auto-close as `rejected` by `system:auto-resolved` when the duplicate resolves itself / suppress a re-raise while the last resolved row for that address is a `rejected` one with the SAME member set), plus TWO resolution verbs, one per real cause of a shared address — `reassignDuplicateIpAsset()` (`POST /conflicts/:id/reassign-ip` — writes ipAddress+ipOverride+ipSource="manual" in one update so the db.ts override guard defers, closes the asset’s pending ip-override conflict like the assets PUT does, refuses an address another network-present asset already holds, then closes the conflict as `accepted` or keeps it open on the survivors of a three-way collision) and `mergeDuplicateIpAssets()` (`POST /conflicts/:id/merge` with the duplicate-IP body — the records are ONE device, so the named members are absorbed into a survivor through `assetMergeService.mergeAssets`, the same engine the asset page's Merge modal and the conflict ghost-absorb use; `Conflict.assetId` is re-pointed at the survivor BEFORE the first merge, since deleting an absorbed asset cascades to conflicts pointing at it; targets are validated by the pure `resolveMergeTargets`, and field winners are deliberately not accepted — blank-fill is what every automatic absorb uses and per-field control lives on the Sources tab). Accept is REFUSED for this flavour (nothing to adopt); Reject = dismiss. Unit-tested in tests/unit/duplicateIpConflict.test.ts.
│   │   ├── descriptionSyncService.ts # Description sync (FMG + standalone FortiGate `syncDescriptions` toggle, default off; Polaris-primary). FortiOS field shapes flagged verify-on-real-device in the header.
│   │   ├── discoveryDurationService.ts # Rolling discovery-duration samples + "slow-run" threshold + auto-abort ceiling `autoAbortMs = max(2× avg, thresholdMs)` (Setting-backed)
│   │   ├── discoveryAutoAbortService.ts # Loop-breaker state for discovery auto-abort: after an auto-abort the NEXT overlong run is exempt (alternating abort/exempt) so a legitimately-grown fleet can complete once and refresh the duration baseline — aborted runs never record samples. │   │   ├── discoveryRunState.ts     # DB-backed live discovery-run state (DiscoveryRun table) — replaces the in-memory activeDiscovery Map; written by the discovery worker, read by the web process (progress, isDiscoveryRunning, slow-run check, cancel)
│   │   ├── discoveryCancelWatchdog.ts # Force-exit backstop for discovery cancel: armed when the run's abort signal fires, disarmed when runDiscovery unwinds. │   │   ├── discovery/discoveryEngine.ts # THE discovery engine — extracted verbatim from the integrations route file (which keeps only CRUD/proxy/trigger routes). │   │   ├── ldapClient.ts            # Shared ldapts connection helpers (withBoundLdapClient bind/unbind lifecycle, newLdapClient TLS, decodeObjectGuid, formatLdapError) + escapeLdapFilterValue (RFC 4515 filter-injection escape). │   │   ├── ldapAuthService.ts       # LDAP user authentication. │   │   ├── dnsService.ts            # Reverse DNS lookup for assets
│   │   ├── ouiService.ts            # MAC OUI lookup with admin overrides

Validates uploads (PNG/JPEG/WebP/SVG with magic-byte and SVG-security checks; 256 KB raster cap, 32 KB SVG cap), stores bytes in the DeviceIcon model, exposes resolveIconUrl(asset, cache) for the topology endpoint to stamp `iconUrl` on each node. **SVG uploads are transparently rasterized to 512×512 PNG** via `@resvg/resvg-js` (`rasterizeSvgToPng`) before storage — Cytoscape's `background-image` pipeline loads images through `new Image()` and design-tool SVG exports (Adobe Illustrator etc.) typically omit `width`/`height` and declare only `viewBox`, so the browser falls back to a tiny default natural size and the topology icon ends up anchored upper-left at a fixed pixel size at every zoom. Rasterizing on the server bypasses the whole class of bug. `rasterizeStoredSvgIcons()` is the matching backfill helper called from the one-shot startup job, idempotent via the mimeType filter; legacy `image/svg+xml` rows are migrated in place to PNG.
│   │   ├── eventArchiveService.ts   # Syslog (CEF) + SFTP/SCP event archival

Volume control: min-level filter → dedupe (collapse identical, sum count) → per-push cap (`maxPerPush`) → per-asset rolling-hour cap (`perAssetHourlyCap`, overflow → one `os_event.suppressed` summary). │   │   ├── logFlagRuleService.ts    # User-defined log-flag rules (Feature C). Operators define rules that FLAG matching process-log lines; evaluated at READ time over the /process-logs window (no per-row persisted flag → new/edited rules retroactively flag history). Rules cached + compiled once (module-level, `invalidateLogFlagRuleCache()` on every write). `compileRule` → matcher (substring/regex/glob + caseSensitive + minLevel gate; invalid regex never matches, never throws). `applicableRules(rules, assetId, name)` scopes global|asset|process. `evaluateLogFlags(assetId, name, rows, onlyFlagged)` annotates each line with matched rules. Backed by the `LogFlagRule` table; CRUD routes in `src/api/routes/logFlagRules.ts` at `/api/v1/log-flag-rules`.
│   │   ├── eventLogService.ts       # Shared audit-event writer: `logEvent` (never throws; drops rows below the operator-configured min level via eventArchiveService's cached retention read; stamps levelRank at write time), `logEventsBatch` (batched `createMany` variant for high-fan-in audit sources like OS event-log ingest — same min-level drop + levelRank stamping, one write instead of N awaits), `buildChanges` (before/after diff for update events), `LogEventInput`. Also the discovery per-asset audit helpers — `snapshotMaterialAssetFields` / `computeMaterialAssetChanges` (pure diff over a material-field whitelist) / `logDiscoveryAssetCreated` (`asset.discovered`) / `logDiscoveryAssetUpdated` (`asset.discovery_updated`, fires only on a material-field change so unchanged discovery passes emit nothing), called from each discovery write site in discoveryEngine.ts so a specific asset's discovery history surfaces on its details Events tab (`resourceType=asset`). Also the per-asset **change-event builders** — `computeFirmwareChange` / `buildFirmwareChangedEvent` / `buildConnectionChangedEvent` / `buildFirewallChangedEvent` — behind the four edge-triggered actions `asset.firmware.changed` (os/osVersion moved), `asset.switch_port.changed` (`lastSeenSwitch`), `asset.wireless_ap.changed` (`lastSeenAp`, every roam) and `asset.gateway_firewall.changed` (freshest FortiGate sighting flipped). They are PURE (return `LogEventInput | undefined`, no Prisma) so discovery loops accumulate into one `logEventsBatch` and the change decisions unit-test on their own; `logDiscoveryAssetUpdated` itself emits the firmware event whenever its material diff carries os/osVersion, which is the single seam covering all nine snapshot-based discovery paths. Semantics differ deliberately by kind: firmware suppresses a null→value first learn (identification, not an upgrade) while a connection event reports it (first observed attachment is the record worth having), and connection values compare trim+case-insensitively because two subsystems write the same AP under different casing. Unlike the `change.*` family these four are written UNCONDITIONALLY — never behind `isChangeActionSubscribed` — and their `notificationTypes.CHANGE_TYPES` entries only give the automations wizard a picker over an always-present event. See TOUCHES.md → cross-cutting/asset-change-events. Extracted from the events route so services don't import from the route layer; `src/api/routes/events.ts` re-exports the older helpers for the ~42 legacy importers (deliberately NOT the change-event builders — new code imports those from the service).
│   │   ├── projectionDriftService.ts # Projection drift detection. After every successful AssetSource upsert, compares projectAssetFromSources output against current Asset values; logs disagreements to pino with `event: "asset.projection.drift"`. Best-effort and fire-and-forget.
│   │   ├── ipOverrideService.ts     # Operator IP pin (Asset.ipOverride) side effects around discovery writes, invoked fire-and-forget from the src/db.ts guard AFTER the write lands. Release path (discovery staged the pinned IP; pin cleared in the same write): auto-closes pending ip-override Conflicts + stamps `asset.ip_override.released` Event. Re-assert path (discovery staged a DIFFERENT IP): raises/refreshes ONE pending Conflict per asset — entityType="asset", proposedAssetFields `{collisionReason:"ip-override", ipAddress:<discovered>, ipSource, overrideIp, hostname}`, existingAssetSnapshot refreshed while pending — and skips re-raising an IP the operator already rejected (the most recent rejected row is the dedup marker). `resolvePendingIpOverrideConflicts(assetId, resolvedBy)` closes pending rows (status="rejected", auto-resolution convention) — also called by the assets PUT when the operator sets/clears the pin. All best-effort; never breaks the underlying write.
│   │   ├── discoveredHostnameService.ts # "What would the hostname be if the operator pin were cleared?" — batched read of the AssetSource blobs run through projectAssetFromSources, returning the discovery-projected hostname per assetId. Exists because Asset.hostnameOverride makes the pinned value THE hostname, so the discovered name is stored nowhere on the row. Queried ONLY for rows that carry a pin (the assets list passes just those ids from enrichAssetList; GET /:id one asset) and surfaced as the wire field `hostnameDiscovered`, which the list Hostname cell + the slide-over Hostname row print as a subdued second line under the pinned name. Computed rather than stashed at write time so it stays live (tracks what discovery says today) and needs no migration/backfill. Pure core `projectHostnamesFromSourceRows` is unit-tested.
│   │   ├── serviceInventoryService.ts # Service-inventory (systemd unit / Windows service) CURRENT-STATE writer. `persistAssetServices(assetId, rows)` full-replaces the asset's AssetService rows in one delete-then-insert $transaction (retryOnDeadlock — same shape as persistAssetProcesses/persistSdwanRules); `isServiceControllable(s)` derives the control flag (systemd loaded/non-masked, or any Windows service). Single writer: the agent `serviceInventory` sample stream. Agent-only (agentless doesn't resolve units).
│   │   ├── serverSettingsService.ts # HTTPS, branding, backup/restore
│   │   ├── backupService.ts        # Database backup + restore. Owns the whole mechanism, extracted from serverSettings.ts (2026-08). `createBackup({password, kind, actor})` STREAMS `pg_dump` stdout → gzip → optional AES-256-GCM cipher → `data/backups/<id>`, registers the file in the `backup_history` Setting row, and returns `{record, path}` — the route streams that file to the client, so peak memory is a couple of stream watermarks instead of three copies of the dump (the prior version was `execSync` + `readFileSync` + `gzipSync` + in-memory cipher + `res.end(payload)` under a 120 s cap, which blocked the web role's event loop for the whole dump and failed or OOMed at the documented 50 GB DB sizing). `restoreBackup({filePath, password})` detects encryption from the magic header, decrypts through a stream, and wraps the psql run in the documented TimescaleDB sequence — `timescaledb_pre_restore()` / restore / `timescaledb_post_restore()` in THREE separate sessions, with post_restore in a `finally` so a failed restore can never leave the database in restoring mode (previously absent entirely, which made restores on any Timescale install unreliable). Connections ride libpq PG* env vars via `utils/pgEnv.ts`, never argv. Progress-based watchdog (`NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS`) replaces the fixed wall-clock cap. Also owns `listBackups` / `getBackupRecord` / `deleteBackup` / `backupFilePath` (traversal-checked) / `isEncryptedBackupFile` / `timescaleInstalled`. **Post-restore the pool is recycled** (`prisma.$disconnect()` in the `finally`): `--clean --if-exists` drops and recreates every table, so connections opened beforehand hold stale relation OIDs and fail with `XX000 could not open relation with OID <n>` — the route additionally returns `restartRequired: true` and the UI shows a restart banner, because a dump from a different schema version also invalidates the running generated client and the other roles have their own pools. File format unchanged so pre-existing backups still restore: `"POLARIS\0"|salt(32)|iv(16)|authTag(16)|gzip(sql)` ciphertext.
│   │   ├── backupScheduleService.ts # Operator-configured AUTOMATIC backups (`backupSchedule` Setting; Server Settings → Maintenance → Scheduled Backups). Default `enabled:false` — many sites already back this Postgres up with an enterprise product, and an upgrade must not start writing gigabytes unasked. Shape `{enabled, intervalHours(1-168), hourUtc(0-23|null), retainCount(1-50), passphrase, copyToDir, lastRunAt, lastError}`. `isScheduledBackupDue(schedule, now)` is PURE (unit-tested): never-run ⇒ due immediately (enabling produces a recovery point now, not intervalHours later); otherwise due once intervalHours elapse since the last SUCCESS; a pinned `hourUtc` holds an otherwise-due run until that hour but runs anyway past 2× the interval so a host that was down through its window is not skipped forever. `copyBackupOffHost` copies each finished backup to a mounted share (best-effort — a full share must not fail a good backup). Passphrase masked on read / preserved on masked write like every other secret surface, and strength-checked through `utils/backupPassword.ts`.
│   │   ├── credentialService.ts     # Named credential store (SNMP / WinRM / SSH / REST API / HTTP) with masking + secret-preservation merge. `http` is the odd type out: it carries almost no secret (an optional bearer token or basic password) and instead describes an HTTP GET HEALTH CHECK — scheme, port, path, the status that counts as up, the body text that must be present. It lives here rather than in a table of its own because a check is a per-STREAM selectable thing and this store already is exactly that: pickable at the asset / class-override / integration tiers, sealed at rest by the db.ts extension, masked at the API boundary, and testable from the Test Connection modal. `validateHttpConfig` COMPILES a `regex` match pattern at save time — an invalid one would otherwise fail once per asset per interval forever, discovered from a probe error column rather than the form it was typed into — and canonicalizes `path` so the stored value equals the request line. Semantics in utils/httpCheck.ts
│   │   ├── manufacturerAliasService.ts # Manufacturer alias map: CRUD + cache + idempotent default seed + backfill of existing Asset/MibFile rows
│   │   ├── assetTypeService.ts        # AssetTypeDef registry: CRUD + cache refresh + idempotent built-in seed + the match-rule preview/apply pair. `listAssetTypes({withUsage})` joins `prisma.asset.groupBy` for the Device Types card's per-row "N assets" column. Rename path is a `$transaction` that rewrites every Asset row holding the old name to the new name atomically with the registry-row update; delete refuses while any Asset still references the type. Built-in rows (`isProtected=true`) are immutable in IDENTITY only — `updateAssetType` scopes the 403 to a name/label/description change and lets the three matching columns through on any row. After every mutation calls `refreshCache()`, which installs BOTH caches in one go (`setAssetTypeRegistry` for `isKnownAssetType`, `setAssetTypeMatchRegistry` for the resolver) — they must never be separately warm, or discovery would type devices by the previous rules with no surface saying so. `previewMatchRules(draft?)` / `applyMatchRules()` are bounded to assets currently typed **`other`**, which is not a UI convenience: it is the same guard the discovery engine has always applied before re-typing an existing asset, so preview, apply and discovery cannot disagree about what is eligible, and a type an operator set by hand is never overwritten. Apply groups its writes into one `updateMany` per TARGET TYPE inside one transaction — bounded by the registry size (~10-15), not the fleet — and re-asserts `assetType: "other"` in each WHERE so a discovery run landing between the read and the write is a no-op rather than a clobber.
│   │   ├── mibService.ts            # SNMP MIB module storage + minimal SMI parser. `parseMib` validates uploads (extracts moduleName + IMPORTS) on the upload hot path. `parseMibStructured` is the heavier peer used by the Browse modal + MIB-aware walk: extracts SYNTAX (with INTEGER enum value labels), MAX-ACCESS / ACCESS, STATUS, DESCRIPTION, INDEX clauses, and SEQUENCE OF table structure. Per-symbol parse failures degrade to "name + parentName known, everything else null" rather than dropping the symbol — operators can still walk it, they just don't get decoding. Parses on demand; `oidRegistry` already keeps every MIB's contents in memory after `ensureLoaded()`. The module-name head regex tolerates mixed-case (`SNMPv2-MIB`, `SNMPv2-SMI`) to match the IETF-canonical names IANA distributes — required for the bundled std MIBs, also fixes the latent edge case where an operator uploaded an RFC-published MIB whose name carries a lowercase `v` segment.
│   │   ├── stdMibLibrary.ts         # Browse-tree + MIB-aware walk support for the eleven bundled standard MIB modules behind twelve keys (SNMPv2-MIB, IF-MIB, HOST-RESOURCES-MIB, ENTITY-MIB, ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB, LLDP-MIB, POWER-ETHERNET-MIB, BRIDGE-MIB, Q-BRIDGE-MIB, RSTP-MIB, IP-MIB; IF-MIB backs both `std:interfaces` and `std:if-ext`). `std:ip` is the ip group — `ipNetToPhysicalTable` (the neighbour cache: ARP for IPv4, NDP for IPv6) plus the deprecated RFC 1213 `ipNetToMediaTable` it replaced, and `ipAddressTable`; it resolves 267 symbols / 0 unresolved with no `BUILT_IN_OIDS` seed, unlike Q-BRIDGE and RSTP. Loads each text file from `stdMibs/<MODULE>.txt` lazily on first request, runs it through the same `parseMibStructured` as uploaded MIBs, then resolves every symbol's `fullOid` against `BUILT_IN_OIDS` only (no DB MIB layering, and no cross-MIB visibility between bundled modules either — a module anchored on a sibling's IMPORTed symbol needs that anchor seeded in `oidRegistry`, which is why `dot1dBridge` / `dot1dStp` are seeded for Q-BRIDGE-MIB and RSTP-MIB). Cache is module-level immutable for the process lifetime — std MIBs don't change at runtime. Exposes `listStdMibs()` / `getStdMibDef(key)` / `getStdMibStructure(key)` / `resolveStdSymbol(key, name)` consumed by the three new routes in `src/api/routes/mibs.ts`. Refresh the bundle via `node scripts/fetch-std-mibs.mjs` (writes SHA-256 + source URL into `stdMibs/SOURCES.md`). LLDP-MIB anchors at `{ iso std(0) iso8802(8802) ieee802dot1(1) ieee802dot1mibs(1) 2 }` using ASN.1 named-number syntax — handled by the `NAMED_NUMBER_RE` extension in `oidRegistry.tryResolveParts`, a strict improvement that benefits any uploaded vendor MIB using the same idiom.
│   │   ├── mibParserUtils.ts        # Shared `stripComments` helper consumed by both `mibService` and `oidRegistry` so the comment-aware string-literal scanner doesn't drift between the two parsers.
│   │   ├── oidRegistry.ts           # Symbolic name → numeric OID resolver. Per-asset **scoped** resolution: device-specific MIBs override vendor-wide MIBs override generic MIBs override the built-in SMI seed. Each scope is computed lazily and cached; cache + parsed entries refresh on MIB upload/delete and at app startup. Tracks per-symbol provenance so the UI can show which MIB provided each resolved name. Exposes `resolveSymbolsForMib(mibId)` and `resolveSymbolForMib(mibId, name)` so the MIB Browse + Walk endpoints can resolve every symbol declared by a chosen MIB at the MIB's natural scope (its own manufacturer + model layer, falling back through vendor-only and generic) without re-implementing the layer pass.
│   │   ├── manufacturerProfileService.ts # CRUD + module-cached resolver for the editable `ManufacturerProfile` data model (Slice 6a). `refreshProfileCache()` is called at boot by `seedManufacturerProfiles` and after every write; `getProfileFor(manufacturer)` is the sync getter the hot probe path calls. Exposes `listProfiles` / `getProfile` / `createProfile` / `updateMetricRow` / `createOverride` / `updateOverride` / `deleteOverride` / `createWidget` / `updateWidget` / `deleteWidget` / `deleteProfile` consumed by `src/api/routes/manufacturerProfiles.ts`. Manufacturer strings are alias-canonicalized on create, regex `modelPattern` validity is checked at write time, and transform/combiner kinds are validated against the matching registry in `src/utils/symbolTransforms.ts` based on the row's `type` (unary `TransformKind` on `scalar`/`table`; binary `CombinerKind` on `double_scalar`). **Per-row shape validation** via `validateMetricRowShape` — enforces the symbol-pair invariant: `scalar` requires `symbol`, `symbolB` must be null; `double_scalar` requires both `symbol` (A) + `symbolB` (B); `table` requires `symbol`, `symbolB`+`transform` must be null. An unconfigured metric row with all of symbol/symbolB/transform null is treated as the legitimate "use built-in seed" state and passes validation regardless of `type`.
│   │   ├── vendorTelemetryProfiles.ts # Per-vendor SNMP CPU/memory/temperature/disk profile registry. Maps `manufacturer + os + model` regex → symbolic OID names; resolved through oidRegistry at probe time. Seeded into the editable `ManufacturerProfile` model on first boot (Slice 6a); the runtime probe path now consults the DB via `pickVendorProfileMerged` (Slice 6c) which layers operator-edited symbol choices + per-model overrides on top of a clone of the hardcoded entry. Operator-untouched profiles preserve full parity (seeded `defaultSymbol` == hardcoded primary symbol) so existing fleets see identical probe behavior. The constant stays as a fresh-install fallback while the DB cache warms up. Transforms from `symbolTransforms.ts` are not yet applied at sample-write time — that plumbing lands in a follow-up. Profile shape carries optional `cpu` / `memory` / `disk` / `temperature` queries — temperature is a single-scalar form for vendors whose hardware publishes one Celsius reading instead of the table-based ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB walk (consumed by `collectTemperaturesSnmp` as a third fallback after ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB + the Fortinet `fgHwSensorTable` sensor-name heuristic). Profile selection is `pickVendorProfile(manufacturer, os, model, assetType)`: the regex haystack is `manufacturer + os + model` PLUS the class hint from `fortinetClassHint(manufacturer, model, assetType)`, which returns "FortiSwitch" / "FortiAP" for a Fortinet-manufactured `switch` / `access_point` whose model doesn't already name a class. The hint exists because identity was riding a display string: a managed switch has no `os`, `MODEL_RULES` in utils/assetProjection.ts deliberately skips the fortiswitch source's own model, and an asset that reached manufacturer "Fortinet" with an EMPTY model matched only the generic FortiOS entry — so CPU/memory were read from `fgSysCpuUsage`/`fgSysMemUsage` under the FortiGate root 12356.101, which a FortiSwitch doesn't publish. That was a deadlock, not a miss: the FortiOS profile carries no `model` query, so `fsSysVersion` was never read and the empty model could never be filled in (prod 2026-08-31, FSR-112D-POE — see business rule 24 for why the misroute charted a flat 0% instead of an error). `pickVendorProfileMerged` applies the same hint when matching the DB profile's `modelPattern`, which is tested against the model ALONE and would otherwise fall back to the manufacturer-wide `fgSysCpuUsage` default and overwrite the correct symbol. Built-ins for Cisco / Juniper / Mikrotik / Fortinet FortiSwitch (matched before generic Fortinet via `model="FortiSwitch"` or the assetType hint; CPU uses `fsSysCpuUsage` @ 12356.106.4.1.2 scalar percent; memory uses bytes form via `fsSysMemUsage` @ 12356.106.4.1.3 + `fsSysMemCapacity` @ 12356.106.4.1.4 — NOT a percent like the FortiGate variant — all three seeded into oidRegistry so the probe works without uploading FORTINET-FORTISWITCH-MIB) / Fortinet FortiAP (matched before generic Fortinet via `model="FortiAP"` or the assetType hint; distinct OID root @ 12356.120 — FortiAPs don't expose anything under FortiGate's 12356.101 or FortiSwitch's 12356.106; CPU = `fapCpuUsage` @ 12356.120.3.41 scalar percent; memory = `fapMemoryUsage` @ 12356.120.3.42 scalar percent (single-value form like FortiGate, NOT FortiSwitch's bytes form); temperature = `fapTemperature` @ 12356.120.3.44 scalar Celsius; all three seeded into oidRegistry so the probe works without uploading FORTINET-FORTIAP-MIB) / Fortinet (SNMP path) / HP-Aruba / Dell. The FortiSwitch profile additionally carries a `model` identity query (`fsSysVersion` @ 12356.106.4.1.1, seeded) — the combined "model-firmware" string parsed by `utils/fortiswitchModel.ts` — which splits on `[-\s]v<digit>`, since the separator is a hyphen on most models ("S548DF-v7.2.5-…") but a SPACE on FortiSwitch Rugged ("FortiSwitchRugged-112D-POE v7.4.8,…"), and doesn't re-prefix a token that already says "FortiSwitch"; `collectSystemInfoSnmp` reads it on the heavy pass and `recordSystemInfoResult` adopts the parsed "FortiSwitch <token>" onto `Asset.model` while the stored model is still empty or the generic "FortiSwitch…" discovery literal (edge-triggered, `asset.model_detected` Event; operator-typed models are never overwritten, and the projection's deliberate fortiswitch-model skip means discovery can't clobber it back). Not part of the editable ManufacturerProfile surface.
│   │   ├── monitorOverrideService.ts # Asset monitor-override semantics. `Asset.monitorOverride` is an **explicit operator-intent bit** — true when an operator deliberately set this asset's `monitored` state away from the discovering integration's per-class `addAsMonitored` default. It is the (monitored XOR addAsMonitored) divergence but is WRITTEN only at operator-action time; nothing re-derives it from incidental state, so incidental divergence (decommission clamp, created-before-flag-enabled, HA standby) leaves it false and self-heals. All SQL paths use the same `assets.config #>> '{<klass>Monitor,addAsMonitored}'` JSON-path technique the cutover migration uses — keep these in sync.
│   │   ├── monitorSettingsService.ts # Business logic for the four-tier monitor-settings hierarchy CRUD, extracted from `src/api/routes/monitorSettings.ts` (which keeps only Zod parsing + permission gates). Manual-tier Setting("manualMonitorSettings") read/upsert, integration-tier `Integration.config.monitorSettings` read/rewrite, MonitorClassOverride CRUD (Phase 2 manual-scope-only guards — integration-scoped writes 400; service-layer uniqueness for the NULL-integrationId case Postgres's @@unique can't catch), and the asset-overrides reverse lookup. `assertPollingCompatible` (source-kind matrix + per-stream STREAM_METHODS + the ICMP-only-on-response-time rule) lives here and guards integration-tier + class-override writes. Every write calls `invalidateMonitorSettingsCache` for the matching scope and logs an Event. Resolution itself stays in `monitoringService.ts` (`resolveMonitorSettings`) — this service owns only the tier CRUD.
│   │   ├── monitoringService.ts     # Authenticated response-time probes (fortimanager/fortigate/snmp/winrm/ssh/icmp) + System tab telemetry (CPU/memory) + system-info (interfaces/storage) collection. runMonitorPass dispatches all three cadences; per-stream tier-aware retention prune helpers. **Prune layer is fleet-coordinated**: `runRetentionPrune` (the single entry called from `monitorAssets`'s heavy loop) gates on a persisted `Setting("lastRetentionPruneAt")` (24h cadence, `RETENTION_PRUNE_INTERVAL_MS`) and takes a Postgres session-level advisory lock (`pg_try_advisory_lock(0x504c5253,1)` on a dedicated `getDirectDatabaseUrl()` connection) so only ONE monitor replica prunes at a time — the rest return `{skipped}`. Inside the lock it runs `pruneMonitorSamples` / `pruneTelemetrySamples` / `pruneSystemInfoSamples`, one prune per (table × tier) — detail (column `timestamp`), hourly + daily (column `bucketStart`) — with retention from `getSampleRetention()` (per-class: `default` / `switch` / `accessPoint`), then bumps the persisted timestamp.
