Intentionally narrower than the full `discoverDhcpSubnets` pipeline — only touches `dhcp_reservation` + `dhcp_lease` rows on this subnet, leaves manual / VIP / interface-IP rows alone (the IP-level conflict reconciliation that the full sync runs is deferred to the next integration-wide discovery cycle). 400 when the subnet wasn't discovered by an FMG/FortiGate integration or has no `fortigateDevice`. Returns `{ lastDiscoveredAt, created, updated, released, skipped }`. Writes one `subnet.refresh` Event. See `subnetRefreshService.ts`.

### Reservations — `requireAuth`
- `GET    /reservations`                        — List (filter by owner, projectRef, status, createdBy). Each row is decorated with `pushEligible: boolean` computed from the row's `subnet.integration` (true when the originating integration is `fortimanager`/`fortigate` AND `config.pushReservations === true` AND `ipAddress` is non-null). The integration config blob is stripped from the response — callers only need the computed flag and config can carry credentials. The mobile Reservations tab uses this flag to color the **Reserve** button green when confirming will also write the entry to the FortiGate.
- `POST   /reservations`                        — Create. An omitted `owner` auto-stamps to the caller's username (mirrors the PUT auto-stamp; an explicitly typed owner wins). Body accepts an optional `macAddress` (12 hex with optional `:`, `-`, or `.` separators). When the target subnet was discovered by an FMG integration with `pushReservations=true`, MAC becomes **required** and the create attempts a write+verify against the FortiGate — see `reservationPushService.ts`. Outcomes: (a) push success → reservation returned with `pushStatus="synced"` and `pushedScopeId`/`pushedEntryId` stamped; (b) **transient device-side failure** (FortiGate offline, FMG unreachable, network timeout, generic 5xx — classified by `classifyPushError`) → reservation persists with `pushStatus="pending"`, `pushQueuedAt=now`, `pushAttempts=1`, `pushError=<message>`, and the retry job pushes it once the gate recovers (see "Queued push lifecycle" below); (c) **permanent failure** (4xx, verify mismatch, auth) → create aborts with a clear 4xx/5xx (no Polaris ghost). **Pre-flight optimization**: if the originating FortiGate's firewall Asset is monitored AND `monitorStatus="down"`, the transport attempt is skipped entirely and the row is queued immediately (saves the 15s+ transport timeout on the create critical path). Audit Events: `reservation.push.succeeded` (info, synced path), `reservation.push.queued` (info, transient path), `reservation.push.failed` (warning, permanent path) — in addition to the usual `reservation.created` Event. The same MAC + push behavior applies to `POST /reservations/next-available`.
- `POST   /reservations/next-available/preview` — Which addresses WOULD be allocated: `{ subnetId, count (1..64), contiguous? }` → `{ ips, count, contiguous }`. Backs the IP panel Auto-Allocate modal's **Multiple IPs** mode, which fills a row per address so the operator can name each one before anything is written. Creates nothing, so it is gated `reservations:read` rather than the ownership gate the create carries; declared before `/:id`. Selection is `reservationService.findNextAvailableIps` over the pure `utils/ipAllocation.ts`, and the taken-set is EVERY active reservation regardless of `sourceType` — so a VIP or an interface IP is simply never offered. `contiguous` is refused rather than downgraded when it can't be met (409 naming the largest run that exists) — a short run is not what was asked for. The modal then creates each row through `POST /reservations` with an explicit `ipAddress`, ONE REQUEST PER ADDRESS: a push-eligible network writes every reservation to the FortiGate, so a 40-address batch behind one request would outlive the proxy read timeout with nothing to show. Per-row requests buy progress while it runs, a per-row outcome when it finishes, and an honest report when an address was claimed by someone else between the preview and the create. Ceiling is `MAX_BULK_ALLOCATE` (64) — a bound on how big a form an operator can be asked to fill in, not a database limit.
- `GET    /reservations/:id`
- `PUT    /reservations/:id`                    — Update. **Refuses (409) on a `vip` or `interface_ip` row** — see the DELETE note below.  Body accepts `hostname` / `owner` / `projectRef` / `expiresAt` / `notes` plus `macAddress` (string; empty clears it, only allowed on non-push-eligible subnets). When the subnet is push-eligible AND the MAC changes, the service pushes a PUT to the FortiOS reserved-address entry via `updatePushedReservation()`, verifies on read-back, then commits the Polaris write — device-side failure throws and the Polaris row stays untouched so the two views never drift. Discovered (never-pushed) DHCP reservations look the entry up by IP on the resolved scope and are upgraded to "Polaris-pushed" on success. Hostname-only or notes-only changes are NOT re-pushed (the FortiOS description only refreshes as a side effect of a MAC update — when MAC changes, the new hostname/notes are picked up alongside). **Queued rows (`pushStatus="pending"`) skip the device-update path entirely** — the new payload is just stashed in Polaris and the retry job will use it on the next push attempt. MAC may be freely changed on a queued row (still required, can't be cleared). Audit: `reservation.push.updated` (info) on success, `reservation.push.update_failed` (warning) on failure.
- `DELETE /reservations/:id`                    — Release. **Refuses (409) on a `vip` or `interface_ip` row**: a FortiGate virtual IP and a statically-configured router/firewall interface address are owned by the DEVICE's own config, not by anything Polaris granted, so Polaris reports them and offers no Reserve / Release / Edit. Creating over one was already refused (neither sourceType is in `isSupersedableByCreate`, so the collision check 409s); `assertNotDeviceOwned` in the route file closes the other two verbs. Enforced at the ROUTE layer rather than in the service, because discovery's own reconcile still has to refresh and retire these rows. The IP panel renders both read-only with a purple `.ip-dot-device-config` status dot ("VIP" / "Interface"), and the mobile reservations tab drops Edit + Release for the same two types.  Best-effort unpush from the FortiGate before flipping the row to `released`. Device-side failure does **not** block the release — Polaris release proceeds and writes `reservation.unpush.failed` (warning) so the orphan on the device is auditable. "Already absent" (operator deleted on the device) writes `reservation.unpush.succeeded` with `alreadyAbsent: true`. **Queued rows (`pushStatus="pending"`) skip both the unpush AND the lease-release blocks** — nothing has been written to the device yet, so there's nothing to clean up; the release just flips the Polaris row and writes `reservation.push.queued.released` (info) for the audit trail. **Discovered `dhcp_lease` rows additionally fire a best-effort lease release** against the originating FortiGate (`POST /api/v2/monitor/system/dhcp/release-lease` with `{ip}`, routed through the same FMG-or-standalone-FortiGate transport as reservation push), gated on the originating integration's `pushReservations` toggle (the **DHCP Push** tab — both halves of the Polaris → FortiGate DHCP write path live under that single toggle). When the toggle is off, freeing a lease only flips the Polaris row and the FortiGate is not contacted. When it's on, FortiOS only forgets the *current* lease — the same client can DHCP-acquire the IP back on its next request, so this is "expire now" not a block. Success writes `reservation.lease_release.succeeded` (info); device-side failure writes `reservation.lease_release.failed` (warning) without blocking the Polaris release.

#### Stale-reservation alerts (mixed scoping)
- `GET    /reservations/stale-settings`         *(auth)* — `{ staleAfterDays }`. 0 = disabled.
- `PUT    /reservations/stale-settings`         *(admin)* — `{ staleAfterDays }`. Default 60. The setting feeds both the `flagStaleReservations` job and the alert lister; lowering it is reflected within ~6 hours (the next job tick).
- `GET    /reservations/alerts?show=active|ignored` — Default `active` returns non-ignored stale rows **on non-deprecated subnets**; `ignored` returns every row the operator has set `staleIgnored=true` regardless of threshold or subnet status so admins can review and un-silence. Each entry: `{ id, ipAddress, hostname, macAddress, subnetId, subnetCidr, subnetName, createdAt, lastSeenLeased, lastSeenArp, staleNotifiedAt, daysSinceSeen, fortigateDevice, pushedToId, pushedToName, assetLastSeen, assetPresenceMatch }`. `assetPresenceMatch` (`"mac" | "ip" | null`) + `assetLastSeen` report the Asset that correlated to the reservation; `daysSinceSeen` counts from the freshest of the DHCP lease, the ARP confirmation (`lastSeenArp`), and that asset's lastSeen, so a statically-addressed device that's still on the network never appears here. Reservations whose subnet is `deprecated` (its owning FortiGate was decommissioned) are excluded from the active list/count entirely — the network is gone, so per-IP stale alerts would be noise.
- `GET    /reservations/alerts/count`           — Just `{ count }`. Always counts the **active** list — ignored rows don't drive the sidebar badge.
- `POST   /reservations/:id/snooze`             *(user-or-above)* — Sets `staleSnoozedUntil = now + staleAfterDays` so the row is suppressed from the active alert list. Cleared automatically when discovery sees the IP active again. Returns `{ reservationId, snoozedUntil, daysAdded }`. Writes `reservation.stale.snoozed` (info).
- `POST   /reservations/:id/stale-ignore`       *(networkadmin)* — Permanently ignore stale alerts on this row (`staleIgnored=true`). NOT cleared by discovery activity; operator's intent persists across online/offline cycles. Writes `reservation.stale.ignored` (info).
- `DELETE /reservations/:id/stale-ignore`       *(networkadmin)* — Un-ignore. Writes `reservation.stale.unignored` (info).

#### Queued push lifecycle (mixed scoping)
- `GET    /reservations/push-queue`             *(auth)* — Lists every reservation in `pushStatus IN ("pending", "failed_permanent") AND status="active"`, sorted by `pushQueuedAt` ascending (oldest first). Each row carries the full reservation plus `subnet: { id, cidr, name, vlan, fortigateDevice }` and `pushedTo: { id, name, type, enabled }` so the UI can render hostname / IP / MAC / target FortiGate / integration name without N+1 fetches. Drives the **Push queue** filter view in the Events page Alerts panel.
- `GET    /reservations/push-queue/count`       *(auth)* — `{ count }`. Contributes to the Events Alerts button badge and the single Events sidebar dot, alongside discovery conflicts (`/conflicts/count`) and stale-reservation alerts (`/reservations/alerts/count`). The dot is red when there are conflicts and yellow otherwise (red precedence); there is no separate IPAM dot.
- `POST   /reservations/:id/retry-push`         *(reservations write — own rows; fullwrite for any)* — Operator-triggered single-row retry. Allowed when `pushStatus IN ("pending", "failed_permanent")`. Bypasses the monitored-gate `monitorStatus="up"` readiness gate AND the unmonitored-gate exponential backoff window. `failed_permanent` rows are flipped back to `pending` first so the retry path treats them uniformly. Still respects eligibility re-check (subnet drift cancels the queue + keeps the Polaris row as plain manual) and discovery-supersede (collision → `failed_permanent`). Returns `{ outcome: "synced" | "transient" | "permanent" | "cancelled" | "superseded", reservation }`. Writes `reservation.push.queued.retry_manual` (info) on entry, plus the same per-outcome Events the periodic retry tick emits.

### Utilization — `ipBlocks read`
Blanket-gated at the mount: the reports enumerate the IP space, so they carry the same read gate as the blocks they describe. Bearer tokens (no role snapshot) and `ipBlocks=none` roles get 403.
- `GET    /utilization`
- `GET    /utilization/blocks/:id`
- `GET    /utilization/subnets/:id`

### Dashboard — `requireAuth` (per-section permission filtering)
- `GET    /dashboard/summary[?sections=blocks,recent,assetTypes,monitorAlerts][&recentSourceTypes=manual,dhcp_reservation,...]` — Backs the home Dashboard's built-in IP-space widgets. `?sections=` narrows the response to the named sections so each widget fetches only what it renders (widgets call it via the 15s-memoized `PolarisWidgets.getSummary({sections,...})`); absent = the full legacy shape `{ blockUtilization, recentReservations, assetTypeCounts, monitorAlerts, monitorAlertsOverflow }`. Unknown section names drop silently. Every section is served through a 10s server-side TTL cache (keys carry the recent-section params) so concurrent widgets/tabs share one computation; permission-denied sections return empty without entering the cache. `blockUtilization` is reused from `utilizationService.getGlobalUtilization()` (no extra DB hit). `recentReservations` is the 10 most-recent active reservations — default filter is `sourceType="manual"` so DHCP discoveries / leases / VIP echoes don't crowd out reservations a person actually typed in; the optional `recentSourceTypes` query param (comma-separated source-type names) lets a widget broaden the filter (e.g. include `dhcp_reservation` to surface Polaris-pushed reservations alongside manual rows). Unknown source-type values are dropped silently; if every value is unknown the filter becomes a no-op rather than 0 rows. Each row includes hostname, MAC, createdBy, and the resolved `{subnetId, subnetCidr, subnetName, vlan}` so the card renders without a second fetch. `assetTypeCounts` is a `prisma.asset.groupBy` over `assetType` excluding `status in (decommissioned, disabled)` — feeds the SVG pie chart. `monitorAlerts` is monitored assets currently in `warning` or `down`, ordered by `monitorStatusChangedAt desc nulls last` (newest transitions first), capped at 50 with `monitorAlertsOverflow` flagging when there's more. **Filter-don't-403 gating**: the dashboard is the redirect target for users bounced off gated pages, so the endpoint never 403s — instead each section is gated on the caller's read access (`ipBlocks≥read` → blockUtilization, `reservations≥read` → recentReservations, `assets≥read` → assetTypeCounts + monitorAlerts) and denied sections return empty arrays with the response shape unchanged. Bearer-token callers have no role snapshot → all sections empty. Covered by `tests/integration/permissionGates.test.ts`.
- `GET    /dashboard/noc-summary[?feeds=topCpu,downNodes,...]` — Feed endpoint backing the SolarWinds-style NOC widgets (status tiles, Down Assets, Down Interfaces, Highest Avg CPU/Memory, Slowest Response, Packet Loss, Highest Disk Usage, Highest Temperature, Stale Polls, Recent Reboots, Active Alerts, Sites with Issues, Status Map uses `/map/sites` instead). `?feeds=` (names from `nocDashboardService.NOC_FEED_NAMES`; `status` = the three tile keys, `downNodes` unwraps `.nodes`) narrows to the named subset so each widget fetches only its own feed and renders as soon as that query returns; unknown names drop silently; absent = the full payload. Every (feed, filter, cap) computation is served through a 10s server-side TTL cache (`NOC_FEED_CACHE_TTL_MS`) shared across widgets/tabs/kiosk walls. The full shape: `{ statusCounts:{total,up,down,warning,unknown,recovering,maintenance}, uptimePercent, activeAlertCount, downNodes[], downInterfaces[], downIpsecTunnels[], topCpu[], topMemory[], slowestResponse[], packetLoss[], diskUsage[], temperature[], stalePolls[], recentReboots[], activeAlerts[], sitesWithIssues[] }` (`diskUsage[]` rows carry a `detail` = mount path; `temperature[]` rows are per-sensor — latest reading per (asset, sensorName) from the temperature-class rows of `asset_hardware_sensor_samples`, always °C, with `detail` = sensor name). **Maintenance-window assets are excluded from every down/warning/stale feed** (`status="maintenance"` freezes `monitorStatus`, so the frozen value is not live state — the shared `NOT_IN_MAINTENANCE` where-spread in `nocDashboardService`, mirrored in the sites-with-issues raw SQL and the `/summary` monitorAlerts clause) and are instead counted into `statusCounts.maintenance` (still in `total`, never in up/down/warning/unknown or the uptime gauge) — the Status Summary widget's purple "Maint" tile. `?includeDependencyDown=1` (the Down Assets widget's gear toggle; "1"/"true"/"yes") drops the `dependencySuppressed: false` filter from the `downNodes` feed — absent (the default) keeps suppressed assets out so a dead gate reads as ONE outage rather than one per device behind it, and the flag participates in that feed's cache key (`usesDepDown`) so a toggled widget can never be served the excluded list. Every `downNodes[]` row carries `dependencySuppressed`, which the widget renders as a "Dep. Down" badge. `downNodesTotal` = the TRUE (uncapped) down-asset count from an indexed `asset.count` over the same where — the Down Assets widget stamps it as a red pill on its header, so the overall number is exact even when `downNodes[]` is clipped by the row cap. `downInterfaces[]` = interfaces that are admin-up but oper-down AND selected for monitoring — the CTE joins `assets` on `ifName = ANY(monitoredInterfaces)` so only pinned interfaces qualify, filtered before the LIMIT (`getDownInterfaces`, one windowed single-pass CTE over `asset_interface_samples` for latest-per-`(asset,ifName)` + last-up timestamp, then a monitored-scope hydrate findMany), each row `{assetId, hostname, ipAddress, assetType, ifName, ifLabel, gate, lastUpAt}` where `gate` = the FortiGate the interface lives on (firewall → own hostname; managed FortiSwitch/FortiAP → parent `learnedLocation`). `downIpsecTunnels[]` = fully-down IPsec tunnels that are ALSO selected for monitoring — same pin gate as interfaces, joining `assets` on `tunnelName = ANY(monitoredIpsecTunnels)` before the LIMIT, so an unpinned tunnel (e.g. one riding a dead parent link, whose CMDB-synthesized samples stay perpetually fresh) never shows as an outage (`getDownIpsecTunnels`, same CTE shape over `asset_ipsec_tunnel_samples` where `status='down'`), each row `{assetId, hostname, ipAddress, assetType, tunnelName, parentInterface, remoteGateway, gate, lastUpAt}` — `parentInterface` is the phase1-interface WAN port the tunnel rides. The frontend `downInterfaces` widget (labeled "Down Interfaces") merges both arrays into one gate-grouped list — gates ordered **youngest outage first** (newest `lastUpAt` among the gate's rows; the row-limit clip also keeps the freshest outages), rows **alphabetical by name within each gate**, and the merged pre-clip total stamped as a red pill on the widget header (`PolarisWidgets.setHeaderCount`) — rendering a down tunnel's parent physical interface inline; its config has per-kind toggles (`showInterfaces` / `showTunnels`). Sections computed by `nocDashboardService.getNocSummaryPayload` (feed registry + per-feed TTL cache), each scale-checked flat to 2000 assets (groupBy / count / one windowed DISTINCT-ON or aggregate / one bounded findMany — no per-row awaits). Same **filter-don't-403** contract as `/summary`: asset-sourced sections gate on `assets≥read`, Event-sourced sections (`activeAlerts`, `recentReboots`) on `events≥read`; denied sections return empty/zero with the shape unchanged (and never enter the cache). Accepts optional per-widget filters `?assetTypes=` (the enabled built-in types) + `?regionTags=` (region names — the caller's "My regions" or a widget's Selected-regions pick) + `?fortigates=` (FortiGate device names — the widgets' Selected-FortiGates per-site narrowing; matches assets behind any named gate via `learnedLocation` / `AssetFortigateSighting`, exact-insensitive — the same haystacks as the tag/maintenance "Behind FortiGate" criteria — with the `__none__` sentinel = the picker's "(No FortiGate)" entry for gate-less assets; combined with regions + asset types this builds one-site dashboards, e.g. a single gate's switches/APs) → `resolveFilteredAssetIds` (cached per filter) constrains every requested feed to the matching asset set. Frontend memoizes for ~15s **per (feeds, filter, limit)** via `PolarisWidgets.getNocSummary(opts, feeds)`. `topCpu`/`topMemory` rank by the per-asset **average of the most-recent N samples** (not the instantaneous last reading) — N comes from `?samples=` (the widgets' "Average over" gear control; default 10, clamped to a 100 ceiling, 1 = latest sample only; the frontend omits the param at the default so those widgets share one cached payload, and only the sample-averaged feeds key their server cache on it); `slowestResponse` averages a fixed most-recent 10. `packetLoss[]` excludes assets at 100% loss (zero successful probes in the window, enforced in the SQL HAVING) — a hard-down node is Down Assets material, not packet loss. Every list widget has a shared Row-limit control (`5/10/20/50/100/1000`; helpers in `public/js/widgets/index.js`); a widget picking the **1000** option sends `?limit=N` (clamped to a 1000 ceiling) which caps every *requested* feed at N — ≤100 omits the param, shares the default-cap payload, and clips client-side (the four `_topnBar` widgets default to a 20-row limit with the red-row guarantee; see the widgets file-map entry). The `summary` endpoint takes a parallel `?recentLimit=` (default 10, clamped 1000) for the recentReservations widget. The `getNocSummary`/`getSummary` fetches carry a 20s client abort-timeout so a large request degrades instead of hanging the widget.

### User Dashboard — `requireAuth`
Per-user dashboard layout. One row per user in `UserDashboard`; absent row = empty dashboard. No admin override (strictly per-caller); no Event audit log (UI preference, not security-relevant).
- `GET    /me/dashboard` — Returns the caller's layout, or `{ version: 2, columns: [] }` when no row exists yet (drives the "Customize Page → Add Widgets" empty-state). NOT re-validated — a stored legacy v1 row is returned untouched and migrated to v2 client-side.
- `PUT    /me/dashboard` — Zod-validates the full v2 layout, upserts, returns the saved shape. Layout shape: `{ version: 2, columns: Column[] }` where `Column = { id (uuid), width 3|4|6|12, widgets: WidgetInstance[] }` and `WidgetInstance = { id (uuid), type, height 1|2|3, config }`. Caps: ≤12 columns, ≤64 widgets total (superRefine). The client always migrates v1→v2 before saving, so PUT only accepts v2.

### Table tabs — scope-resolved function key (per-user)
The Assets page's view tabs. Same scope→key resolution as saved filters below, but both verbs need only **read**: a tab is the operator's own view of data they can already see, so a readonly user gets tabs. Strictly per-caller (no admin override), no Event audit — UI preference, the `/me/dashboard` pattern. Session callers only.
- `GET /me/table-tabs?scope=assets` — `{ version: 1, tabs: [{ id, name, state, savedFilterId, savedFilterName }], activeId }`, or the empty layout `{version:1,tabs:[],activeId:""}` when the caller has never saved tabs (the client then materializes one default tab from whatever the table is showing and doesn't write until something changes).
- `PUT /me/table-tabs?scope=assets` — full replace. ≤20 tabs, unique ids, names ≤40 chars; each tab's `state` goes through the same `sanitizeFilterState` a preset does. A stale `activeId` (tab closed in another window) falls back to the first tab instead of 400-ing the layout away.

### Saved table filters — scope-resolved function key
Named filter+sort presets for a list page (Assets → Filters ▾). There is no dedicated function key: the request's `scope` resolves to the key that already gates that page (`assets` → `assets`), checked inline with `ensureRoleSnapshot` + `hasPermission` because the key isn't known until the body/query is read. Session callers only — a preset has an owner, and bearer tokens have no user identity (401).
- `GET    /saved-filters?scope=assets`   *(scope key: read)* — `{ filters: [{ id, scope, name, visibility, ownerId, ownerName, isOwner, state, createdAt, updatedAt }] }` — everything the caller owns plus every other user's `public` preset, name-ascending. Orphaned private rows (owner deleted) match nobody and are invisible.
- `POST   /saved-filters`                *(scope key: read; `write` when `visibility:"public"`)* — Body `{ scope, name, visibility, state }`. Publishing to everyone is a write to shared state; keeping a private preset only needs the read the page already required. A same-(scope, owner, name) POST **updates** the existing row instead of duplicating, so the client's "save over this name" flow is one call. 201 with the saved DTO.
- `PUT    /saved-filters/:id`            *(owner only, same level rules)* — Rename / re-scope visibility / replace state. `scope` cannot be changed.
- `DELETE /saved-filters/:id`            *(owner: read; someone else's: `fullwrite`)* — 204. The fullwrite branch is housekeeping (a departed colleague's shared preset).
`state` is validated by `sanitizeFilterState` on every write — see the service entry; anything table-sf.js can't itself produce is a 400 rather than stored.

### Users — `users` function key
- `GET    /users`                               *(read)* — Every row is returned with the joined `role: { id, name, color, isProtected, isBuiltIn }` and `regionTags: string[]` (per-user scope).
- `POST   /users`                               *(write)* — Body: `{ username, password, roleId, regionTags?, otherTags? }`. The legacy `role: <enum>` field is no longer accepted.
- `GET    /users/:id`                           *(read)*
- `DELETE /users/:id`                           *(write)* — Refused with 409 when this would leave Polaris with zero users holding `users=fullwrite` AND `roles=fullwrite` (last-admin-equivalent invariant).
- `PUT    /users/:id/password`                  *(write)* — Local accounts only.
- `PUT    /users/:id/role`                      *(write)* — Body: `{ roleId }`. Refused with 400 when reassigning yourself; 409 when this would break the last-admin-equivalent invariant. Auto-clears `needsRoleReview` since picking a role is an implicit review.
- `PUT    /users/:id/regions`                   *(write)* — Body: `{ regionTags?: string[], otherTags?: string[] }` (each optional; omitted dimension left unchanged, empty array clears). Validation via `tagNormalize`: trim, drop empties, dedupe case-insensitively, ≤64 entries, each ≤64 chars. Writes one `user.regions_updated` Event with the per-dimension from/to diff. These are operator-set tags only — group-derived tags are computed at `/auth/me`, never written here.
- `DELETE /users/:id/totp`                      *(write)* — Admin-initiated TOTP reset (for "lost device" recovery). Clears the secret and backup codes so the user can re-enroll on next login.
- `GET    /users/role-review-notifications`     *(read)* — Sidebar feed. Returns `{ users, count }` where `users` is every row with `needsRoleReview=true`, ordered by `lastLogin` asc, projected to `{ id, username, role: { id, name, ... }, regionTags, displayName, authProvider, email, lastLogin, createdAt, ... }`. Polled every 30s by [public/js/app.js](public/js/app.js) for admins only.
- `DELETE /users/:id/role-review`               *(write)* — Dismiss the new-user notification for one user (global — hides the row for every admin).

### Roles — `roles` function key
- `GET    /roles`                               *(read)* — Every Role with `{ id, name, description, permissions, regionTags, color, isBuiltIn, isProtected, userCount, createdAt, updatedAt }`. The frontend filters `isProtected=true` rows (admin + readonly) out of the editable list.
- `GET    /roles/:id`                           *(read)*
- `GET    /roles/functions`                     *(read)* — `{ accessLevels: ["none","read","write","fullwrite"], functions: FunctionKeyDef[] }` — the 25-key catalogue with `{ key, label, description, hasOwnershipDimension? }`. Single source of truth backing the permissions slide-over matrix.
- `POST   /roles`                               *(write)* — `{ name, description?, permissions, regionTags?, color? }`. Name validated against `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{2,32}$/` + case-insensitive uniqueness against existing names + the reserved `admin` / `readonly`. `color` validated as `#rrggbb` (empty/null clears). Permissions normalized: unknown function keys dropped, missing keys defaulted to `"none"`.
- `PUT    /roles/:id`                           *(write)* — Body accepts any subset of `{ name?, description?, permissions?, regionTags?, color? }`. Refused with 403 when the role is `isProtected=true` (admin / readonly). Bumps the role-version cache + writes one `role.updated` Event with per-field diff (including a per-functionKey `permissionChanges` map listing only the keys whose level changed).
- `DELETE /roles/:id`                           *(write)* — Refused with 409 when `isBuiltIn=true` OR when any user holds the role (admin must reassign first).

### Group Mappings — mounted at `/group-mappings`, gated `users:fullwrite`
- `GET    /group-mappings`                      — All mappings (optional `?provider=oidc|ldap|saml`). Each: `{ id, provider, groupKey, groupLabel, roleId, roleName, regionTags, otherTags, enabled, description, createdAt, updatedAt }`.
- `GET    /group-mappings/:id`
- `POST   /group-mappings`                      — `{ provider, groupKey, roleId?, regionTags?, otherTags?, enabled?, description? }`. `groupKey` normalized per provider (LDAP lowercased-DN, OIDC/SAML exact); 409 on duplicate `(provider, groupKey)`. Warning Event when `roleId` is admin-equivalent.
- `PUT    /group-mappings/:id`                  — Subset of the above (provider is immutable).
- `DELETE /group-mappings/:id`

### Integrations — `integrations` function key
> Mount requires `integrations=read`; all write endpoints inside the file are upgraded to `integrations=write` via an inline `router.use(...)`.
- `GET    /integrations`                       — List integrations (paginated). Each row carries `discoveryBaseline: { avgMs, sampleCount } | null` from `discoveryDurationService.getBaselines()` so the card UI can render an "Avg Discovery Time" line operators can size `pollInterval` against. `null` until the rolling window has ≥3 successful runs.
- `POST   /integrations`
- `GET    /integrations/:id`
- `PUT    /integrations/:id`
- `DELETE /integrations/:id`
- `POST   /integrations/:id/test`                — Test connection (also `POST /integrations/test` for unsaved config; `POST /integrations/:id/test/fortigate-sample` + `POST /integrations/test/fortigate-sample` for sample-pull dry runs)
- `POST   /integrations/:id/discover`           — Trigger full discovery run
- `GET    /integrations/discoveries`            — List in-flight discoveries. Each entry: `{ id, name, type, startedAt, elapsedMs, activeDevices: string[], slow: boolean, slowDevices: string[], totalDevices: number | null, completedCount: number, skippedOfflineCount: number, skippedErrorCount: number }`. `slow` flips true when the overall run exceeds its rolling-duration baseline; `slowDevices` lists FortiGates (FMG-only) whose per-device elapsed exceeds that device's baseline. The four progress counters power the sidebar's "N/M complete · K skipped (offline)" line for FMG runs: `totalDevices` is parsed from the `discover.devices` info-level message ("Found N managed device(s) …") and stays null until the roster is fetched; `completedCount` bumps on `discover.device.complete`; `skippedOfflineCount` on info-level `discover.device.skip` (conn_status mismatch — gate down or unmanaged); `skippedErrorCount` on error-level skips and per-device errors. Standalone FortiGate runs leave the counters at their initial values since there's one device. This endpoint also calls the slow-run checker inline, so the UI sees amber within one 4 s poll cycle. See `discoveryDurationService` + the `discoverySlowCheck` job. For FMG-type discoveries, `activeDevices` additionally has the integration name prepended whenever the per-integration FMG worker has any inflight calls (proxy or native), so the sidebar shows the FMG itself as busy during roster fetch + mgmt-IP resolves + native CMDB scrapes — not just during per-device work. In the sidebar popup each `activeDevices` name is clickable (`openDiscoveryDevice` in [public/js/app.js](public/js/app.js)): it resolves the FortiGate name to its firewall Asset by hostname and opens the asset slide-over (in place on `/assets.html`, else via the `#view=asset:` hash); a no-match — the transient FMG self-entry, or a not-yet-inventoried FortiGate — surfaces a toast.
- `GET    /integrations/health-summary`          — Sidebar polling target. Returns `{ failed: [{ id, name, type, lastTestAt }] }` listing enabled integrations whose latest connection test failed (`enabled=true AND lastTestOk=false`). Gated by `integrations=read`. Polled every 30 s by [public/js/app.js](public/js/app.js); rendered as a red sidebar notice (`#integration-failed-status`) that links to `/integrations.html` on click. Pairs with the [integrationConnectionTester](src/jobs/integrationConnectionTester.ts) background job which is the writer that keeps `lastTestOk` fresh.
- `DELETE /integrations/:id/discover`            — Abort an in-flight discovery. *(admin-equivalent: upgraded to `integrations=fullwrite` via an inline `requirePermission` guard — `networkadmin` with `write` can run discoveries but cannot abort them. The frontend hides the abort ✕ for callers below `fullwrite`.)*
- `POST   /integrations/:id/query`              — Manual API proxy. FortiManager: `{method, params}` (JSON-RPC) or `{mode:"fortigate", deviceName, method, path, query?, body?}` (REST direct to a managed FortiGate — FMG resolves the mgmt IP, the integration's direct-mode FortiGate API token authenticates). FortiGate: `{method, path, query?, body?}` (REST). Both REST forms take `method ∈ GET|POST|PUT|DELETE`; `body` is a JSON payload attached for POST/PUT only, and any non-GET writes a warning-level `integration.query.write` Event (ad-hoc device writes are audited, body included). **Both REST forms also accept an optional per-request credential override `{apiToken?, apiUser?}`** (`overrideFortigateCreds`): it swaps `apiToken`/`apiUser` for a standalone FortiGate, or `fortigateApiToken`/`fortigateApiUser` for an FMG in bypass mode — never the FMG's own `apiToken`, which is still needed to resolve the gate's management IP. Exists because bypass mode stores ONE FortiGate token for the whole fleet, so testing a different per-gate token otherwise means editing the integration and repointing discovery/polling/DHCP-push at an unproven credential. The override is used for that one request and persisted nowhere: not on the integration, not in the Event (which records only `usedTokenOverride: true`), and not in the browser's saved-query localStorage entry. A masked-placeholder value (`••••••••`) is rejected rather than sent as a token. It widens no privilege — the route already requires `integrations:write`, which can rewrite the stored token outright. Entra ID: `{path, query?}` GET-only against `graph.microsoft.com`; path must begin with `/v1.0/` or `/beta/`. Active Directory: `{filter?, baseDn?, scope?, attributes?, sizeLimit?}` LDAP search; baseDn defaults to the integration's configured base DN.
- `GET    /integrations/:id/interface-aggregate?class=fortigate|fortiswitch|fortiap|workstation|server` — Auto-Monitor Interfaces "By name" data source. **Served from `Integration.interfaceAggregateCache`** (`getCachedInterfaceAggregate`), the precomputed checklist refreshed at the end of every successful discovery run — so the modal loads instantly instead of running a fleet-wide DISTINCT ON over `asset_interface_samples` on every open. Returns `{ rows: [{ ifName, ifType, deviceCount }], computedAt }` (the heavy per-row `devices[]` list is dropped from the cache — the UI only renders the three fields + a device count), sorted by deviceCount desc. **Live-compute fallback**: when the cache has no entry for this class yet (the window before the integration's first post-feature discovery) the route falls back to `getInterfaceAggregate` and returns `computedAt: null`. The expensive aggregate (latest `AssetInterfaceSample` per `(assetId, ifName)` for assets where `discoveredByIntegrationId = :id` AND `assetType` matches the class, plus synthetic IPsec-tunnel rows for the fortigate class) now runs in the discovery process at end-of-run, not on the interactive web path. There is no operator "Refresh from latest discovery" button anymore — the list re-populates each discovery cycle and the modal shows an "As of last discovery: …" timestamp.
- `POST   /integrations/:id/interface-aggregate/preview` — Live preview for the modal. Body: `{ class, selection: AutoMonitorInterfacesSchema | null, baselineSelection?: AutoMonitorInterfacesSchema | null }`. Returns `{ deviceCount, interfaceCount, perDeviceMax, sampleDevices: [{hostname, pinNames: string[]}], diff? }`. Read-only: does not persist or write `monitoredInterfaces`. `interfaceCount` is the sum of pin lengths produced by `selection` alone (not unioned with operator-pinned interfaces). **`baselineSelection` is optional**: when supplied, the service computes pin sets for BOTH selections from a single DB fetch and returns a `diff: { addedCount, removedCount, addedSample: [{hostname, ifName}], removedSample: [{hostname, ifName}] }` block enumerating per-`(assetId, ifName)` adds/removes. Drives the "+X added · −Y removed" inline delta hint on the auto-monitor card; frontend tracks the previously-sent selection per-card and passes it as the baseline so each checkbox toggle's preview shows what THAT toggle just changed (not the delta from saved). First preview-after-modal-open uses the saved selection as baseline so it shows no diff; subsequent toggles each show their own per-click change. Older UI builds that don't send `baselineSelection` get the same response shape as before — no `diff` field. **As of the cache work, the frontend only calls this endpoint for `byLldp` selections** (topology isn't in the cache); `byNames` / `byPatterns` / `byTypes` previews are computed instantly client-side from the already-loaded `interfaceAggregateCache` rows (`computeClientPreview` in `public/js/integrations.js`) — exact for `byNames`, an upper bound for `byPatterns`/`byTypes` with `onlyUp` (the cache has no per-device `operStatus`), labeled as such. This endpoint stays the authority for the LLDP case and for the **Test against fleet** button.
- `POST   /integrations/:id/interface-aggregate/apply` — Apply-on-save trigger. Body: `{ class }`. Reads the current `selection` from `Integration.config.<klass>Monitor.autoMonitorInterfaces` (whatever was most recently saved) and runs the same apply pass that fires at the end of every discovery: union into each matching asset's `monitoredInterfaces` (additive only). **Fire-and-forget: returns `202 { queued: true }` immediately** and runs `applyAutoMonitorForClass` in the background — the resolve scans every asset's latest interface samples (a multi-second-to-minutes query at fleet scale) and awaiting it wedged the modal's "Applying…" state for minutes. Safe because the apply is strictly additive + idempotent AND re-runs on every discovery (Phase 2c), so a fire-and-forget lost to a process restart self-heals. Writes one `integration.auto_monitor_interfaces.applied` Event on completion when something changed, or `integration.auto_monitor_interfaces.error` (warning) on failure. Called by the integration edit modal's **Save Changes** button for each per-class block whose selection is non-null; the modal confirms "applying in the background" rather than reporting pin counts.
- `POST   /integrations/:id/auto-monitor-assets/preflight` — Save-Changes confirm-modal data source. Body: `{ proposed: { firewall?, switch?, access_point?, workstation?, server? } }` carrying the operator's in-flight `addAsMonitored` choices. Returns `{ integrationId, integrationName, classes: { <classKey>: { currentAddAsMonitored, proposedAddAsMonitored, total, overridden, wouldEnable, wouldDisable } } }` — `wouldDisable` counts assets that would have monitoring swept OFF if this save lands (non-override only), `wouldEnable` counts the inverse, `overridden` counts assets with `monitorOverride=true` that are protected from either direction. Each class entry is included only when `proposed[class]` was supplied. The frontend (`public/js/integrations.js`) calls this from the Save Changes click handler and renders a confirm modal when `wouldDisable > 0` on any class so the operator sees the blast radius before committing.

### Asset Types — `assets` function key
Operator-extensible asset-type registry, plus the **device-type matching** that decides which bucket a newly discovered device lands in. The historical built-ins (server / switch / router / firewall / workstation / printer / access_point / other, plus `hypervisor` and `kubernetes_cluster`) are seeded as `isBuiltIn=true, isProtected=true` rows and cannot be renamed or deleted — but their MATCHING is editable like any other row's, because `isProtected` guards identity (which code branches on) and nothing branches on how a device got into a bucket. Managed from Server Settings → **Identification → Device Types**. Behavioral special-cases (FortiGate / switch / access_point branches in dependency tree, fortinetTopology, polling source defaults, topology rendering) still fire only for the built-ins — custom types fall through to "other"-like generic behavior — but INFERENCE no longer does: a custom type can claim a device through its own rules. Mounted at `/api/v1/asset-types` BEFORE `/assets` so Express's first-match routing picks the registry endpoints instead of treating "types" as an asset id.
- `GET    /asset-types[?withUsage=1]`           *(read)* — `{ types: [{ id, name, label, description, isBuiltIn, isProtected, createdBy, createdAt, updatedAt, usageCount? }] }`. `usageCount` only included when `?withUsage=1` (one extra `prisma.asset.groupBy` to count assets per type — used by the Manage modal to show "N assets" badges and refuse delete when in-use).
- `GET    /asset-types/:id`                     *(read)* — Single row with `usageCount`.
- `POST   /asset-types`                         *(write)* — Body: `{ name, label, description?, matchRules?, matchContexts?, matchPriority? }`. `name` is lowercased + validated against `/^[a-z0-9_-]{2,32}$/` and rejected if it collides with a built-in. Writes one `asset_type.created` Event. Cache refresh fires immediately so the registry is hot for the next `/assets` write.
- `PUT    /asset-types/:id`                     *(write)* — Body accepts any subset of `{ name, label, description, matchRules, matchContexts, matchPriority }`. **Refuses with 403 on a built-in row only for an IDENTITY change** (name / label / description); the three matching fields are accepted on every row. Rename is transactional: every `Asset` row holding the old name is rewritten to the new name atomically with the registry row update via a `$transaction([asset.updateMany(...), assetTypeDef.update(...)])`. Writes one `asset_type.updated` Event.
- `DELETE /asset-types/:id`                     *(write)* — **Refuses with 403 on built-ins**, and **with 409 when any Asset still references the type** (operator must reassign or delete those assets first). Writes one `asset_type.deleted` Event.
- `GET    /asset-types/match-schema`            *(read)* — `{ fields, ops, contexts, authoritativeSources }`: the matching vocabulary plus the catalogue of paths rules CANNOT reach (Fortinet controller CMDB, vCenter inventory, Azure Arc, an operator's own edit), each with the reason it outranks them. Its own route, declared before `/:id`, so the Device Types card renders the server's list rather than a second copy that drifts — the `/assets/pin-filter-schema` precedent.
- `POST   /asset-types/match-preview`           *(read)* — Dry run. Body `{ draft? }`; with a draft (`{name, matchRules, matchContexts, matchPriority}`) the unsaved edit is substituted INTO the live registry rather than evaluated alone, since a clause only matters relative to the types that outrank it. Answers `{ examined, matched, byType[], sample[], truncated }` over the assets currently typed **`other`** — the same eligibility the discovery engine applies — with each sample row naming the clause that claimed it. Read-level: it writes nothing.
- `POST   /asset-types/match-apply`             *(write)* — The retroactive step, deliberately separate from saving a rule (a rule edit is cheap to undo, a fleet-wide re-type is not). Re-types the `other` assets the saved rules claim; answers `{ updated, byType[] }` and writes one `asset_type.rules_applied` Event when anything moved.

### Assets — `requireAuth`
- `GET    /assets`                              — List, **server-side filter / sort / pagination** (the assets page runs `TableSF` in server-side mode like Events; see UI-CANON.md → "Sortable + filterable data table"). Returns `{ assets, total, limit, offset }`. Filters: `status` / `assetType` (CSV multi-select, single value back-compat), `monitor` (the `_monitor` synthetic chip → `monitored` + `monitorStatus`), per-column operator-aware text filters (`<col>` + `<col>Op` of `contains|not_contains|empty|is_not_empty`), `server` (spans `location`+`learnedLocation`), `lastSeenFrom`/`lastSeenTo`, plus the legacy `department` / `search` / `createdBy`. `sortBy`/`sortDir` are whitelisted (400 otherwise); default `createdAt desc`. The list payload also carries `latitude`/`longitude` (the geographic pin behind the Device Map site marker) for the two sort-only, default-hidden list columns, and **`activeAlert`** — `{severity, count, unacknowledged}` or null, the worst uncleared alert on the row, from ONE `activeAlertSummaryByAsset` query per page (never per row — the export path takes up to 10 000). It drives the strobing dot beside the hostname in the Name column: coloured by that severity, and moving only while something is unacknowledged. `favoriteIds` (CSV) floats the operator's starred assets to the top of the whole result set via a two-bucket query. Indexed by `assets(createdAt)` + `assets(lastSeen)`.
- `POST   /assets`
- `GET    /assets/:id`
- `PUT    /assets/:id`
- `DELETE /assets/:id`
- `DELETE /assets`                              — Bulk delete
- `POST   /assets/import`                       — CSV import: backdate `createdAt`/`firstSeen` from serial+date rows (assets admin; `dryRun` for preview). PDF/CSV *export* is client-side (bundled jspdf + client CSV), not a route.
- `POST   /assets/import-pdf`                    — PDF import (assets admin)
- `POST   /assets/oui-lookup` / `POST /assets/:id/oui-lookup`  — OUI vendor lookup (by MAC in body; the `:id` form also stamps the asset)
- `POST   /assets/:id/dns-lookup`               — Reverse PTR lookup (IP → hostname); per-asset, user-triggered
- `POST   /assets/:id/forward-lookup`           — Forward A/AAAA lookup (hostname/dnsName → IP); fills ipAddress when missing
- `DELETE /assets/:id/macs/:mac`                — Remove one MAC from an asset's history (requires `assets` write)
- `GET    /assets/:id/ip-history`               — List IP history entries for an asset (filtered by retention days). Auto-populated by the Prisma query extension in `src/db.ts` whenever any `asset.create` / `asset.update` writes an `ipAddress`, so discovery-sourced IPs are captured without changes to integration services.
- `GET    /assets/ip-history-settings`          — `{ retentionDays }`; 0 = keep forever (default).
- `PUT    /assets/ip-history-settings`          *(assets admin)* — `{ retentionDays }`; saving immediately prunes any history rows with `lastSeen` older than the new cutoff.
- `GET    /assets/source-priority`              — the operator's Sources-column priority `{ order[], integrationPrefix, contributors[{kind,label,mode,describe,fortinetDevice}] }`. `contributors` arrives IN the operator's order (catalogue entries from `utils/assetSourceLocation.ts`) so the drag-and-drop list renders labels + "what this contributes" hints without hardcoding them client-side. Declared before `/:id`.
- `PUT    /assets/source-priority`              *(assets:write)* — `{ order?[], integrationPrefix? }`. Unknown or duplicated source kinds are 400s (the read path self-heals stored rows; a client posting a typo should hear about it); omitted kinds are appended in default order. Returns the same shape as the GET. Audited `asset.source_priority.updated` with the previous order. Takes effect per integration on its next discovery run — that's when `Asset.learnedLocation` is rewritten.
- `GET    /assets/:id/effective-monitor-settings` — Resolved settings for one asset PLUS per-field tier provenance (`asset` / `class` / `integration` / `manual` / `default` — the last meaning no tier set a compatible polling method and the materialized runtime source default is what `resolved` carries), `tier3Source` (`"integration"` or `"manual"`), `classOverrideId` when a class override applies, and `mibLookup: { [uuid]: {moduleName} }` mapping every non-null MIB UUID across the four streams to its `MibFile.moduleName` so the asset-details monitoring chips can render a `MIB: <module>` segment alongside the polling method / cadence / tier label without a second round-trip. Standard MIB ids (the `std:` namespace) are skipped — those resolve through the frontend-local `_SNMP_STANDARD_MIBS` table. Drives the asset edit modal Monitoring tab tier badges AND the asset details monitoring chip stack. See **Monitor Settings Hierarchy** below for the resolution order.
- `POST   /assets/bulk-monitor`                 *(assets admin)* — `{ ids, monitored, monitorCredentialId?, monitorIntervalSec?, probeTimeoutMs? }`. Flips `monitored` on every selected row + applies the supplied credential / cadence overrides uniformly. After the bulk write lands, runs `recomputeMonitorOverrideForAssets(prisma, ids)` (single SQL UPDATE) so each touched asset's `monitorOverride` reflects whether the new `monitored` value diverges from its discovering integration's per-class `addAsMonitored`. Manual / non-integration assets keep `monitorOverride=false`. The polling method comes from the resolver — per-asset choices live on PUT /assets/:id, not here. Returns `{ updated, errors: [{id, error}] }`.
- `GET    /assets/pin-filter-schema`            *(assets:read)* — The **Mass Pinning** section's device-filter vocabulary: `{ scopeCondition: scopeConditionMeta(SCOPE_FIELD_OPS), options: { ...listScopeOptions(), assetTypes, tags }, maxAssets }`. Its own route rather than reusing `/automations/schema` + `/scope-options`, which are gated `automationManagement:read` — pinning an interface must not require permission to edit automations (the `/contacts/filter-schema` precedent, and built from the same shared `scopeConditionMeta` so the vocabularies can't drift). Carries the NARROW automations field set, matching what the automation wizard's Devices step offers. MUST stay above `GET /:id`.
- `GET    /assets/ip-context?ip=`             *(assets:read)* — everything Polaris already knows about ONE address, for the manual Add Asset form. Returns `{ ip, subnet, reservation, arp[], sightings[], switchPorts[], existingAssets[], firewall, suggestions, visibility }` (services/ipContextService.ts). Read-only; creates nothing. Declared **before `/:id`** — a bare word would otherwise be captured as an asset id. The two IPAM halves are gated a SECOND time inside the handler on the caller's own `subnets:read` / `reservations:read` (the dashboard precedent), and `visibility` reports which halves were consulted so the panel renders "not shown" instead of asserting "no network found" for a role that could not look. An unparseable or half-typed address answers `200 {ip, unparseable: true}`, not 400: the caller is a debounced keystroke handler and a per-character 400 would be noise, not validation.
- `POST   /assets/pin-inventory`                *(assets:read)* — `{ allAssets? | condition?, facet: "interfaces"|"storage", mode: "count"|"full" }`. Resolves the condition tree SERVER-side via `loadScopeAssetIds` (the client never ships thousands of ids), then: `mode:"count"` → `{ matchedCount }` (the builder's debounced preview), `mode:"full"` → `{ matchedCount, overCap, inventory? }` where inventory is the aggregated-by-name checklist with per-device pinned state so the client renders tri-state from ONE call. A matched set over `MASS_PIN_MAX_ASSETS` (1000) answers `overCap: true` and NO inventory rather than truncating — the tri-state semantics ("pinned on ALL matched devices") are only honest over the complete set, and a silently-cut device list would make a "pin on all" click miss devices the operator believed were covered. A body with neither `condition` nor `allAssets:true` is a 400: a bare `{}` must never quietly mean the whole fleet.
- `POST   /assets/mass-pins`                    *(assets:write)* — `{ pin: [{assetId, name, field}], unpin: [...] }` where `field ∈ interfaces | ipsecTunnels | storage`. DELTAS, not final arrays, so a concurrent hand-pin of an unrelated name on the same asset is never clobbered. Returns `{ updatedAssets, pinsAdded, pinsRemoved, skipped: [{assetId, reason}] }` — an asset whose array would pass the 64-pin cap, a missing id, or a failed write is a per-asset **skip with reason**, never a batch-wide 400 (one 200-port chassis must not veto pins on 400 other switches). One `asset.pins.bulk_updated` Event per call. See `services/massPinService.ts`.
- `POST   /assets/:id/monitor-override/reset`   *(assets write)* — Clears the explicit `monitorOverride` pin and realigns the asset to its discovering integration's per-class Auto-Monitor default: resolves the flag via `getAddAsMonitoredFromConfig`, sets `monitored = <flag>` and `monitorOverride = false`, so discovery resumes auto-managing the asset. 400 when the asset has no `discoveredByIntegrationId` or its assetType isn't subject to Auto-Monitor. Writes one `monitor.override_reset` Event. Backs the "Reset to integration default" button beside the **Asset Override** badge on the asset-details System tab.
- `GET    /assets/:id/monitor-history?range=1h|24h|7d|30d` *or* `?from=ISO&to=ISO`  — Sample stream for the chart. With `range`, the window ends at *now*; with `from`/`to`, both bounds come from the query (span capped at 1 year). Returns `{ range, since, until, tier, bucketSeconds, lastSuccessAt, downDetection, samples, stats: { total, failed, successRate, packetLossRate, avgMs, minMs, maxMs } }`; `range` is `"custom"` when `from`/`to` was used. `responseTimeMs` is null on failed samples (the "packet loss" signal). `lastSuccessAt` is the newest **successful detail** sample at/after `since` (`readLastMonitorSuccessAt`), populated only on rollup tiers and null on detail (where the series answers it) or when no detail success exists in the window: on a rollup tier every sample timestamp is a `bucketStart`, so the chart's stale banner would read a healthy 1-minute probe as ~a day stale the moment the operator switched to 30d. **`downDetection`** is `{ passive, missedPolls, recoveryPolls }` (or null) — the covering automation's two counts, from `describeDownDetectionFor` + `recoveryPollsFor`. The chart replays them through the shared `PolarisMonitorStates.replay` to colour its dive (amber while the count is short of `missedPolls`, red once it reaches it) and its climb (blue until `recoveryPolls` answers have landed), so the line speaks the same four states as the Last-30-min strip above it. It rides THIS payload rather than a second request because a threshold arriving later would repaint the outage under the operator; `passive: true` means nothing may go red, and an absent block is the unknown case that keeps every miss red. `recoveryPolls` costs an extra asset read only when the automation actually sets a reset hold — otherwise it IS the missed-poll count.
- `POST   /assets/:id/snmp-walk`                *(admin)* — Operator-driven SNMP walk for the asset details **SNMP Walk** tab. Body: `{ credentialId, oid?, maxRows? }`. `credentialId` is any stored SNMP credential (not necessarily the asset's monitor credential — admins can spot-check a host with a different community). `oid` defaults to `1.3.6.1.2.1.1` (system subtree); validated as a numeric dotted OID. `maxRows` defaults to 500, hard-capped at 5,000. Returns `{ rows: [{oid, type, value}], truncated, durationMs, oid, host }` — `type` is the symbolic ASN.1 type name (Counter32, OctetString, OID, IpAddress, ...) and `value` is a printable representation (UTF-8 OctetString when printable, hex otherwise; IpAddress is dotted-quad). Walks the asset's `ipAddress` directly — does not consult the asset's resolved polling method, so it works on any asset including unmonitored ones. Each call writes one `asset.snmp_walk` Event (`info` on success, `warning` on failure). 400 if the asset has no IP or the credential is not type `snmp`; 502 if the SNMP session itself fails.
- `POST   /assets/:id/probe-now`                *(user-or-above)* — Run an immediate response-time probe AND telemetry (CPU/memory), temperature, and system-info pulls in parallel; returns `{ success, responseTimeMs, error?, telemetry: { supported, collected, error? }, temperature: { supported, collected, error? }, systemInfo: { supported, collected, error? } }`. Per-stream statuses let the System tab's **Poll Now** button toast tell the operator which streams polled and which failed (`collected: false` with an `error` is the common case when, e.g., FortiManager-discovered assets in proxy mode have no direct `fortigateApiToken` configured — the SNMP-override probe succeeds but the FortiOS REST system-info call throws "FortiManager direct-mode API token not configured"). The `temperature` stream dispatches on `temperaturePolling` independently from `telemetry`'s `cpuMemoryPolling`, so the toast can show "CPU/memory ok · temperature failed via REST" when only the sensor-info endpoint is unreliable on a branch-class FortiGate. An empty sensor list is rendered as `temperature: n/a (no sensors)` rather than a failure. The endpoint first runs the originating integration's filter via `assetMatchesIntegrationFilter` in `src/utils/integrationFilter.ts` — FMG/FortiGate/Entra check `deviceInclude`/`deviceExclude` against the asset's hostname; AD checks `ouInclude`/`ouExclude` against the OU path. If the asset is out of scope the call returns `409` with the reason in `error` and on every stream's `error`, no probe traffic leaves the host, and one `asset.refresh` Event is written at level `warning` with message `Poll blocked: <name> — <reason>`. The FMG/FortiGate `interfaceInclude` / `interfaceExclude` is applied a layer down inside `collectSystemInfoFortinet` so the System tab interface table mirrors discovery's scope — VLAN sub-interfaces are kept when their parent survives the filter (hiding the parent would orphan its children, so the filter walks the parent → child relationship before dropping rows). Otherwise each call writes one `asset.refresh` Event (level `info` on full success, `warning` on any partial failure) so manual polls are auditable — the periodic monitorAssets job only writes events on up/down transitions.
- `POST   /assets/:id/rediscover`               *(assets write)* — Re-run discovery for ONE FortiGate. Only valid on a firewall asset carrying a `fortinetTopology.role === "fortigate"` stamp discovered by an enabled FortiManager or standalone-FortiGate integration (400 otherwise). Resolves the FMG device name from `fortinetTopology.deviceName` (hostname fallback — same resolver precedent as descriptionSyncService's device-targeted writes), re-checks `assetMatchesIntegrationFilter` against both the hostname and the resolved device name (409 + warning `asset.rediscover` Event when the gate is filtered out — mirrors probe-now), and 409s while any discovery is already running for the integration (`isRunActive` pre-check + `triggerDiscovery`'s coalescing boolean return closing the TOCTOU window; the pg-boss `singletonKey` is the last-line guard). FMG assets queue a **scoped** run — `triggerDiscovery(integrationId, actor, { scopeDeviceName })` rides the full run machinery (DiscoveryRun row with `scopeDeviceName` stamped, progress, abort, pg-boss handoff) but narrows the roster to the one device inside `discoverDhcpSubnets` (AFTER the raw roster is captured into `knownDeviceNames`, same protection as the device filter) and finalizes in `"finalize-scoped"` mode (Phase 2b per-controller switch/AP decommission ONLY — see the SyncMode notes in the FMG Discovery Workflow section); standalone-FortiGate assets get a plain full run (the integration IS the single gate). Scoped runs do NOT stamp `Integration.lastDiscoveryAt` (the scheduler's next full run is unaffected) and skip the integration-level slow-run duration sample. 202 `{ message, integrationId, integrationName, deviceName }` + one `asset.rediscover` Event. Backs the **Re-discover** button on the asset-details System tab (rendered next to the Status pill for FortiGate firewall assets; watches the shared `/discoveries` poll for appear→disappear to refresh the asset, with a graceful fallback toast for roles that can't read `/discoveries`).
- `GET    /assets/:id/system-info`              — Asset details System tab: latest interface + storage + telemetry snapshot. Returns `{ monitored, lastTelemetryAt, lastSystemInfoAt, telemetry: {...}|null, interfaces: [...], storage: [...], temperatures: [...], ipsecTunnels: [...], lldpNeighbors: [...] }`. Both the `interfaces` and `ipsecTunnels` queries anchor to `lastSystemInfoAt` (the full pass's write timestamp) rather than the raw newest sample — the fast cadence only writes PINNED rows, so ordering by raw timestamp would hide every unpinned interface/tunnel within a minute of a fast walk. Each anchor clamps down to the newest sample when it's ahead (transient collect failure / agent split-push), and the ipsec query additionally falls back to the newest batch when the anchor pass produced zero ipsec rows. `lldpNeighbors` is the full set of `AssetLldpNeighbor` rows for the asset (current state, not a time-series); each entry includes `localIfName`, full LLDP TLVs (chassisId/portId + subtypes, port description, system name/description, management IP, capabilities), `firstSeen` / `lastSeen`, the source transport (`"fortios"` | `"snmp"`), and a `matchedAsset: { id, hostname, ipAddress, assetType } | null` cross-link when the neighbor resolved to a Polaris asset by management IP, chassis MAC, or hostname. Empty arrays when no scrape has run yet. The set additionally carries **peer-inferred** rows (`source = "peer-inferred"`) synthesized from `Asset.fortinetTopology` via `peerInferredLldpService` so a FortiSwitch's ports facing managed APs, and a FortiGate's FortiLink interfaces facing managed switches, show up in the Neighbor column even though those edges don't appear in a direct LLDP scrape (FortiSwitches in managed mode consume LLDP without re-publishing via SNMP LLDP-MIB). Inferred rows are deduped against real rows on `(localIfName, matchedAssetId)` — real LLDP wins on collision, including the aggregate/member case (a row learned on a FortiLink member port suppresses the inferred row on the `fortilink` aggregate). The frontend renders inferred entries in italic with a tooltip explaining the inference.
- `GET    /assets/:id/custom-widgets`            — Custom MIB tab payload (Slice 7). Resolves the asset's manufacturer through the `ManufacturerProfile` cache, applies optional per-widget `modelPattern` gating against `Asset.model`, and returns each applicable widget's definition plus a window of recent `AssetCustomWidgetSample` rows (up to 60 per widget, oldest first — line charts read the window directly; gauges + tables use `latest`). Response: `{ manufacturer, profileId, polling, lastCustomWidgetAt, widgets: [{ id, name, symbol, mibId, type, widgetType, transform, displayOptions, order, modelPattern, samples, latest, stateMap, labelSymbol, stateRows? }] }`. **State probes** (`widgetType="state"`) carry no `samples`/`latest` — their 0/1 readings live in `AssetStateSample`, so the handler additionally fetches the recent rows for every applicable state probe and attaches each probe's CURRENT state as `stateRows: [{rowKey, rowLabel, value, rawValue, timestamp}]` (newest-first scan keeping the first sighting of each `(probeId, rowKey)`; one scrape writes a probe's whole row set at one timestamp, so the take cap covers several full snapshots). Rows are sorted problem-first (per the probe's `stateMap.trueIsProblem`) then by name, since an operator opening the tab is looking for what's wrong and shouldn't have to scan a 60-row sensor table. Empty `widgets` array when the manufacturer has no widgets defined (the frontend hides the tab in that case) or the widget set doesn't match the asset's model. Samples are produced by `collectAndRecordCustomWidgets()` which rides the telemetry cadence (Slice 7b): after every successful `runTelemetryFor` pass, the helper walks each applicable widget over the asset's resolved SNMP transport, applies the widget's transform, and persists scalar or table rows into `AssetCustomWidgetSample` while bumping `Asset.lastCustomWidgetAt`. A `widgetType="state"` widget takes the state-probe branch instead: walk the value symbol, walk `labelSymbol` too when set (a failed label walk degrades to bare indexes rather than costing the alarm state), map every reading through `joinStateRows`/`evaluateStateMap`, drop the unreadable ones, and write `AssetStateSample` rows (a scalar probe keeps only the first readable row with `rowKey=""` and the probe's name as its label). Table probes are capped at `MAX_STATE_ROWS_PER_PROBE` (500) rows per scrape with a warn-level log when truncated — each row costs a per-scrape DB row AND a NotificationRuleState row in the engine, and a probe silently dropping rows would look like a healthy one. Both sample writes plus the `lastCustomWidgetAt` bump ride one `$transaction`. SNMP-only in v1; FortiOS REST custom widgets land in a follow-up.
- `GET    /assets/:id/telemetry-history?range=1h|24h|7d|30d` *or* `?from&to`  — CPU/memory time-series. Returns `{ range, since, until, samples, stats: { total, avgCpuPct, maxCpuPct, avgMemPct, maxMemPct } }`. memPct is computed from `memUsedBytes / memTotalBytes` if the source supplied bytes only.
- `GET    /assets/:id/interface-history?ifName=...&range=...`  — Per-interface counter samples; sized by interface (a 30-port switch with one row per 10 min ≈ 4,300 samples per 30-day range). Includes `inErrors` / `outErrors` (cumulative IF-MIB / FortiOS error counters) so the asset-detail interface slide-over can derive a per-interval error rate. The response also surfaces the latest sample's `alias` / `description` at the top level (FortiOS CMDB `alias` + `description`, SNMP `ifAlias`) so the slide-over header can show `<alias> (<ifName>)` and render the comment in the **Interface Comments** editor. `description` is the *resolved* value (override if set, else discovered); `discoveredDescription` and `overrideDescription` are also returned separately so the editor can label the source and show the device-reported value as ghost text when no override is set. The response also carries `lldpNeighbors`: the LLDP rows whose `localIfName === ifName` (usually 0 or 1, sometimes >1 on shared media); each row includes the same fields as the system-info endpoint plus a `matchedAsset` cross-link, so the slide-over can render an LLDP neighbor card with a clickable system name that opens the matched asset's view modal. Peer-inferred rows are merged in here too (same dedup rule as `/system-info` — see that endpoint for details), filtered to the requested ifName.
- `PUT    /assets/:id/interfaces/:ifName/comment` *(assets admin)* — Set or clear the Interface Comments override. Body: `{ description: string | null }` (max 255 chars; null or empty string deletes the override row so the discovered FortiOS CMDB description shows through again — the device-side description is never deleted). Polaris-local by default; when the asset's originating integration has `syncDescriptions` on (business rule 14), a saved comment is also pushed to the device via `descriptionSyncService.syncDescriptionsOnSave` and the response gains `sync: { attempted, status?, error? }` (best-effort — the override row persists even when the push fails; the discovery reconcile retries). Writes one `asset.interface.comment_updated` Event (+ `asset.interface.description.pushed|push_failed` when a push was attempted).
- `GET    /assets/:id/hardware-history?range=...[&sensorName=...]`  — Per-sensor hardware-reading time-series. Samples carry `{ timestamp, sensorName, sensorClass, unit, value, alarmStatus? }`; returns `{ samples, stats: { total, avgValue, minValue, maxValue } }`. Backed by the `hardware` retention entity / tier router.
- `GET    /assets/:id/metric-thresholds?metric=…[&sensorName=&sensorClass=]` — The severity thresholds that would fire on this asset's charted metric (`assets:read`), so a detail chart can shade its line with the engine's own numbers. Returns `{metric, tiers[{severity, operator, threshold, ruleId, ruleName}]}` ordered least → most severe, from `notificationRuleService.getMetricSeverityTiers`: every enabled scope-matching automation contributes either its `resolveTierLadder` (numeric single trigger — tier 0 plus each severity band) or each composite leaf on that metric at the rule's severity. `sensorName`/`sensorClass` identify the charted sensor so a rule whose dimensionFilter doesn't select it is skipped. Only ordered comparators appear (`==`/`!=` shade nothing); ties at one severity keep the more sensitive threshold; hot (`>=`) and cold (`<=`) tiers of the same severity are both returned. Consumed by `_severityChartLayer` in assets.js.
- `GET    /assets/:id/storage-history?mountPath=...&range=...`  — Per-mountpoint usage samples. SNMP-monitored assets only.
- `GET    /assets/:id/ipsec-history?tunnelName=...&range=...`  — Per-tunnel IPsec samples (status timeline + cumulative bytes). FortiOS-monitored assets only.
- `GET    /assets/:id/sdwan-members`  — Per-WAN-member health summary (aggregate up/down, per-health-check latency/jitter/loss, recent up/down status strip, + IP/link/bytes joined from the latest interface sample). Drives the "SD-WAN Members" table above the rules.
- `GET    /assets/:id/perf-sla-links`  — Distinct (healthCheck, link) pairs + latest SLA thresholds. SD-WAN data-exists gate + selector source for the SD-WAN tab.
- `GET    /assets/:id/perf-sla-history?healthCheck=...&link=...&range=...`  — Per-member SD-WAN Performance SLA latency/jitter/packet-loss gauges over time (tier-aware).
- `GET    /assets/:id/sdwan-rules`  — Current-state SD-WAN service rules (selected member + members/criteria/health-checks/destination/status + priority zones), one row per rule from the `asset_sdwan_rules` table, ordered by FortiOS rule priority. No history endpoint — SD-WAN rules are current-state.
- `GET    /assets/:id/upstream`  — The three upstream devices the General tab names (Last Seen Switch / AP / Firewall), each as `{ name, port?, lastSeen?, asset }` where `asset` is `{ id, hostname, ipAddress, assetType, status, monitorStatus, managementAccess }` or **null** when the stored name resolves to nothing (an unadopted switch, a gate another integration hasn't discovered yet — a legitimate state, so the UI keeps rendering the name as plain text). Resolution rides `utils/fortinetParentKey.ts`, which is what makes the firewall half work at all: the sighting carries FortiManager's DEVICE NAME, not the gate's hostname. All three are null for an `assetType: "firewall"` (a gate is the thing doing the sighting). The firewall half reads `AssetFortigateSighting` — gated a second time on `assetsQuarantine:read`, with `visibility.firewall` saying whether it was consulted, so "not shown" stays distinguishable from "no gate has ever seen this device" (the `/ip-context` precedent). 404 only for a missing asset. Gated `assets:read`; backed by `services/assetUpstreamService.ts`.
- `GET    /assets/:id/mclag-peers`  — Current-state MCLAG ICL peers from the `asset_mclag_peers` table (FortiSwitch only; empty for switches not in an MCLAG pair), one row per local ICL port ordered by port name. Each row carries `localPort` / `iclTrunk` / `peerSn` / `peerName` / `peerPort` + `matchedAsset { id, hostname }` (the peer switch resolved by serial, for a clickable link). No history — current-state.
- `GET    /assets/:id/arp-table`  *(assets=read)* — The FortiGate's layer-3 neighbour cache from `asset_arp_entries`. Takes `?range=current|1h|12h|24h|7d|30d` (default `current`; anything else is a 400 rather than a silent widening) and filters on `lastSeen`, which is the same column retention prunes on -- so "last 30 days" and "kept for 30 days" mean one window. Returns `entries` (ipAddress / macAddress / ifName / ageSec / firstSeen / lastSeen / matchedAsset, with the `""` interface sentinel mapped back to null), `interfaceCounts`, `total`, `range`, `retentionDays` and `pollIntervalSec` -- the last two are what the tab's disclaimer is built from, and `pollIntervalSec` is resolved PER DEVICE (`resolveArpPollIntervalSec`: the effective systemInfoIntervalSeconds for a monitored asset, else the discovering integration's pollInterval in seconds, else null) because the two cadences differ by two orders of magnitude and no single fleet-wide number would be true. Plus `collectedAt` = the newest lastSeen — the whole table shares one collection timestamp, and the tab leads with it because an ARP cache is only meaningful next to its age. Backs the asset-details ARP Table tab (firewall-class only). Ordering here is just payload stability; the browser re-orders numerically within each interface.
- `GET    /assets/:id/virtualization`  — Current-state vCenter facts for the asset-details Virtualization section (General tab), assembled per role from the `Asset.virtualization` blob. VM role: the blob + `hostAsset {id, hostname, monitorStatus}` (clickable running-host link, re-resolved every discovery cycle) + `diskDatastores` (name/type/backingLabel for the disks table). **Guest filesystems are deliberately NOT here** — they are a monitored reading, not an inventory fact, so the `vcenter` storage stream samples them into `AssetStorageSample` and they render in the System tab’s Storage table with the history, pinning and alerting every other mount gets; a second static copy on the General tab could only be a stale duplicate. Discovery stopped calling `/guest/local-filesystem` per VM when that moved (2026-08), which also removed one REST call per VM per run. Host role: the blob + `datastores` (VcenterDatastore rows whose `hostMorefs` contain this host, BigInt→string) + `vms` (assets whose `virtualization.hostAssetId` points here, with power state + monitor status). The host blob also carries `vswitches` + `portgroups` (written by discovery's Phase 2), rendered as a virtual-networking table — INVENTORY only: uplink membership, MTU, port counts, teaming policy, and each port group's VLAN, with 0 spelled "untagged" and 4095 "VLAN trunk" rather than printed as an id. The LIVE half of the same facts (uplink link state, vmk addressing, the nesting itself) is on the System tab's interface table. A failed SOAP host half writes `null`, and the blob build CARRIES THE PRIOR LISTS FORWARD rather than blanking the section until the next 12h cycle — the rest of the blob comes from REST, so a wipe here would mix fresh and blank facts in one object. Assets without vCenter data return `{virtualization: null}` and the UI skips the section.
- `GET    /assets/:id/processes`  — Current-state process inventory (one row per program, cpuPct desc) + the `monitoredProcesses` / `alertWatchedProcesses` pin arrays. Drives the merged Services tab's *Include processes* view + its Monitor/Map checkbox state (the standalone Processes tab was folded into Services 2026-07; the Alert pin column was dropped from the UI — alerting is handled by Automations — though `alertWatchedProcesses` is still returned).
- `GET    /assets/:id/services`  *(assets=read)* — Current-state service inventory (one row per systemd unit / Windows service, unit-sorted) from `AssetService` + the `monitoredServices` (Logs) / `mappedServices` (Map) pin arrays. Drives the merged Services tab (units by default; the *Include processes* checkbox folds `/processes` rows into the same table). Read-only — Start/Stop/Restart control was removed (Satellite-posture change). `memBytes` BigInt→string.
- `GET    /assets/:id/service-logs?unit=...&since=...&limit=...&flagged=1`  *(assets=read)* — recent journalctl lines for a pinned unit (newest-first, capped 2000) from `asset_service_log_samples`, each annotated with matching `LogFlagRule`s (read-time `evaluateLogFlags`; global/asset-scoped rules apply, unit passed as the process key). Drives the Services detail-panel log viewer. Phase 2.
- `GET    /assets/:id/process-history?name=...&range=...`  — Per-pinned-program CPU/RAM history, tier-routed (detail → hourly → daily) via `readProcessHistory` + `pickSampleTierForAsset("process")`. Drives the per-process detail slide-in charts.
- `GET    /assets/:id/process-logs?name=...&since=...&limit=...&flagged=1`  — Recent log lines for a pinned program (newest-first, capped), from the standalone `asset_process_log_samples` table, each annotated with the `LogFlagRule`s it matches (read-time eval via `evaluateLogFlags`). `flagged=1` returns only matched lines. Drives the slide-in log viewer + its Flagged-only toggle.
- `GET    /assets/:id/process-connections?name=<processName>|unit=<unit>`  *(assets=read)* — Ports & Connections for the process detail slide-in AND the Services detail panel (Application Map data, per-asset view): `{ listening[], outbound[], inbound[] }` from `AssetProcessConnection`, sorted lastSeen desc, capped 500/section; remote endpoints hydrated with the matched asset id + hostname via `applicationMapService.resolveIpsToAssets`. Optional `name` filters to one process; optional `unit` (Phase 3) filters to one systemd unit / Windows service.
- `GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /log-flag-rules` (`src/api/routes/logFlagRules.ts`)  — CRUD for user-defined log-flag rules. List = `assets:read`; writes = `assets:write`. Backed by `logFlagRuleService` (read-time eval + compiled-rule cache).
- `GET /alerts` (`alerts:read`, region-scoped) / `GET /alerts/:id` (`alerts:read` — ONE alert, region-scoped through the same predicate the list uses and answering **404, not 403**, when the caller's regions exclude it, because which alerts exist outside your regions is not something a route should confirm. Declared LAST so it can never capture `/acknowledge` or `/clear`. Returns the row plus `ruleName` and the flat `requireAckNote`; backs `/alert-ack.html`, the page an emailed or pushed Acknowledge button opens — business rule 25) / `POST /alerts/acknowledge` (`alerts:write` — **400** when the batch contains an alert whose automation sets `requireAckNote` and the body carries no non-blank note; refused WHOLE, since one note applies to every id. Optional `source` from a CLOSED set (`ack_page` | `web_push_action`) is audit provenance for the Event's `details`, never a gate — closed so a caller cannot write arbitrary text into the audit log) / `POST /alerts/clear` (`alerts:fullwrite`) (`src/api/routes/notifications.ts`; deprecated alias mount `/notifications`) — triggered-alert list + lifecycle.
