Backed by `notificationService`. Per-asset bundle at `GET /assets/:id/alerts` (alias `/assets/:id/notifications`; `assets:read`) → `{active, matchingRules}` — `matchingRules` are full v2 rule rows, which is what lets the asset-details Alerts tab render each automation's TRIGGER SENTENCE (the same summary the edit modal shows, severity ladder included) and open that rule in the wizard when its name is clicked. `active` rows are whole Notification records, rendered as **Time / Severity / Alert / Acknowledge / Actions**. The `dimension` rides the **Alert** cell's `title` (with `metric`) rather than a Detail column of its own — the default message already carries it as `[label]`, and without it a per-interface automation's alerts all render one message template at one timestamp and are indistinguishable, which is also why the tab's acknowledge/clear run over a multi-select through the batch routes rather than one row at a time. **Acknowledge** is the only surface that renders `Notification.acknowledgeNote`: `requireAckNote` exists to make an operator say what the problem was and what the fix was, and until 2026-08 the answer was stored on the row and displayed nowhere. All notification-era alias mounts answer with `Deprecation: true` + a successor-version `Link` header (`deprecatedAlias` helper in `src/api/router.ts`).
- `GET /automations` / `POST` / `PUT/:id` / `DELETE/:id` (`automationManagement:read` for list/schema/recipient-users, `fullwrite` for CRUD/preview), `GET /automations/schema`, `GET /automations/scope-options` (device-filter picker lists: distinct manufacturers/models of **MONITORED** assets, the distinct `interfaceNames` those assets report (one `assetInterface.groupBy` over the largest current-state table in the schema, capped at 500 — a fleet reuses port names, so the cap bounds the payload and never the filter, which still accepts free text) + non-deprecated IPAM subnets {id,name,cidr} + region + role catalogues — backed by `notificationRuleService.listScopeOptions`. Monitored-only because a value that only unmonitored inventory reports is a filter choice that can't produce an alert AT ALL; the subnet list is IPAM rather than inventory and stays unfiltered. Matching agrees since 2026-08: `scopeWhere(scope, monitoredOnly)` pushes `monitored: true` into the WHERE on every EVALUATION load, so an unmonitored device triggers nothing — event and change triggers used to be the exception and no longer are. The raw form survives for the surfaces asking a different question: the Step-2 device-list preview, which REPORTS the unmonitored remainder rather than hiding it, and `loadScopeAssetIds`' callers (the dimension picker, mass pinning)), `GET /automations/recipient-users` (users for the recipient picker), `POST /automations/dimension-values` (`automationManagement:read`; body `{metric, dimension, scope, narrow?}` → `{values[{value, assetCount}], strict, noun, narrowLabel, scopedAssets, sampledAssets, assetsWithData, windowHours}` — what the DRAFT'S OWN devices currently report for a metric's — or an asset_state field's, `metric` accepts both namespaces — dimensionFilter field, so the builder renders a picker instead of free text; backed by `notificationDimensionService.listDimensionValues`. Every asset metric and state field also takes the device-identifier dims (`deviceFilterDimensions`: hostname / IP / MAC / manufacturer / model, listed from the scoped Asset rows — the wizard's "+ Condition" filter rows), and the state fields take the filters the engine always honored (`ifNamePattern` on the ifOper/ifAdmin/poe trio, `tunnelName` on ipsecStatus) per `FIELD_DIMENSIONS`. Both operator-pinned dimensions read the pin set rather than the samples: `ifNamePattern` from `Asset.monitoredInterfaces` (which is also the engine's gate) and `mountPathPattern` from `Asset.monitoredStorage` (which is NOT — the storage stream samples every mountpath at `cadence:"slow"`, so a stored rule on an unpinned mount still evaluates; the picker steers to the mounts that keep history, since a multi-day aggregate over a 24h retention window reads almost nothing)), `POST /automations/preview` (accepts partial drafts via `previewInputSchema`: a `{scope}`-only body lists the matched devices — the wizard's Step-2 preview — and `{trigger, scope}` works without a name; the result carries `totalAssets` = DISTINCT devices alongside `totalEvaluated` = readings, since per-dimension metrics fan out to one reading per sensor/interface/mount) (`src/api/routes/notificationRules.ts`; deprecated alias mount `/notification-rules`) — automation (rule) CRUD (incl. delivery `targets` + recipient routing, `emailComposition`, and `escalation` — escalation tier channels are validated email-type at save with a friendly 400) + builder vocabulary (`/schema` includes `templateVariables`, the {token} catalog for the builder's insert-variable palette) + dry-run (preview additionally returns `emailPreview` {subject, text, html?} rendered against the first match when the draft has emailComposition). Backed by `notificationRuleService` + `notificationRecipientService.listRecipientUsers` + `notificationEngine.previewRule`.
- `GET /maintenance-schedules` / `POST` / `PUT/:id` / `DELETE/:id` (`maintenanceManagement:read` for list, `fullwrite` for CRUD), `POST /maintenance-schedules/preview` (`fullwrite`; `src/api/routes/maintenanceSchedules.ts`) — maintenance-schedule CRUD + target-filter dry-run. Preview returns `{ total, assets[≤50] }` (hostname/ip/model/manufacturer, hostname-sorted, monitored-only). Body: `{ name, enabled?, criteria? (tagAssignmentService vocabulary, status rules rejected), assetIds?, schedule (maintenanceRecurrence shape; a oneshot may carry `startNow: true` — resolved to a SERVER-stamped startAt by `resolveStartNow` before validation, marker stripped, so ad-hoc entry is immediate regardless of client clock/TZ skew), suppressChildren? (default true — whether in-window assets count as down for child dependency suppression; a PUT that omits it snaps back to true, so callers pass it through) }`. Every mutation runs `reconcileMaintenance()` inline before responding — a now-active one-shot (the pill's ad-hoc path) has already flipped its assets to `status="maintenance"` when the 201 returns. Backed by `maintenanceScheduleService`.
- `GET /maintenance-schedules/occurrences?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD` (`maintenanceManagement:read`) — the Maintenance modal's **calendar** tab. Expands EVERY schedule's occurrences across the inclusive day range (`expandOccurrences` per schedule; range capped at 400 days, response at 2000 occurrences with a `truncated` flag) and returns `{ from, to, truncated, occurrences: [{ scheduleId, name, enabled, kind, adhoc, start, end }] }`, start/end as **server-local wall-clock strings** (`"2026-08-12T22:00"`), never instants — the recurrence engine runs on the server's clock, so handing the browser a UTC Date would paint windows on the wrong day for any operator in another timezone. A schedule whose stored shape no longer validates is skipped, not fatal. Backed by `maintenanceScheduleService.listOccurrences`.
- `GET /maintenance-schedules/server-time` (`maintenanceManagement:read`) — `{ now, timeZone, offsetMinutes }`: the server's wall clock as the same local-ISO minute string every schedule shape carries (`"2026-08-19T14:30"`), its resolved IANA zone (`""` on a stripped image with no zone data), and its UTC offset **east-positive** (Central DST = `-300`, the sign operators write, opposite `getTimezoneOffset`). Declared **before `/:id`** so the literal path isn't captured. Backed by the pure `serverClockInfo` in `src/utils/maintenanceRecurrence.ts`.  **Why it exists:** every maintenance time is server-local wall clock with NO offset — that is the only reading that survives DST (a 22:00 nightly window means 22:00 at the site). The browser broke the other half of that contract: the one-shot pickers were prefilled from `new Date()` in the BROWSER and posted the operator's digits for the server to read as its own. On a UTC-clocked host with a Central operator, "now → now + 2h" mapped onto a server window that started five hours ago and had **already ended** — so a bulk-selected batch of switches/APs saved cleanly, `isInWindow` was false forever, no `maintenance.entered` Event was written, and every asset kept showing Down. `resolveStartNow` covered only the ad-hoc START; every operator-picked END time had the same hole (the ad-hoc path entered maintenance and then exited on the very next 30s reconcile). The browser now folds timezone difference AND clock drift into one minute-rounded skew (`_maintLoadServerClock` in `public/js/assets-maintenance.js`, cached per page) and prefills, validates and LABELS every picker through it.
- `GET /automations/scope-options` additionally returns **`regions: string[]`** (the map-region catalogue via `mapRegionService.listRegions`, bare names, sorted). It rides this payload rather than `GET /map/regions` because that route is gated `mapRegions:read`, which an automation editor may not hold — the region picker would silently degrade to free text. Feeds the Web Push `recipientRegions` chips. Alongside it, **`regionLevels: { maxLevel, byName }`** — how deep the nesting goes right now (1 = nothing is nested; the two recipient pickers read it to decide how many "Asset's L\<n\> Region Users" entries to offer) and each region's derived level keyed by its LOWER-CASED bare name, which is the key `regionLevelIndex` already builds. `byName` is the GLOBAL level and is **display only** — the address book's Regions list renders it as a Level column; routing never reads it, because a global level is asset-relative-wrong on an uneven tree (see `regionHierarchyService`). Both halves fall back to `{ maxLevel: 1, byName: {} }` if the derivation throws, so the pickers offer no level entries and the column blanks rather than claiming everything is L1. Alongside both, **`tagCatalog: { name, category }[]`** — the `Tag` REGISTRY, for the recipient pickers' Tags list, with the Map Regions category excluded server-side (those rows are the region catalogue under their `region:` names, they are already offered by `regions` WITH their level, and they route through the region-only matcher, so listing them again would put one set of people behind two entries that reach different sets). Distinct from the `tags` on the filter-schema payloads, which is what the INVENTORY currently carries: a tag can scope users without being on a single device, and routing to it still reaches them. Rides this payload for the same reason `regions` does — `GET /server-settings/tags` is gated `serverSettingsSystem:read`.
- `GET /contacts/search?q=&directory=1` additionally queries the opted-in AD/Entra directories (live; nothing stored) and returns `directoryAvailable` so the UI can tell "nobody matched" from "no directory configured". Rate-limited by `contactSearchLimiter` (600 / 5 min) because that path proxies an external API from operator keystrokes.
- `GET /contacts?q=&limit=&offset=` / `GET /contacts/:id` / `POST` / `PUT/:id` / `DELETE/:id`, `GET /contacts/search?q=`, `POST /contacts/preview` (`src/api/routes/contacts.ts`) — the address book. The list is **paginated and searched server-side** (`{ contacts, total, limit, offset }`; default 50, max 200, `q` matches email or name case-insensitively) — it used to return every row for the browser to filter, which made opening the page cost the whole table. `total` is the UNPAGED match count, so a truncated page is distinguishable from a complete one. `GET /:id` exists because the alternative the address book was using is re-reading the entire list to find one row — merely wasteful against a curated table, wrong against a paginated one, where the row being edited may not be on the page that was loaded; it is declared after every literal path so `search` / `preview` / `filter-schema` aren't captured as ids. **Directory-synced entries and the live GAL fan-out are both narrowed by `automationManagement:read`** (business rule 35), not by the `contacts` key every built-in role holds — the whole employee roster is not something every account should enumerate, and gating the stored copy while leaving the live typeahead open would be a gate in name only. It FILTERS rather than 403s: `?origin=manual|directory|all` selects, the gate intersects, and a caller who may not see synced rows and asks for ONLY synced rows gets an EMPTY page — never the manual rows, which would answer a question they didn't ask. `total` counts the gated set. The list response carries BOTH `directoryVisible` (may this caller see synced rows?) and `directorySyncAvailable` (is anything actually syncing?) — two different questions, and the address book renders its Curated / Directory filter only when both are true, since a filter whose "From the directory" option is always empty reads as broken rather than as a boundary. `POST /contacts/:id/adopt` takes a synced row out of the sync's hands (`origin` → `manual`, `createdBy` stamped, provenance deleted, `contact.adopted` Event) — and creating or editing over a synced address does the same implicitly, because `email` is UNIQUE so a synced row would otherwise block the operator entirely. `DELETE` on a synced row is a 409 naming both ways out, since deleting it would succeed and then be undone by the next run. Reads (`list` / `get` / `search` / `preview`) are gated `contacts:read`; the three mutations go through `requireOwnership("contacts")` (≥ write) and then `assertOwnership(req, row.createdBy, …)`, so a write-level caller edits or deletes only rows they created and `fullwrite` bypasses the filter — the subnets/reservations mechanism. Body: `{ email, name?, description?, assetCondition? (the DEVICE_FILTER condition tree), assetCriteria? (LEGACY tagAssignmentService vocabulary — still accepted, folded forward on write when the tree can express it), assetAllDevices?, assetIds? }`. A read adds two DERIVED fields the editor needs: `assetConditionEffective` (the filter as a tree whatever it is stored as) and `assetFilterUnconvertible` (fields a legacy blob uses that the tree can't say — non-empty means the builder can't render it). `POST /preview` answers `{ matchCount, unmonitoredCount, sample[] }`: the count and the list are MONITORED matches, with the unmonitored remainder counted rather than hidden — the filter does cover them (an event/change automation fires on an unmonitored device), they're just not what an operator is choosing between. `GET /search` returns `{ entries: [{ source: "user"|"contact"|"entra"|"ad", id, email, name, description, kind, owned? }] }` — Polaris users ∪ contacts, deduped by lower-cased email (user wins), prefix-first ranked, capped at 50; it is the automation wizard's recipient typeahead as well as the address-book picker's list. `POST /preview` returns `{ matchCount, sample[≤100] }` for a (criteria, pins) pair. `/search` and `/preview` are declared before `/:id`. Backed by `contactService`.
- `GET /contacts/filter-schema` (`contacts:read`) — the device-filter builder's vocabulary + value suggestions: `{ scopeCondition, options: { manufacturers, models, interfaceNames, subnets, regions, regionLevels, roles, tagCatalog, assetTypes, tags } }`. `scopeCondition` is `scopeConditionMeta(DEVICE_FILTER_FIELD_OPS)` — the same catalog builder `/automations/schema` uses, over the wider contact vocabulary, so field labels and operator wording can't drift between the two surfaces. Its own route rather than reusing `/automations/schema` + `/scope-options`, which are gated `automationManagement:read`: browsing the address book must not require permission to edit automations. `options` is `listScopeOptions()` verbatim, so `regions` + `regionLevels` + `tagCatalog` reach the address book's Tags pane (region names with their Level column, then the tag registry) without `mapRegions:read` or `serverSettingsSystem:read`. `assetTypes` + `tags` ride this payload for the same reason regions/roles ride `/scope-options` — their own endpoints are gated `assets:read`, and without them the value pickers would silently degrade to free text. Declared before `/:id`.
- `GET /assets/:id/contacts` (`assets:read` AND `contacts:read`, chained — reading it exposes address-book content) — the address-book entries responsible for this device, for the slide-over's General-tab Contacts rows. Returns `{ contacts: [{ id, email, name, description, via }] }` where `via` is `"pinned"` (an explicit `Contact.assetIds` entry) or `"filter"` (a device-filter match) — an operator chasing an unexpected recipient needs to know which. Backed by `contactService.resolveContactsForAsset`.
- `GET /assets/:id/maintenance-windows?range=…|from&to` (`assets:read`) — `AssetMaintenanceWindow` rows overlapping the range (`{ windows: [{scheduleName, startedAt, endedAt, endReason}] }`); fetched once per asset-panel open and rendered as the labeled chart maintenance bands. `GET /assets/:id/maintenance-info` (`assets:read`) — `{ inMaintenance, returnStatus, openWindows[{scheduleName, startedAt, until}], schedules[{name, enabled, activeNow, nextStart, nextEnd}] }` for the edit-modal Monitoring tab.
- `GET|POST /delivery-channels`, `GET|PUT|DELETE /delivery-channels/:id`, `POST /delivery-channels/:id/test`, `POST /delivery-channels/:id/generate-vapid` (`automationManagement:read` for GET, `fullwrite` for mutations/test) (`src/api/routes/notificationChannels.ts`; deprecated alias mount `/notification-channels`) — delivery-channel registry CRUD (secrets masked on GET, preserved on PUT) + per-channel test send + VAPID keypair generation. Backed by `notificationChannelService` + the channel senders.
- `GET|PUT /delivery-channels/web-push` (`automationManagement:read` / `fullwrite`) — **Web Push as a single on/off capability**, not a channel to assemble. Every other type names a destination (SMTP host, webhook URL, Pushbullet account) and so earns a form; Web Push names nothing — the VAPID keypair is generated, the destinations are whichever devices users enrolled, and WHO receives a given alert is chosen per Notify action when an automation is built. `PUT {enabled:true}` creates the singleton + generates the keypair in one call; `{enabled:false}` flips `enabled` and **never deletes the row or the keys** (every `PushSubscription` is signed against that keypair — dropping it would silently invalidate every enrolled device). `GET` returns `{enabled, configured, subscriberCount, channelId}`; `subscriberCount` is what makes the toggle non-feedback-free. **Both routes must stay declared before `/:id`** or the literal path is captured as an id. The Delivery tab renders this as a toggle card and filters `web_push` out of both the channel cards and the add-channel type picker — but it remains in `GET /delivery-channels` because the automation builder must still be able to target it.
- `POST /delivery-channels/web-push/test` (`automationManagement:fullwrite`) — send a real push to **the caller's own** enrolled devices (`sendWebPushTest`). Scoped to `req.session.userId` deliberately: a test that could notify arbitrary other people is a nuisance vector, not a diagnostic. Sends directly rather than queueing a `NotificationDelivery`, so the operator gets the true per-device result instead of a "queued" shrug — but still builds the payload with `pushDeepLinkUrl(surface)`, so what lands on the device is shaped exactly like a production alert. A 404/410 prunes the row, mirroring the delivery drain. Returns `{ok, sent, failed, pruned, message}` and writes a `notification_channel.test` Event. Must be declared **before `/:id/test`**.
- `GET|PUT /me/notification-preference` (`alerts:read` on both) (`src/api/routes/notificationPreference.ts`) — the caller's own alert delivery preference (`email` | `push` | `any`, default `email`). GET returns `{ preference, options }`; PUT takes `{ preference }`, audits the change and bumps the recipient index. The value also rides `GET /auth/me`, so a client can reconcile this browser's push enrollment on the boot request it already makes. Business rule 39.
- `GET /push-subscriptions/key` / `POST /push-subscriptions` / `DELETE /push-subscriptions` (`alerts:read`) (`src/api/routes/pushSubscriptions.ts`) — VAPID public-key handoff (from the web_push channel) + per-user Web Push subscription store/remove. Backed by `notificationChannelService.getWebPushChannel` + the PushSubscription table.
- `GET /manifest.webmanifest` / `GET /icons/:file` (**no auth**) (`src/api/routes/pwa.ts`) — the mobile SPA's web app manifest, generated from the `branding` Setting so a custom logo/app name becomes the install identity, plus its home-screen icons rasterized on demand by `appIconService`. Mounted OUTSIDE `/api/v1` in `src/app.ts` **before `express.static`** (neither is a file on disk). Unauthenticated deliberately: a `<link rel="manifest">` without `crossorigin` is fetched with credentials omitted, so a session-gated manifest would 401 for every caller — and the payload is the same branding already served unauthenticated at `/server-settings/branding`. `:file` is matched against the `ICON_SPECS` allowlist (anything else 404s — an operator-supplied size would let resvg allocate an unbounded canvas). Manifest is `no-cache` + weak ETag; icons are `immutable` on the manifest's `?v=<version>` URLs and `max-age=300` on the bare paths `sw.js` uses.
- `PUT    /assets/:id/processes/:name/config`  — Operator log-path config for a pinned program (`logSource` auto|journald-unit|file-glob + `logPathGlob` wildcard + notes). Upserts `AssetProcessConfig`; delivered to the agent via `GET /agents/config`'s `pinnedProcesses`. Writes `asset.process.log_config_set`.
The assets list and single-GET attach a synthesized `ipContext` field to each row: `{ subnetId, subnetCidr, reservation: { id, createdBy, sourceType } | null } | null` (null when the asset has no IP, or no non-deprecated subnet contains the IP). The list also attaches `monitoringMethods: string[]` — the reduced set of transports the asset is actually monitored by, computed by `computeMonitoringMethods` in `enrichAssetList` (`assets.ts`): `[]` when unmonitored, `["agent"]` when a `ManagedAgent` is `active` (the agent owns all streams), else the distinct resolved per-stream polling methods from `resolveMonitorSettings` (cached tiers, no per-row DB hit) with ICMP treated as subordinate — reachability-only, so it surfaces only when it's the sole method. Drives the Assets table's **Monitored Via** column (label per method, "Multiple" when several differ). The Assets page reads it to render a **View Lease** button on rows whose IP lives in a known subnet — clicking it navigates to `/subnets.html#ip=<subnetId>@<ipAddress>`, where the network slide-over opens scrolled to that IP's row. To reserve or release IPs, operators use the network slide-over directly (no asset-row Reserve/Unreserve buttons).

#### Quarantine (admin + assetsadmin, or bearer token whose bound role grants `assetsQuarantine` ≥ write)
- `GET    /assets/sighting-settings`            *(assetsQuarantine read)* — `{ sightingMaxAgeDays }` (default 180).
- `PUT    /assets/sighting-settings`            *(assetsQuarantine write)* — `{ sightingMaxAgeDays }`. Max 3650.
- `GET    /assets/:id/sightings`                *(auth)* — DHCP sighting history for this asset (list of `{ fortigateDevice, source, ipAddress, lastSeen, integrationId, subnetName, vlan }`). `subnetName` + `vlan` are resolved at request time by matching the stored `ipAddress` against subnets discovered on the same `fortigateDevice` — both are null when the IP doesn't fall inside any known subnet on that device (e.g. the subnet has been deleted or the sighting predates the `ipAddress` column).
- `GET    /assets/:id/sources`                  *(auth)* — Per-discovery-source view of an asset (Phase 3a of the multi-source asset model). Returns every `AssetSource` row attached to this asset with the originating integration's name + type joined in, sorted in stable presentation order (`entra` → `intune` → `ad` → `fortigate-firewall` → `fortiswitch` → `fortiap` → `manual`). Each entry: `{ id, sourceKind, externalId, integration: { id, name, type } | null, observed, state, inferred, syncedAt, firstSeen, lastSeen }`. `state` is `deriveAssetSourceState(sourceKind, observed)` from `src/utils/assetSourceState.ts` — the source's own enabled/disabled verdict normalized to `{ state: "enabled" | "disabled" | "unknown", kind: "account" | "runtime" | "none", label, field, value }`, so a caller doesn't have to know that Entra says `accountEnabled: false` where AD says `accountDisabled: true` and vCenter says `powerState: "POWERED_OFF"`. Rows are **collapsed by `(sourceKind, integrationId)`, keeping the most-recent (`lastSeen`-desc) row per source** — so a `fortigate-endpoint` source whose MAC-keyed `externalId` churned (each MAC change spawns a new `AssetSource` row and orphans the old one) renders as a single card instead of several near-identical ones. Serial/GUID-keyed kinds (`fortigate-firewall`/`switch`/`ap`, `ad`, `entra`, `intune`) have stable externalIds and never collapse; the dropped MAC/IP detail still surfaces in the Firewall Sightings + IP History tables on the same tab. Powers the **Sources** tab on the asset details modal — operators can see what each integration independently said about the device.
- `POST   /assets/:id/sources/:sourceId/split`  *(admin)* — Recovery action. Detaches the chosen `AssetSource` row from this asset and binds it to a freshly-created Asset whose discovery-owned fields are seeded from the source's `observed` blob via `projectAssetFromSources([source])`. The new Asset gets a `split-from-asset` tag plus a source-kind hint (`entraid` / `activedirectory` / `fortigate` / etc.). **Phase 4d retired the `assetTag` write here** — the AssetSource row that just got re-bound is the canonical identity link; the legacy `entra:`/`ad:`/`fgt:` assetTag prefixes were back-compat markers that re-discovery already stopped consulting in Phase 2. Refusal rules: source not on this asset (404), source is the asset's only source (409 — would leave the original orphaned), source is `sourceKind="manual"` (409 — backfill marker, not a real discovery source). Returns `{ originalAssetId, newAssetId, movedSourceId, newAsset }`. Asset-row FKs (monitoring samples, IP history, sightings, quarantine, conflicts) all stay on the **original** asset; the new Asset starts clean. Writes one `asset.split` Event with details `{ originalAssetId, newAssetId, sourceId, sourceKind, externalId }`.
- `GET    /assets/:id/polling-history`          *(auth)* — Polling-history summary for the merge comparison: how much sample history the asset holds across the monitor-probe + telemetry streams and all three retention tiers (detail / hourly / daily rollups). Returns `{ oldestAt, newestAt, spanDays, sampleCount, monitor: { oldestAt, newestAt, sampleCount }, telemetry: {...} }`. `sampleCount` is **stitched** so overlapping tier coverage isn't double-counted (all of daily + hourly buckets past daily coverage + detail rows past hourly coverage — `readPollingHistorySummary` in `sampleHistoryService.ts`); the UI presents it as approximate. Feeds the Merge Assets modal, which shows each side's history, **auto-selects the survivor with the longer history** (span first, count as tiebreak — the absorbed side's samples are orphaned by a merge), and warns in the confirm step when the operator overrides toward the shorter side.
- `POST   /assets/:id/merge`                    *(admin)* — Operator-driven asset merge — the **inverse of Split**. Absorbs another asset into this one. Body: `{ otherAssetId, survivor: "this" | "other" (default "this"), fieldWinners?: { <field>: "this" | "other" }, dependencyWinner?: "this" | "other" }`. The operator picks which side survives (keeps its monitoring history + quarantine state + FKs) and resolves each differing field; `fieldWinners` keys are a subset of `MERGEABLE_FIELDS` (`src/services/assetMergeService.ts`), any omitted field defaults to blank-fill. Delegates to `mergeAssets()` in `assetMergeService.ts`: **re-binds ALL of the absorbed asset's `AssetSource` rows onto the survivor** (via the shared `absorbAssetRelations` — no `(sourceKind, externalId)` collision possible — globally unique — so the survivor becomes multi-source; this is the key difference from the automatic `mergeDuplicateHostnameAssets` job, which cascade-deletes the ghost's sources. `acceptAssetConflict`'s sibling-conflict absorb calls the same helper as of the fix below, so both operator-facing merges preserve provenance identically), transfers `AssetMacAddress` / `AssetAssociatedIp` / `AssetIpHistory` / `AssetFortigateSighting` (delete-on-conflict against the survivor's existing rows), re-binds the `ManagedAgent` enrollment iff the survivor has none, union-merges tags, keeps the more-recent `lastSeen`, applies field winners (clamping `acquiredAt ≤ lastSeen`), **OR-s `monitored`** (either side monitored ⇒ survivor monitored; when that flips the survivor ON it also adopts the absorbed row's `MONITOR_CONFIG_FIELDS` — per-stream polling methods / credentials / MIB pins / interval+timeout overrides, ghost's non-null wins — and UNIONs its `MONITOR_PIN_FIELDS` monitored/mapped arrays, resets `monitorStatus` + failure/success counters, and recomputes `monitorOverride`; skipped when the merged status resolves to `decommissioned`/`disabled` per business rule 10. Response: `carriedMonitoring` + `monitorFieldsAdopted`, both also stamped on the `asset.merged` Event), then deletes the absorbed asset. **Dependency edges survive** (`transferDependencyEdges`, shared with the conflict absorb): devices depending on the absorbed asset are re-pointed at the survivor (self-edges + duplicate (child, survivor, source) rows left to cascade), the absorbed asset's own parent links blank-fill onto a survivor with none, and when BOTH sides have parent rows `dependencyWinner` decides wholesale (omitted = survivor keeps its own; never a union — one device has one real upstream and a union weakens all-down suppression). The merge modal renders each side's effective parents (+ infra dependent count) as a comparison row that becomes a highlighted conflict with Keep A/B radios when both sides' parent sets differ. `lastSeenSwitch`/`lastSeenAp` carry with lastSeen-recency semantics (blank-fill; both-sides-set → the more recently seen record wins) so the endpoint dependency edge can re-derive. The absorbed asset's interface-comment overrides, LLDP/wireless rows, and pending Conflicts **cascade-delete**; its sample/telemetry/rollup/custom-widget time-series are **orphaned and aged out via `drop_chunks`** (no FK since migration `20260615000000` — a cascade delete would decompress their TimescaleDB chunks into bloat, prod incident 2026-06-08). Either way the survivor keeps its own history and the absorbed asset's is not carried over (the UI surfaces monitored status + sources + each side's polling-history size from `GET /assets/:id/polling-history` and auto-selects the longer-history side as survivor — operator-overridable; the confirm dialog quantifies the history being deleted, warns when the shorter side was kept, and warns the loss is permanent). Refusal rules: self-merge (400), either asset missing (404). Returns `{ survivorId, absorbedId, movedSources, movedMacs, movedIps, movedIpHistory, movedSightings, movedManagedAgent, movedDependencyParents, replacedDependencyParents, movedDependents, appliedFields }`. Writes one `asset.merged` Event. Powers the **Merge asset…** button on the Sources tab.
- `GET    /assets/:id/dependencies`             *(auth)* — Read effective + computed + override parents AND direct children for the dependency-suppression DAG. Returns `{ asset: { id, hostname, assetType, dependencyLayer, dependencySuppressed, dependencySuppressedAt }, effectiveParents, computedParents, overrideParents, hasOverride, children, childrenTruncated, childCount }`. Each parent entry is `{ id (row id), parent: { id, hostname, assetType, dependencyLayer, monitorStatus, monitored }, source, detectedVia }`. **Resolution rule**: if any `source="override"` rows exist for this asset, the override set is the effective set (computed rows ignored); otherwise every NON-override row is effective — `computed` (Fortinet infra), `endpoint` (an endpoint's leaf edge) and `vcenter` (VM→host) alike. Both this split and the per-child binding rule tested `source === "computed"` literally until 2026-08, which hid the endpoint and vCenter halves from the tree even though the reconciler was suppressing on them. Empty override set = explicit "no parents" pin. The `children` array carries two layers down (direct children + grandchildren) — every asset that has THIS asset in its **effective** parent set plus, nested under each direct child, that child's own effective children. Each child entry: `{ id, hostname, assetType, dependencyLayer, monitorStatus, monitored, dependencySuppressed, source, detectedVia, childCount, grandchildren: [...] }` where each grandchild has the same shape minus `grandchildren`/`childCount`. Sorted within each layer by type (firewall→switch→access_point) then hostname. **The downward view is INFRA-ONLY at both layers** (`FORTINET_INFRA_ASSET_TYPES`, filtered in SQL — `take` applies before any in-memory filter, so a gate with 300 switch children would otherwise fill the read and report nothing). The endpoint half of the DAG makes every workstation / server / printer a child of the switch, AP or gate that last saw it, and a site gate is the last-seen device for the entire site, so those rows would bury the two or three an operator opened the tree to read. They are excluded here deliberately even though they are real edges the reconciler suppresses on — an endpoint's dependency is shown on its OWN General tab, as the parent above it, which is where the suppression it drives is worth explaining. Caps therefore bound a controller FortiGate's managed switches/APs, not the endpoint half: `DEP_INFRA_CHILD_CAP` 300 direct + `DEP_GRANDCHILD_CAP` 500 grandchildren, with `childrenTruncated` set when the direct read overflowed. `childCount` counts INFRA children only (a findMany over the indexed `parentAssetId` with the relation type filter, deduped per child — a groupBy can't filter on a relation) so the UI's "+N" hint can never become an endpoint tally, which is exactly the noise the type filter removes. Drives the General-tab Dependency Tree block on the asset details modal so the common firewall → switch → AP chain renders without click-through; operators still click through for anything deeper than two layers.
- `PUT    /assets/:id/dependencies/override`    *(admin)* — Replace the asset's `source="override"` rows. Body: `{ parentAssetIds: string[] }` (max 20). Each id must reference a real Fortinet infra asset (`firewall` / `switch` / `access_point`). Cycle check walks back through every proposed parent's existing effective parents — if any path reaches `id`, returns 400. Empty array = explicit "no parents" pin (asset opts out of suppression entirely; the GET response will then show `hasOverride: true` with empty `effectiveParents`). Writes one `asset.dependency.override_set` Event.
- `DELETE /assets/:id/dependencies/override`    *(admin)* — Clear all override rows; computed set takes effect. Writes one `asset.dependency.override_cleared` Event when at least one row was deleted.
- `POST   /assets/:id/dependency-test`           *(admin)* — Start a dependency-suppression test: marks the asset down (via `dependencyTestUntil`/`dependencyTestStartedBy`) for a window so operators can watch suppression propagate to children without a real outage.
- `DELETE /assets/:id/dependency-test`           *(admin)* — End the test early (clears `dependencyTestUntil`).
- `GET    /assets/:id/connection-path`          *(auth)* — Resolve the upward chain from this asset to its upstream FortiGate so the Device Map topology overlay can dim everything off-path. Returns `{ asset: {id, hostname, ipAddress, macAddress, assetType, monitorStatus}, hops: ConnectionPathHop[], alternateUplinks: number, siteId: string | null }`. Each hop carries `kind: "endpoint" | "switch" | "firewall"`, the asset row's id + hostname + ipAddress + macAddress + assetType + monitorStatus + monitored flag, plus optional `endpointPort` (port label parsed from the leaf endpoint's `lastSeenSwitch`, populated on the first switch hop) and `uplinkInterface` (the switch's local interface that goes UP, from `fortinetTopology.uplinkInterface`). Resolution: firewall short-circuits to a single-hop self-path; switches/APs walk upward from themselves; endpoints (workstations / servers / printers / other) parse `Asset.lastSeenSwitch = "<switchId>/<port>"` to find the upstream switch, then walk. The upward walk reads `AssetDependencyParent` rows (override rows take precedence over computed) and picks the parent with `monitorStatus="up"` AND most-recent `lastMonitorAt` for MCLAG / dual-homed switches; remaining-parent counts are summed across hops into `alternateUplinks` so the UI can hint "+N alternate uplinks." Falls back to `fortinetTopology.controllerFortigate` / `parentSwitch` when dependency rows are empty (fresh installs before the backfill job runs, or freshly-discovered switches awaiting recompute). Capped at 16 hops as a sanity guard against pathological data. `siteId` is the firewall asset id at the top of the chain when the walk reached one; null when the chain terminated short (orphan asset with no `lastSeenSwitch`, or upstream chain not yet discovered). Resolver lives at [src/services/connectionPathService.ts](src/services/connectionPathService.ts); consumed by the Device Map topology modal which overlays the endpoint as a Cytoscape node + dims off-path elements.
- `GET    /assets/quarantine-availability`      *(assetsQuarantine ≥ read)* — `{ pushEnabled, integrationCount, pushEnabledCount }`: is `config.pushQuarantine` on for ANY **enabled** FortiManager / FortiGate integration? MUST stay above `GET /:id`. Every frontend surface that OFFERS a quarantine reads it and withholds the verb when false — `quarantineAsset` skips push-disabled integrations, so with the toggle off fleet-wide the push resolves to zero targets and 502s with "0/0 FortiGate(s) accepted the push". Release is never gated on it (see `getQuarantinePushAvailability` in assetQuarantineService).
- `GET    /assets/:id/quarantine-status`        *(auth)* — `{ status, quarantineReason, quarantinedAt, quarantinedBy, quarantineTargets }`.
- `POST   /assets/:id/quarantine`               *(assetsQuarantine ≥ write — session or token role)* — Push MAC block to every FortiGate that has a sighting within `sightingMaxAgeDays`. Body: `{ reason? }`. Returns `{ message, succeededCount, failedCount, targets[] }`. On at least one push success the asset `status` is set to `quarantined` and `quarantineTargets` is stamped. actor is derived from session username or `req.apiToken.name`. **Infrastructure assets (`assetType` = `firewall` / `switch` / `access_point`) are rejected with 400** — quarantining the device that does the quarantining would lock the operator out of the network. Release endpoints don't enforce the type guard so a misclassified quarantine can still be undone.
- `DELETE /assets/:id/quarantine`               *(assetsQuarantine ≥ write — session or token role)* — Best-effort unpush from all synced targets, then restores `statusBeforeQuarantine` (defaults to `active`) and `monitoredBeforeQuarantine` (defaults to not-monitored) in one write. Device-side failure does not block release.
- `POST   /assets/:id/quarantine/verify`        *(assetsQuarantine ≥ write — session or token role)* — Re-reads each target from the FortiGate and flips any missing ones to `drift`. Persists the updated `quarantineTargets` if drift was detected. Writes `asset.quarantine.drift_detected` Event.
- `POST   /assets/bulk-quarantine`              *(assetsQuarantine ≥ write — session or token role)* — Body `{ ids[], reason? }`. Per-asset errors are collected; partial success is still reported. Returns `{ results: [{ id, ok, message }] }`.
- `POST   /assets/bulk-quarantine/release`      *(assetsQuarantine ≥ write — session or token role)* — Body `{ ids[] }`. Best-effort release per asset.

### API Tokens — `apiTokens` function key (read at mount; writes escalate to `apiTokens=write`)
- `GET    /api-tokens`                          — List all tokens (`{ tokens[], roles[], quarantineIntegrations[], apiBaseUrl }`). `roles` is the role catalogue (`{ id, name, description, grantsQuarantineWrite, adminEquivalent }`) for the "acts as role" dropdown; `quarantineIntegrations` is the FMG/FortiGate roster (`{ id, name, type, enabled, pushQuarantineEnabled }`) so the UI can render the per-token integration picker and the "push disabled — integration off / pushQuarantine toggle off" alert without a second round-trip. `apiBaseUrl` is the address external callers dial — `POLARIS_PUBLIC_URL`'s origin + `/api/v1` (`getPublicApiBaseUrl` in `utils/publicUrl.ts`), `null` when that env var is unset/malformed, in which case the tab falls back to the browser's own origin and says so. Hashes are never returned.
- `POST   /api-tokens`                          — Create. Body: `{ name, roleId, integrationIds?: string[], expiresAt? }`. `integrationIds` is REQUIRED + non-empty when the chosen role grants `assetsQuarantine` ≥ write; ignored otherwise. Each id must reference a real integration of type `fortimanager` or `fortigate`. Binding an admin-equivalent role logs an `api_token.admin_equivalent` warning Event. Returns `{ token: ApiTokenSummary, rawToken: string }` — `rawToken` is shown once and never recoverable.
- `POST   /api-tokens/:id/revoke`               — Mark as revoked (token stops working immediately); row is kept for audit.
- `DELETE /api-tokens/:id`                      — Hard-delete the token row.

### Credentials — mixed scoping
- `GET    /credentials`                         *(auth)* — List stored credentials with secrets masked. Read-open so any role's Asset Monitoring tab can render the credential picker.
- `GET    /credentials/usage`                   *(auth)* — Effective-usage asset count per credential, keyed by credential id (`{ [credId]: number }`). Drives the **Assets** column on the Stored Credentials table in one round-trip. Computed by `credentialService.getCredentialUsageCounts()` — one `asset.findMany` + class-override + integration lookups, resolving the FK fall-through (asset stream → asset default → class override → integration default) in memory. Registered before `/:id` so "usage" isn't read as an id.
- `GET    /credentials/:id`                     *(auth)* — Single credential, masked.
- `GET    /credentials/:id/usage`               *(auth)* — Full usage breakdown for one credential (`credentialService.getCredentialUsage`): `{ total, assetLevel[], classLevel[], integrationLevel[], classRefCount, integrationRefCount }`. Each asset lands in its most-specific tier bucket (asset > class > integration), so `total` is a true distinct count. Drives the credential **usage slide-in** in Server Settings → Credentials, whose asset rows deep-link to `/assets.html#view=asset:<id>`. Resolves by FK wiring ("where is this credential configured"), not by polling-method type-match. Since discovery stamps the integration's credential onto each discovered asset's `monitorCredentialId`, a stamped default whose value is one of the asset's integration's credentials is reclassified asset → integration level (only a per-stream slot or a default the integration doesn't provide is genuine asset-level).
- `POST   /credentials`                         *(admin)* — Create. Body: `{ name, type: "snmp"|"winrm"|"ssh", config }`. Type-specific config is validated server-side.
- `PUT    /credentials/:id`                     *(admin)* — Update. Type cannot be changed after creation. Resubmitting the mask sentinel for a secret field preserves the stored value.
- `DELETE /credentials/:id`                     *(admin)* — 409 if any asset effectively uses the credential (via `getCredentialUsage` — asset / class-override / integration-default tiers, all 8 per-stream slots + the `monitorCredentialId` default), with a level-aware message; also 409 when no asset resolves to it but a class override or integration default still references it (deleting would silently null those out).
- `POST   /credentials/test`                    *(admin)* — Exercise a credential against a chosen target without persisting anything. Body: `{ assetId?, host?, type, config, id? }` — the target is EITHER an asset (borrow its address) or a hand-typed `host`, and the schema `refine` requires one of them (except for `restapi`, which carries its own `baseUrl` and needs neither). The two answer different questions: an asset test aims at real inventory, a typed host is what you need BEFORE the device is onboarded, or when it never will be one (a staging unit, a vendor demo, a local stub). `assetId` WINS when both arrive, so a stale `host` left in a body can't redirect a probe aimed at an asset. A typed host goes through `normalizeProbeTarget` (utils/probeTarget.ts), which REFUSES a URL / embedded port / path rather than salvaging a host out of it — the discarded parts are owned by the credential (`useHttps`/`port`/`path`) or by the transport's default, so accepting them would dial something other than what the operator typed and then attribute the result to the credential; the refusal is returned as a test RESULT, not a 4xx, so the modal renders it inline beside the field. `details.hostSource` (`"asset"` | `"manual"`) is audited on the `credential.tested` Event, because probing known inventory and probing a freely-chosen address are materially different acts when reviewing what Polaris reached out to. Note this adds no reach a `credentials:write` caller lacked — a `restapi` credential has always been testable against an arbitrary `baseUrl`. When `id` is present, masked secrets in `config` are merged from the stored credential via `mergeConfigPreservingSecrets()` so the operator can edit and test without retyping the password. Resolves the asset's host from `ipAddress || dnsName || hostname`, then dispatches to `monitoringService.probeCredentialAgainstHost()` (icmp/snmp/winrm/ssh/restapi/http — the same one-shot probe primitives used by the response-time monitor; note `icmp` is reachable only from internal callers, since the body's `type` validates against the CREDENTIAL type enum). Returns the standard probe shape `{ success, responseTimeMs, error?, host }`, plus — for `http` credentials only — **`httpDiagnostics`** `{ url, statusCode, contentType, bytesRead, bodyTruncatedAtCap, excerpt, excerptTruncated, matched }`. That block is the point of the test flow for this type: an HTTP check's expectation is a string the operator has to pick OUT of the device's response, and pass/fail gives them nothing to pick from — so the modal renders the request line as dialed, the status, and a 4 KB body excerpt under the verdict, and the loop is save-with-a-path → test → read the body → paste a distinctive string into Expected content → test again. `matched` is reported SEPARATELY from `success` because with `failOnMismatch` off those two legitimately disagree, and `matched: null` means "no expectation configured yet" rather than "no match". The response BODY never enters the `credential.tested` Event (only `httpStatus` / `httpUrl` / `httpMatched` are audited — arbitrary device output would otherwise ride every pg_dump and syslog forward), and no response header other than `content-type` is returned, since a full dump would surface a live `Set-Cookie`. Validation failures are returned in the same shape rather than 4xx so the modal renders them inline alongside probe failures. Drives the **Test Connection** button on the add/edit credential modal in Server Settings → Credentials, which opens a second modal with an asset autocomplete (powered by `GET /assets?search=…&limit=25` — not the global `/search` endpoint, whose 8-per-group cap and pinned-firewall→`sites` partition silently dropped firewalls from the picker) and reports the result inline. Each call writes one `credential.tested` Event (info on success, warning on failure).

### Manufacturer Aliases — `requireAdmin`
- `GET    /manufacturer-aliases`                — List every alias row (`{ id, alias, canonical, createdAt, updatedAt }`).
- `POST   /manufacturer-aliases`                — Create. Body: `{ alias, canonical }`. `alias` is normalized to lowercase + trimmed before insert; uniqueness on the lowercased form. 409 on duplicate. Saving refreshes the in-memory cache and runs `applyAliasesToExistingRows()` in the background so existing Asset/MibFile rows pick up the new mapping.
- `PUT    /manufacturer-aliases/:id`            — Update. Either or both of `alias` / `canonical` can be supplied. Same cache-refresh + backfill on save.
- `DELETE /manufacturer-aliases/:id`            — Remove. Cache is refreshed; existing rows are not rewritten (they already hold the canonical value).

### Monitor Settings — mixed scoping
Reads open to any authenticated caller (the asset edit modal's tier-badge UI needs them); writes require **assetsadmin** (admin also passes). All writes invalidate the in-memory resolver cache for the relevant scope and emit one `monitor_settings.{manual|integration|class_override}.{updated|created|deleted}` audit Event. See the **Monitor Settings Hierarchy** section below for the resolution model.
- `GET    /monitor-settings/manual`              *(auth)* — Manual tier (settings for orphan assets — `discoveredByIntegrationId = null`). Returns the saved JSON or `null` when unseeded.
- `PUT    /monitor-settings/manual`              *(assetsadmin)* — Replace the manual tier with the full tier-3 block: `{ intervalSeconds (1..86400), failureThreshold (1..100), probeTimeoutMs (100..60000), telemetryTimeoutMs (1000..120000, optional), systemInfoTimeoutMs (1000..120000, optional), telemetryIntervalSeconds (15..86400), systemInfoIntervalSeconds (60..86400), sampleRetentionDays (0..3650), telemetryRetentionDays (0..3650), systemInfoRetentionDays (0..3650) }`. `telemetryTimeoutMs` / `systemInfoTimeoutMs` are optional/nullable so existing call sites that didn't supply them keep working — null falls through to the hardcoded floor (10000ms each).
- `GET    /monitor-settings/integration/:id`     *(auth)* — Integration tier (settings stored at `Integration.config.monitorSettings`). Returns `{ integrationId, integrationName, integrationType, settings: TierSettings | null }`.
- `PUT    /monitor-settings/integration/:id`     *(assetsadmin)* — Same body shape as the manual tier. Writes the JSON into `Integration.config.monitorSettings` without clobbering other config keys.
- `GET    /monitor-settings/class-overrides`     *(auth)* — List class overrides. Filterable by `?integrationId=` (use the URL sentinel `null` for the manual-tier scope) and `?assetType=`. Each row carries the joined integration `{ id, name, type }`.
- `POST   /monitor-settings/class-overrides`     *(assetsadmin)* — Create. Body: `{ integrationId: uuid | null, assetType, ...partialTierSettings }`. Every settings field is optional — null means inherit from below. 409 if a row already exists for `(integrationId, assetType)`. 400 if `integrationId` is non-null but doesn't reference a real integration.
- `PUT    /monitor-settings/class-overrides/:id` *(assetsadmin)* — Update. Body accepts any subset of the 8 settings fields; each null clears that field (= inherit from below).
- `DELETE /monitor-settings/class-overrides/:id` *(assetsadmin)* — Remove the row.
- `GET    /monitor-settings/asset-overrides`     *(auth)* — Reverse lookup. Returns assets that have at least one of `monitorIntervalSec` / `cpuMemoryIntervalSec` / `temperatureIntervalSec` / `systemInfoIntervalSec` / `probeTimeoutMs` / `cpuMemoryTimeoutMs` / `temperatureTimeoutMs` / `systemInfoTimeoutMs` set OR any per-stream polling column non-null, filterable by `?integrationId=` (URL sentinel `null` = manual scope) and `?assetType=`. Capped at 500 rows. Drives the asset edit modal's "Show other asset overrides under this scope" slide-over.

#### Monitor Settings Hierarchy

Resolution order, most-specific first:

```
asset override  →  (assetType + manual) class override (manual scope only — Phase 2)
                →  per-class streams block on integration  (when discoveredByIntegrationId is set)
                                      Integration.config.<klass>Monitor.streams.<stream>:
                                        - fortimanager / fortigate: fortigateMonitor (assetType=firewall) /
                                          fortiswitchMonitor (assetType=switch) /
                                          fortiapMonitor (assetType=access_point)
                                        - activedirectory / entraid / windowsserver:
                                          workstationMonitor (assetType=workstation) /
                                          serverMonitor (assetType=server)
                →  integration tier   (when discoveredByIntegrationId is set; flat
                                       Integration.config.monitorSettings — used by endpoint
                                       asset types not covered by a per-class subtab set)
                →  systemInfoIntervalSeconds ONLY: derive from integration.pollInterval × 3600
                                      (when discoveredByIntegrationId is set AND tier-3 left it null AND
                                       the per-class streams block didn't set interfaces.intervalSeconds)
                →  manual tier        (when discoveredByIntegrationId is null)
                →  hardcoded floor    (final fallback; never user-visible)
```

- **Tier-1 / per-asset** — columns on `Asset`: `monitorIntervalSec`, `cpuMemoryIntervalSec`, `temperatureIntervalSec`, `systemInfoIntervalSec`, `lldpIntervalSec` *(Phase 2)*, `storageIntervalSec` *(Phase 2)*, `probeTimeoutMs`, `cpuMemoryTimeoutMs`, `temperatureTimeoutMs`, `systemInfoTimeoutMs`. null = inherit. These cadence/timeout fields are the ONLY settings that cascade to the per-asset tier; `failureThreshold` and the three retentions stop at tier-2. CPU/memory and temperature each carry their own per-stream column set as of Slice 2; LLDP and Storage gained their own per-asset cadence columns in Phase 2 alongside the queue carve-out.
- **Tier-2 / class override** — `MonitorClassOverride` row keyed on `(integrationId, assetType)`. **As of Phase 2 this table is manual-scope only** (`integrationId IS NULL`). The `POST` and `PUT` routes reject integration-scoped writes outright with 400; the `migrateMonitorSettingsPerClass` startup job folds historical integration-scoped rows into the per-class streams blocks on each integration and deletes them in the same transaction. Every settings field is nullable; null = inherit. Includes its own `cpuMemoryTimeoutMs` / `temperatureTimeoutMs` / `systemInfoTimeoutMs` alongside `probeTimeoutMs`.
- **Tier-3a / per-class streams (Phase 2 — integration-discovered assets only)** — `Integration.config.<klass>Monitor.streams.<stream>` where the class block is picked by `Asset.assetType`. Per integration type:
  - `fortimanager` / `fortigate` → `fortigateMonitor` (firewall) / `fortiswitchMonitor` (switch) / `fortiapMonitor` (access_point). FortiAP omits storage.
  - `activedirectory` / `entraid` / `windowsserver` → `workstationMonitor` (workstation) / `serverMonitor` (server).
  Each stream cell carries `{polling, credentialId, intervalSeconds, timeoutMs, mibId, failureThreshold?}` — `failureThreshold` only applies on `responseTime`; the resolver ignores it elsewhere. Null on any cell falls through to the flat tier-3 baseline below. Endpoint asset types (printer / router / other / etc.) discovered via FortiGate DHCP or AD/Entra/WinSrv that don't fall into a per-class subtab set bypass this tier entirely and use the flat baseline directly. See `pickClassStreamsBlock` + `applyClassStreamsOverlay` in `monitoringService.ts`.
- **Tier-3b / integration flat baseline or manual** — full tier-settings block (cadence/retention/threshold + the three timeout fields + the Phase 2 LLDP / Storage cadence + timeout fields), complete (no nulls) **except `systemInfoIntervalSeconds` at the integration tier**, which is nullable. Stored at `Integration.config.monitorSettings` for integration-discovered assets, or in the `manualMonitorSettings` Setting row for orphan assets. Existing tier-3 rows written before the LLDP / Storage tuning fields existed fall through to the hardcoded floor (10000ms timeouts, 600s LLDP+Storage interval) via the resolver's `tierFromJson` default until an operator saves new values.
- **Integration pollInterval linkage** (`systemInfoIntervalSeconds` only). When the integration tier doesn't explicitly set this field (operator left it blank, OR the migration job retroactively nulled the literal-default 600s), `loadIntegrationTierSettings` derives the cadence from `integration.pollInterval × 3600` so interface / LLDP / storage / IPsec scrape on the same schedule discovery already runs (1–24h pollInterval → 3600–86400s systemInfo). Ties the heavy-cadence work to a knob operators already understand and cuts interface-sample volume by 24× at the default 4h pollInterval. Explicit per-asset / class / integration-tier values still win. Tracked in `tierSystemInfoFromPollIntervalCache` (parallel to `tierCache`); `resolveMonitorSettingsWithProvenance` reads it to label the provenance `"integrationPollInterval"` so the integration edit modal's Cadence & Retention input renders `Leave blank to follow this integration's discovery interval (currently 4h)`. Manual-tier orphan assets are not eligible (no integration to inherit from) and fall through to the hardcoded floor. Existing 600s defaults are nulled retroactively by the `migrateSystemInfoCadenceLinkage` startup job. The `/assets/:id/effective-monitor-settings` response includes `integration: { id, name, type, pollInterval }` so frontend hints can be rendered without a second round-trip.
- **Hardcoded floor** — values baked into `monitoringService.ts` (60s probe, 60s telemetry, 600s sysinfo, 5000ms probe timeout, 10000ms telemetry timeout, 10000ms system-info timeout, threshold 3, 30d retentions). Final fallback only used when the migration job hasn't seeded tier-3 yet AND the legacy `monitorSettings` Setting row is also gone.

`resolveMonitorSettings(asset)` (in `src/services/monitoringService.ts`) walks the four tiers and returns the effective values. `resolveMonitorSettingsWithProvenance(asset)` returns the same plus per-field `provenance: "asset" | "class" | "integration" | "integration-class" | "manual" | "integrationPollInterval" | "default"` labels and the `classOverrideId` for UI deep-links. **Both derive from one core (`resolveMonitorSettingsCore`, 2026-08 fold)**, so the UI payload is by construction the runtime resolution — polling values are compatibility-gated at every tier with source-default substitution, and `"default"` labels a polling field where no tier supplied a compatible method (the resolved value carries the materialized source default, which may be null when the stream isn't delivered for the source kind). The UI-only extras (per-class origin sub-labels, `classOverrideId`, the pollInterval sub-label) live in the provenance wrapper so the plain resolver stays hot-path cheap. `"integration-class"` (Phase 2 — sub-label of the integration tier) means the value came from the per-class streams block `<klass>Monitor.streams.<stream>` rather than the flat `monitorSettings` baseline, so the asset modal's tier badge reads "FortiSwitch subtab" instead of generic "FortiManager". `"integrationPollInterval"` is a `systemInfoIntervalSeconds`-only sub-label indicating the value was derived from the integration's discovery `pollInterval` rather than read from explicit tier-3 JSON. **Resolver cache key is now `${integrationId}:${assetType}`** (Phase 2 — was previously `${integrationId}`); each per-class branch gets its own cached snapshot. Write paths (the tier CRUD in `monitorSettingsService.ts`, the integration config save) call `invalidateMonitorSettingsCache({integrationId, assetType?})` after every write — when `assetType` is omitted (integration config save), every `${integrationId}:*` entry is walked and dropped.

There is **no probe backoff for confirmed-down hosts, and no acceleration mid-run either**. Down assets keep probing at the resolved `intervalSeconds`, and so does an asset whose failure/recovery run is still being confirmed -- so `down` is reached after `failureThreshold x intervalSeconds`. (The fast-confirm re-probe that shortened that to ~35s regardless of cadence was removed 2026-08-19; `fastConfirmIntervalSec` survives as a dormant column read by nothing, and in-run resolution is now the ICMP loss sampler's job, feeding packet loss only -- business rule 30.) Heavy cadences (telemetry / systemInfo / fastFiltered) are still suppressed while `monitorStatus = "down"` so a wedged peer doesn't burn worker time, but the cheap response-time probe keeps firing — recovery is detected within one base-cadence tick instead of up to 30 minutes.

│   │   ├── pollingCapability.ts    # Does a COLLECTOR EXIST for this (source, stream, method)? Deliberately separate from pollingCompatibility.ts, which answers the different question "is this method MEANINGFUL for this source". Every write validator checked the second and nothing checked the first, so a class of settings validated, persisted, resolved and then collected nothing — invisibly, because `runTelemetryFor` counts a `{supported:false}` stream as a SUCCESSFUL tick and the queue publishers drop the unimplemented transports before enqueueing. `collectorCapability(source, stream, method, {assetType})` returns `{implemented, reason}`; `assetType` matters only on the Fortinet REST paths (a managed FortiSwitch gets up/down only, a FortiAP additionally cpu/mem + temperature off the `wifi/managed_ap` row, a firewall everything but storage). Consumers WARN rather than refuse — a hard 400 would punish an operator re-saving a value they did not create — so `assertPollingCompatible` and `validateAssetUpdate` log, the UI stops OFFERING dead combinations (`_collectorExists` in public/js/integrations.js), and `jobs/auditPollingCapability.ts` names the already-stored ones. **This table is a claim about code elsewhere: flip an entry in the same commit that implements its collector.**
**Cross-transport streams — `processes` + `eventLog`** (migration `20260623000000_processes_eventlog_streams`). Two additional streams flow through the same hierarchy as the original six. They are **not agent-only** — `processes` resolves to agent / SNMP (`hrSWRunTable`/`hrSWRunPerfTable`) / SSH (`ps`,`tasklist`) / WinRM (`Get-Process`); `eventLog` resolves to agent / SSH (`journalctl`,`Get-WinEvent`) / WinRM / REST (FortiOS device log). The allowed method set per stream is enforced by `STREAM_METHODS` + `isMethodValidForStream` in `src/utils/pollingCompatibility.ts` (`processes` rejects REST + ICMP; `eventLog` rejects SNMP + ICMP), and `resolveStream` adopts a tier's method only when it passes BOTH the source matrix AND the stream matrix. Both default to **`disabled`** for every source (`defaultPollingForSource`) — opt-in. Columns mirror the storage stream on `Asset` + `MonitorClassOverride`: `processesPolling`/`eventLogPolling`, `processesIntervalSec(onds)`/`eventLogIntervalSec(onds)`, `processesTimeoutMs`/`eventLogTimeoutMs`, `processesCredentialId`/`eventLogCredentialId`, `processesMibId` (eventLog has no MIB). The integration Monitoring tab renders **Processes** + **Event Log** stream subtabs next to Storage (`_ALL_STREAMS` in `public/js/integrations.js`); `_streamsForClass` scopes them — workstation/server get both, FortiGate gets eventLog only, FortiSwitch/FortiAP get neither. Per-transport collectors land in later phases; the foundational layer is the configuration surface + resolution only.

#### Where each tier is edited

- **Tier-3 integration (Phase 2 per-class)** — each integration's edit modal has a **Monitoring tab** with **per-class subtabs** (FMG / FortiGate: FortiGate / FortiSwitch / FortiAP; AD / Entra ID / Windows Server: Workstations / Servers). Each class subtab carries the six per-stream subtabs (Response Time / CPU/Memory / Temperature / Interfaces / LLDP / Storage; FortiAP omits Storage). Each per-stream subtab holds the polling method, credential, cadence, timeout, and (response-time only) failure threshold. Save Changes serializes each class's stream values into `Integration.config.<klass>Monitor.streams.<stream>` via the regular integration PUT; the flat `monitorSettings` JSON is still written from the FortiGate / Workstations subtab as the "default for endpoint asset types" fallback.
- **Tier-3 manual** — Assets page header → **Monitoring Settings** button → modal's **Manual Monitoring** section. Same per-stream layout. Used by orphan / manually-created assets. Writes via `PUT /api/v1/monitor-settings/manual`.
- **Tier-2 class overrides (manual scope only — Phase 2)** — Assets-page **Monitoring Settings** modal → **Class Overrides** section. The source picker no longer surfaces integrations; the section is labelled "Manual scope only — assets without an integration source." Backend `POST` / `PUT` reject integration-scoped rows with 400. Operators who used to add overrides scoped to a specific integration now use that integration's per-class subtabs (above) which deliver the same effect via the streams block instead of the override table.
- **Tier-1 per-asset** — the asset edit modal's **Monitoring tab** carries the cadence/timeout overrides (`monitorIntervalSec`, `probeTimeoutMs`, plus the per-asset `cpuMemoryIntervalSec` / `temperatureIntervalSec` / `systemInfoIntervalSec` columns), tier-source badges from `/effective-monitor-settings`, and a **Show other asset overrides under this scope** button that opens a slide-over listing peer assets with their own per-asset overrides.

The integration's Monitoring tab additionally carries a **Discovery Defaults** section on FMG/FortiGate types only, with three subtabs (FortiGates / FortiSwitches / FortiAPs). Each subtab holds discovery-time concerns: `addAsMonitored`, `snmpCredentialId`, `sshCredentialId`, `autoMonitorInterfaces`. **Cadence inputs are no longer in these subtabs** — they live in the Cadence & Retention section above and apply uniformly across the integration's entire fleet. The credential rows are **type-aware**: the SNMP picker is rendered only when at least one of the four integration-tier polling dropdowns is set to SNMP, the SSH picker only when at least one is set to SSH, and both stay hidden when neither is selected. Credentials persist regardless of visibility, so flipping back later restores the prior selection.

### Events — mixed scoping
- `GET    /events`                              *(auth)* — Audit log (filter by level, action, resourceType, resourceName, actor, message — the text columns are case-insensitive substring by default and take an operator-aware `<field>Op` of contains | not_contains | empty | is_not_empty)
- `GET    /events/resource-types`               *(auth)* — distinct `resourceType` values across the retention window; feeds the full Resource-column filter option set on the Events page
- `GET    /events/archive-settings`             *(admin)* — reveals SSH host/user/path even with password masked
- `PUT    /events/archive-settings`             *(admin)*
- `POST   /events/archive-test`                 *(admin)*
- `GET    /events/syslog-settings`              *(admin)* — reveals host/port/TLS paths
- `PUT    /events/syslog-settings`              *(admin)*
- `POST   /events/syslog-test`                  *(admin)*
- `GET    /events/retention-settings`           *(auth)*
- `PUT    /events/retention-settings`           *(admin)*
- `GET    /events/asset-decommission-settings`  *(auth)*
- `PUT    /events/asset-decommission-settings`  *(admin)* — `{ inactivityMonths }`; 0 disables auto-decommission

### Conflicts — `requireAuth` (role-scoped list + resolve)
- `GET    /conflicts`                           — List. Gated on `discoveryConflicts:read` — any holder sees both entity types (the historical networkadmin↔reservation / assetsadmin↔asset role-name split was dropped 2026-08); others see an empty list.
- `GET    /conflicts/count`                     — Badge count; same role scoping as the list.
- `POST   /conflicts/:id/accept`                — Reservation: apply discovered values. Asset: upsert an `AssetSource` row (`sourceKind` = `entra`/`ad`, `externalId` = `proposedDeviceId`) tying the existing asset to the proposed Entra/AD identity, plus overlay Entra/AD fields into empty existing fields. **Hostname has one extra rule:** when the conflict was raised via 15-char NetBIOS truncation (`proposedAssetFields.matchedVia === "netbios"`), the longer canonical hostname replaces the truncated one even when the existing field is non-empty — the truncated form is a NetBIOS quirk, not a deliberate choice. **Phase 4d retired the legacy `assetTag = entra:<id>` / `ad:<guid>` write** — the AssetSource row is now the canonical identity link, and audit trail is captured by the auto-resolve syncLog event. (`prev-*` breadcrumb tags are still written pending conflict-resolution refactor.) **Ghost-sibling lookup** (when a different asset already owns the proposed source's externalId) now queries `AssetSource` by `(sourceKind, externalId)` instead of by `assetTag` — the ghost's non-empty fields are absorbed and the ghost is deleted so the unique-constraint upsert lands cleanly. 403 if caller's role doesn't cover this conflict's entityType.
- `POST   /conflicts/:id/reject`                — Reservation: keep existing, dismiss. Asset: create a separate new Asset for the Entra/AD snapshot, then upsert its `AssetSource` row (`sourceKind` = `entra`/`ad`, `externalId` = `proposedDeviceId`) so the next discovery run finds the new asset by source and doesn't re-fire the collision.
- `GET    /conflicts/:id/chassis-diff`          *(discoveryConflicts:read)* — the per-address diff behind a `chassis-replaced` subnet conflict (business rule 41): the archived old chassis's reservations against the live subnet's, as `{ payload, lines[] }`. Each line carries `ip`, `verdict` (`only-old` | `only-new` | `differs` | `same`), both sides, and `migratable` — false with `notMigratableReason: "device-owned"` for `vip` / `interface_ip` rows, whose truth is the new gate's own config. A separate READ rather than a field on the conflict row, because discovery syncs subnets in Phase 1 and reservations in Phases 3–5, so a payload built at detection time would compare the old chassis against itself. 400 when the conflict isn't a subnet variant; 409 when it is already resolved (`loadPendingConflict`).
- `POST   /conflicts/:id/merge`                 — **Asset conflicts only.** TWO bodies, dispatched on the conflict's flavour. **duplicate-IP**: `{ survivorAssetId, absorbAssetIds: [...] }` — the records are one device recorded twice, so the named members are absorbed into the survivor via `assetMergeService.mergeAssets` (sources / MACs / IP history / sightings / agent enrolment / dependency edges move, monitoring OR-carries, the absorbed rows are deleted) and the conflict closes as `accepted` once fewer than two current claims remain — a three-way collision stays open on the survivors. **CHAINED gate: `discoveryConflicts:write` AND `assets:write`** (it deletes inventory). Refusals mirror `/reassign-ip`: 400 on a survivor or target that isn't one of the claimants, or on an empty target list (the survivor is silently dropped from its own list rather than self-merging); the pure `resolveMergeTargets` owns those rules. Writes one `asset.merged` Event per absorb plus the `conflict.accepted` close. Response `{ ok, ipAddress, survivorAssetId, absorbedAssetIds, movedSources, resolved, remaining }`. **Every other flavour**: per-field merge with operator-chosen winners. Body: `{ fieldWinners: { hostname?: "existing"|"proposed", serialNumber?, macAddress?, manufacturer?, model?, os?, osVersion?, assignedTo? } }`. Fields not present in `fieldWinners` fall back to the default accept logic (blank-fill for serial/mac/manufacturer/model/assignedTo, always-overwrite for os/osVersion, NetBIOS-upgrade rule for hostname). AssetSource stamping and ghost-asset absorption are unconditional regardless of selections. Reservation conflicts return 400 — they use the regular accept path. Audit Event message appends the selection map when used.
- `POST   /conflicts/:id/reassign-ip`           — **Duplicate-IP conflicts only** (`proposedAssetFields.collisionReason="duplicate-ip"`). Body: `{ assetId, ipAddress }` — give ONE of the assets sharing the address a different one. **CHAINED gate: `discoveryConflicts:write` AND `assets:write`** (the `/network-scans/:id/adopt` precedent — resolving queue entries and editing inventory are separable grants). Writes `ipAddress` + `ipOverride` + `ipSource="manual"` in one update (operator-pin semantics identical to typing an address in the asset edit form, so the `src/db.ts` override guard defers and a later discovery write reporting the same address releases the pin by itself), closes the asset’s pending ip-override conflict, and stamps an `asset.updated` Event with the field changes. Refusals: 400 on a non-duplicate-IP conflict / an assetId that isn’t one of the claimants / an invalid or unchanged address, 404 on a missing asset, **409 when another network-present asset already records the target address** (that moves the duplicate instead of resolving it). Response `{ ok, ipAddress, newIpAddress, assetId, resolved, remaining }` — the conflict closes as `accepted` when fewer than two current claims remain, otherwise it stays open on the survivors (a three-way collision takes two reassignments). Delegates to `reassignDuplicateIpAsset` in services/duplicateIpConflictService.ts.

**Asset-conflict flavours.** `proposedAssetFields.collisionReason` distinguishes the pathways that raise an asset conflict. The two discovery-sync collision flavours, in decreasing order of confidence:
- `"untagged-collision"` — incoming Entra/AD/vCenter device's hostname matches an existing asset that has no source tag (DHCP-discovered, manually created, etc.). vCenter raises this flavour for both VMs and ESXi hosts (`proposedAssetFields.sourceType="vcenter"`, `assetType` discriminating VM vs host).
- `"duplicate-registration"` — incoming hostname matches an existing asset already tagged by the same source with a *different* deviceId/objectGUID (Entra returned two distinct deviceIds for the same display name — re-enrol, re-image, dual-boot — or AD has two `objectGUID`s for what looks like the same physical computer). Accepting re-keys the existing asset's source row to the incoming externalId (the prior identity is captured in the auto-resolve syncLog Event for audit).

A `bothAssetsExist: true` flag on `proposedAssetFields` marks the **sibling** sub-case of `"untagged-collision"`: the incoming device *already* has its own Polaris asset, and a second, un-linked asset shares its hostname. Raised by the Entra and vCenter (VM + host) sibling checks. It exists to route duplicate-asset cleanup through the Conflicts queue (Apply merge) rather than the asset-details Sources → Merge search. Accept runs the normal ghost-absorb (collision-target survives, the source-owning duplicate is absorbed + deleted); reject creates nothing — `rejectAssetConflict` short-circuits when the proposed `(sourceKind, externalId)` already owns an asset.

**The absorb preserves the duplicate's provenance.** The ghost here is a real multi-source asset, not a placeholder — it routinely holds discovery sources the collision target knows nothing about. So the absorb runs inside ONE transaction that calls the shared `absorbAssetRelations` (from `assetMergeService`) FIRST: every `AssetSource` row plus `AssetMacAddress` / `AssetAssociatedIp` / `AssetIpHistory` / `AssetFortigateSighting` (delete-on-conflict, survivor's row wins) and the `ManagedAgent` enrollment when the survivor has none are re-bound onto the survivor — plus the dependency edges via `transferDependencyEdges` (dependents re-pointed; the ghost's own parent links blank-fill, survivor's win when both sides have some — this path passes no `dependencyWinner`) — *then* the merged field update is applied and *then* the ghost is deleted — so the delete cascade can no longer take them. `resolveMonitoringCarry` OR-s `monitored` across the two rows the same way the operator merge does (adopting the ghost's polling methods / credentials / MIB pins / cadences and unioning its pin arrays when the flip turns the survivor ON, resetting monitor state, recomputing `monitorOverride`, business rule 10 respected), and the blank-fill absorb covers `ipAddress` / `dnsName` / `learnedLocation` / `lastSeenSwitch` / `lastSeenAp` / `snmpLocation` / `learnedAddress` / `department` / `location` / `purchaseOrder` / `acquiredAt` / `warrantyExpiry` / `assetType` (only from `"other"`) on top of the original serial/MAC/manufacturer/model/assignedTo/notes set, keeps the more-recent `lastSeen` through `bumpLastSeen` (rule 12 still applies to the absorbed evidence), and unions the ghost's tags. *Before this fix the ghost delete cascaded its `AssetSource` rows*: merging an AD-only target with a ghost carrying entra + intune + fortigate-endpoint + vcenter-vm left the survivor holding only `ad` plus a thin `vcenter-vm` row re-created from the conflict snapshot — the UI promised the assets would be "combined" while three sources' provenance was destroyed. The `conflict.accepted` Event now itemizes what was carried over. Whatever is NOT re-bound still cascades with the ghost (LLDP / wireless / interface overrides / its own pending conflicts) and its sample hypertable rows orphan and age out — identical to the operator merge. The events.js card swaps in duplicate-asset copy + a "Duplicate assets" badge.

Two further flavours are not hostname collisions at all:
- `"ip-override"` — a discovery write staged an IP that differs from the asset's operator IP pin (`Asset.ipOverride`); raised by `ipOverrideService` after the db.ts guard re-asserted the pin. Carries `proposedAssetFields = { collisionReason, ipAddress: <discovered>, ipSource, overrideIp, hostname }` and no `proposedDeviceId` / AssetSource identity. One pending conflict per asset (refreshed while open; a rejected row suppresses re-raising the same discovered IP). Accept adopts the discovered IP + releases the pin (`ipAddress`+`ipOverride`+`ipSource` in one write so the guard defers); reject keeps the pin, event-only. `/merge` on this flavour degenerates to accept. Renders as a single-row Accept/Reject card in events.js (no per-field picker).
- `"duplicate-ip"` — two or more **network-present** assets (status NOT in `UNMONITORABLE_STATUSES`) record the SAME `Asset.ipAddress`, **at least one of them a type whose address was chosen** (`CONFLICT_ELIGIBLE_ASSET_TYPES` — switch / access_point / firewall / server; endpoint-only collisions are DHCP working and never raise, while an endpoint colliding with infrastructure raises and appears as a claimant); raised by the `detectDuplicateIpAssets` sweep (business rule 40).
