## Background Jobs

| Job | Schedule | Purpose |
|-----|----------|---------|
| `expireReservations` | Every 15 min | Mark reservations past `expiresAt` as `expired` |
| `discoveryScheduler` | Per-integration `pollInterval` | Auto-trigger FMG / FortiGate / Windows Server / Entra ID / Active Directory / vCenter discovery. Filters on `lastTestOk: true`, so broken integrations are skipped. **`integrationConnectionTester` is disabled (2026-06-02), so a stuck `lastTestOk=false` no longer auto-resumes** — it must be cleared by a manual Test Connection until the planned health-from-discovery redesign lands. |
| `integrationConnectionTester` | **DISABLED 2026-06-02** (import commented out in `app.ts`; file kept pending removal) | When active: every 10 min (first run 30 s after boot), sequentially runs the credential preflight test (`/sys/status` for FMG) against every enabled integration and refreshes `lastTestAt` / `lastTestOk`. Sequential, not parallel — FortiManager drops parallel connections above ~1-2. **Skips any integration with an active discovery run** (checked via `isDiscoveryRunning`) — a fresh `/sys/status` during a long FMG discovery would collide on the shared API-key session and stamp a false-positive `lastTestOk=false`; discovery itself is the live proof during a run. Emits `integration.test.recovered` / `integration.test.failed` Events on ok-state transitions. **Why disabled:** the probe still fired false-positive `integration.test.failed` warnings on FMG — a transient RPC `-11` ("no valid session", from FMG reaping the shared session at its lifetime or a concurrent call on it) is hardcoded to "Invalid or expired API token" and stamped as `lastTestOk=false`, while a manual Test Connection seconds later succeeds. The probe never logs out of FMG (the prior hourly `/sys/logout` was removed in commit 3e70476 as the suspected cause of prod `-11` churn — see the FMG auth note in CLAUDE.md; **never call `/sys/logout`**). Planned follow-up: full removal + deriving FMG health from real discovery-run outcomes with retry-on-`-11`. |
| `ouiRefresh` | Weekly (and on startup if missing/stale) | Refresh IEEE OUI database for MAC vendor lookup |
| `pruneEvents` | Nightly | Delete Event records older than 7 days |
| `updateCheck` | Periodic | Check for software updates |
| `clampAssetAcquiredAt` | Once at startup | Clamp `acquiredAt` down to `lastSeen` on any Asset row where the invariant was violated |
| `clampMonitoredForStatus` | Every startup (self-healing, NOT marker-guarded) | Turn `monitored` off (and zero `consecutiveFailures`) on every Asset whose `status` is one of the four that cannot carry monitoring — `decommissioned` / `disabled` / `storage` / `quarantined` (business rule 10, `UNMONITORABLE_STATUSES`). One indexed UPDATE against `(monitored)`; logs a warning naming the count when it changes anything. The `20260827000000_monitorable_status_clamp` migration does the same pass once at upgrade time — this keeps it true afterwards for raw-SQL writers and for rows the best-effort write-time guard skipped. |
| `clampFailureBucket` | Every startup (self-healing, NOT marker-guarded) | Clamp `Asset.consecutiveFailures` to `MAX_MISSED_POLL_BUCKET` (100) on rows written before the bucket gained a ceiling, and zero the now-dormant `awaitingRecoveryConfirm` (business rules 30 + 36). Unbounded, an overnight outage left the bucket hundreds deep and the asset owed one answered poll per minute it had been dark before it could read `up`, with its down alert repeating and escalating throughout. `nextFailureBucket` self-heals an over-cap row at its next probe of either outcome, so this is for the readers that reach the column first — the Last-30-min strip's tooltip, `runsHeavyCadences`, and `consecutiveFailures` as an automatable `asset_state` field. Two idempotent UPDATEs that match nothing in the steady state. |
| `enforceSubnetUniqueIndex` | Every startup (self-healing, NOT marker-guarded) | Create the `subnets_block_cidr_key` UNIQUE index on `subnets (blockId, cidr)` when it is missing and the data permits it. Migration `20260806000000` skips creation on an install that already carries duplicate rows from the pre-lock race rather than failing the whole upgrade; this retries each boot so the index lands once the duplicates are cleaned up. Writes `subnet.unique_index_blocked` (warning, per boot, listing the offending CIDRs) or `subnet.unique_index_created` (info). Never fatal — the per-block advisory lock in `subnetService` is the primary guard. |
| `auditPollingCapability` | Every startup (advisory, NOT marker-guarded) | Read-only: report stored polling methods that have no collector, via `utils/pollingCapability.ts`. These are the worst kind of misconfiguration — `runTelemetryFor` counts a `{supported:false}` stream as a successful tick, so the stream reports healthy forever and simply never produces data. Writes one `monitor.polling_capability_gap` warning Event per boot when any exist. Never mutates settings and never fatal. |
| `backfillSecretEncryption` | Every startup while a key is set (NOT marker-guarded) | Seal previously-plaintext secrets in `Credential.config` / `Integration.config` / `NotificationChannel.config` / `Setting.value`. Reads through the UNEXTENDED `prismaBase` client so it can distinguish sealed from unsealed, writes through the extended client so the seal applies. Not markered because `POLARIS_SECRET_KEY` may be configured after the upgrade that ships this code; naturally idempotent (`sealValue` no-ops on sealed input) and it only writes rows that still hold plaintext. No-ops entirely when no key is configured. Writes one `server.secrets.encrypted_at_rest` Event when it converts anything. |
| `normalizeManufacturers` | Once at startup | Idempotent: seed default manufacturer aliases on a fresh install, load the in-memory cache used by the Prisma extension in `src/db.ts`, and rewrite any existing `Asset.manufacturer` / `MibFile.manufacturer` values that the alias map canonicalizes to something different. Mutations to the alias map at runtime (`POST/PUT /manufacturer-aliases`) re-run `applyAliasesToExistingRows()` in the background so admin edits propagate to historical data without a restart. |
| `seedAssetTypes` | Once at startup | Idempotent. Defense-in-depth seed of the built-in `AssetTypeDef` rows — the eight historical types + vCenter's `hypervisor` (the `virtual_machine` sibling was retired by migration 20260722000000 and deliberately absent from the seed list so it can't self-heal back). The registry-cutover migration is the authoritative seed; this catches fresh Docker volumes / restored backups where the migration didn't run. After the seed, `refreshCache()` populates the in-memory map used by `isKnownAssetType()` in `src/utils/assetTypes.ts` — which is the synchronous validator backing every `/assets` and `/monitor-settings` Zod schema. Failures log but never block boot — the validator falls back to accepting the eight built-in names while the cache is cold. |
| `seedManufacturerProfiles` | Once at startup | Idempotent (marker `Setting.seedManufacturerProfilesSeededAt`). Slice 6a — converts the hardcoded `VENDOR_TELEMETRY_PROFILES` constant into `ManufacturerProfile` + `ManufacturerProfileMetric` + `ManufacturerProfileMetricOverride` rows. One profile per distinct canonical manufacturer; the Fortinet sub-family entries (FortiSwitch / FortiAP) become `modelPattern`-keyed overrides under the umbrella Fortinet profile. The memory metric row + override carry the bytes-form `composition` blob via `memoryQueryToComposition()` so the editable profile lines up with the hardcoded baseline's multi-OID memory queries. Calls `refreshProfileCache()` at the end so the in-memory cache is warm. The hardcoded constant stays runtime-authoritative — this job only owns persistence. Best-effort: failures log and never block boot. |
| `seedBaselineAutomations` | Once at startup | Idempotent SEED-ONCE per set — NOT self-heal. Three independently-markered sets: ~11 widget-mirror rules (marker `Setting.seedBaselineAutomationsSeededAt` — asset/interface/IPsec-tunnel down, high CPU/memory/temperature/disk, slow response, packet loss via `probeLossPct`, storage-fills-soon, recent reboot) + 12 event-trigger rules over notable system Event families (marker `Setting.seedBaselineAutomationsV2SeededAt` so existing installs pick them up — discovery/push/agent failures, capacity escalations, conflicts, auto-decommissions, HA standby down, lockouts; enabled, in-app only, cooldown + a timed reset, or a counterpart-event reset for the three whose recovery Polaris writes). Built through `ruleInputSchema` + `createRule` (canonical v2). | **V4 (counterpart resets)** is a FOURTH marker (`seedBaselineAutomationsV4ResetEventSeededAt`), a one-shot for installs that stamped the V2 marker before an event automation could reset on anything but a clock: it repoints onto `reset.mode="event"` ONLY the rules whose trigger pattern has a known counterpart (`RESET_EVENT_SUGGESTIONS`), that are still on a timer, and that the operator has never edited (`updatedAt === createdAt`) — writing the legacy `clearBehavior:"auto"` mirror in the same update and logging one `automation.seed.v4_reset_event` Event naming what moved. Once a set's marker is stamped it never re-runs, so an operator's edit/DELETE of a baseline rule sticks. Delete a set's marker + restart to force a re-seed (resurrects that whole set). | **V3 (down detection)** is a THIRD marker (`seedBaselineAutomationsV3SeededAt`) and differs in kind: it is COMPUTED from live data, not a static array. Down stopped being a monitor-settings value (business rule 36), so V3 resolves each monitored asset's effective pre-cutover `failureThreshold` and mirrors it into automations — one all-assets rule at the dominant value plus one `assetTypes:[t]` rule per class that differed (rank 1, so it wins for that class) — then retires the pre-cutover "Asset down" row via `deleteRule` (the SERVICE, so its active notifications are soft-cleared) ONLY when `updatedAt === createdAt`. An edited row is kept + flagged (`automation.seed.v3_retained`): it still governs at `DEFAULT_MISSED_POLLS`, and the operator must be told the count is theirs now. Order is CREATE-then-retire (the reverse leaves a window with zero down automations = a momentarily blind fleet), and it refuses to retire if the replacement failed to save. Known gap, logged rather than hidden: `scopeRank` doesn't rank `integrationIds`, so one class with different thresholds across two integrations collapses to the more-sensitive value + an `automation.seed.threshold_conflict` warning Event.
| `backfillManufacturerProfileMemoryComposition` | Once at startup | Idempotent (marker `Setting.backfillManufacturerProfileMemoryCompositionAt`). Stamps the multi-OID memory `composition` blob onto existing `ManufacturerProfileMetric` + `ManufacturerProfileMetricOverride` rows that predate the column. Pairs with the inline emission in `seedManufacturerProfiles` so fresh installs get composition from the start; this job is for installs that ran the seed before the column existed. Two safety checks per row: composition stays null, AND the existing `defaultSymbol` / `symbol` matches the hardcoded entry's primary OID (operator-edited rows are skipped). Refreshes the profile cache on completion. |
| `backfillAssetSources` | Once at startup | Idempotent, **create-only** (never updates an existing row — the pre-2026-07 upsert clobbered discovery-owned observed blobs with Asset-derived skeletons on every restart). Walks every Asset row and creates missing `AssetSource` rows derived from the legacy `assetTag` / `sid:` / `ad-guid:` tag conventions (entra → "entra:" assetTag; ad → "ad:" assetTag; fortigate firewall → "fgt:" assetTag) **plus a Fortinet-infrastructure fallback** keyed on `manufacturer="Fortinet" + non-empty serialNumber + assetType` — `firewall`/`switch`/`access_point` map to `fortigate-firewall`/`fortiswitch`/`fortiap` respectively. Catches pre-tag firewalls and the un-tagged switch/AP fleet in one pass. ad-guid breadcrumbs become `inferred=true` AD recovery rows; everything else falls through to a single "manual" row keyed on Asset.id. Pairs with the shadow-write Prisma extension in `src/db.ts` which keeps the table fresh between restarts whenever an asset's `assetTag`, `tags`, or `discoveredByIntegrationId` change. |
| `resolveStaleReservationConflicts` | Once at startup | Idempotent cleanup. Auto-rejects pending reservation Conflict rows whose stored proposed values now match the live Reservation values on every field listed in `conflictFields` — i.e. conflicts that were raised by an old discovery run but where the values have since come back into sync. Pairs with the inline fix in `upsertConflict` that prevents new lingering conflicts going forward. |
| `scrubLegacySidGuidTags` | Once at startup | Idempotent. Phase 4b cleanup of the multi-source asset model: strips legacy `sid:<SID>` and `ad-guid:<GUID>` entries from `Asset.tags`. Both signals now live on AssetSource and the tag mirroring is redundant. Pairs with discovery-side cuts in `syncEntraDevices` / `syncActiveDirectoryDevices` that stop writing the markers going forward. Leaves `Asset.assetTag` (entra:/ad:/fgt:) and `prev-*` breadcrumb tags untouched — those need parallel migration of searchService + conflict resolution before retirement. |
| `cleanupStaleDnsResolvedReleased` | Once at startup | Idempotent. Hard-deletes every `Reservation` row with `sourceType="dns_resolved" AND status="released"`. Before the release→delete cutover, `releaseRows` / `releaseDnsResolvedAt` flipped dns_resolved rows to `status="released"` and left them in place, permanently occupying the (subnetId, ipAddress, "released") slot under the `@@unique([subnetId, ipAddress, status])` index. That blocked later status transitions at the same target — surfacing on prod as discovery-sync P2002 errors where the inline retry's `update→released` step itself couldn't complete because the slot was already taken. dns_resolved is a system-created fallback marker with no audit value, so the rows are deleted outright. No marker — the deleteMany IS the converge check. |
| `mergeFortiswitchEndpointGhosts` | Once at startup | Idempotent. Merges orphan `fortigate-endpoint` assets that represent a managed FortiSwitch's own management MAC (created by DHCP/ARP/MAC-table pathway before FortiSwitch discovery captured `baseMac` in any cycle) INTO the corresponding `assetType="switch"` asset that lacks a MAC. Cursor-pages through `Asset.macAddress IS NULL` switches; for each, joins to its `fortiswitch` source `observed.mgmtIp` and looks for a sibling endpoint whose `ipAddress` matches AND `lastSeenSwitch` starts with `<switch.hostname>/` AND carries a `fortigate-endpoint` source. Exactly-one match → transactional merge: re-points `AssetMacAddress` / `AssetAssociatedIp` / `AssetIpHistory` / `AssetFortigateSighting` rows (delete-on-conflict for unique violations), stamps the adopted MAC on the switch, drops the orphan's AssetSource rows, cascade-deletes the orphan. Multiple matches log a warn and skip. Pairs with the inline MAC-fallback lookup in the FortiSwitch update path in `syncDhcpSubnets` which prevents recurrence going forward. |
| `mergeDuplicateHostnameAssets` | Boot + every 30 min | Idempotent. Periodic safety net — discovery re-creates duplicate-hostname rows continuously, so it runs at boot and on a 30-min interval (a boot-only pass let duplicates accumulate between restarts on long-lived prod). Broader sibling of `mergeFortiswitchEndpointGhosts` — catches every shape of accumulated duplicate-hostname Asset row that the narrower NULL-MAC job misses (workstation ghosts where the FortiGate created one `fortigate-endpoint` per MAC sighting, Phase-1 backfill `manual`-only placeholders, post-baseMac FortiSwitch ghosts, FortiAP equivalents). Groups every Asset row by `lower(hostname)`, walks groups with ≥2 rows, picks a canonical by source-kind priority (entra/intune/ad/polaris-agent (1) > fortiswitch (2) > fortiap (3) > fortigate-firewall (4) > fortigate-endpoint (5) > manual (6) > no sources (7); tiebreak by most-recent `lastSeen` then `updatedAt`), then transactionally transfers `AssetMacAddress` / `AssetAssociatedIp` / `AssetIpHistory` / `AssetFortigateSighting` rows from each sibling onto the canonical with delete-on-conflict for unique violations. Cascade-delete on the sibling clears its `AssetSource` rows, every sample/rollup table, LLDP/wireless rows, pending `Conflict` rows pointing at it (so the queue empties naturally), and `AssetDependencyParent` rows on either side (the 60s `dependencyReconciler` tick recomputes from authoritative topology). Scalar-field absorption fills empty canonical fields from each sibling (macAddress / ipAddress / serialNumber / manufacturer / model / os / osVersion / assignedTo / notes / learnedLocation / acquiredAt) and keeps the more-recent `lastSeen`; tags union-merge. Tie-safety: groups where two rows share the top tier AND have non-null disagreeing primary MACs are skipped as "genuinely two devices" and logged at warn with the asset ids for operator review. **Dry-run mode**: set `POLARIS_GHOST_MERGE_DRY_RUN=1` to log every decision (host + canonical id + ghost ids + source kinds + tiers) without writing — use on first deploy to review choices, then unset the env var and let the next cycle actually merge. Writes one `asset.duplicate_merged` Event per merged group for the UI audit trail. No marker — the query itself is the converge check; re-runs without the env var find zero candidates once convergent. |
| `detectDuplicateIpAssets` | Boot + 45s, then every 10 min | Idempotent. Duplicate-address sweep (business rule 40): raises / refreshes / auto-closes the `duplicate-ip` Conflict flavour when two or more network-present Assets record the same `ipAddress`. Thin wrapper over `reconcileDuplicateIpConflicts()` in services/duplicateIpConflictService.ts. ONE grouped SQL read per pass whose CTE narrows to duplicated addresses before returning rows (so a 2000-asset fleet returns the collisions, not the fleet), LEFT JOINed to `AssetIpHistory` so the freshness test is per ADDRESS rather than per asset, and `HAVING ... bool_or("assetType" = ANY(...))` keeps endpoint-only duplicates — most of them on a DHCP fleet — out of the result set entirely; writes only on change, so a clean fleet issues zero writes. Raise stamps a `conflict.detected` Event — which is what the baseline "IP conflict detected" automation alerts on — and auto-close stamps `conflict.rejected` by `system:auto-resolved`. Scheduler role only, so a split-role install scans once rather than once per monitor replica. No marker — the scan itself is the converge check. |
| `migrateMonitorStatusRename` | Once at startup | Idempotent. Renames the recovery state on `Asset.monitorStatus` from the legacy value `"pending"` to `"recovering"`. The state machine in monitoringService writes `"recovering"` exclusively going forward; this catches rows stamped before the rename. Marker key `monitorStatusRenamePendingMigratedAt`. Recovery: delete the marker and restart. |
| `migrateAutomationRuleShape` | Once at startup | Idempotent. Persists the Automation rule-shape-v2 view (`reset` + `actions` Json columns) onto NotificationRule rows still carrying NULLs there, using the same `normalizeRuleToV2` conversion every reader normalizes through (clearBehavior/clearAfterSec → reset; targets + rule-level emailComposition → notify actions) — behavior is identical before/after, this just materializes the v2 shape. Legacy columns are NOT nulled (they remain the CRUD-maintained lossless mirror). Marker key `automationRuleShapeV2MigratedAt` + a `reset IS NULL` filter (re-run-safe after restores). Recovery: delete the marker and restart. |
| `migrateContactFilterShape` | Once at startup | Idempotent (`contactFilterConditionMigratedAt` marker). Folds every address-book `Contact`'s flat `assetCriteria` forward into an `assetCondition` condition tree via the pure `criteriaToCondition`, nulling the legacy column (exactly one filter shape is live per row). Rows whose criteria names a field the tree can't express (`integration`) are skipped, left matching through the legacy predicate, and logged at warn. Recovery: delete the marker Setting and restart. |
| `migrateTagFilterShape` | Once at startup | Idempotent (`tagFilterConditionMigratedAt` marker). The same fold for the tag registry: every auto-assigning `Tag`'s flat `criteria` becomes an `assetCondition` condition tree via the pure `criteriaToCondition`, legacy column nulled. Match-equivalent, so it triggers no reconcile. Rows naming a field the tree can't express (`integration`) are skipped and logged at warn; a tag deleted mid-fold is skipped per-row rather than aborting the loop. Recovery: delete the marker Setting and restart. |
| `clearNotificationCooldowns` | Once at startup | Idempotent (`notificationCooldownsClearedAt` marker). Clears `NotificationRule.cooldownSec` fleet-wide when the "Re-notify cooldown" control is retired from the wizard, so no automation keeps an invisible, uneditable suppression the engine still honours. Stamps one `automation.cooldown.retired` warning Event naming each affected rule and its previous value BEFORE the update, since the update destroys them. The column stays (dormant) for API callers. Recovery: delete the marker Setting and restart — though a re-run finds nothing left to clear, the first pass's Event being the record. |
| `migrateAutoMonitorInterfacesShape` | Once at startup | Idempotent (`autoMonitorInterfacesShapeMigratedAt` marker). Rewrites every FMG/FortiGate integration's `Integration.config.{fortigateMonitor|fortiswitchMonitor|fortiapMonitor}.autoMonitorInterfaces` from the legacy single-mode discriminated union (`{mode: "names"|"wildcard"|"type", ...}`) into the multi-block union (`{byNames?, byPatterns?, byTypes?, byLldp?}`). Pairs with the Zod-layer + apply-route + frontend-renderer `coerceLegacySelection` calls that handle the mixed state between deploy and this job running. Already-new-shape rows pass through unchanged on re-runs. Recovery: delete the marker and restart. |
| `migrateSystemInfoCadenceLinkage` | Once at startup | Links `systemInfoIntervalSeconds` at the integration tier to each integration's discovery `pollInterval`. Idempotent (`systemInfoCadenceLinkageMigratedAt` marker). For every integration whose stored `Integration.config.monitorSettings.systemInfoIntervalSeconds` equals the literal hardcoded default (600s), rewrites the field to null so the resolver's pollInterval-derived tier kicks in (`pollInterval × 3600`). Operators who explicitly typed any other value are NOT touched. Cuts interface-sample volume by 24× at the default 4h pollInterval. Writes one `monitor_settings.systemInfo_cadence_linked` Event per affected integration with `{previousValue: 600, pollIntervalHours, newDerivedCadenceSec}`. Invalidates the resolver cache at the end so the next monitor tick picks up the change without a process restart. Recovery: delete the marker and restart. See "Integration pollInterval linkage" under Monitor Settings Hierarchy. |
| `migrateMonitorSettingsPerClass` | Once at startup | Phase 2 of the monitoring-tab redesign. Idempotent (`monitorSettingsPerClassMigratedAt` marker). For every `fortimanager` / `fortigate` / `activedirectory` / `entraid` / `windowsserver` integration: (1) seeds the per-class `streams` blocks under `config.<klass>Monitor.streams.<stream>` from the flat `config.monitorSettings` baseline (FMG/FortiGate populates `fortigateMonitor` / `fortiswitchMonitor` / `fortiapMonitor`; AD/Entra/WinSrv populates `workstationMonitor` / `serverMonitor`; FortiAP omits storage). (2) Folds integration-scoped `MonitorClassOverride` rows (`integrationId = <this integration>`) onto the matching `(class, stream)` cell — per-row values win over the flat baseline — and deletes the absorbed rows in the same transaction. Manual-scope rows (`integrationId IS NULL`) are intentionally left untouched. (3) FMG/FortiGate per-class `snmpCredentialId` / `sshCredentialId` legacy fields pre-populate stream `credentialId` slots: SNMP credential for SNMP-polling streams, SSH credential for SSH-polling streams. (4) Writes one `monitor_settings.per_class_migrated` Event per integration listing absorbed override ids + class blocks seeded. Invalidates the resolver cache at the end so the next monitor tick picks up the per-class shape without a restart. Recovery: delete the marker and restart. |
| `renameMonitorClassKeys` | Once at startup | Phase 0 of the tiered sample-retention work. Idempotent (`monitorClassKeysRenamedAt` marker). Copies legacy `fortiswitch` / `fortiap` per-class keys to the generic `switch` / `accessPoint` names in `Setting("monitorSettings")` / `Setting("manualMonitorSettings")` / every `Integration.config.monitorSettings`. Defensive — leaves old keys in place so the backwards-compat reader in `getMonitorSettings()` keeps working through the transition. |
| `migrateSampleRetentionToEntities` | Once at startup | Idempotent (`sampleRetentionEntityMigratedAt` marker + shape sniff). Converts the legacy class-shaped `Setting("sampleRetention")` to the per-entity shape (`assets`/`cpuMem`/`temperature`/`interfaces`/`storage`/`ipsec` × detail/hourly/daily), mapping `sample→assets`, `telemetry→cpuMem+temperature`, `systemInfo→interfaces+storage+ipsec` and flipping legacy `0`=forever to `FOREVER`(-1). Replaced the class-shaped `migrateRetentionTiers` / `consolidateSampleRetention` seeders. Safe on fresh installs (seeds entity defaults). |
| `decommissionStaleAssets` | Every 24 hours | Move assets whose `lastSeen` (verified network presence) is older than the configured inactivity threshold (months) to `decommissioned` status. Recent directory/agent activity on the asset's `entra`/`intune`/`ad`/`polaris-agent` AssetSource rows vetoes the decommission (a cloud-only laptop syncing to Intune is alive, just never on the LAN); `lastSeen = null` rows are never eligible. Configured via Events → Settings → Assets tab; 0 disables. |
| `flagStaleReservations` | Every 6 hours (and 30 s after startup) | Scans active `dhcp_reservation` rows for ones whose target client hasn't been seen within the configured threshold (`reservation.staleAfterDays`, default 60, 0 disables). "Seen" counts the freshest of the DHCP lease (`lastSeenLeased`) AND a correlated `Asset.lastSeen` (matched by MAC first, then IP) — so a statically-addressed device that never pulls a lease but is still on the network is not flagged. For each fresh transition into "stale," writes one `reservation.stale` Event at warning level and stamps `staleNotifiedAt` so the alert doesn't refire. The discovery sync clears `staleNotifiedAt` (and `staleSnoozedUntil`) when the IP is seen active again, so a reservation that comes back online and goes silent later re-arms cleanly. Cold-start safety: a `reservationStaleDetectionStartedAt` Setting is stamped on first run and used as a per-row baseline fallback (`max(createdAt, detectionStartedAt)`, used only when there's neither a lease nor a correlated asset) so the first scan after migration doesn't flood every existing dhcp_reservation row before discovery has had time to populate either signal. Rows with `staleIgnored=true` are excluded permanently until an admin un-ignores, and rows on `deprecated` subnets (decommissioned-firewall networks) are excluded entirely — the whole network is gone, so per-IP stale alerts would be noise. |
| `reconcileInfraReservations` | Every 6 hours (first run 5 min after startup) | Safety net for managed FortiSwitch/FortiAP reservations whose device is gone. The lifecycle hooks (Phase 2a cascade, Phase 2b sweep, asset DELETE, operator status change, `decommissionStaleAssets`) release at the moment the device goes away; this converges what they can't reach — a decommission that happened while the gate was unreachable, rows predating the release path, or a future code path that forgets the hook. Calls `reconcileOrphanedInfraReservations`, whose verdict is the pure `classifyOrphanInfraRow`: every matching device `decommissioned` → release (pushed rows included); NO matching device → release only when Polaris never pushed the row, because "no asset" is also what a transient discovery state looks like and a false positive on a pushed row would delete a reserved-address entry on a live gate. Never touches non-infra source types — an operator's manual reservation for a not-yet-inventoried device is a normal state. Bounded per pass (`INFRA_RELEASE_CEILING`, 100) with the remainder deferred to the next tick; the delayed first run keeps the weak "no device" signal from firing against a half-synced cold-start database. |
| `discoverySlowCheck` | Every 30 s | Compares each in-flight discovery's elapsed time to its rolling-duration baseline (`discoveryDurationService`). Emits one `integration.discover.slow` event per run (and one per FortiGate inside an FMG run) when elapsed exceeds `max(avg + 2σ, avg × 1.5, avg + 60 s)`; baseline requires ≥3 prior successful runs. **Auto-abort:** a full (non-scoped) `running` run whose elapsed exceeds `autoAbortMs = max(2× avg, thresholdMs)` gets `cancelRequested` set (the operator-cancel plumbing: worker 3 s poll → abort → cancel watchdog force-exit if wedged) plus one `integration.discover.auto_aborted` warning Event naming the slow-flagged FortiGates and every still-active FortiGate with per-device elapsed; the run after an auto-abort is exempt (`discoveryAutoAbortService` alternates abort/exempt until a success re-baselines, since aborted runs never record duration samples — the exemption grant logs `integration.discover.auto_abort_skipped`). The `/integrations/discoveries` endpoint also calls the same checker inline so the sidebar and Integrations page flip amber within one 4 s poll cycle. Also calls `expireVerboseLogging()` on every tick to write `verboseLogging: false` back to the DB for any integration whose 30-minute verbose-logging window has closed. |
| `discoveryRunReaper` | Every 60 s (web/all role only) | Marks orphaned `DiscoveryRun` rows (`queued`/`running` whose `workerHeartbeatAt` — or `createdAt` when null — is older than 3 min) as `error` via `reapStaleRuns()`, so a crashed/restarted discovery worker doesn't leave an integration stuck in `running` and block the `polaris-discovery-run` singletonKey from re-triggering. Pairs with the 60 s heartbeat refresh inside `runDiscovery`. Independent `running` guard; best-effort (failures log at debug, never thrown). |
| `capacityWatch` | Every 10 minutes (and 60 s after startup) | Builds a capacity snapshot via `getCapacitySnapshot` and calls `recordCapacityTransition` so a flip into watch/amber/red writes one `capacity.severity_changed` Event independent of whether anyone has the Maintenance tab open. The route handler in `serverSettings.ts` also calls `recordCapacityTransition` on every `/pg-tuning` fetch so the audit trail lands in real time when an admin is actively viewing — the periodic job is the out-of-band safety net for "the DB is moments from dying and the UI is about to be unreachable." Best-effort: failures are logged at debug and never thrown. The first run on each fresh install also stamps the baseline `capacity.lastSeverity` Setting. |
| `evaluateNotificationRules` | Every 60s (web/all role; 30s after boot) | Drives `notificationEngine.evaluateAllNotificationRules()` — threshold/state evaluation (per-metric sample resolvers + the NotificationRuleState machine) + the event-tail (cursor over Event rows matching event/change rules). Inserts `Notification` rows on the clear→firing transition (with the templateCtx snapshot when the rule has emailComposition/escalation); clears per each rule's clearBehavior. Sweeps `notificationService.clearSuppressedAlerts()` first, so an asset that entered a maintenance window (or fell behind a dark parent) since the last tick has its live alerts retired before the rules run, and `clearExpiredTestAlerts()` after, which soft-clears wizard test alerts over an hour old (`TEST_ALERT_TTL_MS`, `clearedBy: "system:test-expired"`) — a test fire carries `ruleId: null` and no state row, so it is outside every other recovery path and would otherwise sit on the device’s Alerts tab forever. Best-effort: failures log at debug. |
| `escalateNotifications` | Every 60s (web/all role; 45s after boot) | Drives `notificationEscalationService.runEscalationSweep()` — for unhandled notifications of rules with ANY escalation chain (rule-level, per-action, band-level, band-per-action), iterates the chains active at the alert's severity (`escalationChainsForSeverity`; per-chain stopOn — ack stops "acknowledge" chains, "clear" chains keep going) and runs each due tier's ACTIONS (v2: notify / api_call / script) through `automationActionService.executeActions` with escalation provenance, updating Notification.escalationState (per-tier firstSentAt/lastSentAt/count keyed bare-numeric for the level chain / `a<i>:t<j>` for per-action chains, bumped only when ≥1 action executed; optional repeats up to maxRepeats). Legacy email tiers convert via normalizeEscalationToV2 with byte-identical output. ALSO re-sends the notify actions of any alert whose automation carries `repeat`, while it stays unhandled — unbounded unless `stopAfterHours` is set, `[REMINDER n]`-labelled, audited separately as `notification.repeated`. Best-effort: failures log at debug. |

Best-effort. |

Script actions never execute inline in the engine or the delivery drain. |

When a row-level DELETE/UPDATE matched rows inside a compressed chunk, TimescaleDB decompressed it into the rowstore heap and autovacuum then reclaimed dead tuples to the FSM but never returned the pages to the OS — leaving multi-GB low-density heap whose real columnstore data is a few hundred MB (prod incident 2026-06-08: detail chunks at 0 live tuples / ~10 GB on disk / ~350 MB real data; 2026-06-17: a `asset_interface_samples_hourly` rollup chunk at 10 GB / 323 MB, which the detail-only scan had left stranded). Read-only scan via `chunk_compression_stats()` + `pg_total_relation_size()`; only chunks whose on-disk size both exceeds 256 MB AND dwarfs their compressed bytes (>3×) are touched. `VACUUM (FULL)` each on a dedicated direct connection with a short 5 s `lock_timeout` (never blocks live reads longer than that) but **retried up to 6× with 30 s backoff** — the resolver's minutes-long interface-sample reads hold `AccessShareLock` and steal the lock, so a single attempt skipped every chunk in prod; retrying catches a read gap, and once acquired the 0-live rewrite is seconds. Capped at 12 chunks/run. **Residual-bloat net** now that the root causes are fixed (bounded slow-prune `unselectedSlowPruneWindow` + the dropped asset→sample FK cascade, migration `20260615000000`); also reclaims pre-fix bloat on first runs. No-op when TimescaleDB is absent. Observed via `polaris_job_duration_seconds{job="reclaimBloatedChunks"}`. |

| `monitorAssets` | Light loop every 5 s, heavy loop every 30 s (independent `running` guards) | Handles four independent cadences per monitored asset: **(1) response-time probe** when `lastMonitorAt + (Asset.monitorIntervalSec ?? monitor.intervalSeconds)` has elapsed (FortiOS REST, SNMP `sysUpTime`, WinRM SOAP Identify, SSH connect+auth, ICMP ping). The `activedirectory` monitor type dispatches to WinRM for Windows or SSH for realm-joined Linux, both reusing the AD integration's bind credentials. Writes one `AssetMonitorSample` per probe (`responseTimeMs` null = packet loss), updates `Asset.monitorStatus` / `lastResponseTimeMs` / `consecutiveFailures`, and emits one `monitor.status_changed` Event on `up ↔ down` transitions (threshold is `monitor.failureThreshold`). **(2) Telemetry pull** when `lastTelemetryAt + (telemetryIntervalSec ?? monitor.telemetryIntervalSeconds)` has elapsed — CPU% + memory snapshot via FortiOS `/api/v2/monitor/system/resource/usage` or SNMP. The SNMP path consults `vendorTelemetryProfiles` for the asset's `manufacturer + os + model` and queries vendor-specific OIDs first when the profile resolves through `oidRegistry` (i.e. the relevant MIB has been uploaded to Server Settings → Credentials → MIB Database). Built-in profiles cover Cisco IOS/IOS-XE/NX-OS (`cpmCPUTotal5secRev`, `ciscoMemoryPoolUsed`+`ciscoMemoryPoolFree` — all three seeded into `oidRegistry`'s built-in table so the probe works without uploading CISCO-PROCESS-MIB or CISCO-MEMORY-POOL-MIB), Juniper Junos (`jnxOperatingCPU`, `jnxOperatingBuffer` % — both seeded into the built-in table so the probe works without uploading JUNIPER-MIB), Mikrotik (`mtxrSystemUserCPULoad` — not seeded; RouterOS CPU resolves via the HOST-RESOURCES-MIB `hrProcessorLoad` fallback path), Fortinet FortiSwitch (matched before the generic Fortinet entry via `model="FortiSwitch"` or, when the model is empty, the `fortinetClassHint` assetType hint; CPU uses `fsSysCpuUsage` @ 12356.106.4.1.2 scalar percent; memory uses the bytes form — `fsSysMemUsage` @ 12356.106.4.1.3 + `fsSysMemCapacity` @ 12356.106.4.1.4 — NOT a percent like the FortiGate variant. Disk uses the same shape: `fsSysDiskUsage` @ 12356.106.4.1.5 + `fsSysDiskCapacity` @ 12356.106.4.1.6, consumed by `collectSystemInfoSnmp`'s vendor disk fallback when HRM returns no disks. All five symbols seeded into `oidRegistry` so the probe works without uploading FORTINET-FORTISWITCH-MIB), Fortinet SNMP path (`fgSysCpuUsage`, `fgSysMemUsage` — both seeded into `oidRegistry`'s built-in table so FortiGate CPU/memory work without uploading FORTINET-FORTIGATE-MIB, matching the always-on hardware-sensor temperature fallback), HP/Aruba ProCurve (`hpSwitchCpuStat` — seeded into the built-in table so the probe works without uploading STATISTICS-MIB), and Dell PowerConnect / Force10 (`rlCpuUtilDuringLastMinute` under the RADLAN enterprise 89, seeded into the built-in table so the probe works without uploading the RADLAN MIB). When a vendor query yields nothing — no profile match, MIB not uploaded, or the device doesn't expose the OID — each metric independently falls back to standard HOST-RESOURCES-MIB (`hrProcessorLoad`, `hrStorageRam`). Writes one `AssetTelemetrySample` per tick. **Hardware-sensor scrapes dispatch separately** via `collectHardwareSensors`, driven by `temperaturePolling` (the internal stream key is still `temperature`; not `cpuMemoryPolling`) — `runTelemetryFor` calls both in parallel on each telemetry tick so an operator can run CPU/memory over REST while hardware sensors scrape over SNMP (the branch-class FortiGate workaround when `/api/v2/monitor/system/sensor-info` is unreliable). It captures the **whole** hardware-sensor table (temperature / fan / voltage / power / disk), each row classified via `classifyHardwareSensor` and carrying value/unit/alarmStatus: from FortiOS `/api/v2/monitor/system/sensor-info` (all classes) or, for Fortinet over SNMP, the `fgHwSensorTable` walk (name/value/alarm — the comprehensive source, preferred for Fortinet and when the manufacturer-profile `temperature` metric is set to `table`), else ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB (entPhySensorType=8 → temperature class) and the FortiAP `fapTemperature` scalar. Writes N `AssetHardwareSensorSample` rows per successful scrape; failures leave the prior rows in place so the System tab keeps showing the last known reading. **(3) System info pull** when `lastSystemInfoAt + (systemInfoIntervalSec ?? monitor.systemInfoIntervalSeconds)` has elapsed (default systemInfo cadence is now linked to the originating integration's `pollInterval` × 3600 unless an operator pinned an explicit tier-3 value — see the "Integration pollInterval linkage" tier under Monitor Settings Hierarchy) — interfaces (FortiOS `/monitor/system/interface` + CMDB merge for `alias`/`description`, or SNMP IF-MIB including `ifAlias` for the operator-set label; both paths capture ifInErrors/ifOutErrors and FortiOS errors_in/out) + storage (SNMP HOST-RESOURCES-MIB `hrStorageTable`; when that returns no disk rows, the SNMP path falls back to a vendor disk scalar query — currently FortiSwitch `fsSysDiskUsage` / `fsSysDiskCapacity` — and emits one StorageSample per matched profile; gated on the resolved `storagePolling === "snmp"` so the rows are dropped when the operator hasn't opted in) + IPsec tunnels (FortiOS `/monitor/vpn/ipsec` plus a parallel `/cmdb/vpn.ipsec/phase1-interface` lookup that resolves each tunnel's `parentInterface` — the FortiOS CLI `set interface` value used by the System tab to nest tunnel rows under their parent in the Interfaces table; phase-2 selectors are rolled up to a single up/down/partial state per phase-1 with summed byte counters; ADVPN dynamic shortcuts are filtered out by their `parent` field) + LLDP neighbors (FortiOS `/monitor/system/interface/lldp-neighbors` for fortinet probes, SNMP LLDP-MIB walk for SNMP probes — `lldpRemTable` joined to `lldpLocPortTable` for the localPortNum→ifName mapping plus `lldpRemManAddrTable` for management IPs). Writes N `AssetInterfaceSample` rows + M `AssetStorageSample` rows + K `AssetIpsecTunnelSample` rows + L `AssetLldpNeighbor` rows (replaced in full per asset on each successful pass — neighbors that aren't in the latest scrape are deleted in the same transaction; matchedAssetId is resolved at persist time by joining management IP / chassis MAC / system name against the asset inventory); also mirrors per-interface IP+MAC into `Asset.associatedIps` (preserving manual entries). **(4) Fast filtered scrape** rides the response-time cadence when the asset has any `monitoredInterfaces`, `monitoredStorage`, or `monitoredIpsecTunnels` pinned (and the full systemInfo pass didn't already run this tick). Calls `collectFastFiltered` which performs one collector round-trip — interfaces + storage on SNMP, interfaces + (conditionally) IPsec on FortiOS — and only writes sample rows for the pinned subset. **The SNMP path uses wire-level filtering** (`collectFastFilteredSnmp`): a small discovery walk maps pinned ifNames → ifIndex (and pinned mountPaths → hrStorageIndex when storage is pinned), then one batched `snmpMultiGet` pulls only the column-at-index OIDs the fast pass needs (~13 per pinned interface, ~3 per pinned storage). On a 48-port switch with one pinned interface that's ~110 OID-fetches in one PDU vs ~770 across 16 column walks under the legacy full-walk path — drops fast-cadence p90 from multi-second to sub-second on busy fleets and cuts the Capacity Advisor's recommended `POLARIS_MONITOR_FAST_WORKERS` proportionally. LLDP and wireless are always omitted on the fast cadence (LLDP rides the heavy pass; wireless isn't a fast-pin target). The FortiOS REST path still pulls the full `/api/v2/monitor/system/interface` payload and filters in code — the endpoint has no per-name query param. Storage and IPsec rows ride the same monitorInterval setting (default 60s) so the operator gets sub-minute disk-usage and tunnel-state history for chosen mountpoints / tunnels without re-walking the full tables. ICMP/SSH cannot deliver telemetry/system-info; WinRM/AD return supported=false until WMI Enumerate-over-WS-Management lands. **Worker scheduling**: cadences are split across two independent ticking loops. The **light loop** (probe + fastFiltered) ticks every 5 s with concurrency `cpus().length * 2` (clamped 8..64, env-overridable via `POLARIS_PROBE_CONCURRENCY`); the **heavy loop** (telemetry + systemInfo) ticks every 30 s with concurrency `cpus().length` (clamped 4..32, env-overridable via `POLARIS_HEAVY_CONCURRENCY`). Each loop has its own `running` guard, so a 75-second wedged systemInfo on a dead host blocks ONLY the next heavy tick — the light loop keeps firing on its own clock and probes stay close to their configured cadence regardless. Within a pass, workers don't reserve assets; they just pull the next item from the cadence queue. `runMonitorPass({cadences})` selects which cadences a given call owns; the default (no `cadences` arg) covers all four for legacy callers like `POST /assets/:id/probe-now`. **Five-state monitor machine**. `Asset.monitorStatus` is one of `up | warning | recovering | down | unknown`, driven by two counters: `consecutiveFailures` (existing) + `consecutiveSuccesses` (added with the hierarchy work). The resolved `failureThreshold` doubles as the recovery threshold — same number of confirmations gates both directions. (UI label note: `recovering` shows as **Recovering**, `unknown`/null shows as **Pending**; same blue color, different labels.) **(5) ICMP loss sweep** (2026-09-01, replacing the per-asset sampler of 2026-08-19 that was disabled a day after shipping) when `lastLossSampleAt + the sweep interval` has elapsed — a UNIFORM burst of 5 echoes at every eligible asset, whatever monitor state it is in, writing one `AssetMonitorSample` per asset with `probeKind="icmp"`, a NULL `responseTimeMs` and the `packetsSent` / `packetsReceived` pair that makes loss a ratio of PACKETS instead of poll outcomes. The sampler it replaces ran only while an asset was `warning` or `recovering`, and that window was itself the oversampling bias that got it switched off (business rule 29d); uniform spacing is what makes the ratio mean what an operator thinks it means. Affordable only because it is BATCHED: one queued job is one CHUNK of up to 500 assets measured in a single `fping` process (`utils/burstPing.ts`), bounded by burst period rather than host count, so a 2000-asset fleet costs four process spawns per cycle against the ~2000 a per-asset design would need. fping is OPTIONAL — RHEL ships it only via EPEL and Windows Server has no build — and a bounded per-host fan-out keeps loss correct where it is missing, with `resolveSweepIntervalSec` flooring the cadence at what the installed pinger can actually finish. It NEVER calls `recordProbeResult`, so it cannot touch the counters or `monitorStatus` (ICMP does not authenticate the device it reaches). Eligibility (`utils/lossSweep.ts`) excludes only unmonitored, `maintenance`, and `responseTimePolling === "disabled"`; `down`, dependency-suppressed and agent-monitored assets are all deliberately IN. Keeps the `lossSample` cadence name / pg-boss queue (`polaris-monitor-losssample`, 15s expiry, 2s polling) / worker pool (`POLARIS_MONITOR_LOSS_SAMPLE_WORKERS`, default 24 — now sizing concurrent CHUNKS) so the cutover orphans no persisted queue and no operator-set env var, and still deliberately NOT in the floating pool's priority list: if its budget is saturated the right answer is to drop resolution, not to borrow capacity from the pool that absorbs real monitoring work. Replaced the fast-confirm re-probe, which was removed the same day: the response-time poll no longer accelerates mid-run, so time-to-down is `failureThreshold x intervalSeconds` (business rule 30).

`Asset.consecutiveFailures` is a **leaky bucket**, not a run length (business rule 30): a missed poll adds one, an answered poll takes one back, floored at zero. The verdict is then a pure function of the bucket level plus the outcome of the current probe — the previous status is not an input at all.

| Bucket after this probe | This probe answered | This probe missed |
|---|---|---|
| `cf ≥ threshold` | `down` | `down` |
| `0 < cf < threshold` | → `recovering` (answering, misses outstanding) | → `warning` (rendered **Missed**) |
| `cf = 0` | `up` | — (unreachable: a miss always raises the bucket) |

**The LEVEL decides and the current probe only breaks the tie below the threshold.** Letting a success win outright would mean a device dark for an hour (cf=60) reads `recovering` — and clears its down alert, which tests `monitorStatus == down` — on ONE answered packet out of sixty; it has to pay the debt back under the threshold first. Draining 3 → 2 → 1 → 0 therefore takes exactly `threshold` answers, the same number of confirmations `consecutiveSuccesses` used to count, which is why the machine no longer consults it (the column is still written — it is a true fact and it is charted — it simply decides nothing). `recovering` correspondingly no longer means "was down": it means answering with misses still outstanding, reachable straight out of `warning`. The Status pill on the assets list and asset details modal renders the five colors: green (up), amber **Missed** (`monitorStatus="warning"` — the stored value is unchanged; the label is "Missed" because the alert severities are also named warning/serious/critical, so the pill read as "an alert fired" when it only ever meant "a poll was missed"), blue **Recovering** (was-down, now succeeding — `#0288d1`, the SAME value the Last-30-min strip and the response-time chart below it paint a recovering probe, and the same `POLARIS_HEALTH_COLORS.recovering` the Device Map uses; it was keyed to `var(--color-accent)` until 2026-08-29, the only monitor badge pointed at a theme token rather than its own colour family, which rendered it in the morning theme's GOLD — the family of the amber **Missed** pill beside it), red (down), grey (`monitored=false`, "unmonitored"). The `unknown` / null state (asset never probed) reuses the same blue CSS treatment but with the label **Pending** so operators can distinguish "we don't know yet" from "we know it's recovering". The `monitor.status_changed` audit Event still fires only on `up ↔ down` transitions; the per-tick failures show up visually in the asset System tab's intermittency bar (one cell per probe sample over the 1h window). The bar's cells come wholly from the machine: amber for a miss while the bucket is below the covering automation's `missedPolls`, red at or above it, and BLUE for an answered poll while misses are still outstanding — held past the drain until the automation's reset run of answers has landed (business rule 36). That split is the point: a single missed poll still reads as one amber cell (green-amber-green) rather than a multi-cell warning run, and a failed probe is never painted blue, but the multi-cell stretch the pill spends in **Recovering** is now visible on the one surface built to show it (it used to be green, i.e. indistinguishable from confirmed-up). A blip during recovery keeps the machine in `recovering`, so the successes after it stay blue. Both counters are warmed up across the full hour before slicing the trailing 30 cells, so a dip — or a recovery — that began before the visible window keeps its correct color; the pre-window state is assumed `up`, since seeding `unknown` would paint the first cells of every bar blue (unknown and down share the same success arrow). The replay is the pure `PolarisMonitorStates.replay` in `public/js/monitor-states.js` (reached from `assets.js` under its historical name `_intermittencyStates`), shared with the response-time charts on both desktop and phone and mirrored server-side by `probeOutageService.replayProbeStates` for the alert-email charts; unit-tested — and pinned against that server mirror — in `tests/unit/assetIntermittencyBar.test.ts`.

**Heavy-cadence suppression**: telemetry / systemInfo / fastFiltered run **only** when `monitorStatus === "up"`. Every other state — including `warning` (mid-degradation), `recovering` (mid-recovery), `down`, and `unknown` — suppresses heavy cadences so the System tab stops accumulating samples that aren't going to be reliable. The cheap response-time probe keeps firing in every state.

**No probe backoff** — down hosts keep probing at the resolved `intervalSeconds`. Recovery is detected within one base-cadence tick (worst case 60 s on default settings, vs. up to 30 min under the old bucketed backoff that was dropped along with the new monitor-settings hierarchy). Trades a small amount of worker budget on chronically-down hosts for fast recovery detection. `lastSystemInfoAt` doesn't advance during the outage (only bumps when a scrape returned data), so systemInfo is due immediately on recovery and the System tab refreshes naturally. The same "only on data" rule also stops a transport failure from silently emptying the System tab Interfaces table — the GET endpoint anchors interface display to `lastSystemInfoAt`, and bumping it without inserting any rows would point the query at a moment with zero samples. Once a day the job prunes the sample tables (`monitor.sampleRetentionDays` for monitor, `telemetryRetentionDays` for telemetry **and temperatures**, `systemInfoRetentionDays` for interface + storage + IPsec tunnels **and LLDP neighbors** — LLDP rides system-info retention because it's collected on the same cadence; the per-scrape full-replace already drops gone-away neighbors so the prune mostly catches rows for assets that have stopped scraping entirely). |
