## Frontend

Vanilla JavaScript SPA served from `/public/`. No build step — plain ES modules.

- Multi-page layout with client-side navigation (`app.js`)
- Light/dark theme toggle — in the **account menu**, not the sidebar
- **Account menu** (`renderUserBadge` / `openUserMenu` in `app.js`) — the page-header user badge is a real `<button>` (`.user-menu-trigger`, `aria-haspopup="menu"`) opening the shared `showRowMenu` right-aligned under itself: the Web Push row when push is on offer, the **two-factor row** when the account is `local`, then Logout. Items are rebuilt per open, so the push / 2FA state needs nothing kept repainted. The **theme picker is deliberately not here** — it moved back to the sidebar bottom (below Server Settings, above the version line) in 2026-08 on operator preference: a display preference flipped often reads better as an always-visible control than as a row behind a menu, so `_setTheme` repaints that long-lived button's icon + label again (the label names the CURRENT theme, since the button opens the list rather than flipping to a single other one). The separator above Logout is emitted only when something precedes it — with neither conditional row the menu is Logout alone, and a leading rule would divide nothing. The 2FA row (`wireTotpState` → `_totpState`, `_totpMenuItem`, `_openTotpSelf`, and `refreshTotpState` — exposed because /users.html hosts the same flow off its own row menu and the cached row would otherwise still read "Set up" on the page where it was just enabled) is push enrollment’s permission-mismatch fix applied again: `/auth/totp/*` is self-service for any logged-in local account, but the only UI was on the admin-gated /users.html. State is fetched ONCE per page load and deliberately NOT gated on `currentUserAuthProvider` — `renderNav` also runs off the localStorage cache, which doesn’t carry the provider (it defaults to `"local"`) — so the row gates on the status payload’s own `authProvider`, the same value the routes enforce. Labels track state (`Set up` / `Finish` / `Disable two-factor auth`; the enabled row’s tooltip names the remaining backup codes), and the modals come from the shared `public/js/totp-self.js`.
- **Per-user panel lock** (`app.js`) — a lock button sits left of the X on every modal and slide-over. Two app-wide switches (one for all modals, one for all slide-overs), saved per user in `localStorage` under `polaris.panellock.<username>`. **Locked** → a backdrop/off-panel click does NOT dismiss the panel (the X gets the same escalating glow + radial bloom as the modal X via the shared `flashModalCloseBtn`); **unlocked** (default) → an off-click closes it. The X and Escape always close regardless. Modals route through `openModal` (handled inline); slide-overs each wire their own backdrop-close, so a capture-phase document listener blocks that close when locked instead of editing every panel, and a `MutationObserver` injects the lock button into any newly-created panel (so new slide-overs get one for free). A hover tooltip explains the current state.
- Real-time discovery progress polling (`integrations.js`)
- Bulk operations (delete, release)
- PDF and CSV asset export
- Conflict resolution slide-over panel (Events page)
- First-run setup wizard (`setup.html`) backed by `src/setup/`
- Device Map page has an **Edit regions** toolbar button (admin/networkadmin only — gated by `canManageNetworks()` on the client; backend guard is the source of truth). The default map view never renders region polygons — they appear only after entering edit mode. Edit mode mounts `L.Control.Draw` (vendored leaflet-draw 1.0.4) for drawing new polygons, overlays existing regions on a dedicated `L.featureGroup`, and binds permanent name labels at each polygon's centroid. **Draw new** prompts for a name via `openModal()` and posts to `POST /map/regions`. **Click an existing polygon** opens a popup with **Rename** / **Change color** / **Send to Bottom Layer** / **Delete** actions. **Send to Bottom Layer** calls `poly.bringToBack()` so a region nested inside another (overlapping polygons where the outer one was drawn later and visually obscures the inner one) can be clicked through to — per-session only, the saved-on-server order doesn't change. **Drag a vertex** (or midpoint) reshapes the polygon in-memory — vertex editing is always on per polygon in edit mode (no separate Edit toolbar round-trip); every drag fires `editvertex` and marks the polygon dirty without issuing a PUT. **Right-click drag** pans the map (always on; context menu is suppressed inside the map container). Useful while drawing a polygon, since left-click is captured for vertex placement. **Save Regions** commits every dirty polygon via SEQUENTIAL PUTs (they serialize on the server's region-blob advisory lock anyway — parallel requests just parked N connections on it), then exits edit mode; per-polygon failures alert the operator and leave edit mode open so the operator can retry or discard. Every successful save — including a click with zero dirty polygons — then fires `POST /map/regions/reconcile` (`reviewRegionTags` in map.js): the fleet-wide region-tag review that re-adds members, strips provenance-tracked drift, and removes region tags from pinned FortiGates no longer inside the named polygon (the gate that MOVED case, which no polygon PUT would otherwise cover). The review is non-fatal — a failure downgrades to a toast, since the polygon saves already landed — and its summary is appended to the toolbar status line. **Discard Changes** reverts every dirty polygon to its loaded shape via `setLatLngs` (with an editing-handle refresh) and exits edit mode — rename/delete/draw-new actions taken during the session are NOT in the dirty bucket because they hit the server immediately on click, so Discard can't undo them. The save/discard buttons sit alongside the Edit-regions button in the toolbar; visibility flips via `setEditModeButtons` so only the relevant set is shown for the current mode. The draw plugin's CSS sprite assets live alongside the existing Leaflet marker images at [public/css/vendor/leaflet/images/](public/css/vendor/leaflet/images/) (`spritesheet.png`, `spritesheet-2x.png`, `spritesheet.svg`). Each region maps to a `region:<name>` tag stamped by the backend reconciler on every enclosed firewall asset, cascaded to its managed FortiSwitches / FortiAPs (`fortinetTopology.controllerFortigate`), and stamped on the `Subnet` rows those gates serve plus the assets addressed out of them — see "Map Regions" under the API surface.
- Asset list shows a five-state Status pill (**Up** green / **Missed** amber / **Pending** blue / **Down** red / **Unmonitored** grey). For admin/assetsadmin the pill is **clickable** — single click toggles `monitored`; the server then recomputes `monitorOverride` (true when the new monitored value diverges from the discovering integration's per-class `addAsMonitored`, false when they match — including when the operator's click brings them back into agreement). On the asset details slide-in **System tab**, an **Asset Override** badge (`_assetOverrideBadge` in `public/js/assets.js`) renders next to the Status pill when `monitorOverride === true` so the operator can see at a glance which assets have been pinned away from the integration's auto-monitor default. The Type column pill is also clickable for admin/assetsadmin and opens a dropdown of the live `AssetTypeDef` registry for inline reclassification (built from `ASSET_TYPE_OPTIONS`, so operator-added custom types are offered and a type retired from the registry is not — the asset's OWN type is always kept as an option, so opening the menu can never hide what the row currently is). The bulk-action toolbar (always visible, idle-styled and disabled until rows are selected) is built from three dropdowns and three labelled buttons: **Type ▾** / **State ▾** loop a per-asset `PUT /assets/:id` for the chosen `assetType` / `status`; **Monitoring ▾** (Enable / Disable) hits `POST /assets/bulk-monitor`; **Edit** opens the single-asset edit modal (`openEditModal`) for the selected row — it stays visible but greys out unless exactly one asset is selected, and it replaced the former tags-only bulk **Edit Tags** modal (tags are now edited per-asset in that modal, or fleet-wide via `Tag.criteria` auto-assignment); **Quarantine selected** / **Release Quarantine** route through the dedicated `/assets/bulk-quarantine` and `/assets/bulk-quarantine/release` endpoints; **Delete selected** posts to `DELETE /assets`; **Compare** overlays the telemetry of the selected assets and, needing two to overlay, stays VISIBLE and greys out below two rather than appearing only once the right number is ticked (**Merge** is the exception that still hides — it is pairwise AND admin-only). The State menu is populated from the `ASSET_STATUS_LABELS` map in `public/js/assets.js`; the Type menu reads `ASSET_TYPE_OPTIONS` — the registry list — via `_renderBulkTypeMenu()`, which is called BOTH at wire time and again from `_loadAssetTypeOptions()` once `GET /asset-types` answers, because the bulk bar is wired before that fetch resolves (without the second call the menu carried the built-in seed forever and a custom type was unreachable from the bulk bar); `quarantined` is intentionally not a State option (the regular asset PUT rejects that status — quarantine has its own flow). The Acquired date is intentionally omitted from the list — it lives only on the asset details slide-in (General tab) to keep the row narrow.
- The bulk-action toolbar also carries a **Compare** button (shown when 2+ rows are selected; no `data-manage-assets` gate — comparing telemetry is read-only). It opens a **metric picker modal** (`openCompareModal` in `public/js/assets-compare.js`) — Response time / CPU % / Memory % / Storage % / a single combined **Interface throughput & errors** toggle (which fans out internally to the `ifThroughput` + `ifErrors` sub-metrics, one chart each), a layout choice (one chart per metric with assets overlaid, vs overlaid one-chart-per-unit), and — when the interface toggle is on — an interface-name picker built from the union of `system-info` interfaces across the selected assets. The picker has **Select all / Deselect all** (deselecting all is allowed — interface charts just don't render; only blocked when interfaces is the sole metric), lists each interface's assets with their **alias / aggregate annotation in parentheses** (`alias: …` / `member of <agg>` / `VLAN on <parent>`, from the already-fetched system-info), and shows a per-asset **usage preview** (recent 1h average throughput, or "down" / "no data") so the operator can tell which interfaces carry traffic — auto-loaded when ≤60 (asset × interface) readings, button-gated above that to stay cheap at fleet scale ("N of M assets" counts mark how shared each name is). **Compare** then opens a slide-over (`openComparePanel`) that overlays the selected assets' telemetry on SVG charts built with the canonical chart helpers (`_renderCompareChart` reuses `_chartTimeBounds` / `_chartClip*` / `_dateChangeMarkers` / `_observeChartResize` / `_wireChartTooltip`), with a 1h/12h/24h/7d/30d/Custom range bar, a per-chart legend, and footer **Screenshot** (html-to-image → clipboard at the canonical 1100px width) + **Export PDF** (`trackedPdfExport` → one chart image per block via html-to-image). Selection is soft-capped at 10 assets for readability. Fetches per (asset × metric [× interface]) reuse the existing `monitorHistory` / `telemetryHistory` / `interfaceHistory` / `storageHistory` endpoints — no backend changes. Storage % uses the asset's largest mountpoint. Mock data for exercising it: `npm run mock:compare` (`prisma/mock-compare.ts`).
- Assets page header has a **Settings** button (`data-admin-only`) opening a modal of `<hr>`-separated **stacked sections** (`_monsetRender`), in order: **Asset Lifecycle** (auto-decommission threshold + IP-history retention) · **Sources** (drag-to-reorder learned-location priority, business rule 22; the builder returns `""` when the fetch failed, which drops the section AND its rule) · **Manual Monitoring** (tier-3 settings for orphan assets — eight fields including `probeTimeoutMs`; carries the nested `monset-manual-streams` stream-subtab strip, the modal's ONLY tab strip) · **Class Overrides** (cross-source list with add/edit/delete; the asset-source picker offers every integration plus a "Manual" entry) · **Mass Pinning** (`window.PolarisMassPin.sectionHTML()` + `.init()`, same absent-module-drops-the-section guard as Sources; `init` is idempotent per render via a `dataset.mpInited` stamp on `#mp-section` that dies with the section DOM, so the re-render an override delete triggers rebuilds cleanly). Manual Monitoring + Class Overrides share the data store the integration Monitoring tab edits. **An outer tab strip was tried and reverted (2026-08-20 — operator preference):** the four sections briefly became `_renderTabbedBody("monset-main", …)` panels when Mass Pinning was added; don't re-tab it without asking. Note the nested Manual-Monitoring strip is why a future outer strip needs a non-colliding prefix — `_wireModalTabs` deactivates panels by an `[id^="<prefix>-tab-"]` selector.
- Asset details slide-in **System** tab status block: just under the Status pill is a **last-hour intermittency bar** — one cell per probe sample over the past hour, colored by the resolved monitor state at that point (green=up / amber=**Missed** / **blue**=recovering / red=down — blue `rgba(2,136,209,·)`, the SAME value the response-time chart directly below uses for the same state; it was the magenta-leaning purple 400 until 2026-08-29, chosen when that chart's series was still the theme accent, and it sat one shade from the muted lavender that means maintenance). Each cell's tooltip carries the RUNNING missed count and the direction it moved (`Missed 2 (+1)` / `Received — 1 missed outstanding (−1)`), because "Missed" on four cells in a row does not say whether the device is climbing toward Down or paying its way back out. `_intermittencyStates` — a one-line delegate to the shared `PolarisMonitorStates.replay` in `public/js/monitor-states.js`, which the response-time chart below the bar and the phone's copy of that chart read too — replays the leaky bucket forward over the samples client-side using the COVERING AUTOMATION's counts from `/effective-monitor-settings`' `downDetection` block (`missedPolls`, and `recoveryPolls` for the climb — business rule 36, no longer the settings tiers' `failureThreshold`), so a brief blip shows up as one yellow cell, a true outage as a sustained red run, and the recovery that follows it as a BLUE run until the automation's reset count of answers has landed. Failed probes stay yellow/red even mid-recovery. `passive` (no automation covers the device) means no cell may go red. Hovering a cell shows the timestamp + status. Hidden on unmonitored assets.
- Each asset row's Actions cell renders a **View Lease** button when the asset has an `ipAddress` and the row's `ipContext` resolves a non-deprecated containing subnet. Clicking it navigates to `/subnets.html#ip=<subnetId>@<ipAddress>`, where the network slide-over opens with the asset's IP scrolled into view and visually highlighted; reserve / release / edit happens in that panel directly. The Networks slide-over is also where the **View Asset** button (per-IP, on rows where the IP resolves to a Polaris asset) lives — clicking it navigates to `/assets.html#view=asset:<id>` so the asset details slide-in opens on the assets page.
- Asset edit modal is tab-based (General + Monitoring). The details modal has three tabs by default (General + System + **Sources**) and adds a fourth **SNMP Walk** tab for admins (admin-only on both the frontend and the backend) — and only when at least one monitoring stream actually resolves to SNMP for the asset: `_assetUsesSnmpPolling` checks the eight resolved `*Polling` fields from `/effective-monitor-settings` (prefetched in the view modal's parallel auxResults pass so the tab never flashes-then-vanishes, admin-only fetch) plus the per-asset `customWidgetPolling`; a failed fetch fails open so a transient error can't hide the tab. The backend route stays admin-gated but method-agnostic (an admin can still walk via the API). Controls: a **MIB** dropdown (optional — groups Standard MIBs and Uploaded MIBs), a **Base OID / Object name** input that switches label and validation based on the selected MIB, an SNMP credential picker (any stored SNMP credential), and a Max-rows input (default 500, capped at 5,000). **Standard MIBs** (System, IF-MIB, IF-MIB Extended, HOST-RESOURCES-MIB, ENTITY-MIB, ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB, LLDP-MIB) render the same browse tree + object-name input as uploaded MIBs, backed by the bundled text files under [src/services/stdMibs/](src/services/stdMibs/) (see `stdMibLibrary.ts`). Tree fetcher is selected per id-prefix in `_loadAndRenderMibTree`: `std:*` calls `api.serverSettings.getStdMibStructure(key)`, UUID calls `getMibStructure(id)`. The walk button likewise dispatches to `walkStdMib` for std ids and `walkMib` for uploaded UUIDs. **Uploaded MIBs** (from the MIB Database in Server Settings) switch the input to an object name field, render a **browse tree** beneath the buttons row (Tables + Scalars / Other sections from `GET /server-settings/mibs/:id/structure`, cached per mibId in `_snmpMibStructureCache`) where clicking a symbol fills the Object name input + highlights the row without auto-walking (typing in the input still works as the source of truth), and use the MIB-aware walk (`POST /server-settings/mibs/:id/walk` with `{ assetId, credentialId, objectName, maxRows }`) — results render decoded: `kind: "table"` as a 2D grid with column headers and index column (decoded enum labels with raw value in tooltip on hover), `kind: "scalars"` as OID / Symbol / Value rows (decoded value with raw in parentheses). A yellow banner fires when `decodedCount < rowCount / 2` (MIB doesn't match the asset's manufacturer). **No MIB** (default) uses raw numeric walk with manual OID entry. Abort is available for every walk kind (the MIB-aware API helpers accept an abort signal too), and a 60-second client-enforced deadline renders as a live countdown next to the Walk button — at zero the request is aborted and the tab reports "Walk timed out after 60s." (the server-side walk still runs to completion; abort only abandons the response). Walks acquire the per-host SNMP gate with a 50s wait budget (`SNMP_WALK_GATE_WAIT_MS`, vs. the collectors' 30s `POLARIS_SNMP_GATE_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS` default) so a walk queued behind a monitoring poll on the same device gets the whole countdown window to start; a gate timeout is surfaced as a "device was busy" message since the walk never ran. Copy results produces TSV for tables and one-per-line `symbol = decoded (raw)` for scalars. MIB selection, OID/object name, and credential persist across tab open/close via module-level variables (`_snmpWalkLastMibId`, `_snmpWalkLastObjectName`, `_snmpWalkLastOid`, `_snmpWalkLastCredId`). Uploaded MIBs load lazily on first tab wire from `api.mibs.listMibs({})` and are cached in `_snmpMibCache`. Each walk is audited as an `asset.snmp_walk` Event. The Monitoring tab on the edit modal renders an editable type dropdown for every asset; integration-discovered assets (FMG/FortiGate-discovered firewalls and AD-discovered Windows/Linux hosts) get an extra option representing the integration default (e.g. "FortiManager: \<name\> (default)") plus a hint pointing operators to SNMP for small-branch FortiGates whose REST sensor endpoint 404s. The **System** details tab leads with the monitoring section — status pill, source, last RTT/poll/consecutive failures, and an SVG response-time chart (1h / 12h / 24h / 7d / 30d / Custom; failed probes render as red dots at 0 ms, the line fading into red across the outage — no more full-height failure lines; click-drag on any chart applies the selection as a custom window) plus a "Refresh" button for user-or-above (kicks off all three streams — response-time probe, telemetry, system-info — and the toast names exactly which streams refreshed and which failed, e.g. `Refresh partial (probe 12 ms · telemetry) — interfaces: FortiManager direct-mode API token not configured`) — then a horizontal divider, then a single combined CPU+Memory chart (both lines on a shared 0–100% y-axis with one hover tooltip naming both values) over 1h / 12h / 24h / 7d / 30d / Custom, a Temperatures section (current sensor table — hidden when the device exposes no sensors — with each sensor name clickable to open a per-sensor slide-over chart), an Interfaces table with a "Poll 1m" checkbox column + clickable interface name + **Native VLAN** + **Tagged VLANs** columns that render only when at least one row in the table actually carries port-VLAN data (managed FortiSwitches overlaid from the parent FortiGate's CMDB — see `AssetInterfaceSample.nativeVlan` / `taggedVlans` / `trunksAllVlans`); the Tagged cell collapses long lists past 6 entries to "first 6, +N more" with the full list in the cell tooltip, and renders a teal `all` pill for trunk-all ports. **Per-column sort + filter (TableSF), and no rows are hidden** (2026-08). Traffic-less interfaces and tunnels used to ship `display:none` behind a `▶ Show N inactive interfaces (no traffic)` expander; that whole mechanism is gone — "no counters yet" was a poor proxy for "not interesting" (an admin-shut port being hunted for, a link that just came up, a dead tunnel that should be up), and the expander was a bespoke control answering one question. The table now carries the same `TableSF` header controls every other Polaris list table does, over a flat **row model** built alongside the tree (`_ifaceEntry` / `_tunnelEntry` in `_buildInterfacesTableDOM`): text filters on Interface / IP / MAC / Neighbor, multi-select filters on Status / PoE / Addressing / Native VLAN / Tagged VLANs, sort-only (`data-sf-nofilter`) on Speed / In / Out / Errors. Each entry field is named for the column's existing `data-col-id` (`ifname`, `native-vlan`, `in`, …) because `setupColumnLayout` derives a column's persistence id from `data-sf-key` first — keeping them identical is what lets already-saved column widths / hidden columns / drag order keep applying. `ifname` is an ARRAY (`[alias, ifName]`) so an aliased port sorts by the label the operator reads and still matches its real ifName. Status, PoE and both VLAN columns get their options from what THIS device reported (`setColumnOptions` over the entries) — the VLAN pair through `_distinctVlanOptions` rather than `_distinctSorted`, because the latter's alphabetical order lists 100 and 1000 between 10 and 20 in a column whose every value is a number (non-numeric sentinels, i.e. the Tagged column's trunk-all `all`, sort last). Both VLAN columns are pickers rather than text boxes on purpose: a VLAN is an identifier out of a closed set the switch just reported, so there is nothing to type that isn't already offered — and a substring filter matched 100/110/210 when the operator typed 10. That is also why the Tagged column's row value is an **array** (`taggedVlanList`) instead of the joined display string: TableSF matches a multi-select selection against each element, which is what lets "Tagged VLANs: 30" select the ports carrying VLAN 30 out of a 40-VLAN trunk list. A trunk-all port carries the single `all` element and deliberately does NOT match a specific VLAN — the device enumerated none, and that matches what its cell renders. Stored string filters from before the columns became pickers are dropped on restore by `restoreFilterUI`'s shape check (a string left in place would filter by substring through a control that can't display or clear it), and a tunnel's unanswerable columns are null/"" rather than 0, so a tunnel never turns up under "PoE: fault" nor sorts as the slowest link. **Two render modes** (`renderBody`): with no sort and no filter it's the nested tree with its section headers exactly as before; the moment either is active it renders **flat** — no section headers, no indentation, no expand toggles (a row's position no longer implies parentage, and half a tree is worse than an honest list; a member port keeps its "Member" badge as the only remaining cue). Only the tbody is rewritten, so TableSF's rebuilt header row and `applyTableLayout`'s widths/handles survive. The header is **frozen** — the wrapper carries `.table-wrapper-panel-sticky` (`#asset-iface-wrapper`) so rows scroll inside it and the column labels, with the sort + filter controls that live in them, stay on screen while walking a 48-port switch. Its sizer is deliberately NOT the Services tab's: `_sizeAssetIfaceTableWrapper` takes a fraction of the slide-over body's own height, because this table sits MID-tab (Storage / Sensors / LLDP / Physical Entities follow it) so `_sizeAssetSvcTableWrapper`'s distance-to-the-body's-bottom measurement would yield a different bound on every panel scroll — and measuring only the panel body works while the System tab is still `display:none`, which is the state the table is first built in (the panel opens on General, and there is no per-tab hook to re-size from). Consequences that shaped the code: every row handler is **delegated off the tbody** (a per-row listener would be dropped on the first keystroke), the pin Sets are **mutated in place** (a rebound local would leave a re-render drawing stale checkboxes), and the collapsed-parent state is **baked into the row markup** rather than applied to the DOM afterwards. Sort + filter state persists per user AND per device class under `polaris-prefs-asset-interfaces-<assetType>-<username>` (the System tab rebuilds this container on every refresh tick, so in-memory state would be wiped mid-investigation); state naming a column this device doesn't render (PoE, the VLAN pair) is dropped on restore, since a filter on an absent column would match nothing with no visible control to clear it. Plus a cumulative errors column + LLDP **Neighbor** column (rightmost; shows the first neighbor's `systemName` plus its remote `portId` as `<sysName> / <portId>` — the system name links to that asset's view modal when the neighbor matched a Polaris asset; a `+N` badge appears when the local port saw multiple neighbors and the slide-over enumerates all of them) (FortiOS-monitored phase-1 IPsec tunnels are nested under their parent interface as child rows here — orange "IPsec" badge, status pill, remote gateway in the IP column, cumulative in/out bytes; tunnels whose `parentInterface` lookup fails fall into a final "IPsec Tunnels (unbound)" group at the bottom of the same table), and a Storage table (Poll 1m checkbox, mount, used, total, %); empty-state messages render for unmonitored assets, ICMP/SSH-monitored assets, and WinRM/AD-monitored assets (the last is a placeholder until WMI Enumerate-over-WS-Management lands). The Interface column shows the operator-set **alias** as the primary label when present (FortiOS CMDB `alias` / SNMP `ifAlias`), with the real `ifName` rendered as a small subtitle and as the cell tooltip so the operator can still correlate to switch port labels. The Poll 1m checkboxes — interface, storage, and nested tunnel — write to `Asset.monitoredInterfaces` / `monitoredStorage` / `monitoredIpsecTunnels` respectively and pin the row for sub-minute polling on the response-time cadence. Each table's checkbox-column **header** carries a select-all checkbox mirroring the aggregate state (checked = all pinned, indeterminate = some; disabled without assets-write): the interfaces one acts on every **listed** row (collapsed children and nested IPsec tunnels included) and leaves rows a filter is hiding pinned as they were — un-pinning an interface the operator can't currently see would silently stop its fast-cadence polling and drop it to 24h retention; with no filter that is every row, i.e. the pre-filter behavior — writing `monitoredInterfaces` + `monitoredIpsecTunnels` together in one PUT, while the storage one writes the whole `monitoredStorage` set. The interface/storage checkbox-column header select-alls are unchanged. The **Services tab** (`_assetServicesTabHTML` / `_wireAssetServicesTab`, gated off firewall/switch/access_point AND the `other` catch-all type — none report a unit list or a host process table, frozen-header `.table-wrapper-panel-sticky` wrapper + TableSF + `applyTableLayout("asset-services-merged")`) is a **merged unit + process inventory** (the standalone Processes tab was folded into it 2026-07). It shows one row per systemd unit / Windows service (`GET /assets/:id/services`) by default; an **Include processes** checkbox in the toolbar lazily fetches `GET /assets/:id/processes` and folds the per-program process inventory into the SAME table (services first, then processes). Rows are a unified model (`combinedRows` — `kind` service|process + synthetic sort keys `sortName`/`typeLabel`/`stateSort`/`cpuPct`/`memSort` that TableSF reads by `data-sf-key`). Columns: two **per-row** pin checkboxes (no header select-alls) — **Monitor** (combined: a service row's checkbox toggles `monitoredServices` = journal tailing, a process row's toggles `monitoredProcesses` = CPU/RAM history + logs; Monitor and Logs are one column since a row is only ever one kind) and **Map** (both → `mappedProcesses` / `mappedServices`) — then Name (unit or program, clickable), Type, State (services get the colored active-state pill `_svcStatePill` — active/running green, failed red, activating amber, else grey; processes show a dash; filtered by active/inactive/failed checkboxes via `data-sf-options`), CPU % and Memory (sort-only via `data-sf-nofilter` — no filter box). The narrow pin columns use the `.svc-pin-col` class (nowrap header + tight padding). There is **no Alert column** — process alerting moved to Automations (`alertWatchedProcesses` is no longer written from this UI). Clicking a process name opens `openProcessDetailPanel`; clicking a unit opens `openServiceDetailPanel` (reuses the process detail nested slide-over shell) showing unit metadata (read-only — Start/Stop/Restart control was removed in the Satellite-posture change) + a **journalctl log viewer** (`_loadServiceLogsFor` → `GET /assets/:id/service-logs`, flagged-only toggle, LogFlagRule badges — same rendering as the process log viewer; Linux units only) + a **Ports & Connections** section (`_loadServiceConnectionsFor` → `GET /assets/:id/process-connections?unit=`, reusing the shared `_renderConnView` renderer; populated when the unit is pinned for Map). Both detail panels share a footer (`_setProcPanelFooter`) with **Copy** (plaintext extraction of the panel body via the shared `_extractTabBlocks` + `_blocksToPlaintext` — the same formatter behind the asset-details Copy button) and **Screenshot** (`_screenshotProcPanel` — html-to-image capture of the body's content wrapper at a canonical 900px width with a title strip, → clipboard PNG; same force-width + settle-delay approach as `_runScreenshotCapture`), and both log viewers carry an **Export** button (`_exportPanelLogsCsv` — re-fetches up to the server's 2000-line cap honoring the Flagged-only toggle, CSV via `downloadCsv`, oldest-first like the viewer). Clicking an interface name opens a **nested slide-over** whose header reads `<alias> (<ifName>)` when an alias is set, followed by an **Interface Comments** editor — a 255-char textarea + Save/Revert buttons (assets admin and admin only; everyone else gets a disabled box). Save writes to `AssetInterfaceOverride.description` via `PUT /assets/:id/interfaces/:ifName/comment` and is **Polaris-local by default**; when the originating integration's `syncDescriptions` toggle is on the saved comment is **also pushed to the device** (Polaris-primary — business rule 14) and the source line under the editor flips to a per-row sync status ("Synced to device N ago" / "Sync to device failed: … — retries on the next discovery cycle" / "Sync conflict — both edited since the last sync; save to resolve"), driven by the `descriptionSync` block on the interface-history response. When no override is set, the device-reported FortiOS CMDB `description` is shown as the textarea placeholder ("Device says: …") so operators can see what's currently surfaced before deciding to type over it. Saving an empty box clears the override and the discovered description shows through again. Auto-refresh ticks don't clobber in-progress edits — the editor tracks a dirty flag and skips repopulation while the user is typing. Below the comment editor the body renders an **LLDP Neighbor card** (one card per neighbor on this interface; shows system name as a clickable link when matched to a Polaris asset, plus chassis ID + management IP + capabilities + system description; an "unmatched" badge when no Polaris asset resolved by mgmt IP / chassis MAC / hostname) followed by **two charts**: one combined Throughput chart (input + output on a shared bps axis, single tooltip naming both) and an in/out errors-per-interval chart. Clicking any mountpoint name opens **one consolidated slide-over** containing one section per mountpoint discovered on the asset (not one slide-over per mount); the clicked mount is scrolled into view and briefly highlighted so it's obvious which one the click landed on. The pane has one shared range bar (1h / 12h / 24h / 7d / 30d / Custom; defaults to 24h since storage rides the ~10m systemInfo cadence) and one shared **Used %** / **Used bytes** view toggle at the top — both apply to every section below. Each per-mount section has its own usage chart, stats line, forecast headline, and a per-(asset, mount) forecast visibility toggle. Each chart overlays a dashed **forecast** line projecting trajectory — linear least-squares regression over the last 7 days of usedBytes samples (always 7d, independent of the chart's selected range; one extra `storageHistory` fetch in parallel with the range fetch per mount, deduped when the operator picked 7d). When forecast is on, the chart's X-axis extends by **exactly one history-span** to the right — a 1h range shows 1h of history + 1h of projection, a 7d range shows 7d + 7d, etc. — and the dashed line is drawn for **every** signal (growing / flat / shrinking / beyond-horizon), not just growing, so the operator always sees the projected trajectory next to history. A headline above each chart reads `Days until full: N` (color-coded red <30d / amber <90d / green ≥90d) or `Shrinking` / `No measurable growth` / `> 1 year` depending on the regression's `signal`. A vertical dashed "now" divider marks the projection origin. Forecast computation always runs; toggling the forecast off only hides the dashed overlay + "now" divider + the X-axis extension on that one section (the headline stays visible because the days-to-full number is the operationally useful piece). Per-mount fetches fan out via `Promise.all` so a 5-mount host opens in roughly one round-trip; one mount's fetch failure is caught and rendered as an inline error on that section only without taking down the rest of the pane. Clicking a tunnel name opens a similar nested slide-over with a status timeline (1h / 12h / 24h / 7d / 30d / Custom) and per-interval throughput charts; clicking a sensor name opens a per-sensor temperature slide-over (1h / 12h / 24h / 7d / 30d / Custom) with axis labels and a chart title. Closing only that panel returns to the asset details panel underneath. All charts share `_wireChartTooltip` for hover behaviour. The selected range on each chart type (response time, system tab CPU+memory, sensor, interface, IPsec tunnel, storage) is remembered per user via `localStorage` under `polaris-prefs-charts-<username>` — one JSON map keyed by chart id (`assetMonitor`, `assetSystem`, `assetSensor`, `assetInterface`, `assetIpsec`, `assetStorage`) so each surface keeps its own last selection independently. "Custom" range selections are not persisted (the from/to inputs reset on reopen). The storage chart's Used %/bytes view mode persists under `polaris-prefs-storage-view-<username>` (single string per user — same mental model across the fleet); the forecast-overlay visibility persists under `polaris-prefs-storage-forecast-<username>` as a `{ "<assetId>:<mountPath>": boolean }` map (per asset+mount — defaults on; only stored when explicitly toggled). Collapsed-state for nested rows in the Interfaces table (aggregate members, VLAN sub-interfaces, nested IPsec tunnels) is also remembered per user via `localStorage` under `polaris-prefs-iface-collapse-<username>` — one JSON map keyed by `assetId` to an array of collapsed parent ifNames. Per-asset because the same parent name on different assets can have wildly different children. Empty entries are pruned so the blob self-cleans when everything is re-expanded.
- The **Sources** tab on the asset details modal renders one card per `AssetSource` row attached to this asset, in stable presentation order (`entra` → `intune` → `ad` → `fortigate-firewall` → `fortiswitch` → `fortiap` → `manual`). Each card shows the source's friendly label (e.g. "Microsoft Entra ID"), a **state badge** answering "does this source consider the asset enabled?" (green Enabled / Powered on / Connected / Online, red Disabled / Powered off / Suspended / Disconnected / Not responding / Offline, grey "State not reported" for sources that make no lifecycle statement — server-derived `state` from `src/utils/assetSourceState.ts`, tooltip naming the observed field + raw value it came from; the two account booleans it consumes, `accountEnabled` / `accountDisabled`, are hidden from the key-value table below since the badge *is* them), the originating integration as a badge, an **Inferred** badge for phase-1-backfilled rows that haven't been replaced by real discovery yet, the `syncedAt` / `firstSeen` / `lastSeen` timestamps + the source's natural `externalId` as a metadata strip, and the source's `observed` blob rendered as a humanized key-value table (camelCase keys → "Title Case", ISO timestamps → human dates, booleans → Yes/No, complex values → JSON). Above the cards, a **"Reported state by source"** roll-up lists which sources call the asset enabled and which call it disabled (rendered only when at least one source reports a state); when two *directory* sources contradict each other it adds an amber note that a disabled account decommissions the asset, so the disabling directory wins on the next discovery run — runtime readings (a powered-off VM whose AD account is enabled) are deliberately not counted as a contradiction. Loaded once per modal open via `GET /assets/:id/sources`; failures fall through to an empty-state message so the rest of the modal still works. This is the operator-visible payoff of the Phase 1+2 multi-source foundation — see what each integration independently said about the device, side-by-side. **Admins** see a **Split** button per card (hidden when the asset only has one source, and on `manual` source rows): clicking detaches the chosen source onto a freshly-created Asset via `POST /assets/:id/sources/:sourceId/split`, after a confirm dialog. The current modal closes and the new asset's view modal opens so the operator can verify the move.
- The **Events** tab on the asset details modal shows this asset's audit history, gated on `events`-read (mirrors the `GET /events` backend permission) and positioned right after Sources. Reuses the Events-page table (7 columns — Timestamp / Level / Action / Resource / Message / User / Detail; it deliberately omits the Events page's **Resource Name** column, which on this tab is always the asset the modal is open on) and follows the same **server-side `TableSF`** pattern as the Events page (UI-CANON.md → "Sortable + filterable data table (server-side mode)") — per-column sort + filters translate into `GET /events` params, with `resourceType:"asset"` + `resourceId` pinned into every fetch — plus offset **pagination** outside `TableSF` and `applyTableLayout(table, "asset-events")` for the column resize/chooser. Everything is **self-contained** in `public/js/assets.js` (`_assetEventsTabHTML` / `_renderAssetEventRow` / `_buildAssetEventsQuery` / `_loadAssetEventsTabFor` / `_renderAssetEventsPagination` / `_save`+`_restoreAssetEventsPrefs` / `_wireAssetEventsTab` / `_showAssetEventDetail`), because `events.js` is only loaded on `events.html`. **Lazy-loaded** on first tab click (subsequent loads come from filter/sort/page changes) so the modal fires no extra `/events` query on open — matters at the 2000-asset fleet size. pageSize + filter/sort prefs persist under `polaris-prefs-asset-events-<user>` (column layout under `polaris-table-layout-asset-events-<user>`). Rows whose event carries `details.changes` get a **Detail** button that opens the before/after change-diff popup (`_showAssetEventDetail`, a copy of the Events-page `showEventDetail`). The join is purely string-based (`Event.resourceId == Asset.id`); asset events are logged with `resourceType:"asset"` so no schema/backend change was needed.
- The asset details slide-in **header** carries the per-asset action group — **Copy** / **Screenshot** (or **Export** on the Events tab) / **Refresh** / **Open HTTPS** / **Open SSH** — right-aligned and left of the lock + close pair (`#asset-panel-actions` / `.slideover-header-actions`; the footer keeps only Close / Edit). It moved out of the footer in 2026-08: those buttons act on the tab the operator is reading, and at the bottom of a full-height panel they sat a screen away from it. Because the group now sits at the TOP of the viewport, both its dropdowns (Export, the SSH caret) drop DOWN rather than carrying `.drop-up`. Copy and Screenshot act on the active tab. **Copy** walks the panel via `_extractTabBlocks` (assets.js) into kv / table / heading / text blocks and writes plaintext to the clipboard. **Screenshot** (`_openScreenshotOptions`) opens a **section-picker modal**: each tab builder wraps its logical sections in `<div data-shot-section="<key>" data-shot-label="<Label>">` wrappers (chart sections add `data-shot-chart="assetMonitor|assetSystem|assetSdwan"`, Interfaces adds `data-shot-sub="hiddenIfaces"`), and `_collectShotSections` enumerates them from the live panel — so sections absent on an asset never appear, and the modal needs no per-tab knowledge. Each section gets an include checkbox (state remembered per user+tab under `polaris-prefs-screenshot-<username>`); the Interfaces section gets an "Include hidden interfaces" sub-checkbox (reveals inactive + collapsed-child rows for the capture only, and drops the toggle-button row from the image); chart sections get a 1h/12h/24h/7d/30d/Custom range picker **defaulting to the chart's current on-screen selection** (ranges are never persisted). Tabs with a single plain section (SNMP Walk, Stations) skip the modal. On Capture, `_captureWithChoices` swaps each differing chart to its chosen range (awaiting the existing loaders, which cancel their own auto-refresh timers; range buttons + `_setChartRangePref` are never touched), then runs `_runScreenshotCapture` with an html-to-image `filter` that prunes deselected section wrappers, then restores everything in a `finally` — the operator's on-screen state is guaranteed unchanged. The capture itself is a **faithful DOM capture at a canonical width**: the slide-over is temporarily forced to `CAPTURE_WIDTH` (1100px — the design max) so the output is identical regardless of the operator's display size or drag-resized slide-over (a double-rAF + settle delay lets the relayout and the charts' ResizeObserver re-renders land first; the operator's width is restored when the rasterization settles). The vendored `html-to-image` library deep-clones the active `.page-tab-panel`, inlines computed styles + pseudo-elements + the page's webfonts, renders the clone through an SVG `<foreignObject>` at `pixelRatio: 2`, and the result is composed under a self-identifying title strip (hostname + tab label) with uniform padding, then copied to the clipboard as PNG. Scrollbar chrome is excluded via `.screenshot-hide-scrollbars` (styles.css); webfont embedding fetches the Google Fonts CSS + woff2 (whitelisted in CSP `connect-src`) and degrades to system fallbacks when unreachable; inner scrollable regions render scrolled-to-top in the clone. Per-table camera buttons (`_screenshotTableEl`) and per-chart camera buttons (`_addChartScreenshotButton`) keep their existing synthetic canvas composers. Because the table composer re-DRAWS rather than rasterizes, it carries each cell's color across explicitly (`_shotCellColor`: an explicit `data-shot-color` first, then the cell's own computed color, else the first text-bearing descendant differing from the table base, ignoring decorative glyphs) — without it every cell painted in `--color-text-primary` and a red PoE "Fault" or a down status pill came out near-white. The companion `_shotCellText` flattens the cell, honoring `data-shot-text` as a stand-in for content that carries its meaning with NO text (a status dot, a green/red per-scrape strip) — those contributed nothing and their column came out blank, which is what hid the SD-WAN Members up/down state and its entire Health Check Status column. **On the Events tab the Screenshot button gives way to an Export dropdown** (`_syncAssetFooterButtons` flips visibility on tab clicks; both are rendered in the header group up front — the function name predates the move): Current page / All events for this asset × CSV / PDF, mirroring the Events-page export but scoped through `_buildAssetEventsQuery` (so "all" honors the active column filters + sort, pinned to `resourceType=asset`, fetched at `limit=10000` inside `trackedPdfExport`). The generators (`_generateAssetEventCsv` / `_generateAssetEventPdf`, filenames `polaris-asset-events-<hostname>-<date>`) live in assets.js because events.js isn't loaded on assets/map pages; the menu uses the plain right-anchored drop-down (styles.css) so it stays inside the slide-over below the header; map.html now ships the jspdf vendor scripts so the PDF export works from the Device Map's slide-in too.
- The asset details **System tab**'s Interfaces table nests member ports and VLAN sub-interfaces under their parent (`_buildInterfacesTableDOM` in `public/js/assets.js`), drawing the shared `_treeElbow` connector — `├─` while more rows follow at that level, `└─` on the last (see UI-CANON.md → "Expand/collapse tree inside a data table"). The **Poll 1m** pin checkbox is the aggregate's, not the member's: a nested member renders an empty poll cell titled with the aggregate to pin instead, since a LAG is one link as far as history goes and three boxes answering one question is what the member checkboxes were. Two carve-outs, both because the alternative loses a real capability: a member that is ALREADY pinned keeps its (checked) box — hiding it would leave an auto-monitor or legacy pin collecting history and feeding interface triggers invisibly, with no way to switch it off — and a member rendered at TOP level keeps its box too, that being the downed-FortiLink-trunk case where the member port IS the signal. Select-all iterates the rendered boxes, so it no longer sweeps members in.
- The asset details modal's **Wireless** tab (monitored FortiAPs only; it was called *Stations* while it listed clients alone) renders a **radio → SSID → client tree** in one `data-table`: each radio with its band, PHY, operating channel + width and transmit power, the SSIDs that radio broadcasts under it (with BSSID and VLAN), and the clients on each SSID under those. Radios come from `GET /assets/:id/system-info`'s `apRadios[]` (AssetApRadio + nested AssetApVap); clients are the existing `wirelessStations[]`. A client is filed by **BSSID first**, falling back to (radio, SSID-name) — never by its own `wlanId`, which is only as trustworthy as the source's VAP numbering — and anything that matches nothing is listed under a "Not matched to a broadcast SSID" heading rather than dropped, since a hidden client makes the tree disagree with the client count. A radio's client count is COUNTED from the rows below it, not taken from the controller's `clientCount`, which disagrees mid-roam. Transmit power is shown as each source reported it (`70%` from the controller, `17 dBm (1–20)` from the MIB) and never converted — that needs a per-model maximum Polaris doesn't have. Expand/collapse follows the System tab's interface tree (see UI-CANON.md → "Expand/collapse tree inside a data table") with its own persisted collapse scope. An AP with no radio inventory yet — discovery hasn't run since the feature shipped, or it isn't controller-managed — falls back to the previous flat station table, so the tab never regresses to empty while it fills in.
- The asset details slide-in header carries a **back/forward pair** (‹ / › left of the title, plus Alt+Left / Alt+Right) walking the assets visited since the panel opened. It exists because the panel is walkable IN PLACE: the Dependency Tree rows below, the HA-peer link, the interface slide-over's LLDP neighbour, a MAC-table match and the Application Map rail all call `openViewModal` on another asset, which swaps the body rather than stacking a second panel — so before this the device the operator started from was simply gone. State is the module-level `_assetPanelHistory` (`{entries:[{id,label}], idx}`) reduced by the pure `_assetHistoryOpen` / `_assetHistoryTarget` / `_assetHistoryLabel`, rendered by `_renderAssetPanelNav`, walked by `_assetPanelGo`. Four behaviours are load-bearing: **a re-open of the CURRENT asset is a refresh, not a visit** (`openViewModal(sameId)` is the footer Refresh button, every post-save re-render and the monitor-pill flip — pushing there would make a refreshed panel take one ‹ press per refresh to escape); **a walk doesn't push** (`_assetPanelWalkDelta` is set by `_assetPanelGo` and consumed SYNCHRONOUSLY at the top of `openViewModal`, before any await, so it can't leak into whatever opens next — without it stepping back would itself push and the start would be unreachable); **"fresh session" is an empty stack, not a closed overlay** (the overlay only gains `.open` on the next frame, so two fast opens would otherwise read as two sessions); and `_assetPanelReturnFocus` is captured only on the FIRST open of a session, since every later open's `activeElement` is a control inside the panel and restoring focus to a hidden button loses it to `<body>`. The pair is `hidden` until there are two entries, each button is `disabled` when its direction is spent (the only signal the stack has an end) and its `title` names the target asset once the hostname has loaded. Entries cap at `ASSET_HISTORY_MAX` (50) from the front; `closeAssetPanel` resets the stack, so back means back to the device I came from, not to something looked at an hour ago. The Alt chord is gated exactly like Escape — topmost layer only, so an open nested drilldown or a stacked modal keeps the keys. Covered by `tests/unit/assetPanelHistoryDom.test.ts`.
- The General tab's three **upstream rows** — Last Seen Switch / Last Seen AP / Last Seen Firewall, all hidden on an `assetType: "firewall"` (a gate is the thing doing the sighting) — each carry a **row context menu** rather than being dead text: **Open asset**, then that device's own **Open HTTPS / Open SSH** off the shared `_assetMgmtAccess` gate. Rendered in two passes on purpose: `_upstreamRowHTML` paints the stored string into an id'd value cell on first paint, then `GET /assets/:id/upstream` resolves each name to an Asset row and `_upgradeUpstreamRow` swaps the DEVICE half for a `.row-menu-trigger` (the port half of `lastSeenSwitch` stays plain text — "port15" is not something you can open, and folding it in would make the trigger's accessible name `SW-01/port15`). A name that resolves to nothing stays text, so a 403, a failed fetch and an unadopted switch all leave the row exactly as it was. The DISPLAYED value never changes — a switch is often stored as its serial, so the resolved hostname rides the trigger's `title` instead of replacing what the row has always shown. The verbs come from `_managementAccessMenuItems` applied to the resolved device's stub — the same function the Assets list row menu uses — so a FortiSwitch offers exactly what its controller's local-access policy permits and never a verb that would land on a closed port. Covered by `tests/unit/assetUpstreamRowsDom.test.ts`.
- The asset details modal **General** tab renders a **Dependency Tree** block beneath the details table on **every asset type** (it was infra-only until the endpoint half landed in 2026-08) — a vertical mini-tree showing this asset's effective parents above, the asset itself in the middle (rendered bold + non-clickable, with a layer annotation), and direct children below. Each row carries a status pip (▲ up / ▼ down / ● dep-down/pending/unmonitored) using the same priority as the Status pill (dep-test beats dep-down beats five-state). Hostnames are clickable buttons that pivot `openViewModal` to that asset, so operators can walk up or down the tree without leaving the modal. An **override active** badge appears in the header when the asset has any `source="override"` row; an `override` tag also marks override-pinned parents inline. Children render two layers down (direct children + their own children) with the deeper row indented and rendered slightly smaller so the firewall → switch → AP chain shows in one view; operators click through to walk further than two layers. The block is loaded in parallel with the Sources tab via `GET /assets/:id/dependencies`; the placeholder `<div id="asset-dep-tree-mount-<id>">` is filled after the modal body is rendered so the rest of the General tab paints immediately. A parent row reached by an endpoint-half or vCenter signal carries a `detectedVia` tag naming that signal in operator words — "last-seen switch port" / "last-seen access point" / "last-seen firewall" / "hypervisor placement" — because an inferred edge that silences alerts should say out loud what put it there; the Fortinet infra signals stay untagged (the tree's shape already says it). **Downstream endpoints are never listed** (operator decision, 2026-08: the downward view is the infra chain — see the endpoint's own tab for its dependency), so a `+N` on a switch row and the "Showing X of Y downstream switches / access points" line under the children both count switches and APs the caps left out, never the workstations and printers behind them. Empty states: a standalone Fortinet infra asset reads "Standalone — no upstream or downstream switches / access points discovered" (worded around the infra chain on purpose, since a gate with endpoints sighted on it but no managed switches lands here and does have dependents — just not ones this tree lists), and an endpoint with no resolvable upstream says so explicitly ("No upstream device identified … so dependency suppression can't apply to this asset") rather than rendering nothing — that asset alerts on its own probe state even when its whole site is dark, which is worth stating where an operator will look for it.
- Asset list status-column filter includes **Quarantined**. Per-row Actions cell shows a **Quarantine** button (deep-red) for assets-admin+ on assets that have at least one MAC on record; quarantined assets get a **Release Quarantine** button instead. Bulk bar has matching **Quarantine** / **Release Quarantine** buttons that appear only when the selection mix makes them relevant. Asset details panel adds a **Quarantine** tab for assets-admin+ (shown whenever the asset has MACs or is quarantined): displays quarantine status, per-FortiGate push targets table (FortiGate name, status badge, pushed MACs, pushed-at timestamp), DHCP sightings history, and Quarantine / Release / Verify Push action buttons.
- Server Settings → **Credentials** tab manages the stored SNMP / WinRM / SSH credentials (admin-only). Secrets are masked in every GET; resubmitting the mask preserves the stored value on PUT.
- Server Settings → **API Tokens** tab (admin-only, lazy-loaded) lists all bearer tokens with status badges (Active/Revoked/Expired), last-used IP, the bound **role** (with an "admin-equivalent" marker when applicable), **per-token integration scope** (the list of FMG/FortiGate names this token can quarantine via, with inline red/amber alerts when an integration is disabled or has `pushQuarantine: false` so the operator sees at-a-glance that pushes will be skipped), and Revoke/Delete actions. Create-token form has name, an **"Acts as role" dropdown** (from the `roles` array on `GET /api-tokens`; selecting an admin-equivalent role surfaces a red warning banner), an integration multi-picker that appears only when the chosen role grants quarantine write (REQUIRED — at least one integration; each row is decorated with the same disabled / pushQuarantine-off alert text as the table), and optional expiry. The picker source is the `quarantineIntegrations` array on `GET /api-tokens` so admins don't need a separate `/integrations` round-trip. On creation a modal shows the raw token value with a Copy button — the only time it is visible.
- Server Settings → **Credentials** tab has a **MIB Database** card for managing SNMP MIB modules. **Visibility**: admin sees the full Server Settings page; **assets-admin** also sees a Server Settings link in the sidebar but the page is restricted to just the Credentials tab AND only the MIB Database card within it (every other tab is hidden client-side, and within the Credentials tab the Stored Credentials list + Manufacturer Profiles card are gated to admin inside `renderCredentialsTab()`; backend guards on `/server-settings/*` are the source of truth). Uploads are validated by `mibService.parseMib` (rejects anything that isn't a real ASN.1/SMI module — including binaries and arbitrary text); upload + delete remain admin-only, surfaced inline in the card and hidden for assets-admin. The form has a three-tier **Scope** selector: **Manufacturer-wide** (the most common case — covers every model from one vendor), **Device-specific** (overrides the manufacturer-wide MIB for one model only), or **Generic** (shared across all vendors, e.g. SNMPv2-SMI). Resolution priority at probe time is *device → vendor → generic → built-in seed*. The card also renders a **Vendor Profile Status** pill that shows, per built-in profile, whether each profile symbol resolves at the universal (manufacturer-only) scope and which MIB provided it; any model-specific MIBs uploaded under that manufacturer are listed beneath as "Model overrides". Uploads are wired into the SNMP telemetry probe via `oidRegistry` + `vendorTelemetryProfiles`: dropping in CISCO-PROCESS-MIB / CISCO-MEMORY-POOL-MIB / JUNIPER-MIB / MIKROTIK-MIB / FORTINET-FORTIGATE-MIB / etc. immediately starts populating CPU/memory on assets whose `manufacturer` matches the profile's regex. Until the MIB is uploaded the probe falls back to HOST-RESOURCES-MIB (which is null on most network gear). Each row carries a **Browse** button (open to admin + assets-admin) that opens an XL-sized two-pane modal driven by `GET /server-settings/mibs/:id/structure`: left pane lists Tables and Scalars / Other in collapsible sections (table entries show their column count inline); right pane renders the selected object's name, full OID, SYNTAX, ACCESS, STATUS, DESCRIPTION, an Enum Values table when the SYNTAX is `INTEGER { up(1), down(2), … }`, and a **Walk on asset…** button shown when the symbol is readable AND its OID resolved. Walk pivots inline within the same modal: an asset autocomplete (`GET /assets?search=&limit=25` — explicitly NOT the global `/search` endpoint, whose 8-per-group cap can drop firewalls), then an SNMP credential dropdown (`api.credentials.list()` filtered to `type === "snmp"`), then a Run Walk button that posts to `POST /server-settings/mibs/:id/walk`. Results render scalars as a flat decoded list (`<symbol>.<suffix>  =  <decoded>  (<raw>)`) or, when the walk lands on a table, a 2D `<table>` with column headers from the MIB and rows keyed by the SMI INDEX; cell tooltips carry the raw value when it differs from the decoded form. A **Copy results** button emits TSV (table view) or one-entry-per-line text (scalars). When `decodedCount < rowCount/2` a yellow banner reads "Decoded N / M rows — this MIB may not match the asset's manufacturer."
- Server Settings → **Credentials** also has a **Manufacturer Profiles** card (admin-only) — editable surface backed by the `ManufacturerProfile` data model. Lists every profile with caret-expandable detail; click a profile to see the seven metric rows (CPU / Memory / Temperature / Interfaces / LLDP / Storage / Wireless Stations). Each metric row has a **MIB → Symbol** chained picker — operator selects the MIB first (Built-in seed or any uploaded MIB scoped to this manufacturer), and the Symbol field becomes a dropdown populated by walking that MIB's structured parse via `GET /server-settings/mibs/:id/structure` (cached per-MIB in `_mfgMibSymbolsCache`); when the MIB is "Built-in seed" the Symbol stays a free-text input since seeded symbols don't have an enumerable directory. The **Type** column on every metric row is a 3-way dropdown (`scalar` / `double scalar` / `table`); flipping to `double scalar` turns the Symbol cell into TWO stacked pickers ("A:" + "B:") and swaps the **Transform** column's option list from unary transforms (`celsius_to_fahrenheit` / `bytes_to_gb` / `ratio_to_percent` / ...) to binary combiners (`a_over_b_as_percent` / `a_over_a_plus_b_as_percent` / `a_minus_b` / ...). Per-model exception rows hang under each metric row with the same Type + Symbol + Transform pattern + a Model regex input + Edit / Del buttons. +Add Manufacturer at the bottom; delete via the per-row Del button (cascade-removes metric rows, overrides, widgets). The legacy read-only **Vendor Profile Status** card was removed — this editable surface now covers that ground end-to-end. A **Custom widgets** section sits below the metric table — one card per `ManufacturerCustomWidget` with view + inline-edit modes plus a `+ Add widget` button. Fields: Name, Widget type (gauge / line / table), MIB (uploaded MIBs only — std MIBs rejected at save with a clear toast since the asset-side collector needs an enumerable symbol directory), Symbol type (scalar/table — **widgets do NOT support double_scalar** because the renderer has no combiner support), Symbol (filtered picker driven by Type), Transform (unary only), Model regex (optional per-asset gate), Order, plus a per-widget-type **Display options** sub-form (gauge: min/max/unit/warning-at; line: unit; table: no options — renderer derives columns from the latest sample). Shadow stores `_mfgWidgetEditMib` / `_mfgWidgetEditType` / `_mfgWidgetEditWidgetType` keep the dependent pickers live before save. **Every chained-select handler re-renders the whole tab, so none of them may call `renderIdentificationTab()` bare** — the rebuild comes from STORED state and would discard whatever the operator has typed. Synchronous handlers go through `_mfgRerenderPreserving(el)` (snapshot the triggering row/card's live controls → re-render → write them back, keyed on the same identity the shadow stores use). The MIB pick ALSO kicks off the async `_ensureMibSymbols` fetch, whose completion re-renders again *after* that restore from a callback holding no element — so it uses `_mfgRerenderPreservingAll()` (snapshot/restore every open editor). Without it the Name came back and then vanished a few hundred ms later on every first pick of a MIB, warm-cache picks looking fine — pinned by `tests/unit/manufacturerProfileFormPreserve.test.ts`, whose async cases fail against a bare re-render. Backend: `POST/PUT/DELETE /server-settings/manufacturer-profiles/:id/widgets[/:widgetId]`. Read path on assets: `GET /assets/:id/custom-widgets` (fetched up front in the asset-modal parallel `auxResults` pass and rendered synchronously via `_customMibTabHTML`; the **Custom MIB** tab is pushed onto the tab set only when the payload has at least one widget, so it never flashes-then-vanishes for manufacturers with no custom widgets — mirrors the SD-WAN tab's prefetch-then-conditional pattern). Samples populate on the next telemetry cadence tick via `collectAndRecordCustomWidgets`.
- Server Settings → **Identification** also has a **Manufacturer Aliases** card (admin-only) — sits between OUI Overrides and the OUI Database card. Lists every alias grouped by canonical name (table columns: Alias, Canonical, Edit/Del). Add form is a two-input row: Alias (the input string to rewrite) + Canonical (the stored value) + Add button. Edit opens a small `openModal` dialog; delete uses `showConfirm`. Every save refreshes the in-memory cache and runs the existing-row backfill in the background, so the change propagates to historical Asset/MibFile rows without a restart. The card also handles the underlying problem the OUI database creates: IEEE registers vendors under their legal name (`Fortinet, Inc.`) while discovery code stamps the marketing name (`Fortinet`), and without normalization they show up as two distinct values in every manufacturer dropdown, MIB scope picker, and vendor profile match.
- Server Settings → **Maintenance** tab (formerly "Database") groups everything operational: the Capacity Advisor card on top, then the Sample Retention card, then capacity grading, in-app updates, database engine info, storage breakdown, backups, restore, and backup history. The **Capacity Advisor** card shows per-lever current vs recommended for connection-pool sizes, monitor worker counts, queue mode, and PostgreSQL tuning settings; each lever has a per-row checkbox + a single **Stage selected** button that writes the chosen env-driven values to `.env` (restart-required) and routes the QUEUE_MODE lever through the existing `POST /queue-mode` endpoint. Advisory-only rows (`PG_MAX_CONNECTIONS` and PostgreSQL settings) have no checkbox because they require a PostgreSQL restart Polaris can't trigger. Cold-start badges appear next to cadence-driven rows while the `polaris_monitor_work_duration_seconds` histogram is still filling. The **Sample Retention** card holds the 27-input grid for `Setting("sampleRetention")` — 3 streams (Response time / CPU+memory+temperature / Interfaces+storage+IPsec) × 3 tiers (Detail / Hourly avg / Daily avg) × 3 classes (Default / Switches / Access points). Defaults 7/30/365; values are days, 0 means "keep forever for that cell". Save + Restore-defaults buttons; out-of-range values (≥3651 or negative) are blocked client-side. Takes effect on the next nightly prune and on the next chart history request (5-second cache TTL on reads). A successful Save opens a "When will the database shrink?" explainer modal (`_showRetentionPruneInfoModal` in `public/js/server-settings.js`) describing the 24-hour retention-prune cadence, whole-chunk drops vs row-delete residue, and when on-disk size actually steps down. Below the advisor + retention cards, the **Database** card carries the status pill (`Healthy` / `Action recommended` / `Critical`) plus a list of capacity reasons with suggestions, then four side-by-side stat cards: App host (cpu/ram/disk + DB co-located flag), Database (current size, steady-state size, sample-table breakdown with dead-tuple % per table), Database engine + connection pool, and Monitoring workload (monitored asset count, monitored interface count, cadences, retention). The legacy `pg_tuning_needed` inline current→recommended rows have moved into the advisor card; the `pg_tuning_needed` reason itself still surfaces in the reasons list pointing at the advisor. The legacy `pgboss_recommended` / `pgboss_overdue` / `pgboss_pending` reasons and their inline "Enable on next restart" / "Cancel" buttons were absorbed into the advisor's QUEUE_MODE lever and no longer fire. When `capacity` is unavailable (e.g. statfs unsupported), the Database card degrades to a plain "Database" header with just the engine+pool sub-card so operators don't lose connection visibility. Driven by `GET /server-settings/capacity-advisor` (replaces the prior `/pg-tuning` fetch as the Maintenance tab data source — `/pg-tuning` stays as the source for the sidebar critical-alert check in `app.js`). Back-compat: `?tab=database` deep links automatically map to `?tab=maintenance`. The sidebar on every page shows a non-dismissible **red** alert when capacity severity is critical; amber / watch reasons are card-only — there's no sidebar nag for them.

Everything below moved out of CLAUDE.md's Frontend section — CLAUDE.md keeps the page
inventory, the shared-module list and the conventions; the per-surface detail lives here.

### SPA shell, navigation, and the assets page

Vanilla JavaScript SPA served from `/public/`. No build step — plain ES modules. Multi-page layout with client-side navigation (`app.js` — every sidebar entry whose page can 403 carries a permission gate, `perm: [key, level]` or `anyPerm: [[key, level], …]` for a multi-key page like IPAM, kept in lockstep with `pageRequiredPermission` in `src/app.ts` which bounces a typed URL for the same page; an ungated entry advertises a page whose first list fetch is the only thing telling the operator they can't be there), **three themes in two families** (`morning` / `noon` daylight, `nightfall` dark; the retired `dark`/`light` ids are recognized nowhere, and any surface picking art or a palette by brightness branches on `isLightTheme()` rather than on an id), an **account menu** behind the page-header user badge (`openUserMenu` in app.js, built on the shared `showRowMenu`: Web Push enrollment, **two-factor (TOTP) enrollment** for local accounts, Logout — these used to sit at the bottom of the sidebar, where per-account actions competed with navigation. The theme control went WITH them and then back, and now lives at the sidebar bottom below Server Settings and above the version line (`btn-theme-toggle` in `renderNav`, repainted by `_setTheme`). Since the three-theme cutover it is a PICKER, not a toggle: it is labelled with the CURRENT theme and opens the full list through `openThemeMenu` → `showRowMenu` (past two themes a two-way switch makes the third reachable only by cycling past one you didn't want). `_setTheme` fires a `themechange` CustomEvent on `document` carrying `{theme, family}` — anything that cached colors at render time (Leaflet basemaps, Cytoscape stylesheets, canvases, the brand art) listens for that rather than hooking the control. The 2FA row is the same permission-mismatch fix push enrollment was: `/auth/totp/*` is self-service for any logged-in local account, but the UI lived only on the admin-gated /users.html, so an ordinary local user could never configure their own second factor. `wireTotpState` caches `GET /auth/totp/status` once per page load and `_totpMenuItem` derives the row — omitted for every non-`local` `authProvider` (the enroll route refuses those outright, so the menu can’t offer a control the server will reject) and labeled off the state: "Set up two-factor auth" / "Finish two-factor setup" (a minted-but-unconfirmed secret) / "Disable two-factor auth". The enroll / confirm / backup-code / disable modals live in the SHARED `public/js/totp-self.js` (`window.PolarisTotpSelf`), which users.js now delegates to instead of holding its own copy), real-time discovery polling, bulk operations, PDF/CSV export, conflict resolution slide-over, first-run setup wizard, Device Map (`public/map.html`, nav- and page-gated `deviceMap:read`) with a read-only **Show regions** toggle — ungated beyond viewing the map, unlike Edit regions, because how an install's regions NEST is not privileged information: it paints the region polygons read-only (fill opacity held low because nesting stacks it, a permanent label only on the outermost ring of a nested set) and its HOVER renders the containment tree, each row badged with its derived level. It reads `GET /map/region-overlay`, which lives under the `deviceMap:read` mount for exactly that reason, and it reuses `#topology-edge-tooltip` as the page's shared hover tip. The two region layers hand off rather than stack (`regionViewState` is deliberately NOT a field on `regionState`, whose teardown nulls its own layer): entering edit mode hides the overlay and disables the button, leaving edit mode restores it and DROPS the memoized payload, since an edit can have changed every level in the tree. Everything decidable lives in `public/js/region-tree.js` (`window.PolarisRegionTree` — `summaryLine` / `childrenOf` / `buildTreeHtml` / `warningsHtml` / `paintOrder` / `overlayStyle` / `attachTreeTooltip`, the last taking the tooltip surface as an injected `{show, move, hide}` so the hover logic is testable without a map), because `map.js` is one IIFE with no exports that nothing can test. Plus edit-regions polygon mode (topology modal: drag layouts persist server-side per (site, view) via `TopologyLayout` for `deviceMap` writers — shared across operators, localStorage fallback for readers — plus a per-user Snap-to-grid chip that lands drags on the column solver's 130×95 lattice and re-snaps all positions on enable; the toolbar also carries a read-only **“My regions” strip** left of Edit regions — the signed-in operator’s own effective region scope as colored pills, each tooltipped with where that scope comes from (their account, their role, else an IdP group), with an empty scope stated as “all regions” since empty means unrestricted. It answers “which regions am I assigned to?”, which the Users page could only tell whoever administers users, and is deliberately NOT a filter — the map already shows exactly the sites the viewer may read. Pill colors come from the shared `public/js/region-pills.js` (`window.PolarisRegionPills`), the one browser-side reader of the region catalogue, which users.js also delegates to so a region can’t render two colors on two pages), **Application Map** (`public/appmap.html` + `appmap.js`, nav-gated `applicationMap:read`): a Cytoscape connectivity graph of mapped traffic — compound asset boxes containing process child nodes (purple, `Asset.mappedProcesses`) and service child nodes (teal, `Asset.mappedServices`, matched on the connection row's owning `unit`; both render even with zero connections), grey /24-grouped unknown-IP nodes (named from the IP registry, or via reverse DNS for public IPs — `ipNameSource` reservation/dns), per-port-labeled edges (child nodes also render their listening ports as a second label line, so a service that listens but has no observed peers still reads as collected rather than empty; edge ports carry the observed `ips` — the edge rail's "Via IP" column, and same-asset sibling edges get a `via <ip>` label line plus a wider child-stack gap with connected siblings ordered adjacent so the intra-asset edge is actually readable); two-pass layout (headless dagre over the collapsed asset-level graph, process/service children stacked under their parent — the `isChildNode` helper handles both kinds uniformly across the layout/filter passes), a **Seen within** range built from the server's configured `appMapConnections` retention window (so its widest option states the real window instead of a hardcoded 7 days) + Hide-external and Hide-workstations toggles + a **token/pill filter box** (typeahead over the current payload — protocol / port / host / device type / process / service / external IP, plus free text; Enter turns a suggestion into a pill, pills combine **OR within a kind and AND across kinds**, `×`/Backspace removes; the pure `applyGraphFilter` core is exposed on `window.PolarisAppMap` and unit-tested), a **Fade stale** toggle (dims connections unseen for 15 min — render-only, the edge is never removed; default on), a **Screenshot** button (composites `cy.png()` for the canvas graph with an html-to-image capture of the info rail, so the listening-port list is IN the image; clipboard then download fallback), listening ports consolidated into ranges (the pure `consolidatePorts` — runs of ≥3 collapse to `tcp/9000-9004`, a pair stays listed since "9000, 9001" reads better, protocols never merge), 60s auto-refresh (positions preserved), shared drag layout via `ApplicationMapLayout` for `applicationMap` writers (localStorage fallback for readers), a stacked toolbar (filter box + **Saved** menu on top, applied pills in their own row below — a long filter set can't squeeze the typing area, and the row collapses when empty — then the Seen-within/Hide-external/Hide-workstations/Fade-stale controls with the status + action icons right-aligned; Saved = named pill sets in `polaris-prefs-appmap-filters-<username>`, pills only — recalling one must not move the operator's time window, and it REPLACES rather than merges), per-user toolbar state (`polaris-prefs-appmap-<username>`: range / hide-external / hide-workstations / legend / pills), `#focus=asset:<id>` deep link (adds an asset pill so the narrowing is visible and clearable), an empty state that points at the **discovery rules** card and the per-asset Services tab (the map page's Discovery button was removed when the rules list moved), a legend (asset box / lilac process / teal service / external), **tap-any-node → info rail only** (the asset-details slide-in opens from the rail's *Open asset details* button alone — `openViewModal`, no navigation off the map; tapping a box used to pop it, which buried the services/ports list the operator had just opened) and a pointer-hover highlight that brings the edge under the cursor to full opacity (stale edges render at 0.35 — the `.appmap-hover` class, since Cytoscape has no `:hover` selector); processes/services are opted in per-asset via the Services-tab **Map** checkbox (pin column beside Monitor → `Asset.mappedProcesses` / `Asset.mappedServices`) and the process detail slide-in gains a **Ports & Connections** section, five-state Status pill with click-to-toggle (an unmonitored pill instead opens the edit modal on the Monitoring tab so the operator sets the polling method before enabling — table and System-tab pills alike; the disable direction still confirms inline), asset details modal (General + System + Services + Quarantine + Events + SNMP Walk + Sources tabs, in that order — Sources last; SNMP Walk only for admins AND only when at least one monitoring stream resolves to SNMP for the asset (`_assetUsesSnmpPolling` over the prefetched `/effective-monitor-settings`, plus a per-asset `customWidgetPolling="snmp"` check; fail-open on fetch error); the **ARP Table** tab (firewall-class only) renders the gate's layer-3 neighbour cache — the L3 sibling of the switch-only MAC Table tab, grouped interface-first the same way, but headed by a **range selector** (Current / 1h / 12h / 24h / 7d / 30d, each option past the configured retention disabled rather than hidden so the operator can see it exists and is not being kept), a filter box over IP / MAC / interface / matched hostname (the question that brings an operator here is a lookup, not a survey), and a **disclaimer stating this device's actual poll cadence** and that each read is a snapshot of a cache the gate ages out in ~1–5 minutes, so short-lived entries can be missing entirely and an absent address was not necessarily absent from the network.
