A historical range adds a per-row Last seen column, which Current omits because every row shares one instant; the **Services** tab is a merged unit + process inventory — systemd units / Windows services with state (read-only; Start/Stop/Restart control was removed in the Satellite-posture change), an *Include processes* checkbox folds in the per-program process inventory into the same table, two pin columns — Monitor (combined: a service's journal tailing → `monitoredServices`, or a process's CPU/RAM history + logs → `monitoredProcesses`; one checkbox per row) and Map (both), no Alert column since Automations handle alerting, hidden on Fortinet infra (firewall/switch/access_point) and on the `other` catch-all type — none of them report a unit list or a host process table); the **Alerts** tab (gated `alerts:read`) lists this asset's active alerts above the automations whose scope matches it — and **the tab itself strobes** in the colour of the worst of them (`_paintAssetAlertsTabStrobe`, painted from the alerts the tab just loaded rather than a second payload, so it is right on first render and settles on the next acknowledge or clear with no page refresh; it moves only while something is unacknowledged, and an empty list clears the marking outright). Same signal, same `--color-sev-*` vocabulary and same "handled stops moving" rule as the Assets list's own indicator: a strobing dot to the right of the hostname in the **Name** column (`assetAlertDotHTML`, off the list payload's `activeAlert`), so the operator who opened the slide-over from a strobing row can see which tab it was about. The animation lives in styles.css (`.alert-strobe-*`) and `prefers-reduced-motion` drops both to the steady rendering — the title text carries the whole message, since neither colour nor motion reaches every reader. The active table is **[select] | Time | Severity | Detail | Message | Actions**, headed by a count and scrolling under a frozen header (`.table-wrapper-modal-sticky` at a self-set `max-height` — no JS sizer runs inside a slide-over). **Detail is `Notification.dimension`** — the interface / sensor / mount the alert was raised for — and it is what makes the list readable at all: a per-interface automation on a switch that loses its uplink raises one alert per pinned port, same minute, same message template, so without it the operator gets two dozen rows that differ in nothing (the metric rides the cell's `title`, since it repeats down the whole column). Equal timestamps order by dimension NUMERICALLY (port2 before port10). **Actions** holds an **Acknowledge** button on an unacknowledged row (`alerts:write`; the first in-app caller `api.alerts.acknowledge` ever had) whose note is collected by a Polaris **modal** (`_promptAckNote` → the shared `showPrompt`, the `_promptQuarantineReason` pattern) rather than `window.prompt` — the browser box is unstyled, dead in the installed PWA, suppressed outright by some browsers, and cannot mark a field required, which `requireAckNote` needs. The question ("What is the problem and what is the fix?") is a **placeholder, never a value**, so an untouched box submits as no note at all; the field is marked required, and refused when empty with a reason rather than a silent red border, on a row whose automation demands one (`data-note-required` rides the button and the row's checkbox, so the bulk dialog can demand it when ANY selected alert does) or the name of whoever did it and when, plus a **Clear** button beside either (`alerts:fullwrite`, `showConfirm`-guarded since clearing ends the alert, runs the automation's reset actions and stops escalation). The same two verbs run over a **multi-select** (per-row checkboxes + a select-all, an idle-until-selected `.bulk-bar`) in ONE request each, because closing out one outage row-by-row is a dozen prompts and a dozen confirms; the note is prompted once for the batch (the route takes one shared note by design) and the confirm names the count. The selection column renders only for a viewer who can act on it, and the empty-state colspan is derived from the same shape resolver so it can't drift. Every action toast reports the **server's** count (`{acknowledged}` / `{cleared}`), so a no-op says "already cleared" instead of a success toast over nothing — the acknowledge route skips already-acknowledged rows, and on a table of identical rows a silent no-op is indistinguishable from a broken button. The bulk buttons + select-all live in the tab shell rather than the re-rendered tbody, so `_wireAssetAlertSelection` clone-replaces them before binding (every action reloads the tab; a naive re-wire would fire N batches on the Nth click) — that second table is **Name | Trigger | Scope**, where Trigger is the automation's plain-English trigger sentence (the same one at the top of the edit modal, every severity tier included, which is why there's no separate Severity column) and the name opens the automation in the edit wizard in place for operators with `automationManagement:fullwrite`. That's why `automations-wizard.js` now loads on every page that loads `assets.js` — it owns its own builder catalogs and needs no `automations.js`, and a page without it degrades to the old trigger-type badge + a non-clickable name), multi-asset Compare slide-over (bulk-bar → metric picker → overlaid telemetry charts), a bulk-bar **Merge** button (admin, shown only when exactly two assets are selected — opens the Sources-tab merge modal with the target pre-selected, skipping its search step) and a bulk-bar **Deploy Agent** button (`data-manage-assets` — one modal collects SSH + WinRM credentials + arch, POSTs `/assets/bulk-agent-install`; per-asset OS/transport resolved server-side, ineligible assets returned as skips with reasons) and a bulk-bar **Maintenance** button (`data-maintenance-mgmt` — opens the same Maintenance modal the toolbar button opens with the selection pinned as the schedule's explicit `assetIds`, i.e. the named/one-time-or-recurring counterpart to the status pill's single-asset ad-hoc window; nothing is created until Save, and a selection past the route's 500-id cap is refused with the count rather than 400-ing after the form is filled in), **back/forward history on the asset details slide-over** (‹ / › in the header plus Alt+Left / Alt+Right — a dependency-tree row, an HA peer, an LLDP neighbour, a MAC-table match and the Application Map rail all pivot the OPEN panel to another asset in place, so the pair is what returns the operator to the device they started from; the stack lives for ONE panel session (closing resets it), a re-open of the CURRENT asset is a REFRESH rather than a visit — `openViewModal(sameId)` is the footer Refresh button, every post-save re-render and the monitor-pill flip — a walk deliberately doesn't push, and opening from mid-history drops the forward tail like a browser; the pair hides itself until there is somewhere to go, `_assetHistoryOpen` / `_assetHistoryTarget` / `_assetHistoryLabel` in assets.js are pure and unit-tested), per-user lock toggle on every modal/slide-over (locked = backdrop click won't dismiss; a locked slide-over also survives an affordance that would otherwise close it to open something else — the asset panel's Edit button keeps the panel pinned and lets the edit modal stack over it, refreshing the panel after save), Server Settings (Credentials / Identification / Maintenance tabs). The **Add Asset** form cross-references the IP as it's typed (`public/js/assets-ipcontext.js`, `window.PolarisIpContext`, create-only): a debounced `GET /assets/ip-context` fills a panel under the IP/MAC row with the containing network, the gate the address sits behind and why that gate is believed (its ARP table resolved it / it serves the network's DHCP / a device was sighted behind it), the lease or reservation already on it (phrased from `sourceType` AND `dhcpBinding` together — "In use by a managed FortiAP … the gate leases it dynamically"), the switch port its MAC was learned on, and — first, and warn-coloured — any asset that already carries it as a PRIMARY IP, which is a duplicate about to be created. A "Use these details" button fills MAC / hostname / location / coordinates, but only into fields the operator has left blank, and coordinates only as a complete pair (`getAssetFormData` refuses a half-filled one). It reports; it never writes. A section the caller's role can't read renders "Not shown" rather than "none found". Assets-page **view tabs** (`public/js/assets-tabs.js`): a strip above the bulk bar where each tab holds its own filter+sort state, persisted per user (`UserTableTabs`) so it follows the operator across browsers. Click switches (applies that tab's state + re-fetches), double-click/F2 renames inline, ✕ closes (never the last one), + adds; a saved preset can be opened straight into a **new tab** from the Filters menu. assets.js awaits `PolarisAssetTabs.init()` before its first fetch so the page loads once. Assets-page toolbar: a **"Filters ▾"** dropdown (`public/js/assets-filters.js`) that saves the table's current column filters + sort as a named preset, loads one back (into the current tab or a new one), and deletes them — presets are server-side (`SavedTableFilter`) so they follow the operator across browsers and a **public** one is offered to every user who can read the page (private is the default; publishing needs `assets:write`, deleting someone else's `assets:fullwrite`), one merged "Import / Export ▾" dropdown (per-item `data-manage-assets` gating on the import entries), a merged "Settings" modal of `<hr>`-stacked sections (Asset Lifecycle + **Sources** + Manual Monitoring + Class Overrides + **Mass Pinning** — the old standalone Asset Settings modal was folded in; an outer tab strip was tried and reverted 2026-08-20 on operator preference, so don't re-tab it without asking. **Sources** is the drag-to-reorder learned-location priority list, business rule 22 — grip rows reusing `.aw-grip` + the `.aw-drop-before/after` edge cues, labels and "what this contributes" hints rendered from the server catalogue so a new source kind needs no client change, plus the `<integration name>:<fortigate name>` prefix toggle. **Mass Pinning** (`public/js/assets-masspin.js`, `window.PolarisMassPin`) is the manual way to pin AND UNPIN interfaces / IPsec tunnels / storage mounts across many devices at once — the subtractive counterpart to the integrations auto-monitor pass, which is additive-only by design: it mounts the SHARED `PolarisConditionBuilder` over the automations device vocabulary, lists the matched assets' inventory aggregated by name with TRI-STATE checkboxes (checked = pinned on every reporting device, partial = some) expandable to per-device checkboxes, and STAGES edits — a Map of diffs vs the server state, so staging a value back to the server's deletes the key — until one Apply. The aggregate-row click cycle is explicit because an indeterminate box reports `checked === false`: not-all-pinned → pin on all, fully-checked → unpin on all. `_monsetActiveTab` preserves the open tab across the re-render an override delete triggers), and a "Maintenance" button (`data-maintenance-mgmt`) opening the three-tab schedules modal in `public/js/assets-maintenance.js` (Create Schedule with live device-list preview / Schedules list / **Calendar** — a month grid of every schedule's occurrences, expanded server-side by `GET /maintenance-schedules/occurrences` because the recurrence engine is server-local wall-clock and a browser in another timezone would paint them on the wrong days; a day cell opens the editor prefilled with a one-time window on that date, a chip opens its schedule for edit; `openMaintenanceModal({assetIds})` is the bulk-bar entry, pinning a selection through the same explicit-assetIds channel an edited schedule's pins ride). The monitor status pill gains a purple "Maintenance" state; its popover offers "enter maintenance mode until…" (creates an ad-hoc one-shot schedule) or "end maintenance now", on both the table and the slide-over System tab. All asset-detail SVG charts render labeled translucent maintenance bands over window gaps (`_maintenanceBandLayer`, fed once per panel open from `/assets/:id/maintenance-windows`). A chart may additionally **shade its line by automation severity** — the per-sensor hardware chart does: the line + dots fade through warning / serious / critical (a vertical user-space SVG gradient) wherever the reading enters a tier of an automation watching that metric on that asset, severity bands included, with dashed labeled reference lines at each in-range threshold. The ladder is computed SERVER-side by `GET /assets/:id/metric-thresholds` (`notificationRuleService.getMetricSeverityTiers`, off the engine's own `resolveTierLadder`) so shading can't disagree with what fires; the pure gradient math is `public/js/chart-severity.js` (`window.PolarisChartSeverity`, thresholds outside the visible range clamp rather than widening the axis) and the SVG assembly is `_severityChartLayer` in assets.js, which returns the flat accent stroke when no automation watches the metric.

### Service & Process Discovery Rules (Integrations → Polaris Agent)

**Service & Process Discovery Rules** (Integrations → **Polaris Agent** tab, the card above the agent-build card; `public/js/appmap-discovery.js` renders the inline list via `window.PolarisDiscoveryRules.init`, `public/js/appmap-rules-wizard.js` is the builder — both load on integrations.html now, not appmap.html): named rules that pin process/service items on the assets they select, now AND on assets discovered later via the `reconcileAppMapAutoMap` job; several rules' pins union per asset. Each rule has a **mode** — *Monitor + map* (Application Map + telemetry; mapping implies monitoring) or *Monitor only* (per-program CPU/RAM + logs, per-unit journal tailing; never touches map pins) — chosen on step 1 of the 4-step wizard (name → devices → items → summary, `openAutomationWizard` idiom, shared `.stepper` CSS). The device step is a flat `TagCriteria` builder (ported from the maintenance criteria UI with `apr-` prefixed ids — NOT the automations condition tree, which can't round-trip through `normalizeCriteria`), and the item step is **scope-driven**: it lists only what the selected devices report (services-only by default, with a running selected count), which is what keeps a rule from pinning a unit on every host that happens to run it. Rules only ever target `PROCESS_CAPABLE_ASSET_TYPES` (workstation + server) since nothing else reports an inventory. **Auto rules:** ticking Monitor/Map on an asset's Services tab mints a single-item `source:"auto"` rule targeting just that asset (`scope:null` + explicit `assetIds`); pinning the same item on another asset consolidates into the existing auto rule, un-ticking removes the asset (an auto rule losing its last asset is deleted), manual rules are never consolidated, and editing an auto rule in the wizard converts it to manual. Auto rules wear an "Auto" badge; the Devices column renders their hostnames via the GET's `assetLabels`. **Mapping implies monitoring, one-way:** every item a map-mode rule maps is also pinned for monitoring (note the log volume that implies); monitoring never implies mapping, so nothing writes a map pin from a monitor pin — computed against the full want-set, so an item mapped before this behaviour existed catches up on the next reconcile. Removing an item or disabling/deleting a rule stops future auto-pinning; a separate *Unmap everywhere* action does the actual strip.

### SSH Deployment (Integrations → Polaris Agent)

**SSH Deployment** (Integrations → **Polaris Agent** tab, the card below the agent-build card; `public/js/agent-ssh-onboarding.js` renders it via `window.PolarisAgentSshOnboarding.init`, lazy-mounted by integrations.js alongside the other two cards). Polaris generates the ed25519 keypair used to install the agent on Windows over OpenSSH, owns the `ssh` Credential holding it ("Windows SSH (Polaris-managed)" — selectable in the normal Install Agent / bulk-deploy pickers), and emits the PowerShell that authorizes the public half across the fleet. Routes live under `/server-settings/agents/windows-ssh*` (the agent-build card's UI-on-Integrations / routes-on-serverSettings split); `POST /generate` carries a **chained gate** — `serverSettingsSystem:fullwrite` AND `credentials:write` — since it mints a fleet-wide admin credential. The private half is sealed at rest and **never returned by any read path** (the VAPID posture; no escrow — recovery is regenerate + re-run the script, which is why the script is idempotent), while `SshConfig.publicKey` is deliberately non-secret so the script can be re-rendered without rotating the key. Account settings are **per platform** (`windows` / `linux` blocks in the Setting; `polarisServerIp` is shared), and Polaris maintains **one managed credential per platform** carrying the same keypair — a Credential holds one username and a Windows `DOMAIN\user` is meaningless on Linux. Two scripts come out **per platform**: **remediation** (installs the OpenSSH Server capability, starts sshd, optionally creates the local admin account, appends the key to `%ProgramData%\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys` with the Administrators+SYSTEM ACL sshd demands, optionally scopes inbound TCP/22) and **detection** (exit 0 = onboarded, 1 = remediate) — pairing them under an Intune Remediation or SCCM Configuration Baseline is what makes rollout self-healing, since a plain platform script runs once per device and never retries. Both share one key-presence predicate so they can't disagree. The **Linux** pair differs where the platform does: the key goes in the user's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` (700/600, correctly owned) with a `restorecon` for SELinux, and the script installs a **NOPASSWD sudoers drop-in** — `visudo -cf`-validated before install, since a bad one locks sudo out for everyone — because the agent installer runs `sudo -n`, so key auth alone cannot install an agent. It deliberately does not install `openssh-server`. Linux detection also checks the account + drop-in, unlike Windows. The scripts are **delivery-neutral and fleet-generic** (no machine-specific values; `administrators_authorized_keys` is one group-wide file), so the same body runs under Intune / GPO startup / SCCM / Arc / RMM / a one-off `Invoke-Command` — worth knowing that Intune does not manage traditional Windows Server, so the Servers class needs GPO/SCCM/Arc regardless. Operator input (`username`, `polarisServerIp`) is **rejected, not escaped**: it lands in a script an admin runs fleet-wide as SYSTEM. See `sshOnboardingScript.ts` / `windowsSshOnboardingService.ts` in [TOUCHES.md](TOUCHES.md).

### Script publishing (Intune + Azure Arc)

**Script publishing** (the SSH Deployment card's Publish pane + a *Script Publishing* tab on the Entra and Azure Arc integrations). Delivers the generated onboarding scripts instead of the operator downloading and uploading them. Both vehicles are **opt-in per integration, off by default** (`EntraIdConfig.publishToIntune` / `AzureArcConfig.allowRunCommand`), because each needs a vendor-side grant the read-only discovery credential deliberately lacks — the tab renders the setup steps and the cost of the grant inline. **Intune** (`intunePublishService`, Windows only) upserts a Remediation by displayName and **never calls `/assign`**: assignment is the human review gate for a script granting fleet-wide administrative SSH, and it is test-pinned. The Graph API version is probed (v1.0 then beta) since `deviceHealthScripts` has historically been beta-only — a 404 means wrong version, a 403 means the endpoint exists and permission is missing. **Azure Arc** (`arcPublishService` → `azureArcService.dispatchRunCommand`, Windows AND Linux, the only vehicle reaching Linux or Windows Server) runs the script via Run Command. Arc has **no inert state** — a run command executes on creation — so the review gate is explicit target selection: no 'all machines' affordance, ids re-resolved against the live roster, 200-target cap, and an undeterminable OS is skipped rather than guessed. Its grant is an Azure **RBAC role assignment** (`Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines/runCommands/write`), NOT a Graph permission. Both routes live under `/server-settings/agents/script-publish/*` behind a chained **fullwrite on BOTH** `serverSettingsSystem` and `integrations` — `integrations:write` is the blanket gate on that whole router and must not confer tenant writes. See `intunePublishService.ts` / `arcPublishService.ts` in [TOUCHES.md](TOUCHES.md).

### Automations page and the 6-step wizard

**Address Book tab** (`public/js/automations-address-book.js`): the People pane is paginated and searched SERVER-side (`GET /contacts?q=&origin=&limit=`), so a synced GAL cannot make opening the page cost the whole table, and its "showing N of M" hint reads the unpaged `total` rather than inferring truncation from a full-looking array. A directory-synced row (`origin !== "manual"`) badges as its backend through the existing `sourceBadge` vocabulary, shows "Directory sync" in Added by, falls back to `jobTitle — department` when it has no description of its own (derived at RENDER time, never stored — writing it would put it in the operator-owned description column where the next sync would look like it had overwritten their text), and offers **Adopt** in place of Edit/Delete: a delete would be undone on the next run, so the honest verb is the one that takes ownership. Adopt needs `contacts:fullwrite`, which falls out of the existing gate with no special case because synced rows carry `createdBy = null`. **Automations page** (`public/automations.html` + `public/js/automations.js`): tabs **Automations**, **Delivery**, **Scripts** and **Address Book** (`public/js/automations-address-book.js`, visible with `contacts:read` — the SAME two panes the wizard's recipient picker opens: **People** (searched — contacts ∪ Polaris accounts ∪ the opted-in directory, 250 ms debounce, source badge per row) and **Tags** (browsed, read-only — every tag an automation can route to, and the users each reaches. Two sources, built by the shared `tagRoutingEntries(schema)` and deliberately kept apart because they match differently at fire time: map regions from `options.regions`, which route through `recipientRegions` → `resolveUsersByRegions` (`User.regionTags` ONLY), then the tag registry from `options.tagCatalog`, which routes through `recipientTags` → `resolveRecipientUsers` (the flattened region ∪ other scope). Every row reads `<name> Users`, because what is being picked is the people, not the label; the Source badge is what tells a Region from a Tag. Regions keep their derived **Level** — L1 is an innermost region and each level above contains the one below, read from `schema.options.regionLevels.byName` on the same payload, so the list says which rows are local teams and which are the divisions over them; a region the catalogue couldn't level, and every registry tag, shows an em dash, never "L1", which would be a claim about how the map is drawn. Renamed from **Regions** in 2026-08, when the registry joined it), minus the selection checkboxes and the Add-to-To/Cc/Bcc footer, which only mean something while composing a Notify action. Before 2026-08 the tab listed stored contacts alone, so the page an operator opens to ask "who can Polaris email?" answered a narrower question than the modal did. Both surfaces paint through ONE renderer — `abTable(cols, entries, hint)` over the shared `AB_CELLS` name/email/description/source cells — and differ only in columns: the tab adds **Devices** / **Added by** / Edit+Delete on People and **Level** on Tags, the picker a checkbox and one Edit. The tab's contacts come from `GET /contacts` rather than out of the search payload, for two things a search entry can't carry: the row's `createdBy` + device filter (the two extra columns, and the per-row ownership check behind the buttons), and completeness — `searchAddressBook` caps at 50 deduped hits ordered users-first, so on an install with more than 50 accounts the contacts would fall off the end of the very page that manages them. A search hit whose address a contact already holds is dropped, so one mailbox stays one row. The shell is built once and only the panes reload, since rebuilding it would blur the search box mid-keystroke; the term survives a Refresh or a save. Edit/Delete render only on the rows the caller may touch, per the ownership dimension, and a table filled with nothing but user accounts still says "no contacts yet" rather than letting a populated list read as a configured address book; "+ Add contact" and the row Edit open the editor: email / name / description plus the optional **device filter** — the SAME nested AND/OR condition builder the automation wizard's Devices step uses (`window.PolarisConditionBuilder`) over the wider `DEVICE_FILTER` vocabulary from `GET /contacts/filter-schema`, behind the wizard's own control: an **"All devices" checkbox, default CHECKED**, unchecking reveals the builder with a seeded starter row. One difference in what an EMPTY builder means — for an automation that's a validation error (a rule must select something to be worth saving), for a contact it's simply "no filter", i.e. only the pinned devices, which is the address-only state most contacts are in. Reached by removing the seeded row; a row left blank is still refused with the builder's own "give every condition a value". A legacy blob the tree can't express (an `integration` rule) is flagged in the dialog and posted back untouched rather than replaced by whatever the empty builder collects — a pinned-device picker, and a debounced live "devices covered right now" preview against `POST /contacts/preview`. The same module exposes `openPicker({field})`, the address-book picker the wizard's recipient fields open — two panes, **People** (the typeahead over users ∪ contacts ∪ the opted-in directory) and **Regions** (one row per map region, catalogue riding the `filter-schema` payload). Where regions are NESTED the Regions pane additionally offers one **Asset's L\<n\> Region Users** entry per asset-relative level (`regionDynamicEntries(maxLevel)`, depth read from `schema.options.regionLevels.maxLevel`) — L1 reaches the local team, L2 whoever covers the division. Offered ONLY once `maxLevel >= 2`: on a flat catalogue "L1 Region Users" is a synonym for the all-levels entry, and offering it would invite a rule that quietly changes meaning the day someone draws a containing polygon. In the wizard these become `deviceRegionLevel` pills whose VALUE is the level (unlike the other dynamic kinds, which are flags keyed by kind, so several levels can coexist on one action); a stored level deeper than the catalogue still nests renders as an **unknown** pill rather than being dropped, the same contract as an unknown user or role. A collapsed Notify row now also names who it reaches (`notifySuffix` — "Notify via Email — L2 region users"), because the pairing this feature exists for is two notify actions on the SAME channel and they read identically otherwise. The two dynamic entries head the pane matching what they RESOLVE to — **Asset's Responsible Contacts** tops People (they're people out of this very address book), **Asset's Region Users** tops Regions — and each sits above the results rather than in them, because neither is a search hit: a query matching nobody must still leave the standing "whoever owns the device" option on screen. Both panes stay in the DOM and selection is keyed by address-or-`source|id`, so a People selection survives a look at Regions; the Add-to-To/Cc/Bcc buttons return every picked entry with its `source`, and the wizard maps that to a pill kind. **Both surfaces build their own standalone overlay** (picker z-index 1300, editor 1320) rather than calling `openModal`, which reuses ONE shared `#modal-overlay` and would destroy the wizard's form DOM underneath — the `showConfirm` / `_showMergeReviewModal` pattern, but restoring focus and trapping Tab, the two things `_showMergeReviewModal` drops, and carrying the app-wide modal lock — `buildOverlay` calls app.js's `_ensureLockButton` itself, since that injector's MutationObserver only ever watches the shared `#modal-overlay`). Tab detail — **Automations** (default; list + enable toggle. The terse **Scope** column was replaced (2026-08) by four PROSE columns — **Devices / Trigger / Reset / Actions** — each holding that part of the automation in the builder's own words, so two automations can be told apart without opening either. Trigger and Reset come from the shared `PolarisAutomationSentences` factory the wizard renders its own steps from (a second phrasing here is how the list and the editor would come to describe one automation differently); Devices is `devicesSummary` (the condition tree spelled out, "All devices", or a pre-builder rule's flat dimensions) and Actions is the same `actionsTooltipText` tally, in-app alert first since every automation has one, with escalation tiers counted across all four places a chain can live. A fifth column, **Addresses** (2026-08), answers the question those four cannot: WHO an automation actually reaches. The cell is the flat deduped address list, so the filter answers "every automation that mails Jane"; the hover breaks it down by where each recipient is declared — the base notification, each severity band, each escalation tier (per-action chains named apart from the rule-level one), the all-clear and the reset — with the delivery channel on each group. The walk is `PolarisAutomationRecipients.ruleRecipientGroups` in automations-wizard.js, so it lives beside the recipient vocabulary the editor uses and mirrors the server’s `allRuleActionRefs` order; the three catalogues it resolves against (users, roles, channels) are fetched lazily from the list and only when a rule names one, since `/automations/scope-options` (the only role source a non-`users:read` caller has) is the page’s most expensive read. A chat/webhook channel posts to its own destination, so its action’s recipient fields are shown as the channel rather than as people who would never receive it. The sentences are stripped to PLAIN TEXT (`plainText`) because TableSF filters and sorts on the cell's string — markup left in would match a search for "strong" and sort as tags — which is also what makes "every automation that emails" answerable from the list. Each cell repeats its full text as the `title`, since the columns are resizable and the sentences are long. The narrow trigger-type column stays as **Type** (same `data-sf-key`, so stored sort/filter prefs survive): it filters by trigger kind, which prose can't. The row `title` (`_scopeTooltip`) keeps both halves and now shares `devicesSummary`, so hover and cell can't disagree. The list itself is a standard Polaris list table: per-column sort + inline filters (TableSF), resizable/hideable columns (`setupColumnLayout`), a frozen header with the body scrolling inside `.table-wrapper-sticky`, and centered pagination with a right-aligned "Show N" selector via `renderPageControls`. The row’s verbs are **not** an Actions column: clicking an automation’s **name** opens a context menu (`showRowMenu` in app.js — Edit / Clone / Delete; UI-CANON.md → “Row context menu”), and below `automationManagement:fullwrite` the name renders as plain text instead. **Clone** opens the wizard pre-filled from the row and saves as a CREATE, named `<name> (copy)` (uniquified against the list, an existing copy suffix stripped rather than nested) and **created disabled** — business rule 18 makes two same-signature automations at the same scope rank both fire, so an identical enabled clone would double-alert the matched fleet; step 1 says so, since the wizard has no enabled control. Sort, filters, column widths/visibility and page size persist per user under the `automations` `PolarisPrefs` key and are restored BEFORE the first render, so the initial paint carries the operator's setup instead of flashing defaults. Paging is client-side — the list endpoint returns every rule, so TableSF filters the full set and only the page slice is rendered), **Delivery** (channel registry), and **Scripts** (the AutomationScript registry — card list + add/edit modal + server-side Test run that polls `/automations/scripts/runs/:id` for exit code/output; tab visible with `automationScripts:read`, CUD/test at fullwrite; every surface carries the human-review warning). Create/edit opens the **6-step wizard** in `public/js/automations-wizard.js` (`openAutomationWizard`): 1 name/description only — plus, when CREATING, an **"Import from file…"** control (`automationManagement:fullwrite`; never offered while editing, where replacing the open automation would be a data-loss trap). Import reads the file in the BROWSER (`FileReader`, no upload route, no multer) and reopens the wizard in a new `import` mode layered onto the clone path (`importing || clone` — detached deep copy, saved as a CREATE, `visited = 6`, excluded from the draft stash), so it saves through the ordinary `POST /automations` and the server's `ruleInputSchema` + `assertActionRefs` stay the authority. **The FILE'S NAME becomes the automation's name**, and an import is **always created disabled** whatever the file says (business rule 18: two same-signature automations at the same scope rank both fire). A step-1 banner lists the file's declared **dependencies** as present / missing / can't-tell against this install and names which later steps need attention — Actions always, since an exported file carries no delivery wiring (severity + enabled removed from this step — severity now leads the trigger step, enabled is managed from the list toggle), 2 device filtering — a default-checked **"All assets" checkbox**; unchecking reveals the nested CONDITION BUILDER (root group with AND / OR / NONE / NOT-ALL combinators, rows of field+operator+value with a click-to-suggest combobox fed by `GET /automations/scope-options` + the asset-type registry + tag list, nested sub-groups ≤5 deep, **drag-and-drop** via grip handles — `PolarisConditionBuilder.wireDnD` in the shared `public/js/condition-builder.js`, dashboard tab-grip pattern — moves conditions between groups and groups into groups with a depth-cap check): stored as `scope.condition`, evaluated by the shared `evaluateScopeCondition`; unchecked+empty is a validation error (never silently all-assets); debounced matched-device preview, 3 trigger conditions — **led by severity**: a **"Use multiple severity levels" checkbox** (`#aw-multi-sev`) sits above the Alert severity control. Single mode = one **Alert severity** dropdown (`#aw-trigger-severity`, sets `rule.severity`); on select, the step heading + the conditions group border are **accent-colored to the severity** (`applySevAccent`, palette mirrors `.sev-select`). Device/Polaris-host categories use the **same AND/OR tree builder** (leaf rows = metric or device-state conditions with agg/dims — a condition row has **no window box**: the step's single **"Sustained for (minutes)"** field is the trigger's one time knob, and it means the **measurement window** for an aggregated condition (`avg` / `median` / `min` / `max` — `tgStampWindows` stamps it into every aggregated leaf's `windowSec` and zeroes `forDurationSec`, since the reading already covers the period) or the **sustain clock** for a `latest` one (`windowSec` 0, minutes → `forDurationSec`). For a **windowed-ratio metric** (packet loss) that same field is instead relabeled **History (minutes)** — mandatory, default 15, range 5..1440 — the aggregation control is hidden, and a SEPARATE optional **Sustained for** field (`#tf-sustain-min` → `forDurationSec`, ratio-only, hidden otherwise) carries the hold on top of the window; severity tiers keep their own hold boxes like any other numeric metric (business rule 29c). It is therefore mandatory exactly when an aggregation is chosen — red asterisk + "this is the period the value is measured over" note, toggled live by `syncDurationRequirement`, and refused at save (`tgValidateLeaf`) rather than silently measured over the engine's default lookback; and/or only, ≤3 deep / ≤10 leaves; 1 leaf saves as the legacy single trigger via the client+server collapse, 2+ as a per-asset composite; event/change keep flat fields; live sentence + "Test against current data" — the sentence at the top of the step names EVERY severity the condition can raise, not just tier 0 (`triggerSentence(trigger, {severity, severityBands})` in the pure factory `window.PolarisAutomationSentences`: "…at or above 80 % — warning at this level, serious at or above 90 %, critical at or above 95 % for 5 minutes", a band printing its own sustained-for only when it overrides the base). Directly under it sits the same trigger as a **formula** (`triggerFormula(trigger, {severity, severityBands})` in the same factory → `{lines, note}`, rendered monospace in `.aw-formula`), which exists because the step's ONE "Sustained for (minutes)" field means two different things and prose reads them alike: the formula puts a MEASUREMENT window INSIDE the term (`median(Hardware sensor[class="temperature"], 15m) >= 65 °C`) and a HOLD clock OUTSIDE it (`latest(CPU usage) > 90 %  held 10m  ⇒ warning`), stacks severity bands as blank-padded lines aligned under the shared term, renders a composite one condition per line with the tree-wide hold on its own line, reads min/max over a 0/1 flag as `all(…)`/`any(…)`, and returns NO lines for event/change (they compute no value, so their English sentence is already exact). Its `note` carries the one place the wizard overstates precision: the engine fetches `max(windowSec, 15 min)` of samples and reduces every row it fetched (`SAMPLING_FLOOR_SEC`), so a window under 15 minutes is really measured over 15 — the formula prints the CONFIGURED window and says so rather than quietly substituting either number. Also a metric's **dimensionFilter inputs are pickers, not free text** — populated from `POST /automations/dimension-values` with what the draft's own devices report, as a select for the closed enum (`sensorClass`) and, for the substring-matched ones (`sensorNamePattern` — pick ONE named sensor like "CPU ON-DIE Temperature" out of a firewall's dozen, narrowed to the class already chosen — plus interfaces / mounts / health-checks / members / tunnels / hostnames), the `.aw-combo-dim` **combobox** the Devices step already uses: click opens everything the scoped devices report with per-value device counts, typing filters by substring (case-insensitively, mirroring the engine's `dimensionSubstringMatch`), ArrowUp/Down + Enter pick, and a **match cue** beside the field says whether what's typed actually selects anything — "✓ matches 2 of 14 reported hardware sensors" / "✓ exact match", or a warning that it "matches none … would never fire", because the dimension is a free-text PATTERN the server can't reject, so a typo used to save cleanly and then silently never match. (A datalist was tried first and confirmed nothing — see UI-CANON.md → "Don't use `<datalist>`".) **Filter rows** (2026-08): the "+ Condition" select also offers **Device identifier** (Hostname / IP address / MAC address / Manufacturer / Model — `deviceFilterDimensions` on `/schema`, valid on EVERY asset metric/state leaf) and **Component name** (Interface name / IPsec tunnel name / Storage mount / SD-WAN rule name — the last narrows `sdwanRuleStatus`/`sdwanSelectedMember` to the named rule via `sdwanRulePattern`) entries, rendered as "`<what>` matches `<value>`" rows with the same picker combobox. **The stored rule never carries a filter row**: `tgFilterCompile` folds each into its AND-group's condition leaves as `dimensionFilter` at save (nested groups included, deeper values win; an OR-group placement or a filter no sibling condition can take is a validation error), and `tgFilterLift` re-derives the rows on edit (a dimension uniform across a group's supporting leaves lifts to the topmost AND group; differing values stay as inline leftover inputs on the leaf — the only time those liftable dims render inline). The engine narrows the ASSET SET via `applyDeviceFilters` (`deviceFilterMatch` in notificationTypes — hostname/manufacturer/model substring; **IP is CIDR / octet-boundary-prefix / exact, never bare substring; MAC is separator-insensitive**, both mirrored client-side for the match cue), which is what lets ONE composite automation mix device-specific branches ("interface wan1 down on CORE-SW OR storage /backup full on BACKUP-01"); identifiers ride `triggerSignature`, so same-metric rules with different device filters never carve each other out, and `getMetricSeverityTiers` skips a rule whose device filter excludes the charted asset. Metric-integral dims (sensor class/name, health-check/member, probe/row, widget) stay inline on the condition row as before. Also a warning note when the selected devices report none of that dimension, i.e. the condition could never match; a stored value the devices no longer report is kept and flagged rather than silently widened to "any". A **0/1 state metric** (`schema.booleanMetrics`, today just `customStateValue`) renders differently throughout: the threshold box becomes a **select of the chosen probe's own two labels** ("Alarm" / "OK" — `tgStateFlagControl`, still carrying `.tgl-threshold` so the saved trigger stays a plain `== 1` numeric comparison and needs no engine special case), the comparator select is narrowed to is / is-not, the aggregation to `latest` / `max` / `min` worded as "current state" / "at any point in" / "throughout", the `stateProbeId` dimension is a NAME select (values are registry UUIDs — the picker's optional `label`), and changing the probe re-renders the row so the value control relabels. The sentence reads "Hardware sensor alarm is Alarm on rows matching TMP1"; severity bands and hysteresis are hidden and server-rejected, since a ladder or a dead band over two values means nothing). Multi mode (only for a single numeric metric; `syncSeverityMode` + `injectBaseSeverity`) hides the standalone dropdown and instead injects a **base severity select into the condition group header** (before the AND/OR select) + a **"+ Severity"** button into the group's button row (next to +Condition/+Group), accent-coloring the group border. The BASE tier's block takes the same layout as the added ones — including its own fold chevron (`t3:base`; keyed on "base" rather than the severity, since unlike a band this block IS the automation's own severity and re-picking it must not read as a different block). Its foldable parts are marked IN PLACE with `.aw-collapse-part` rather than wrapped in a `.aw-collapse-body`, because `tgCollectGroup` walks `:scope > .scg-children` — moving that into a wrapper breaks collection the same way relocating the combinator did. Also: severity alone on the header line with the remove **×** right-aligned, and the AND/OR combinator wrapped onto the line below (`flex-basis:100%` + `order`, NOT moved out of the header — `tgCollectGroup` reads it as `:scope > div > .scg-op`, so relocating the select makes trigger collection throw, which silently breaks both Next and the tier mirroring). That × is the single condition's own remove button, proxied into the header by `syncBaseTierRemove`, which keeps exactly one on screen: the header's while the base holds one condition (the only shape multi-severity mode allows, since every tier mirrors one metric), each row's own once there are several to tell apart. **"+ Severity"** appends another accent-colored **condition-group block** (tier) below: a severity header + a locked-metric condition row (metric + aggregation **shared** with the base (the window rides the base tier's duration field) — greyed; only the **operator** + **value** are editable, `band.operator` persisted when it differs) + its own "+ Severity". The step-5 severity sections open **folded** (`data-collapse-default="closed"`, seeded once by `wireCollapsibles` — a key absent from `_awCollapsed` means "never touched", so an operator's expand survives every later re-render). Step 3's tiers stay open by contrast: their content is the condition being edited, not a list to skim. **Action ROWS fold too, closed by default** (`foldActionRow`): a per-severity ladder is three or four action lists deep, each row carrying a channel picker, To/Cc/Bcc, an email body and an escalation footer, so expanded the step is unreadable — and the row's `.aw-action-summary` already says what it does, which makes it the collapsed state. State lives on the ELEMENT rather than in the keyed map, because an action has no stable identity to key on (rows are positional; removing one shifts the rest) and closed-by-default leaves nothing to restore. A row the operator ADDS opens (you don't create an action to read its summary), as does one rebuilt by changing its type mid-edit. **Every severity block folds** (`data-collapse-key` + `.aw-collapse-head` / `.aw-collapse-body`, wired by the shared `wireCollapsibles`): the step-3 tier blocks and, in per-severity mode, each step-5 actions section including the base. A four-tier automation is otherwise four condition groups plus four action lists to scroll past. Fold state lives in a module map keyed by **severity** (`t3:critical`, `t5:base`) rather than on the element, because step 5 rebuilds its sections from the draft on every toggle and step 3 re-renders when the base sampling changes — and keyed by severity rather than index so removing a tier can't slide another tier's state onto it (re-picking a severity re-keys, carrying the state with the tier). Everything opens expanded on a fresh wizard; a folded block keeps a summary line so it still says what it does — the tier's own operator/threshold/hold read off its controls, and for an actions section the count, so "no actions of its own" (the state that falls back to the base actions) is visible without unfolding. A step-3 tier block is severity + the locked-metric condition + its **own "Sustained for (minutes)"** (`.band-duration` → `band.forDurationSec`; a new tier inherits the base's current value so adding one changes nothing until edited) — its **actions live on the Actions step** (per-severity sections; the band's actions/escalation ride a stash on the band DOM row so re-collecting either step can't strip them). In multi mode the BASE tier's `#tf-duration-min` is **moved inside the base condition group** (`injectBaseSeverity`, node move not re-render so the typed value survives), since a rule-wide-looking field sitting between accent-colored tiers reads as applying to all of them. A new tier defaults one rank above the previous, severities are enforced **strictly increasing** (client + `validateSeverityBands`), and the "+ Severity" buttons hide once the top severity (or 4 tiers) is reached (`syncBandAddButtons`); the per-automation notify policy shows once a tier exists — **increase/decrease only**: the band-level **Resolved** control was retired (2026-08) because recovery is announced by the rule's reset actions ("When this resets", which every automation has, banded or not) and the engine ran BOTH — `fireResolved` for the band, then `fireReset` from `recover()` — so a banded automation with reset actions told people twice. The wizard now writes `onResolved: false` EXPLICITLY (the server defaults it true, so omitting it would keep the duplicate) and retires the policy on the DRAFT at load rather than only when step 3 renders, since an edit saved from step 1 never runs that collector. What the old policy announced is adopted into the reset actions when they are empty — `dedicated` contributes its own `resolvedActions` verbatim, `reuse` the trigger's notify actions (which is what "reuse the alert's actions" resolved to) — and an operator who already wrote reset actions is left alone. `bandNotify.onResolved`/`resolvedMode`/`resolvedActions` remain in the schema and the engine still honours them on rules this wizard has not re-saved. Tiers **share the base sampling** (aggregation/window/dimensionFilter) — only severity/threshold/operator/sustained-for vary, 4 reset conditions — default-checked **"Reset when the trigger is no longer true"**, whose sentence says what that MEANS rather than restating it: the trigger's own clause rendered INVERTED through the same phrase builder (`invertedLeaf` → `tgLeafPhrase`), so "CPU usage (avg over 5 minutes) is at or below 90 %", at the hysteresis clear threshold when one is set. A 0/1 metric flips the VALUE instead of the comparator ("Hardware sensor alarm is OK", not "is not Alarm" — a state to look for, not a double negative), and a composite falls back to a generic clause since a tree stops being satisfied in as many ways as it has branches. Two caveats are spelled out because they can't be read off the clause (`resetCaveat`): a **monitor-status** alert clears at the FIRST successful probe, when the status reads `recovering` — not when it is back `up`, which is the difference between "answered once" and "healthy again"; and a numeric alert with no clear threshold resets at the very value that raised it, so a reading on the line can re-alert (the dead-band control is on that same step) (= auto, with hysteresis + clear-sustain extras for single numeric triggers); unchecking reveals **Custom conditions** first, then timed / manual. Custom conditions is the same AND/OR tree builder the trigger step uses (→ reset mode `condition`, with a sustain input + a cooldown nudge) and is offered on EVERY trigger with a continuous condition, not just composites — **seeded with the trigger inverted** (`invertedTree`, De Morgan for a tree; severity bands ignored, since every tier recovers at tier 0), so unchecking the box lands on the editable spelling of what the box did rather than on "manually only". A stored condition is kept verbatim and never re-seeded; one written in the wrong kind (the trigger was switched device↔host on step 3) is dropped and re-seeded rather than left for the operator to hand-fix. Reset leaves carry no window control of their own and inherit the trigger's measurement window (`triggerWindowSec` → `tgStampWindows` in `collectStep4`) — a second minutes field beside "must stay true for" is exactly the window-vs-hold confusion business rule 29c removed, and without the inheritance an aggregated reset leaf was refused by a message naming a field that isn't on the step. A per-dimension trigger additionally gets a note saying whether a reset condition clears one alert or all of them (business rule 32). An **event/change** trigger has nothing to invert and so gets no auto checkbox and no tree; its radios are **When a matching event arrives** (→ `reset.mode="event"`, `#aw-reset-ev-action` / `#aw-reset-ev-restype`, prefilled from the catalog's `resetEventSuggestions` — `agent.disconnected` → `agent.connected` — and a NEW draft with a known counterpart lands on that mode rather than on the four-hour timer that used to be the default) then timed / manual. The **re-notify cooldown left this step in 2026-08** for the Actions step's in-app card (`#aw-cooldown-min`), where it sits with the other two properties of the alert RECORD (`requireAckNote`, `repeat`) — it governs how often a NEW alert may fire and does nothing to one already up, so on the reset step it read as part of how an alert clears (business rule 32), 5 actions — led by the mandatory **in-app card** `#aw-inapp-card` ("Create an in-app alert (always happens)"). **Escalation is PER SEVERITY, not per action** (2026-08): the base actions section hosts the rule-level `escalation` — which is exactly the chain the engine resolves for an alert sitting at the base severity — and each per-severity section hosts its band's own. It used to sit on the in-app card (not about the alert record) and on every action ROW, where "if this stays unhandled, do more" read as "if this email goes unanswered" while the one chain actually fired for the whole tier. A stored per-action chain is **hoisted and MERGED** into its severity's chain on draft load (`hoistActionEscalations`): tiers concatenate and sort by `afterMin`, so since each tier carries its own actions the deliveries and their timings are unchanged; the level's `stopOn` wins when it has one, and the action-level chains are stripped so the sweep can't fire both. Per-action `escalation` stays in the schema and `allRuleActionRefs` still walks it, so a rule this wizard hasn't re-saved keeps working. It covers the ALERT only: the audit Event moved OUT into a removable **"Create an Event"** action row in the list below (present by default, no config, no escalation footer, and flagged as a no-op on event/change triggers). The card stays mandatory because every delivery row, the escalation sweep, acknowledge/clear and the state machine key on `Notification.id`: not removable, hosts the **alert/event message template** (`#aw-msg`, moved here from the trigger step), the **"Require a note when acknowledging"** checkbox (`#aw-require-ack-note` → `requireAckNote`; it belongs to the ALERT record, not to any one delivery, which is why it sits here and not on a Notify row) AND the alert's **"Escalate if unhandled" chain** (= the rule-level `escalation`, so pre-redesign rules render with no migration). Below it, action rows (unified: notify with per-action email composition — **"Customize the email" is a CHECKBOX**, not a disclosure: the question is whether this action sends the default alert email or a bespoke one, and unchecked stores NO templates at all, so the action keeps tracking the shared default (including later changes to it) instead of freezing a copy. The fields stay prefilled from that default so ticking the box shows the real text to edit; un-ticking clears nothing, it just stops collecting. Inside, **Body is ONE editor with a Plain text / HTML view switch**: both bodies are still stored and both are still sent (a mail client picks the part it renders, and the default template ships both), so the toggle only chooses what's on screen — the old "Send an HTML body" checkbox is gone, since a blank HTML template already fell back to the default HTML and the checkbox never controlled delivery. The **token palette is visible in both modes** rather than behind a second disclosure, and `wireTokenPalette` is idempotent so an action row added later gets its chips wired / api_call with headers editor + credential-name warning / script from the registry, gated on `automationScripts`) — notify recipients on an EMAIL channel are **To / Cc / Bcc token fields** (`.na-recip-box`; pills reuse the shared `.tag-chip`, the typeahead reuses `.aw-suggest` and merges TWO halves — **the dynamic recipients, roles and map regions resolve LOCALLY** (`dynamicSuggestions` / `roleSuggestions` / `regionSuggestions`) and paint on the first keystroke: roles and regions from the `/automations/scope-options` catalogues the wizard already holds, the dynamic entries from `PolarisAddressBook.dynamicEntries(maxLevel)` — the SAME list heading the picker's two panes, since a second copy would drift. They are **To-only** (mirroring `pillAllowedInField` — offering one into Cc would look like it worked and then send to nobody), badge as `dynamic`, and match through `recipNeedle`, which folds both apostrophes: the entries are written “Asset’s …” and nobody types a typographic apostrophe, so before that fold typing the obvious `asset's` matched nothing and the feature read as picker-only. Then users / contacts / directory hits from the debounced `GET /contacts/search` are appended, so the local half still works for a caller without `contacts:read` and never waits on a round trip; typing a region name is therefore a first-class way to reach one, not just the picker's Regions tab. Enter/comma commits, Backspace on an empty input removes the last pill, and a pill **drags between the three fields** — a cross-container move via the `application/x-polaris-recipient` dataTransfer MIME type, scoped to one action's `.na-recips` so a pill can't jump into another Notify action; a typed address not already in the book gets a "save to address book" affordance, and an **Address book** button opens the picker). Cc/Bcc were promoted OUT of the "Customize the email..." disclosure (which keeps subject/body only) and now carry user ids as well as raw addresses — `emailRecipientsSchema` always allowed both, the old comma-separated inputs just could not produce them; storage is unchanged (`emailComposition.cc/bcc`), so stored rules need no migration. **Web Push mirrors the email field: ONE To box of the same pills** (`recipBoxHtml(..., "push")`, `data-mode="push"` on the box) and no Cc/Bcc — a push is delivered per endpoint, so a “copy” is just another recipient. The recipient VOCABULARY is the same minus what has no subscription behind it: `PUSH_PILL_KINDS` admits user / role / region / tag / the two region-dynamic kinds and refuses `address` and `assetContacts`, matching `usersForTarget`, which ignores both on the web_push transport — so a typed address is refused with a toast at the box rather than accepted and dropped at delivery, and the `/contacts/search` half of the typeahead is narrowed to `source=="user"`. What the retired account multi-select must keep doing is SAY WHO IS UNREACHABLE (push is opt-in per BROWSER, so a named user with no enrolled device is a recipient that silently receives nothing): each suggested account is badged with its device count, the warning under the field names the unreachable ones and recomputes from the pills on every edit, and the **address-book picker opened from a push box runs in push mode** — a “Push devices” column (`none` in warning colour), no checkbox on rows push cannot reach, no Responsible-Contacts entry and no “+ New contact”, and a To-only footer. Counts ride INTO the picker from the wizard (`openPicker({mode:"push", pushDevices})`), which already holds them on the `/automations/recipient-users` payload, so the picker needs no endpoint of its own. Above the field sit two BROADCAST toggles — **"Send to All Users"** (`recipientAllUsers`) and **"Send to All User Regions"** (`recipientAllRegions`), both **checked by default on a NEW action** (an operator decision; a STORED action reflects what was saved, so an old rule listing three people can't silently become fleet-wide on the next edit). Unchecking the first reveals the account list; unchecking the second reveals a region-chip picker (`recipientRegions`, bare names, catalogue from `GET /automations/scope-options` rather than the `mapRegions:read`-gated `/map/regions`). While "All Users" is on the region controls are DISABLED with a note, and a resolved-count line keeps the default honest. **`recipientAllUsers` and `recipientAllRegions` are Web-Push-only and rejected at rule save on any other channel type** (they're broadcasts, and the builder offers them nowhere else); `recipientRegions` is NOT — naming specific regions became a recipient TOKEN offered on every routed channel, so an email rule holding one is a state the builder renders and can edit back out, which was the whole reason for the old restriction. A **role token** is a third pill kind alongside people and addresses: `recipientRoles` routes to every user holding that Role, so "notify the NOC" survives a staffing change with no automation edit. Stored as role **IDs** — a rename must never silently reroute an alert — with the catalogue on `GET /automations/scope-options` (like regions, because `GET /roles` is gated `roles:read`); a deleted role survives as a flagged unknown pill rather than vanishing on the next save. Roles resolve to USERS, so they work on email and Web Push alike (on push they are the same role pill, the chip picker having been retired with the multi-select) and in Cc/Bcc as well as To. **Level-scoped device regions.** `recipientDeviceRegionLevels: number[]` routes to the users tagged with the triggering asset's regions at chosen **asset-relative** levels — 1 = the device's own innermost region, 2 = the division containing it, walked outward along the containment edges by `regionHierarchyService.deviceRegionsAtLevels`. It is an INDEPENDENT union source, not a modifier: `recipientDeviceRegion` keeps meaning "every region the asset carries, any level", so no stored rule changes meaning and the two can sit on different actions — region users on the trigger, L2 users on the escalation, which is what the feature exists for. It matches `regionSet` (region tags only) rather than `recipientDeviceRegion`'s flattened `matchSet`, because these names come from the map-region catalogue by construction; that asymmetry is deliberate and recorded in TOUCHES.md — unifying them would change who existing rules deliver to. Levels are capped at `MAX_DEVICE_REGION_LEVELS` (8) and the live nesting depth rides `listScopeOptions().regionLevels.maxLevel`, so the pickers offer level entries only once something is actually nested. **The field must be threaded through BOTH `actionsToTargets` and `targetsToNotifyActions`** — every notify action is round-tripped through the legacy `DeliveryTarget` shape before `expandDeliveries` sees it, so omitting either line leaves a field that validates, persists, renders in the wizard and routes to nobody. **Region and dynamic pills.** A `region:` pill (`recipientRegions`) reaches every user tagged with that map region and works in To/Cc/Bcc like a role — `emailRecipientsSchema` carries `recipientRegions` for exactly that reason, and `resolveEmailRecipients` resolves it through `resolveUsersByRegions`. Two **dynamic** pills name no address but a RULE for finding one from the TRIGGERING device: **"Asset's Region Users"** (`recipientDeviceRegion`) and **"Asset's Responsible Contacts"** (`recipientAssetContacts`, email transports only). Both were checkboxes sitting under the recipient fields, which asked "who gets this alert?" in two places at once and left the To field looking empty when the answer was "whoever owns the box"; they're now added from the address-book picker's **Regions** tab and read in the same list as everyone else. They are **To-only** — the wire shape has no per-field slot for them (they're flags on the ACTION, while Cc/Bcc are `EmailRecipients` lists) and the expander folds contact addresses into the To owner map, so a Cc drop would look like it worked and send to nobody; the drag shows no drop cue for a field that would refuse it. **The device-region CHECKBOX is gone from Web Push too** — it is a To pill there as well, the push box having gained the token field it lacked; asset contacts stay email-only, enforced by the box's kind list rather than by a second control. The legacy scope-region checkbox still renders only on actions already carrying it. Validation rejects a **Cc/Bcc-only** action — `expandDeliveries` skips a target whose resolved To list is empty, so it would look configured and silently never send — and **every action row carries its own "Escalate if unhandled" footer** (`action.escalation`; tier-hosted rows never do — no chains inside chains). With multiple severity levels, per-tier actions are **opt-in behind a `#aw-band-actions-multi` checkbox** ("Use different actions for each severity level", mirroring step 3's multi-severity toggle): OFF (the default, and what a stored rule shows unless some band actually carries its own actions) = one action list that runs at every severity, per-tier sections hidden and stripped from the payload (`payloadBands`) so the server's empty-band fallback does the work; ON renders **one accent-colored actions section per tier** (base + each band → `severityBands[].actions`). Toggling re-renders the step from the draft, and the draft keeps per-tier rows either way, so an accidental un-tick doesn't destroy typed actions before save, 6 **Summary** — an **Export** and a **View code** button on the Summary card (also on the list row menu; both `automationManagement:read`, the code editor's Save `fullwrite`), then a **Test delivery** block (gated `automationManagement:fullwrite`, omitted entirely otherwise) offering one button per distinct delivery the draft would perform — **Send Test Web Push** / **Send Test Email** / **Send Test &lt;channel type&gt;** (slack/teams/pushbullet) / **Write a Test Event**, deduped by channel across base actions, band actions, escalation tiers, resolved and reset actions, with `api_call`/`script` never offered because the server refuses to run them from a button. Each press creates a REAL `[TEST]` alert (`Notification.testRun`, `ruleId` ALWAYS null) and dispatches that one action immediately via `POST /automations/test-delivery`. **Every button sends to the configuring operator and nobody else** — a server-side recipient rewrite, not a flag — and since 2026-08 there is no mode to choose: the radio pair and its real-recipients confirmation are gone, so this step cannot page anyone. The block names the address and push-device count the test will land on, runs one test in flight at a time, and prints a per-target inline result line beside the toast. The webhook kinds have no private form (one Slack post reaches the whole channel), so their buttons are DISABLED here with a pointer to the Delivery tab's per-channel Test button, where the reach is what an operator expects. Plus the review grid (message template, per-severity action lines, chain/tier counts, severity-bands line) + "Devices this automation affects" (live scope+trigger preview, first 100 + total — headlined by `totalAssets` (DISTINCT devices) with `totalEvaluated` (readings) spelled out separately, since a per-dimension metric evaluates one reading per sensor/interface/mount and rows repeat the hostname; each row names its dimension so those rows are tellable apart — with a **specificity indicator** and the bidirectional **carve-out warning** — which lower-rank automations this one removes devices from, and which of its devices a more-specific automation already covers). Asset ID is no longer offered as a condition-builder field. Stepper CSS is shared in styles.css (UI-CANON.md → "Wizard (stepper modal)"); free navigation to visited steps; all steps unlocked in edit mode; unsaved new-automation drafts stash in memory with a restore prompt. The list's enable toggle resends the full record in v2 shape (`reset`+`actions`) so it can't strip the wizard's fields.$

### Automation export / import / view code

**Export / import / view code** (`public/js/automations-portability.js`, `window.PolarisAutomationPortability`; loaded after the wizard on all five pages that carry it). One automation travels as a `.automation.json` file whose **`dependencies` block comes first**, because that is what a human opening the file reads: everything install-specific is STRIPPED from the rule and recorded there by NAME instead (delivery channels, registry scripts, state probes, custom roles / regions / tags, pinned devices), so the file is portable and — the security half — carries no ids and **no secrets**: dropping api_call actions is what keeps an `api_call.headers` bearer token, stored unmasked by design, out of a file operators email and commit. It also means an imported file can never name a `script` action, so the RCE surface is untouched and `automationScripts:fullwrite` is never involved. **Export and "View code" are deliberately different serializations**: export is portable, the code editor is FULL fidelity (ids and headers included) because an edit there must round-trip losslessly onto the same automation, and it says so. Three traps the module exists to hold, each pinned by a test: (a) the top-level `actions` list is emitted **explicitly** as `[{type:"event"}]` — the server re-injects the audit Event only for `actions === undefined`, which `_awDraftFromRule` never produces (it coerces absent to `[]`), so omitting would save a rule that writes a Notification row, and therefore looks like it fired, while logging nothing; (b) an empty `scope` is never emitted — `{}` means MATCH NOTHING to the engine's `scopeWhere` while `step2Html` renders it with **"All assets" checked** and `validateStep2` calls it valid, so a scope that strips to nothing becomes an empty CONDITION TREE, which `validateStep2` does refuse (note `{}` and `{condition:{op:"and",children:[]}}` are OPPOSITES server-side, and an emptied nested group is REMOVED from its parent rather than kept, an empty AND group being true for every asset); (c) `dimensionFilter.stateProbeId` / `.widgetId` are optional and the engine applies them only when present, so blanking one **widens** the trigger from one PSU-alarm probe to every state probe on the device — it is recorded as a dependency AND `tgValidateLeaf` now refuses to save a `customStateValue` / `customWidgetValue` leaf without it (a latent builder bug fixed in passing). The code editor's own hazard is that **PUT is a full replace**: `normalizeRuleInputCore` maps an absent nullable JSON column to `null` and `jsonOrClear` turns that into `DbNull`, while `enabled` / `severity` / `reset` fall back to SCHEMA DEFAULTS — so deleting `enabled` takes a disabled automation live. It therefore renders the complete body, strips the legacy mirror (`targets` / `clearBehavior` / `clearAfterSec`: leaving `targets` in lets a deleted `actions` be silently rebuilt from it, losing per-action escalation and script/api_call actions), says that removing a key removes the setting, and confirms a diff of the destructive fields with the dangerous ones called out.

### Dash wallboard

**Dash wallboard** (`public/dash.html`): an unauthenticated, read-only duplicate of the Dashboard at `/dash`, served by its own process (`POLARIS_ROLE=dash`, `src/dash/dashServer.ts`) for NOC wallboards/kiosks. Default-off; enable toggle + source-IP scope on Server Settings → **Web Server** → Dash Wallboard. `dashConfig.ipScope` is `rfc1918` (RFC1918+loopback, default) / `all` / `custom` (an operator-entered IPv4-CIDR allow-list in `allowedCidrs`). **Unauthorized source IPs are silently dropped** (socket destroyed, no HTTP response) rather than 403'd, so a scanner can't confirm the surface exists — behind nginx that manifests to the remote client as a 502. Answers as the built-in `readonly` role (widgets the role can't read hide themselves via `PolarisWidgets.getAllowed()`); layout persists per-browser in localStorage (`polaris-dash-layout`); page flags in `dash-mode.js` (`POLARIS_DASH_LOCAL`, `__polarisApiBase=/dash/api/v1`) + slim boot `dash-boot.js` replace `app.js`. Keep dash.html's widget script list in lockstep with index.html.

### Mobile PWA and Web Push

**Mobile PWA** (`public/mobile.html` + `public/js/mobile/*` + `public/css/mobile.css`): the phone SPA is an **installable PWA with push notifications**. Phones hitting `/` or `/index.html` are UA-redirected to it (`src/app.ts`, `?desktop=1` escapes); `/mobile.html` itself stays out of `protectedPages` so an installed app cold-starts into the in-app mobile login rather than a chrome-less desktop `/login.html`. That exemption also skips the **“Skip login page”** redirect app.ts applies to protected pages, so `renderLogin` in `public/js/mobile/auth.js` enforces the setting itself — the choke point every local login goes through (boot, the api.js 401 hook, Cancel out of TOTP) reads `skipLoginPage` off `GET /auth/azure/config` and redirects SAML-then-OIDC, falling through to the form when neither provider resolves. An explicit Sign out spends a one-shot `sessionStorage` marker (`PolarisAuth.markSignedOut`, set by more-tab.js) to draw the form once, since a silent `prompt=none` provider would otherwise sign the operator straight back in — the desktop gets this for free by landing logout on the unprotected `/login.html`. **Install identity is mobile-only** — `/manifest.webmanifest` is generated per-install from branding by `src/api/routes/pwa.ts` (`start_url=/mobile.html`, `id=/mobile.html` — never change it, it keys the install; `scope="/"` so the "Desktop view" link, `/login.html`, and push deep links don't eject the standalone window), with icons rasterized from the operator's logo by `appIconService`. Desktop pages deliberately carry **no** manifest link. The manifest + icon routes are **unauthenticated**: a `<link rel="manifest">` without `crossorigin` is fetched with credentials omitted, so a gated manifest 401s for everyone. Standalone layout needs the `@media (display-mode: standalone)` safe-area insets on `.app` in `mobile.css` — with `viewport-fit=cover` + `black-translucent` there's no browser chrome, and the existing asset-sheet/snackbar anchors (`calc(var(--navbar-h) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`) already assume the navbar sits above the inset. **Push:** the More tab's Notifications row is a **preference**, not a switch — it names the account's current choice (Email / Push / both) and opens a bottom sheet with the three options; the second half of its supporting line is about THIS phone (“tap to allow push on this phone”, “blocked in your browser settings”), because the preference can be perfectly saved and still reach nothing here. The load-bearing state is **iOS-outside-standalone** — Apple grants Web Push only to a home-screen-installed app, but `"PushManager" in window` is true in plain Safari from 16.4, so the line says "Add to Home Screen to receive push here" and CHOOSING a push-bearing preference routes to `#more/install` and saves nothing, rather than prompting for something that always throws (a preference this phone cannot honour, chosen on this phone, is a promise Polaris would break). **Alerts reach the phone in four places.** The Assets tab flags a device that has live ones — a strobing **Alerts** control beside the hostname, coloured by the worst active alert and going steady once everything on it is acknowledged, off the `activeAlert` summary the list payload already carries (so no extra request per card, and no extra query per row — see `activeAlertSummaryByAsset`). Tapping it opens the **per-asset alerts sheet** (`PolarisMobileAlerts.openForAsset` in [public/js/mobile/alerts.js](public/js/mobile/alerts.js)) over `GET /assets/:id/alerts`, which is the mobile counterpart of the desktop slide-over's Alerts tab: one card per active alert with Acknowledge at `alerts:write` (per row, plus one batched control for the whole device) and **Clear at `alerts:fullwrite`** — the phone's first clear, previously desktop-only. The sheet hands its recomputed summary back through `onSummary`, so the flag on the card behind it settles without a list re-fetch and the last alert being cleared stops the strobe. That module also owns the mobile severity vocabulary (`--md-sev-*` tokens in mobile.css, ranked the way `ALERT_SEVERITY_RANK` ranks them) and the two sheet-based prompts — the acknowledge note and the clear confirm — because `window.prompt`/`confirm` are suppressed in some installed PWAs. The **asset detail sheet** carries the same flag on its hero, beside the monitor pill (the two together are how the device is doing), loaded by its own `GET /assets/:id/alerts` because `activeAlert` is enriched onto the LIST payload only and the sheet opens from places that never went through the list — a search hit, a push deep link, a pasted `#asset/<id>`. **Search results** carry the same statement reduced to a dot (`dotHTML`, deliberately not a tap target — the row opens the device): `SearchHit.alert` is stamped by `withAlertSummaries` in `searchService`, ONE `activeAlertSummaryByAsset` call over the asset AND site hits of a whole result set, mutating the hits in place so the mobile renderer's virtual Device Map rows inherit it when they clone. The **desktop search dropdown** draws it too, from the same field: `assetAlertStrobeColor` / `_alertSevRank` / `assetAlertDotHTML` MOVED from `assets.js` to **`app.js`** to make that possible — the dropdown renders on every page and half of them never load `assets.js`, so a guarded call would have shown the dot on some pages and not others. `alertSummaryDotHTML(summary)` is the new core (same markup from a bare summary, for callers holding no asset row); `assetAlertDotHTML(asset)` delegates to it. The dot sits before the monitor pill in a hit — the alert is the reason to look, the monitor state is the detail, and a hit can carry both since an alerting device is often Up. `#more/alerts` is the fleet-wide list and the mobile push deep-link destination (and acknowledges in place: each unacknowledged row gets a one-tap **Ack** control with `alerts:write`, rendered as a SIBLING of the row button rather than inside it — a nested `<button>` swallows the tap that opens the device. Clearing stays desktop-only, being the fullwrite half) (without it `routeChanged` bounces to `#search`). `public/js/pwa-install.js` (loaded FIRST — `beforeinstallprompt` can fire before boot) exposes `window.PolarisInstall`. **Web Push generally** (both surfaces, `public/js/push.js` + `public/sw.js`): there is **no enable/disable control anywhere** since business rule 39 — the account menu row, the mobile More tab row and the Automations page's `#btn-enable-push` were all replaced by ONE per-account preference (`User.notificationPreference`). `polarisPush.syncToPreference(pref, surface)` is what enrolls or un-enrolls a browser, called at boot by `wireNotificationPrefs` (desktop, app.js — caches the preference into `_notifPref` and the push status into `_pushState`; `_notifPrefMenuItem` renders “Notifications: Email” and `_openNotifPrefMenu` the three-way chooser, the openThemeMenu pattern) and by `wireNotifPrefRow` (mobile, more-tab.js) — and, on the phone, by `initPushOnce` in [public/js/mobile/app.js](public/js/mobile/app.js) at BOOT, not only when the More tab is opened: the point of storing the preference on the account is that a device the operator never touches again still honours a choice made somewhere else (a failed preference read there falls back to the bare `reconcileSubscription`, so a network blip costs the sync but never the rotated-endpoint repair). It **never prompts** — a boot-time call has no user activation — so it enrolls silently only where permission is already granted, and a browser that has never been asked stays un-enrolled until the operator picks the preference there. Choosing a push-bearing preference calls `enable()` FIRST, synchronously in the click/tap handler, before persisting. `enable()` calls `Notification.requestPermission()` **before** any network await (Safari drops transient user activation across a fetch, so no click handler may `await status()` — both preference surfaces cache the status for exactly that reason). Where the old toggle HID itself unless `status().enabledOnServer`, the preference row stays visible and disables only the two push OPTIONS: the choice belongs to the account, so an unsupported or permission-denied browser must not be able to withhold it (the operator's phone may honour what this laptop cannot). Only the SERVER having no Web Push channel makes them pointless. Both surfaces also wrap the boot-time preference read in `Promise.resolve().then(...)` — it runs inside the sidebar / More-tab render, and a synchronous throw there would take the navigation down with it. a push carrying an `ackUrl` grows an **Acknowledge action button** whose `notificationclick` branch POSTs the token (`credentials: "omit"` — the token is the credential, so no cookie and no CSRF header) and replaces the alert in the tray with a silent confirmation; iOS/Safari renders no action buttons, so the body tap remains the path there. `sw.js` has **no fetch handler and no Cache Storage** (online-only tool; a unit test enforces this) and gets its icon from `/icons/app-192.png`.
